On ''Big Brother 4 (US)'', Alison played one of the season's most aggressive and strategically flexible games, positioning herself between opposing alliances while maintaining relationships on both sides of the house. After surviving an early nomination through her influence over [[Nathan Marlow]], she used her HOH reign to eliminate [[Dana Varela]] and solidify herself as a key swing vote. Throughout the season, Alison constantly shifted allegiances, helping orchestrate major evictions while working closely with fellow floater [[Jun Song]]. Her ability to play both sides carried her to the Final Two, but her cutthroat gameplay and poor jury management left many jurors bitter. Despite winning the final HOH and choosing to sit next to Jun, Alison lost in a 6–1 vote, finishing as the runner-up. On ''Big Brother 7 (US)'', Alison was among the 14 out of 20 contestants chosen to go back into the house. She quickly targeted the [[Sovereign Six]] and joined [[Danielle Reyes]] with a plan to make [[Jase Wirey]] disagree with [[Janelle Pierzina]]’s nominations as the dual HOHs' disagreement on nomination would have placed the HOHs on the nomination block instead. Jase caught wind of the plan, which led to him and Janelle nominating Alison and Danielle. Alison began to campaign in the house, gaining [[Diane Henry]]'s and [[Nakomis Dedmon]]’s votes. [[Mike Malin]] and [[Will Kirby]] campaigned for Alison as well as they felt she would be a better ally to go after the Sovereign Six. On the other hand, The Sovereign Six viewed Alison as a bigger threat and campaigned to get her evicted. {{NorthAmerica}} {{gameplay | image= [[File:Backdoor-Jase-Wirey.png]] | description= A strategic move to evict a targeted player. | seasonsappeared=''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]'' - ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''
''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'' - ''[[Big Brother 28 (US)]]'' }} The '''backdoor technique''', also known as the '''six-finger plan''', is a strategic move in ''Big Brother'' intended to evict a targeted player by ensuring they are nominated for eviction without having the chance to secure their own safety through a Power of Veto competition. ==Background== Originally devised by [[Marvin Latimer]] and executed, and named, by [[Nakomis Dedmon]] in ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]'', the move was officially called the “backdoor” during the same season by Marvin. The strategy requires the [[Head of Household]] to avoid nominating the primary target at the [[Nominations|nomination ceremony]]. Instead, the HOH instead nominates two [[Pawn|pawns]], which helps prevent the actual target from being guaranteed a spot in the [[Power of Veto|POV]] [[Competitions|competition]]—a benefit when the target is a [[Competitive Strategies|strong competitor]]. [[File:Jason "Jase" Wirey.jpg|thumb|179px|link=Jase Wirey|[[Jase Wirey|Jase]] is the first person to get backdoored, during his stay on ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]''.]] If the target does not get to play in the POV competition, and the Veto is used to remove a pawn from the block, the HOH can then nominate their real target as the replacement. The house then votes to evict the newly placed nominee. Fans generally agree that a true backdoor only happens when the evicted houseguest did not play in the POV competition, making this strategy only possible up until the Final 7, when there are enough players to exclude someone from competing. Successfully executing a backdoor typically requires a tight alliance or a group of at least six cooperating houseguests, including enough non-HOHs and non-nominees willing to vote out the target. Pulling off the plan is difficult and relies on coordinated action across multiple stages. Starting with ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]'', the process became riskier when houseguests drew Veto players at random, rather than being selected. If the target is drawn and plays in the POV competition, but does not win, they can still be nominated as a replacement; however, this does not count as a traditional backdoor since the target had a chance to save themselves. The randomness added an element of chance, making it more difficult to guarantee the target cannot compete. In ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'', the introduction of the [[Second Chance Challenge]] via BB AI Arena and BB Block Buster made backdoors tougher to land strategically. With three nominees getting an extra shot to save themselves before eviction, a would-be target could dodge the block, blunting the traditional backdoor and forcing the HOH to adapt with backup plans and tighter vote control. Surviving a backdoor plan is rare but possible. Some houseguests are notable for repeated involvement with backdoors. [[Cody Nickson]] of ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'' was backdoored twice in one season: first by [[Paul Abrahamian]] in Week 2 (after which he returned by winning the [[Battle Back Competition]] in Week 4), and again by [[Alex Ow]] in Week 7. According to a July 2018 analysis by Peridiam, between ''Big Brother 5'' and ''Big Brother 20'', the backdoor was used 30 times. ''Big Brother 17'' features the highest count for a single season with four successful backdoors. Additionally, male contestants have been targeted more frequently, with 22 men versus 8 women being backdoored. Every season during that span saw at least one backdoor, except for ''Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)''.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kd1i5AvvYuw ==Statistics== ===Survived Attempts=== There have only been '''four''' contestants that have survived a backdoor attempt. *[[Eric Stein]] - ''[[Big Brother 8

}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Power of Veto]] and [[Head of Household]] competition. This competition is famous for featuring comic book covers with houseguests drawn as superheroes. It requires mainly attention to detail while having a physical component to it as well.

==Rules==
One at a time, players must climb a ladder and zip line slowly to view a window with comic books situated behind them. Down below, the players must precisely replicate the comics in order. There are, however, fake comic books in the pile of comics to choose from, so players have to be careful.

The player who gets all the comic books in the correct spot with the quickest time wins the POV.

Usually, there is a time limit of 35 minutes, upped to 45 in ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. If houseguest's time runs out, they are forced to stop and their result equals to this time limit.

In ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', the format was changed a bit for a new version of the competition that only appeared in this season thus far. The spot the difference aspect remained, but it involved looking at four screens that cycled through all the comics electronically, and then going out into the field and knocking down cardboard cutouts of the comic characters that didn't match the original picture. The physical aspect was also upgraded, with the zip line and drop still remaining, but with the addition of a balance beam as well. The competition was still timed, and so it is still possible for a houseguest to time out.

==History==
The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]''. [[Christine Brecht]] was the winner and it was her first individual win of the summer. Christine's time was 11 minutes 50 seconds. [[Nicole Franzel]] came in second and was 30 seconds behind Christine. Brecht's result was still the fastest after four times this competition was played, with Franzel's being the second best. The worst result was also achieved during this appearance of BB Comics when [[Victoria Rafaeli]] was not able to finish the task in 35 minutes.

BB Comics returned on ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]''. Eventual winner [[Steve Moses]] won this competition claiming his second PoV of the season. Steve's time was 13 minutes 57 seconds.

The competition showed up again on ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]''. Nicole Franzel played it for a second time and this time she won. Nicole completed the task in 13 minutes 55 seconds which was more than four minutes better than everybody else that season. [[James Huling]] didn't manage to finish the task in time repeating Victoria's failure during ''Big Brother 16''.

For ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'' the entire first half of the 11th week was based on BB Comics, and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5KFA6hBKwo4 many past HouseGuests reunited as their comic book characters for a short film called "The Revengers."] Any Revengers who did not have comics before this season had their comics and characters made for this one. Like ''Big Brother 17'', this appearance would have featured more comics than the others due to the larger number of houseguests on the season, however due to [[Megan Lowder]] [[Walking|walking]] from the game, she did not receive a comic. [[Paul Abrahamian]] won this competition with a time of 12 minutes and 10 seconds. [[Kevin Schlehuber]] couldn't finish in time (45 minutes), and so he timed out just like James and Victoria.

The competition returned again for ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', but in a slightly different format. The spot the difference aspect remained, but the physical portion of the competition was upgraded from just a zip line and a huge drop, with the addition of a balance beam. ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' |countriesappeared={{United States}}}} '''America's Nominee''' is a minor first introduced during the [[Most Valuable Player|MVP twist]] in ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]''. Initially presented as a secondary element within the MVP format, it later evolved into a central feature in ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]''. The twist returned once again in ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'', appearing alongside [[Diamond Power of Veto#Modern Variations|America's Veto]]. ==History== ===[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]=== In the initial three weeks of the show, viewers voted for the [[Most Valuable Player]], who was tasked with anonymously selecting a third nominee for eviction each week. The MVP's choice was disclosed just before the [[Power of Veto]] competition, and they had the option to reveal their identity to other HouseGuests. After these three weeks, the role of the MVP shifted to the American public, who continued to nominate a third player for eviction during the subsequent three weeks. ===[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]=== Each week America could nominate a third houseguest to be nominated for eviction, alongside the two nominees chosen by the [[Head of Household]]. However, America could not vote for the same person two weeks in a row, ensuring that the nominations remain varied. Additionally, if the third nominee is saved by the Power of Veto, there is no replacement nominee. This twist adds complexity to the game, as houseguests must consider the influence of America's vote and adapt their strategies accordingly. ===[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]=== [[Diamond Power of Veto#Modern Variations|America's Veto]] is a twist in ''Big Brother 26'' that allows the holder to use the Power of Veto within the first four weeks of the game. When used, it removes one nominee from the block, but instead of the Head of Household selecting a replacement, the decision is put to a public vote. [[Jillian Parker]]|TwitterUserName = ItsAlexOwDuh|InstagramUserName = itsalexowhey|birthdate = {{Birth date and age|1988|12|20|mf=yes}}|Currently1 = Jury Member}} '''Alexandra Rose "Alex" Ow''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. Alex was best known for her alliance with [[Jason Dent]], a secret partnership with [[Paul Abrahamian]], and her bitter rivalry with [[Kevin Schlehuber]]. Initially and frequently targeted by [[Jessica Graf]], Alex was nominated as a replacement for [[Megan Lowder]], who was initially nominated but had Walked from the game. She had scored the Veto and won a lot of competitions from there on, which sent out targets like [[Dominique Cooper]] and [[Cody Nickson]]. When Jason was blindsided during the first half of the second [[Double Eviction]], this left Alex as the odd one out. She managed to survive the second half by winning HoH. In the final 5, she was nominated. When Paul won the PoV, he decided not to save her, sealing his true alliance with Josh and Christmas, betraying her. [[Josh Martinez]] ultimately cast the tiebreaker vote against her with Paul casting a sympathy vote to evict Kevin, sending her out of the game. She placed 5th and was the seventh member of the [[jury]]. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from CBS.com'' http://www.cbs.com/shows/big_brother/cast/215651/
'''Age:''' 28
'''Hometown:''' Thousand Oaks, CA
'''Current city:''' Camarillo, CA
'''Occupation:''' Eco-friendly marketing rep
'''Three adjectives that describe you:''' Center of attention, hyper, and adorable.
'''Favorite activities:''' I love knitting, crocheting, baking, going to the gym, going out with friends, hanging out with my family, watching Netflix, hiking, dating, and being lazy. My spirit animal is a sloth. LOL.
'''What do you think will be the most difficult part about living inside the Big Brother house?'''
Honestly, what will kill me the most is being on TV, but not being able to watch it. I listen to Netflix at work, and I watch like five straight hours of TV after dinner until I fall asleep. It'll be nice though for the TV detox!
'''Which past Big Brother cast member did you like most?'''
I love [[Nicole Franzel]] from Season [[Big Brother 16 (US)|16]] and the winner of Season [[Big Brother 18 (US)|18]]! She's seriously a fan favorite. I find her the most honest and most relatable. While she did do some shady things, like turning her back on alliances, she was in it to win it and I respect the way she went about it. She reminds me of myself. We look all cute and cuddly, but we're here for one thing—to win Big Brother.
'''Do you have a strategy for winning the game?'''
Yes. Standing at my fun-sized, 5-foot-nothing height might make me look like an easy target, and I anticipate that people in the house will overlook me and confuse my kindness for weakness. But I play for the long endgame, and that's to win. If they see me as a non-threat, I can fly under the radar until the stronger players are weeded out. Once this happens, I can show my true colors, but still, play as a "weakling." [[Sam Bledsoe]] |YoutubeUserName = BayleighDaily |InstagramUserName = bayydayy |HackerComp=0 | thechallenge = {{otherfandom|thechallenge|Bayleigh_Dayton}} }} '''Bayleigh Amethyst Dayton'''{{cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Big_Brother_20_houseguests_(U.S.)|title=List of Big Brother 20 houseguests (U.S.)|publisher=Wikipedia|accessdate=14 July 2018}} was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. In ''Big Brother 20 (US)'', Bayleigh was known for her [[showmance]] with [[Chris Williams]], and aligned early with the ill-fated [[FOUTTE]] alliance. After losing her showmance in Week 2, Bayleigh laid low, secretly winning a power app and forming bonds with other houseguests. This continued until she won HOH in Week 5, where during her disastrous reign as HOH, Bayleigh told [[Rachel Swindler]] about her power app to establish trust, leading to Rachel telling her [[Level Six]] alliance about the power app. Deciding to target [[Brett Robinson]] (whom was a failed target of her alliance). After a miscommunication between Bayleigh, Rachel and [[Tyler Crispen]], the Level Six alliance decided to turn on Rachel and keep Bayleigh’s target Brett in the house. Come eviction night, they were successful in blindsiding Bayleigh and her allies, and the following week, Bayleigh was lured into a false sense of security by HOH [[Angela Rummans]]. After deciding not to use her power app and save it, Bayleigh would be framed as the [[Hacker Competition|hacker]] for the week, resulting in Angela's backdoor attempt against her, proven successful at the POV meeting. After [[Haleigh Broucher]] called a house meeting, Bayleigh got into an explosive argument with Tyler. This would seal Bayleigh’s fate as she was later evicted by a vote of 6-1, placing 11th and becoming the first member of the jury. In ''Big Brother 22'' ''(US)'', Bayleigh found herself in a comfortable position in the first four weeks, finding herself friendly with [[Enzo Palumbo]], [[Ian Terry]], [[David Alexander]], a previous foe in Tyler, and [[Da'Vonne Rogers]], whom she created an [[Black Girl Magic (BB22)|alliance]] with. In Week 5, however, she notified HOH [[Christmas Abbott]] that her closest ally Da'Vonne was her "untouchable" (final 2 alliance), causing Christmas to nominate both of them. Angry that Christmas used their personal conversation to target her and Da'Vonne, Bayleigh would have an explosive feud with Christmas and get into a confrontation with her after arguing with Da’Vonne. Bayleigh would then be evicted that week by a unanimous 9-0 vote, placing 12th. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | BB20= '''Age:''' 25

BB App Store.head:
{{twists |image = [[File:BB App Store.jpg|225px]] |description = One houseguest will be given a power and one houseguest will receive a punishment. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} |seasonsappeared = ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'' }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the main twist of ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''. ==Press Release== ''Retrieved from CBS.com''
This summer, it's time to twist up the game of ''Big Brother''—and the power is in your hands, America! You get to decide which Season 20 Houseguest is trending in the BB house by answering a series of questions. Each week, the Houseguest who gets the most responses will be considered "trending" and allowed to enter the BB App Store, resulting in power apps or punishments that could crash their game. Once a Houseguest wins a power app or punishment, they are ineligible to receive another one.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbs.com/shows/big_brother/news/1008598/how-to-cast-your-big-brother-vote-in-the-cbs-bot-on-facebook-messenger-kik-and-skype/|title=How To Cast Your Big Brother Vote In The CBS Bot On Facebook Messenger, Kik, And Skype|publisher=CBS Big Brother|date=27 June 2018|accessdate=3 July 2018}} ==="BB App Store" Room Gallery=== BBAppStore 1.JPG BBAppStore 2.JPG BBAppStore 3.JPG ==Big Brother App Store== {{BBAppStore}} ==List of Chosen Apps== ===Power Apps=== |-|Week 1=[[File:BBAppBonusLife.png|70px]] '''Bonus Life'''
Description: This power gives you or the houseguest of your choosing the CHANCE to return to the game if evicted. This power is good through the first four evictions. But here's the catch, if the Bonus Life is not used at one of the first three evictions, the 4th person evicted automatically gets a chance to return to the game.
Outcome: The App was won by [[Sam Bledsoe]]. After not using the app for the first 3 weeks, Sam won the Week 4 HoH in order to still have control over who the app was used on, and eventually got [[Kaitlyn Herman]] evicted, but when the Bonus Life competition was offered, she couldn't complete it in time, thus eliminating both her and the Bonus Life. Had Kaitlyn returned, it was announced that she would have been granted immunity for that week. |-|Week 2=[[File:BBAppTheCloud.png|70px]]'''The Cloud'''
Description: Keep yourself from going on the block at any one Nomination Ceremony or Veto Meeting. If you are worried you could be nominated, sit in the cloud, and you cannot be put on the block. You have a two-month subscription to the Cloud. So for the next eight weeks, you may choose one time in which to use the Cloud to keep yourself safe!
Outcome: The App was won by [[Tyler Crispen]]. It ended up becoming the last app left in the game, as the Bonus Life was used automatically, and the Identity Theft was eliminated alongside its holder. However, the app remained unused throughout most of the two month period, and after his [[Level Six|alliance members]] [[Angela Rummans]] and [[Kaycee Clark]] won HoH and PoV respectively during Week 9, the last week that the app was in play, Tyler did not need to use the Cloud, and so it expired. |-|Week 3=[[File:BBAppIdentityTheft.png|70px]]'''Identity Theft'''
Description: At any point in the first half of the game, you can secretly steal the identity of one Head of Household at the Nomination Ceremony! The reigning HOH cannot be nominated and will still control the replacement nominee at the Veto Meeting. When only 8 houseguests remain, the Identity Theft power is no longer in play.
Outcome: The App was won by [[Bayleigh Dayton]]. After initially telling [[Faysal Shafaat]] about the app immediately after winning it, Bayleigh kept it a secret until she won the Week 5 HoH and told [[Rachel Swindler]] in order to convince her to be a [[Pawn]]. Each week before the final eviction vote, the final three nominated contestants would compete in a last chance competition to save themselves. The winner of each competition would then be saved from the eviction vote with no chance to replace the nominee by reducing the three nominees to final two nominees. The competition was later introduced to the American franchise in ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' as the '''AI Arena'''. With the success of the concept, the twist returned for ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]],'' according to Julie in the premiere episode the twist would be a permanent aspect of the game, known in subsequent seasons as the '''BB Block Buster'''. In the [[Gran Hermano Chile (franchise)|Chilean]] and [[Big Brother UK (franchise)|United Kingdom]] versions, this competition has been named the '''Salvation''' competition. ==History== ===Australia=== ====Season 13==== ===== Day 60 ===== At the start of Week 9, the remaining houseguests were introduced to Second Chance Week. On Day 60, the three nominated houseguests [[Adriana Fernandez]], [[Christina Podolyan]], and [[Sarah Jane Adams]] competed in the first ever Second Chance Challenge. In order to earn safety, the nominated houseguests had to build a 60-piece puzzle wall and then demolish it using a swinging wrecking drum. Sarah Jane demolished her puzzle first, saving herself from eviction. ===== Day 61 ===== Continuing Second Chance Week, an additional Second Chance Challenge was held on Day 61. As the nominated houseguests for the round, [[Ari Kimber]], [[Daniel Hayes]], and [[Sid Pattni]] competed for safety by attempting to balance on a slackline while holding a rope for as long as possible. '''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' Outgoing, bubbly, and an oversharer! [''Laughs''.]
'''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' Oh my gosh, to be on ''Big Brother'', I’m actually jumping up and down. I’m so still right now, but internally, I’m oh so very excited, and like a little nervy. There is some competitive players, but I might be one of them! [''Laughs''.]

So I would love to backstab, but while having such a blast of a time.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' The biggest misconception that people have about me is that they think I am “box of rocks” dumb. They think I’m a little ditz, they think I’m a little airheady. But it’s just because I’m having a blast.

I guess it just depends on whenever I get there, and if people really grind my gears. The people grinding your gears, you’re gonna be a villain. If people grind my gears, the villainess might come out. I would hope, honestly, for the excitement of it all, I want to be in my villain era.

Ian O'Malley (2000) |seriesrun = July 5, 2000 - |title=}} '''''Big Brother''''' is a popular international reality show franchise with an American version owned by [[CBS]]. ==How it Works== [[File:BBUS Days Chart.png|thumb|right|250px|The amount of days per season.]] Big Brother is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are 10-17 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ===American series=== [[File:Episodes of Big Brother US (per season).png|thumb|right|250px|The amount of episodes per season]] While most versions of ''Big Brother'' feature evictions that are voted on by polling television audiences over the phone or the internet, the American version shifted before ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)|Big Brother 2]]'' to play off the popularity of ''[[w:c:survivor|Survivor]]'' and changed the format to have the other house guests evict players. '''''Retrieved from CBS'''''
BIG BROTHER follows a group of people living together in a house outfitted with dozens of high-definition cameras and microphones recording their every move, 24 hours a day. Each week, the houseguests will vote someone out of the house. At the end, the last remaining houseguest will receive the grand prize of $500,000.http://www.cbs.com/shows/big_brother/about/ ===Original Format (Big Brother 1)=== The original American version of Big Brother follows a different format compared to its succeeding seasons. This format followed the Dutch format used by many Big Brother franchises around the world, notably [[Big Brother UK (franchise)|Big Brother UK]]. In this format, the narrative of the series focuses more on the organic relationships among the housemates while staying in their authentic selves rather than the competitive and strategic narrative that the current American format does. In this format, the housemates were not allowed to strategize nor influence fellow housemates on who to vote for nominations and evictions and doing so is considered a major violation. In addition, the American public has the sole power to evict a houseguest as well as select a winner at the end of the season. The major elements of the format are as follows: ====Weekly Tasks==== Every week, Big Brother gives the houseguests a [[Weekly Task]]. The result of the weekly task determine the house's grocery budget for the upcoming week. These weekly tasks typically last for more than a day up to an entire week and often require teamwork in order to succeed. Prior to the start of their weekly tasks, Big Brother allows them to bet their budget depending on the house's confidence on succeeding the task. It began on July 5, 2000 and aired on [[CBS]] for 88 days, concluding on September 29, 2000 when [[Eddie McGee]] was crowned the winner with votes from America. Season 1 of ''Big Brother'' is radically different from following American seasons of the series. It was a near-exact port of the hit Netherlands series of the same name. Every week, Housemates would nominate two fellow housemates and the two or more housemates with the most nominations were eligible for banishment. American viewers could then call a 1-900 number and cast a vote to evict a HouseGuest. There was no [[Head of Household]], [[Power of Veto]], or [[Food Competition|Food Competitions]], but rather the HouseGuests would have to complete [[Weekly Task|Weekly Tasks]] (also called Week Long Challenges) to win rewards for the house. There were 6 episodes each week: a one-hour live eviction show, and five 30-minute daily recaps. ==Background== ===Development=== The series first launched in the Netherlands, with editions in countries such as Germany proving to be hits with the public. Following the international success of the series, a bidding war for the rights to series engaged between CBS, ABC, and a cable network, with the series initially set to last 100 days. Ultimately, it was confirmed that the show had been picked up by [[CBS]] for an estimated $20 million. On the concept, executive producer Paul Romer stated "The show is all about human interactions. It's people who are, loving each other, hating each other. They fight, they cry, they laugh -- all emotions, we'll see in the house." In a later interview, Romer added "The first thing people think of when they hear the Big Brother idea are the sexual things, the nudity, the sexual activity in the house [...] That's not what the show is about." The series was one of the first reality shows to air in the US and required a crew of over 150 people. ===Hosts=== The first season of Big Brother featured two hosts, [[Julie Chen]] as the main host, and Ian O'Malley as a co-host. ===Casting=== The cast for the series was revealed during the premiere. HouseGuest William was revealed to be a member of the Black Panther Party, while Jamie was crowned Miss Washington USA the year prior to her participation on the show. HouseGuests Curtis and Josh had done modeling prior to entering the house. Jean Jordan had been an exotic dancer before entering the house, while Karen and George were married and had children. Cassandra and William were both African-American. Series creator John de Mol later stated "''The 10 people in our house, you can relate to them. It's the girl next door, it's the guy in the grocery store [...] It's ordinary people, and I think that Big Brother proves ordinary people can be interesting.''" ===Airing & Schedule=== The first season of Big Brother premiered on July 5, 2000. It began on July 5, 2001, and aired on [[CBS]] for 82 days, concluding on September 20, 2001, when [[Will Kirby]] was crowned the winner with five votes from the [[Jury|evicted HouseGuests]], winning $500,000. The format of ''Big Brother 2'' differed from that of the first American season, which had been a direct adaptation of the original Dutch version. In Season 2, every week the houseguests competed to become the [[Head of Household]] (HOH). The HOH would then nominate two houseguests for eviction. The fellow contestants would vote, and the player with the most votes would be evicted. On Finale night, all former houseguests returned to vote for whom they thought should win the grand prize. ==Background== ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists/Changes== *'''More Gameplay-Oriented Format:''' The show pivoted from a [[America's Eviction Vote|public-vote]] social experiment to a competitive, player-driven game centered on weekly power, nominations, and strategic voting. *'''Nomination Discussion Allowed:''' Unlike many international versions that restrict nomination talk, houseguests in Season 2 could openly discuss nominations and strategy, facilitating [[Alliance|alliances]] and coordinated gameplay. *'''[[Head of Household]]:''' Each week, one houseguest won Head of Household, securing themselves immunity and the power to nominate two houseguests for eviction; the outgoing HOH sat out the next HOH competition. *'''[[Food Competition]]:''' Weekly Food Competitions determined access to normal food; losers were placed on a peanut butter and jelly diet for the week. *'''[[Luxury Competition]]:''' Luxury competitions awarded perks such as screenings and treats for houseguests. *'''[[Vote to Evict|HouseGuests Vote to Evict]]:''' Eviction power shifted from the viewing public to the houseguests, who cast votes to evict one of the nominees each week. *'''[[The Jury| The Jury Determines the Winner]]:''' For the first time in the Big Brother format, previously evicted houseguests returned to vote between the Final 2 to [[Winners (US)|win]] the grand prize. ==HouseGuests== {{BB2 Progress}} ===Survivor Visitors=== {{US 2 Visitors}} ==Voting History== {{BB2 Voting History}} ==Food History== {{BBUS2 Food History}} ==Competition History== {{BB2 Competition History}} ==Game History== {{BB2 Game History}} ===Week 1=== {| | {{WhichBoxSquare|Square-Mike "Boogie" Malin.jpg|Mike "Boogie" Malin|'''[[Mike "Boogie" Malin|Mike]]'''|9966CC|HOH}} | {{WhichBoxSquare|Square-Nicole Nilson Schaffrich.jpg|Nicole Nilson Schaffrich|'''[[Nicole Nilson Schaffrich|Nicole]]'''|CC6666|Nominee

Introducing a cast of 13 new houseguests, the season featured a focus on more strategic and social gameplay with fewer twists. Season highlights include the powershift that took out [[Brian Hart]]'s initial control leading to his eviction, the huge arguments among the houseguests, the infamous [[Keesha Smith|Keesha]]'s birthday fight, the week-long [[America's Player]] twist, and [[Dan Gheesling]]'s high-level strategy and maneuvering from the bottom. After 71 days of unpredictable and high-octane gameplay, Dan Gheesling defeated [[Memphis Garrett]] by a vote of 7-0, making the former the first to win a [[Perfect Game]] in ''Big Brother (US)'' history. ==Background== The show premiered July 13, 2008 on the CBS television network,airing three times a week; Sundays at 8 p.m. (ET/PT), Tuesdays at 9 p.m. (ET/PT), and Thursdays at 8 p.m (live ET/delayed PT). Julie Chen returned as host, and Allison Grodner, Rich Meehan and Scott Einziger were the executive producers. The show was produced by Endemol USA and Allison Grodner Productions. The finale was Tuesday, September 16, 2008. This was the second edition of the show to air in the same year. Originally, only one summer edition was due to air, but the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike prompted CBS to air an additional season, Big Brother 9, from February to April during the regular television season and Big Brother 10 for the summer of 2008. Big Brother 10 lasted just 71 days, nearly a week and a half shorter than most seasons, making this the shortest season of the American series of Big Brother. This also marked the last time that the season number or year of airing would be mentioned in the broadcast and in the logo; subsequent seasons were simply referred to as Big Brother, with the logo omitting the season number in favor of an animation of a shutting door. ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists== * '''Back to Basics:''' All of the houseguests were total strangers, unlike previous seasons where some contestants had pre-existing relationships. In addition, live audiences returned for the Thursday eviction episodes, marking the first time this had been done since [[Big Brother 1 (US)|Season 1]]. * '''[[America's Player|Temporary America's Player]]:''' During Week 4, Dan was offered the chance to become America's Player for one week. [[wikipedia:Showtime (TV network)|Showtime Two]] (BBAD)|numberofepisodes = 29|viewership = 7.95m|companionshows = [[Big Brother: After Dark]]|challengeproducer=Trent Eaton}} '''Big Brother 13''' is the 13th season of the broadcasted edition of ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother (U.S.)]]''. This season introduced significant gameplay changes. Initially, the eight new houseguests were required to pair up with a partner. Subsequently, six [[Returning Players|former players]] entered the house in pre-formed [[Dynamic Duos|duos]]. Each week, houseguests competed for Head of Household, granting immunity from eviction to the HOH and their partner. The HOH was responsible for nominating another duo for eviction. A Power of Veto competition was held later in the week, allowing both members of a nominated duo to potentially [[Boomerang Power of Veto|save themselves from eviction]], forcing the HOH to nominate a replacement duo. The season had two major alliances: the [[Newbies]], consisting of all new houseguests, and the [[Veterans]], comprising all returning houseguests. ==Background== ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists== *'''[[Dynamic Duos]]:''' Shortly after entering the house, Julie informed the eight new houseguests that they had to pick a partner to compete in the game alongside. If either person won [[HOH]], both members would be safe from nomination. Conversely, the HOH could only nominate an entire duo. The [[POV]], if used, would remove an entire duo, causing the HOH to have to nominate another duo. In addition to the eight new houseguests, three duos from past seasons returned to the game and attempt to become the champion of another edition of ''Big Brother''. * '''[[Golden Key]]:''' Because the houseguests are competing in duos, once a member of a duo is evicted, the other member then is awarded a Golden Key, which grants them immunity until there are ten houseguests remaining. They will not be allowed to participate in any competitions, but will be allowed to vote. * '''[[Previously Evicted Contestant|Previously Evicted Houseguest]]:''' During the Week 5, it was revealed to the houseguests that the next person evicted would have a chance to come back into the house. The first four evicted houseguests would also have a chance to come back. America was allowed to vote for one of the first four evicted houseguests and the one with the most votes would compete against the next evicted houseguest to go back into the house. * '''[[Pandora's Box]]:''' Pandora's Box returned this season, which; when opened either unleashed a reward or a punishment for either house or the HOH that opened it. ** '''Temporary Duo Twist:''' The Duo Twist was brought back once again for one week as soon as {{bb13|Porsche}} opened Pandora's Box. ==Houseguests== {{BB13 Progress}} ===Duos=== {{BBUS13 Duos}} ==House== See pictures of the [[Big Brother 13 House gallery]].

These veterans entered the house to mentor teams of new houseguests. On Day 1, the coaches drafted their teams, each selecting three new players to guide through the game. While living in the house alongside their teams, the coaches could initially not compete in the Head of Household or Power of Veto, could not be nominated, and did not vote in evictions. If one of their selected houseguests wins the season, their coach will win a $100,000 prize. **'''[[Premiere Night Eviction|Night One Eviction]]:''' On Night 1, Julie revealed that one houseguest would be evicted by the end of the night. After the coaches drafted their players, they competed in a special Hit The Road competition where the first three teams to finish would be immune for the night, while the losing team would be nominated for eviction. The first placing team's coach would choose one of their members to become the first HOH of the summer, while the losing team's coach would have to evict one of their own members. **'''[[Coaches Competition]]''': Each week, the four coaches competed in a competition exclusively for them. The winner of this competition was granted a powerful choice: they could award immunity to one of their own players for the week, or, in some weeks, trade one of their team members for a player from another coach’s team. The outcome of the Coaches Competition also impacted the Have-Not status in the house. That individual, the MVP, earned the power to secretly nominate a third nominee for eviction. The MVP’s choice was announced to the house just before each week’s [[Power of Veto]] competition. The MVP could decide privately whether to reveal their power to fellow houseguests. ** '''[[America's Nominee]]:''' After three weeks, the twist shifted: America took over as the MVP and directly determined the additional nominee and replacement nominee for another three weeks. * '''[[Previously Evicted Contestant|Jury]] [[Re-Entry Competition]]:''' For the first time in ''Big Brother'' history, evicted jurors were given a chance to return to the game. }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the seventeenth series of ''[[Big Brother (UK)]]''.

This season saw the return of the house being rebuilt. Since the show moved to their current location in 2002, the house has stayed the same with the rooms occasionally being changed. Over the past months leading up to the premiere, a second house was built next door to the current house with a hallway separating the two.

==The House==
On February 2nd, 2016 it was revealed that a planning application had been made towards the Hertsmere Borough Council, confirming that Endemol had applied for an extension to the Big Brother UK house. Within the documents it had been teased that a second house would be constructed, alongside a second garden. Both the evictions set and eye studio were both demolished after [[Celebrity Big Brother 17 (UK)|Celebrity Big Brother 17]] had concluded. On March 18th of the same year it was announced that the application had gone through, with the outdoor set being smaller than previously.

The first house pictures were released on June 2nd, 2016 and revealed, featuring a 70's-style themed house, with a black, white, yellow and pink aesthetic. The main house featured a large living room, featuring a yellow circular couch and pink stools with black and white stripy flooring and has been merged with the kitchen, including the door to the diary room situated at the back of the kitchen. The stair-case was also moved more into the centre position at the back of the living room. The room also features black and pink neon panels, as well as 70s-styled ceiling lights. There's one singular bedroom that features four double beds and four singular beds, also featuring a make-up table, where Housemates can do their make-up. The room also features a black and white leathery aesthetic. The garden is shared by both the main and "Others" house and features a large section of astro-turf, 3 sets of deck-chairs, a pool and hot-tub and a smoking area.

The ten housemates entered on July 14, 2000, just 9 days after the [[Big Brother 1|American]] version began, and 64 days later, [[Craig Phillips]] emerged victorious over runner-up [[Anna Nolan]]. This series set the trend for the format of the rest of the ''[[Big Brother (UK)]]'' franchise - each week, the housemates would nominate two of their fellow housemates for eviction. After all of the nominations were counted and the nominees were decided, the public would vote on which housemate they would like to leave the house, though the format has varied to some degree over the course of the franchise. Each week the housemates would compete in tasks set by Big Brother in order to win rewards for the house, such as alcohol or their weekly shopping budget. Housemates [[Nick Bateman]] and [[Melanie Hill]] returned for the spin-off ''[[Big Brother Panto]]'' during the 2004 holiday season. The season's winner, Craig, would later return in ''[[Big Brother 10 (UK)|Big Brother 10]]'' to participate in a task. Nick would later compete in ''[[Ultimate Big Brother]]'', with Craig, Anna, [[Darren Ramsay]] and [[Caroline O'Shea]] participating in tasks. == Twists == * '''Additional Housemates: '''As a result of Nick's [[Ejection|ejection]], on Day 37 an additional housemate (Claire) entered the house. ==Housemates== {{BBUK 2000 Progress}} ==Tasks== {{BBUK1 Tasks}} ==Nomination History== {{BBUK 2000 Nominations History}} '''Note:''' During the first round of nominations Week 7, the housemates overheard Darren making his nominations in the Diary Room. To avoid affecting the outcome of the game, Big Brother voided this round of nominations and had everyone nominated again. During this Darren changed his nominations, resulting in Craig and Claire being nominated. Had Big Brother gone with the original nominations, Darren and Melanie would have also been nominated. ==Game History== ''Retrieved from Channel 4''https://web.archive.org/web/20100914140350/http://www.channel4.com/entertainment/tv/microsites/B/bb1/what.html {{BBUK1 Game History}} ==Trivia== *The "eye" for this season is actually contestant [[Melanie Hill]]'s eye. *[[Darren Ramsay]] was the only housemate from this series to have a child. *[[Nick Bateman]] was the only contestant not to receive a single eviction nomination from any of his fellow housemates. *This season featured the first ejection in the ''Big Brother'' franchise. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{UK Seasons}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:United Kingdom Seasons]]

The house feature a kitchen with a gold aesthetic, with the living room being seen in the centre of the house, featuring a large orang circular seating area that replicated the Big Brother eye. The bedroom of the house was located next to the living room and featured 4 double beds and six singular beds. The bedroom also featured a large dressing room and a vanity mirror. {{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (also known as '''But First''',''' Time After Time''' and '''Foggy Memory''') is a recurring [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]] competition. ==Rules== This is a typical [[Head of Household#Quiz Competition|Head of Household quiz competition]] even when it is used as a [[Power of Veto]] competition. Each question is about two events that occurred earlier in the game. The houseguests should determine if the first event happened before or after the second event. ==History== ===United States=== The competition first appeared at the final four HoH competition on ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]''. [[Drew Daniel]] was the only one to answer all eight questions correctly, winning against [[Diane Henry]] and [[Michael Ellis]]. The competition appeared on ''[[Big Brother 6 (US)]]'', again at the final four HoH competition. [[Janelle Pierzina]] beat [[April Lewis]] and [[Maggie Ausburn]] to claim the HoH, securing a spot in the final three. In total seven questions were asked although Janelle's win was already determined after six of them. Like Drew Daniel the previous year Janelle had a perfect score. Next time the competition was played on ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]''. This time it was called "But First" referring to [[Julie Chen]]'s regular using of this expression. Instead of the traditional question "Was event A before or after event B?" there was a statement "Event A happened but first event B happened" and houseguests needed to determine whether the statement is true or false. At the elimination-based quiz after only three questions [[Erika Landin]] was the last one standing and she became the new HoH. Next season, on ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]'', the competition was played during the double eviction. It was a point-based quiz with eight questions. Eventual winner [[Dick Donato]] beat [[Eric Stein]] and [[Daniele Donato]], gaining his second HoH win. The competition also appeared during [[Big Brother 9]] right after the end of the couples twist. It was in a form of an elimination-based quiz with true or false questions about the order of events in the house. After three questions only [[Adam Jasinski]] and [[Ryan Quicksall]] remained. After three more questions Ryan claimed the victory and became the next HoH. Before or After competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)]]'' during Week 6. For the first time it was used as a Power of Veto competition, and it is believed that one of the reasons for that was [[Chima Simone]]'s expulsion from the house. After four questions of an elimination-based quiz only [[Jordan Lloyd]] and [[Michele Noonan]] were left standing. The next four questions were answered correctly by both remaining houseguests. Then for the first time in the history of this competition a tie-breaker question was played. And it was Jordan, the eventual winner of the season, who won the competition, securing her first PoV win. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', there was again a Before or After PoV competition. It was played during double eviction. The quiz was elimination-based and after six questions [[Ragan Fox]] won the competition, securing his second PoV win of the summer. The competition once again appeared on ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]'', during the first double eviction of the summer, back as a Head of Household competition. In an elimination-based quiz after four questions [[Kalia Booker]] won the competition claiming her second HoH title. Daphne Deckers |prizemoney = ƒ250,000 |numberofdays = 106 |network = [[wikipedia:Veronica TV|Veronica]] | nextseries = [[Big Brother 2 (Netherlands)]] |nomberofhousemates = 12 |returnees = [[Bart in 't Veld]] ''([[Hotel Big Brother|HBB]])'' |winner = [[Bart in 't Veld]] |runnersup = [[Ruud Bénard]]|castphoto=Netherlands1 Cast.jpg}}'''''Big Brother 1''''' is the very first season of the ''Big Brother'' franchise, shot in the [[Big Brother Netherlands (franchise)|Netherlands]]. This was the only season of ''Big Brother'' to be shot in the 1990s. ==Background== === Development === Plans for the show started in 1997 when John de Mol, Patrick Scholtze and brothers Bart and Paul Römer were having the idea of a show with real people as protagonists. The working title was ''Project X'' and it was supposed to run for a year. The element of nominations was already part of the concept to underline the soap element of loyalty and potential betrayal.https://www.bigbrother1999.nl/het-programma/about/project-x/ On a later stage, the working title changed to ''De Gouden Kooi (The Golden Cage)'' and would eventually air from 2006 to 2008. After the original concept was not picked up by TV stations it was modeled to a 100-day-event. Dutch writer Haye van der Heyden is credited to gave the show its name after the producers made an open call for suggestions.https://revu.nl/artikel/19684/wie-denkt-big-brother-wel-dat-hij-is The inspiration came from the phrase "Big Brother is watching you" in the George Orwell novel ''1984.'' First commercials to announce Big Brother were shown from middle of August.https://www.bigbrother1999.nl/versie-1999/commercial/ === Hosts === The first season of Big Brother featured Rolf Wouters as the main host and Daphne Deckers as co-host. === Casting === Nearly 3.000 people applied to be on the show. Applications could be sent via internet, telephone or a voucher in the newspaper. In the end, nine people were chosen to be on the show. Three additional female contestants moved in later to replace those that where leaving the house voluntary. === Airing & Schedule === The first season of Big Brother premiered on September 16, 1999. In the beginning, daily recaps with events that covered the day before where shown weekdays from 7.55 to 8.30 pm. However, the show was later moved on hour ahead from 6.55 to 7.30 pm to avoid clashed with the daily soap ''Goede Tijden Slechte Tijden'', which belonged to the same Holland Media Group.https://www.bigbrother1999.nl/het-programma/uitzendingen/ Additionally a weekend episode was aired sundays at 6.10 pm. The live show which saw nominations and evictions took place thursdays at 10.20 pm. With the ongoing success of the show, from November 6, the show also aired saturday at 8.30 pm. === Theme Song === The theme song was called "Leef!" (Live!) and was performed by Han van Eijk. Thanks to the success of the show, it topped the dutch single charts. It was later covered in several international adaptations of ''Big Brother'' such as in Germany , Belgium, the US, Australia or Brazil. == Twists == * '''The Bribe''': In week 5, the producers decided to make an offer of 10,000 Guilder which the two houseguests that would voluntary walk on the same night would earn. [[Bianca Plune|Bianca]] and [[Mona Rooth-de Leeuw|Mona]] took the Bribe. ==House== The house was constructed in Almere with an estimated area of 145 m2 plus a garden of 216 m2 and a technical control center of 162 m2. 24 cameras and 59 microphones recorded the life of the houseguests. Following a ''Back-to-Basic-''format the interior design was simple and consisted of IKEA-styled-furniture. ==Background==
===Possible Cancellation===
After a drop in ratings in 2017, Channel 5 boss Ben Frow stated that he would like to take ''Big Brother UK'' off of the air.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbspy.co.uk/cbb20/news/0825/channel-5-director-programmes-ben-frow-admits-he-would-be-happier-if-the-broadcaster-didnt-air-big-brother-uk|title=Channel 5 boss admits he’d prefer NOT to have Big Brother|publisher=bbspy|date=25 August 2017}}</ref> The summer's [[Big Brother 18 (UK)|civilian series]] fell at an all-time low average at less than one million viewers a night where most of the viewers watched ITV2's Love Island. “A year ago, everyone was saying 16-34s aren’t watching television. Love Island has proved that if you get the right programme, they will come", said Frow. “I’ve got Big Brother on the channel which is, you know, decline decline decline. Still a useful programme. But this is a really good time for me to take a step back and look at a programme that was the be all and end all for our 16-34s and go, what are we gonna do?” [[Wikipedia: Richard Desmond|Richard Desmond]] head of the channel when executives decided to revive the format back in 2011 after Channel 4 canceled the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Desmond|title=Richard Desmond|publisher=Wikipedia}}</ref> “That was a contract that was there before I came,” said Frow. “I would be much happier with a channel that did not have Big Brother on it.” However, Frow would go on to say that he did, in fact, enjoy the rating boost that ''Big Brother'' brought to the channel. Back in 2013, he said at the Guardian Edinburgh International Television Festival that “Big Brother’s very important, I think it was genius, genius, genius of Channel 5 to take it. My only concern about it is that it’s such a big beast, and we need to manage the big beast because we can’t become over-reliant on it".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbspy.co.uk/cbb20/news/0825/channel-5-director-programmes-ben-frow-admits-he-would-be-happier-if-the-broadcaster-didnt-air-big-brother-uk|title=Channel 5 boss admits he’d prefer NOT to have Big Brother|publisher=bbspy|date=25 August 2017}}</ref> After the [[Celebrity Big Brother 20 (UK)|twentieth celebrity series]], it was revealed that ''Big Brother'' ratings were the highest for the network.<ref>supertv ([https://twitter.com/superTV247 superTV247]). "[https://twitter.com/superTV247/status/907265091195863041 Channel 5 ratings for Sunday... 7pm - 0.23m (1.0%) 8pm - 0.21m (0.9%) 9pm - 0.49m (1.1%) "I'd quite like a Channel without Big Brother"]” 11 September 2017, 11:30 AM. Tweet.</ref>

On August 1, 2022, it was announced that ITV had purchased the rights to the show and would be broadcasting a new season on ITV2 in 2023. Initially slated for a March 2023 debut, ITV elected to push back the premiere to the fall, citing concerns with competing reality shows, and "wanting to give the Big Brother revival the best chance to succeed." ===Casting=== '' On October 10, 2022, ITV opened applications for the renewed season, with a main goal in mind: to bring 'authenticity' back inside the Big Brother house. ITV's Peter Tierney said his team relentlessly listened to audience and fans who have constantly expressed wanting "real, authentic reality." The casting process was initially slated to close on January 27, 2023, but was extended thrice until it ultimately closed on July 27, 2023. The 10-month casting process led by ITV and Initial resulted in a pool of 30,000 applications according to Executive Producer Katy Manley, and eventually sifted down to 500 applicants for the interviews. {{cite web||last=Sarrubba|first=Stefania|date=October 3, 2023|url=https://deadline.com/2023/10/big-brother-execs-talk-russell-brand-casting-welfare-1235560034/|title=‘Big Brother’ UK Is Back: Execs Talk Sifting Through 30,000 Casting Applications, Prioritizing Welfare & “Making Reality ‘Real’ Again”|publisher=Digital Spy|language=}} On October 3, 2023, just less than a week before the season's launch date, presenter AJ Odudu hinted that the housemates will reflect the UK in 2023 and that the show will always be a mirror to today's society. {{cite web|last=Goldbart|first=Max|date=October 3, 2023|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/reality-tv/a45422153/big-brother-aj-odudu-housemates-hint/|title=Big Brother host AJ Odudu drops first hint about housemates|publisher=Deadline|language=}} ITV also revealed that the show will be prioritizing the welfare of the cast through a welfare package that supports all housemates before, during and after their time in the Big Brother House. It aired on July 8, 2003, and ended on September 24, 2003, lasting 82 days. This season's [[Winners (US)|winner]] was [[Jun Song]], who beat her on-off ally [[Alison Irwin]] in the Final 2 by a 6-1 vote. The season is characterized by the complex social dynamics between the [[Housemates|houseguests]] and their [[X-Factor|ex-lovers]], the rise and fall of the majority alliance [[Elite Eight]], [[Scott Weintraub]]'s [[ejection]] as a result of his ex [[Amanda Craig]], being in the house, the power shifts and [[eviction]] blindsides throughout the season, the introduction of the [[Power of Veto|Golden Power of Veto]] and [[The Jury|jury]] sequester, the successful execution of the [[Social Strategies|floater strategy]] by both Jun and Alison and the subsequent decimation of all warring alliances. Major alliances of this season include the [[Elite Eight]] (Dana, Alison, Jack, Erika, David, Jun, Nathan & Scott), the [[Three Stooges]] (Justin, Jee, Robert) which extended to Jun to make the Dream Team, and the [[Girl Power]] group that Alison, Jun, and Erika formed near the end. ==Background== ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists/Changes== * '''[[Power of Veto|Golden Power of Veto]]:''' Introduced in the previous season as the last veto competition of ''[[Big Brother 3]]'', was the ''[[Power of Veto#Golden Power of Veto|Golden Power of Veto]]'', was now the mainstay veto for this, and future seasons. [[File:Big Brother 4 Ex's.jpg|thumb|right|The Exes]] * '''[[X-Factor|The X-Factor]]:''' While 8 Houseguests entered the house initially, they were told that 5 of the remaining Houseguests were ex-lovers with one of the 8. * '''Power of Veto Played Before Nominations:''' In Weeks 7 and 8 the veto competition happened before the nominations ceremony was held. * '''[[Power of Veto|Diamond Power of Veto]]:''' The Diamond Power of Veto was introduced as the final veto power in the final 4. It allowed the holder to save a nominee from eviction and name the replacement. * '''Sequestered Jury:''' A [[Jury]] of seven who would decide the outcome of the game. When there were nine players left in the game, the evictees formed the jury. The sequestered jury was introduced after many outcry among fans when {{bb3|Danielle}} lost [[Big Brother 3 (US)|Big Brother 3]] arguably due to evicted houseguests seeing her diary room sessions. ==Houseguests== {{Clear}} {{BBUS4 Progress}} ==Voting History== {{BB4VotingHistory}} ==Food History== {{BBUS4 Food History}} ==Competition History== {{BBUS4 Competition History}} ==Game History== {{BB4 Game History}} ===Week 1=== {| | {{WhichBoxSquare|Square-Nathan Marlow.jpg|Nathan Marlow|'''[[Nathan Marlow|Nathan]]'''|9966CC|HOH}} | {{WhichBoxSquare|Square

It began on July 10, 2002 and aired on [[CBS]] for 82 days, concluding on September 25. [[Lisa Donahue]] was crowned the winner with nine votes from the evicted houseguests, claiming the $500,000 prize. Season 3 of ''Big Brother'' was similar to ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]''. Each week, the [[Head of Household]] would nominate two players for eviction. On a live Eviction episode, the other houseguests would vote to evict one member. However, the [[Power of Veto#Silver Power of Veto|Silver Power of Veto]] was introduced in Season 3. All houseguests competed to win the power. The Veto could be used to save one of the nominees from eviction, forcing the Head of Household to nominate another houseguest. The Head of Household could not nominate the Veto winner. If a nominee won the Silver Power of Veto, they could not save themselves, but could choose to save the other nominee from eviction. The [[Power of Veto#Golden Power of Veto|Golden Power of Veto]] was introduced in Week 9. The Golden Veto was similar to the Silver Veto, except that if a nominee won the Veto, they could use it on themselves. {{bb3|Marcellas}} was nominated and won the POV, but famously did not use it on himself and was sent packing. {{bb3|Amy}} was evicted in Week 3, but in Week 6 the house voted her back into the game and she made it until Week 10. ==Background== ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists== *'''[[Power of Veto#Silver Power of Veto|Power of Veto]]''': Introduced for the first time in the franchise, the '''Silver Power of Veto''' allowed the winner save one nominee; the [[Head of Household]] then named a replacement nominee. This season had 14 [[houseguests]], so they were evicted at a quicker rate than before, sometimes multiple evictions in one week. In the fifth season, only six players would participate in the Power of Veto competition. The HOH and both nominees would choose a houseguest to also compete. This new format was utilized by {{bb5|Nakomis}} to [[backdoor]] {{bb5|Jase}}. ==Background== ===Development=== ===Casting=== ==Twists== * '''Only Six Power of Veto Players:''' Unlike previous seasons where all houseguests competed in the Veto Competition, only six players were allowed to compete: The Head of Household, the two nominees, and three players selected by each of them respectively. * '''[[Project DNA|Project DNA: Do Not Assume]]:''' There were two sets of relatives in the house who may or may not have known they were playing together. ** '''Twin Twist: Adria & Natalie:''' Although the houseguests were informed that some of their fellow contestants had identical twins, they were not told that [[Adria Klein]] had a twin. In fact, Adria and her identical twin, [[Natalie Carroll]], would switch places during the first four weeks. Since they survived the first four evictions playing as Adria, both twins entered the game and played as individuals in Week 5. ** '''Unknown Relatives: Nakomis & Michael:''' [[Nakomis Dedmon]] and [[Michael Ellis]] did not know they were biological siblings until they talked and figured out they were related. Their fellow houseguests were aware of this, but did not break up the potential duo. Interestingly, Michael cast the sole vote to evict Nakomis, but she later voted for him to win. * '''[[Double Eviction|Double Eviction Week]]:''' In Week 9, for the first time in ''Big Brother (US)'' history, two houseguests were evicted within one week. ''Big Brother 6'' also introduced a new feature: the [[Head of Household]] was allowed to blog while inside the house, a tradition that would continue in all subsequent seasons. A preview was shown on the ''The Early Show'' on July 5, 2007, the day of the premiere. The show aired three times a week; Sundays at 8pm, Tuesdays at 9pm, and Thursdays, which was broadcast live, at 8pm.https://web.archive.org/web/20130908075423/http://www.realitytvworld.com/realitytvdb/big-brother-8/ [[CBS]]'s cable/satellite premium network Showtime Two carried a spin-off of the series called ''[[Big Brother: After Dark]]'', which aired nightly from 12 midnight—3am. The show was live for the viewers on the east coast, however viewers on the West coast viewed it on a [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_delay broadcast delay]. This program featured all of the house activity happening between the local hours of 9pm-12 midnight in the House, and was edited only for slanderous statements and music copyrights. ===Casting=== === The House === The Big Brother house embraced a whimsical "Alice in Wonderland" theme, transforming the space into a surreal, storybook-inspired environment. Upon entering, houseguests passed through a mirrored doorway designed to evoke the iconic looking glass. The living room departed from tradition, featuring oversized wall lighting and a single nomination couch in place of the usual nomination chairs. The bedrooms continued the imaginative design, each crafted to distort the houseguests’ sense of scale. One bedroom was designed to make them feel small, with oversized beds, towering dressers, and a miniature doorway leading to a second room. In contrast, the adjoining bedroom created the illusion of being large, furnished with tiny beds and scaled-down décor. A giant magnifying glass connected the two spaces, reinforcing the whimsical theme. Elsewhere, the side bedroom adopted a Moroccan-inspired, Aladdin-style aesthetic, complete with two round beds. The kitchen maintained the exaggerated motif, featuring oversized cups integrated into the cabinetry. The gym was decorated with a vibrant mix of colors, while the hallway leading to the bathroom was intentionally skewed to alter perspective as houseguests entered. The statement said: ''"This is a summary of findings from Ofcom, the communications regulator, about the Channel 4 series "'''Celebrity Big Brother'''".'' In January 2007, Ofcom received over 44,500 complaints, mainly about potentially racist material. Ofcom has concluded that Channel 4 failed to handle appropriately the strong content it was transmitting. This resulted in breaches of the Ofcom Broadcasting Code, which is designed to ensure that when broadcasters show potentially offensive material, they do so in a way which offers adequate protection to the viewer. Ofcom has found that Channel 4 breached the Code on three separate occasions. Its decision to repeat one of these incidents in its early morning show resulted in a further breach for failing to protect children. There was also a serious failure in Channel 4's compliance processes which meant that it was not aware of all the relevant activity in the House at a particularly critical time. This compounded its failure to ensure compliance with the Code. These are significant failings. Ofcom has therefore imposed a formal sanction on Channel Four, directing it to broadcast this statement. To help with promotion, a large 300 ft hill figure of the eye logo was painted on the top of White Horse Hill, Oxfordshire, right above the famous Uffington White Horse, believed to be around 3,000 years old. Even though they got permission before painting, the eye was washed off days later. ==House== The Season 4 house design was completely different to the previous season's house, with the living room being one third smaller than the previous season's house, with red and green couches. This season saw the return of the chicken coop, alongside a vegetable patch that could be found in the garden. The garden also featured a decking area, where housemates could sit down. Season 4 also introduced the rewards room where the winner of the weekly live task would be thrown a party. This series was the first to be centered around an evil theme, which sparked new altercations like never before. It was the very first season to have more than one contestant ejected from the house. Eventually, after 71 days, bookie-favorite [[Nádia Almada]] was crowned the winner over [[Jason Cowan]] with a whopping 74.32% of the vote to be the first transgender contestant to win the game. ==Background== This was the year ''Big Brother'' turned evil. Due to poor ratings the previous year, evil Big Brother changed parts of the game. The grand prize was increased to £100,000. However, throughout the series, the housemates participated in tasks to save the prize from dropping in size. At the end of ten weeks, the final prize was £63,500, the lowest ever at the time, meaning the housemates lost an additional £36,500 in prize money. This series also included different eviction styles that would further be evolved in the future of the show. ==House== The house for this season was much smaller than the previous seasons to keep in line with the "Evil Big Brother" theme. The house featured an elevated floor, as well as a lowered ceiling. The kitchen was simplistic only featuring the absolute necessities, such as an oven, a fridge, and a sink. Only one bedroom was featured in the house with housemates having to walk through the garden to get to it. The room featured eight singular beds and two double beds. The showers led out into the garden and were made out of glass. Bedroom 5.jpg|Bedroom Garden 5.jpg|Garden Kitchen 5.jpg|Kitchen Living Room.jpg|Living Room == Twists == * '''Evil Big Brother:''' This season Big Brother was more strict in his enforcement of rules, and often punished the housemates by going against what he had previously told them. * '''Changing Prize Money:''' This season's prize money was raised from £70,000 to £100,000. However, in addition to shopping tasks, the house would have to complete tasks that would see money being either added to or removed from the prize. August 5, 2007 - December 7, 2014 }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a continental version of ''Big Brother'' for the continent of Africa. ==How It Works== ''Big Brother'' is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually fewer than 15 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ===African Series=== The African version of the show largely follows the same format as the original Dutch version of Big Brother where each week the housemates will nominate two of their fellow housemates for eviction and the public will then vote to evict the two (or more) housemates who received the most nominations. Although the house is located in South Africa, many different countries can send housemates into the house to compete. This series is different from many other series, due to the fact that many different countries can compete in the house, rather than one. At the start of the series, twelve different countries competed. Five other countries have been added since the debut of the show. ==History== ===Season 1=== The first season of Big Brother Africa, featuring 12 housemates from 12 different African countries, premiered to audiences in 42 African countries on Sunday 25 May 2003, and ended on 7 September of the same year, lasting 106 days. It was the first time in the world that the internationally famous program will be created using participants of different nationalities from one continent. Mark Pilgrim was the host. ===Season 2=== The second season of Big Brother Africa, featuring 12 housemates from 12 different African countries, premiered 5 August 2007, and ended on 11 November of the same year, lasting 98 days. The show returned from its four-year hiatus, with a brand new host, KB Ngakane. ===Season 3=== The third season of Big Brother Africa, featured 12 housemates from 12 different African countries, premiered 24 August 2008, and ended on 23 November of the same year, lasting 91 days. KB returned as host. ===Season 4: The Revolution=== The fourth season of Big Brother Africa, featured 25 housemates from 14 different African countries. The season premiered 6 September 2009, and ended on 6 December of the same year, lasting 91 days. This year, Ikponmwosa "IK" Osakioduwa took over as the new host.It was the first season featuring more than 12 contestants. It was also the first time 14 countries participated. ===Season 5: All-Stars=== Big Brother Africa 5 started on 18 July 2010, and ran for 91 days until 17 October 2010. This was an all-star series which featured 14 former Big Brother Africa contestants. For the second time, IK was the host. The winner was Uti Nwachukwu. ===Season 6

After the first HOH was crowned, the Backstage Boss was required to select three houseguests to receive "Backstage Passes". These three would be nominated to potentially leave during the first eviction and would not be able to participate in any competition either. Unknowingly to the rest of the house, America was given the option to save one of the three. On Eviction Night, one of remaining two Backstage houseguests would compete against the houseguest evicted by the house vote in a [[Hit The Road]] Competition where the loser would be that night's evictee. **Due to [[Paloma Aguilar|Paloma]] walking from the game, the twist was cancelled. The competition that would've been the Backstage Duel was incorporated into the first part of the Week 2 HOH competition instead. The same casting call was later tweeted out that nighthttps://twitter.com/CBSBigBrother/status/1573476301456822272 with the "#BB25" hashtag and a link to the CBS casting webpage,https://www.bigbrothercasting.tv/home which was also updated to say that applications for season 25 are open. The official renewal announcement was made on finale night of BB24.https://twitter.com/JCMoonves/status/1574218978502873088 ===Development=== Due to the [[wikipedia:2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 Writers Guild of America strike]] impacting their fall schedule, CBS announced on May 22nd, 2023 that ''Big Brother 25'' and [[w:c:thechallenge:The Challenge: USA 2|''The Challenge: USA 2'']] would be getting delayed debuts in August instead of July as they did the year prior. BB25 specifically was set to air on Wednesday, August 2nd with a special 90-minute live premiere at 8 PM EST, continuing with its usual Wednesday-Thursday-Sunday schedule. However, airing on Wednesdays in the fall would clash with the already announced [[w:c:survivor:Survivor 45|''Survivor 45'']] and [[w:c:amazingrace:The Amazing Race 35|''The Amazing Race 35'']], which were confirmed to be getting 90-minute episodes for their entire seasons just weeks ahead of the BB25 announcement.https://ew.com/tv/big-brother-delayed-start-summer-2023-all-new-cast/ When CBS officially announced their fall schedule on July 17, 2023, it was revealed that the schedule clashing would be resolved by moving the second half of BB25 from Wednesdays to Tuesdays, but remaining in its 8 PM EST timeslot. In addition, the Thursday episodes would be pushed up from 9 PM EST to 8 PM EST, while the Sunday episodes would be pushed back from 8 PM EST to 10 PM EST.https://twitter.com/CBS/status/1681018180687515648 The last time a writers strike impacted CBS scheduling was in [[wikipedia:2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike|2007-2008]], which led to ''[[Big Brother 9 (US)]]'' airing that winter, with ''[[Big Brother 10 (US)]]'' taking the usual summer slot in its place. Those who chose the Blue Team became housemates, while those that chose the Red Team became non-housemates. During the first two days of the game, the non-housemates competed in three separate challenges, attempting to steal the housemate status from their peers. If the non-housemates successfully won the challenge, they would earn the power to send two non-housemates out of storage. Finally, the non-housemates still in storage after the three challenges competed in a final competition for safety. The remaining non-housemates were nominated for eviction. *'''[[Head of House]]''': For the first time since ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 6 (UK)]]'', starting in Week 2, the housemates competed in the [[Head of House]] competition. One housemate was selected to be the Head of House, where they would have immunity from eviction, be able to influence nominations, and sleep in a special bed. **During Weeks 2, 3, 4 (2nd round), and 5, the HOH(s) had the choice to influence nominations by either saving and replacing a nominee or by giving one housemate of their choosing a Killer Nomination. **'''Double Trouble Week''': During Week 3, everything was done in pairs. The traditional Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday episode schedule returned, with all episodes airing at 8 PM throughout the season. In a first, all Wednesday episodes will be 90-minutes for the duration of the season, while the Sunday and Thursday episodes would return to an hour long following the premiere week. It was also announced that a special companion show, ''[[Big Brother: Unlocked]]'', would air every other Friday at 8 PM starting on July 25. At the end of the week, the group that would be able to guess better will be saved from nominations. Each group would be given four lives, and lives would be deducted by Big Brother, if Housemates directly asked a Housemate if they had a particular secret that was on the list. At the challenge, if the group guessed incorrectly, they would lose a life. If the group ran out of lives, they would lose the challenge. *'''Naughty Corner:''' Brought back again since [[Big Brother Australia 6]], the Naughty Corner was found in the Lounge Room was a room where a housemate who had done a violation will stay for a specific time. *'''Nominations Super Power:''' It is a special secret power given to a chosen housemate by a previous week's evictee. The Nominations Super Power gives an advantage to one housemate for nominations in a given week. The most recent evictee decides on which housemate they would like to have the power, without knowing what that power is. *'''[[Intruders]]:''' Brought back from the [[Network 10|Network Ten]] series was the Intruders twist where aspiring housemates will try to get their place in the house as an official housemate. *'''Surly the Fish:''' A talking fish was put inside the house where it gives various commands to the housemates, some were mischievous while some reveals new twists, including the golden toilet hidden behind a shelf in the bedroom. *'''House Pet:''' This season had a house pet, a dog named Delilah. ==The House== Big Brother returned to the original filming location at Dreamworld on Queensland’s Gold Coast, with the house and studio given extensive renovations and repairs after being dormant for four years. The theme for the season's house was Australian architectural history, featuring three eras, the 1950s, the 1970s and the modern era. *The '''Kitchen''' was now separated from the main house, which was designed to resemble a 1950s Australian home on the exterior while a typical 1950s Kitchen inside.. *The '''Rewards Room''' was brought back now called as the ''Captain's Quarter's'' having a Nautical theme to it. However unlike the previous series, they could only have a 24-hour access to the Rewards Room. *The '''Garden''' also featured a large triangular swimming pool at the center, with a small sitting area adjacent to it. There was also a barbecue grill in the patio.

==Twists==
*'''No Prize Money:''' On launch night, it was revealed that there was no prize money, but instead housemates earned prize money through their weekly tasks.
*'''White Room:''' After 4 of the 6 possible housemates were not voted into the house, they moved into the "White Room". Throughout their stay, they had to stay in a small white room, wear only white clothes, and eat porridge. The last one to leave the room would win a spot in the Main House.
*'''Save and Replace:''' In replaces of the Three Point Twist, the winner of the [[Friday Night Live]] Games was given the option to save one nominee for the nominations lineup and replace them with another.
*'''Big Brother Starburst Golden Key:''' Four months before the season started, Starburst partnered with Channel Ten to hold a contest for a member of the public to enter the house as a wildcard. One hundred "golden keys" were available inside of packages of Starbursts, a similar reference to ''[[wikipedia:Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory|Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory]]''. On Day 18, [[Nick Sady]] entered the house as the winner.
