November 9, 2025 - }}'''Big Brother Australia''' is the Australian version of ''Big Brother''. ''Big Brother Australia'' first aired in 2001 and ran for eight civilian seasons and one celebrity edition on [[Network 10|Network Ten]]. In July 2008 the show was cancelled following audience erosion and controversy. On 13 August 2012, ''Big Brother Australia'' returned for its ninth season, airing on the [[Nine Network]] with the tenth season airing from 29 July 2013 to 6 November 2013 and the eleventh season airing from 8 September 2014 to 26 November 2014. Nine did not renew the show for a twelfth season. In 2019, [[Seven Network]] acquired the rights and confirmed that the show’s second revival would launch in June 2020. Following four civilian seasons and one celebrity edition Seven did not proceed with a 2024 season. On 16 September 2024, Network 10 announced that [[Big Brother Australia (franchise)|Big Brother]] ''is returning home, where it belongs'', for a [[Big Brother Australia 16|sixteen season]] and with the original eviction format. Following the announcement the [[Seven Network]] issued a legal letter towards Endemol Shine Australia, citing a breach in their “Hold Back” agreement, an agreement that prevents negotiations with another network for the series rights.https://tvtonight.com.au/2024/09/seven-issues-endemol-shine-legal-letter-over-big-brother-hold-back.html ==How it works== [[File:BBAU_Original_Logo.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Original Logo of Big Brother Australia]] Big Brother produced by Endemol in the Netherlands which began in 1999, is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually fewer than 15 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ===Australian Series=== ====Original Format==== The series generally constitutes 14 or more contestants who live in an isolated house for several months. Housemates are at all times under the control of Big Brother, a rule enforcing authority figure who monitors the behaviour of the housemates, set tasks and punishments and provides the mechanism for contestants to make external requests. Housemates must remain in the house at all times, and avoid being evicted by viewers of the show with the aim of winning a substantial cash prize at the end of the series. Alternatively, housemates can also be removed from the house if Big Brother feels this is necessary, and can voluntarily leave the show at any time. In order to support the housemates' well-being on matters such as wanting to leave the house, all participants have access to the Big Brother psychologist Carmel Hill, and a doctor, at all times. Housemates are filmed 24 hours per day with edited highlights broadcast during prime time slots every evening. The series returned to this format starting with [[Big Brother Australia 16]]. ====2020 Format==== ===Casting=== The show's producers aim to get "real people" in the house. This has been done by personality testing, engaging with people around the country and appearances. While there are housemates who are "unique" and reflect many diverse people in Australia, there has been a high number of individuals each season who come from a modeling background which has alienated them from the public audience. ==The Big Bro

==Controversies==
===Klodian's Coming Out===
This season of Big Brother had a lot of controversies starting from Klodian's coming out as gay. In one of the Saturday's shows there was shown a clip for both the housemates and the public of Klodian in the diary room telling that he was gay. Arbana called Klodian in the diary room to talk more about his sexual orientation. When he came out of the diary room all the housemates hugged him and told him that they would support him. But this thing didn't happen for some of the housemates, especially with Valon who claimed to be a homophobic and said that all the Albanians are as well. Two weeks after Klodian came out, in his hometown, Lezhë there were people protesting to Big Brother cast to draw Klodian out of the house. Klodian survived a lot of risks to be evicted and some people think that the voting may have been rigged to keep Klodian in the house until the situation in his hometown calm down. Also the American Ambassador and the European one showed their support to Klodian's family. The reactions from the magazines and the press were in the support of Klodian.
===Arbana Osmani's Comments===
Right after the start of the fifth season of Big Brother Albania on Top Channel, the hostess of the show, Arbana Osmani made some really harsh comments about the cast of the housemates of the third season. Asked during an interview about which cast of housemates of which season she disliked the most, Osmani answered that she totally disliked and hated the cast of the third season because she thought that each and every one of the housemates of the third season were totally false and had no personality whatsoever. Osmani went on to say that Klodian Çela, according to her, was one of the worst people she had ever met and said that Çela used his homosexuality to make people feel bad about him. However, these comments weren't left unanswered by the other side. Shortly after the interview was published, Tatiana Sandei, one of the housemates of this season, stormed back at Osmani's comments defending herself, the cast of the third season and Klodian Çela, meanwhile Çela himself claimed to have been used by the production for his homosexuality and offended the hostess by making explicit comments. Klodian also claimed that the production of Big Brother offered to pay him just because he outed himself during the show although the payment was never made.

==Controversies==
===Altina's Secret===
Altina's secret leaked on social networks because of a photo someone had found in her Facebook account. After this thing it is supposed that the production took care to shut down all of the housemates' personal profiles and accounts. However, there were still fan pages administrated by the housemates' relatives that posted photos.
===Anaidi and Joana's Relationship===
After two weeks the show had started there were rumors that two of the housemates: Anaidi and Joana were in a relationship out the house and that they knew each other. However, in an exclusive interview for Bluetooth Magazine, Rezart Aga, the producer of the show said that the housemates were picked carefully and there are no acquaintances between them.
===Arian Konomi and Xhimi's Joke===
In the Week 8 Live Show of Saturday, Arian Konomi the panelist of the show offended Xhimi by saying that he was a person without personality and then a fight erupted between these two. Arian was criticized by many journalists and people for his harsh comments towards the housemates. In the Week 9 Live Show he publicly apologized to Xhimi, the housemates and the viewers. At the same night Xhimi was evicted from the house and on an interview he said that he regrets making a joke in the house saying he had put condoms in the meal. However, this statement was a proof to the question if there are or not condoms in the house.
===Rike's Entry===
Since Rike entered the house in Week 8 she already knew all of the housemates' secrets. Even though, Arbana Osmani said that Rike won't tell any of the secrets to the other housemates she broke the rules on Day 60 by telling the secret of Anaidi to both Joana and Elona. Two days after this thing happened the production took on the official Facebook page of Big Brother Albania to tell that Rike doesn't know any of the secrets and so she couldn't tell any of the housemates any secret. The fans claimed that Osmani herself told that Rike already knew the secrets making this story a lot more controversial.
===Xhimi's Photo===
The day he was evicted, Xhimi posted a photo on Facebook with a caption blaming the panelist of the show, Arjan Konomi, for being the one who decided to evict him and said that the public's votes were rigged.

===Racist Comments===
A lot of racial comments were made during this season because for the first time in the history of Big Brother in Albania a Romani woman, Esterina, entered the house. Erald was one of the housemates that started making comments about how Esterina's clothes stank and also made comments about her skin color. Later on the game Meridian started telling Esterina that she shouldn't have entered the Big Brother house because she wasn't a very smart person, a comment that caused a fight between the two housemates. Osmani, the host of the show, addressed these bigoted remarks on a television interview and also during the live show of March 7, 2014. She also talked to the housemates about them. The panelist of the show, Armand Peza also criticized Meridian and Erald for their racial slur and their racist jokes towards Esterina and other housemates. The comments were brought up again later on the show during the night Esterina was evicted as she expressed her feelings on the derogatory comments made towards her. She added that the racist remarks were the only reason she wanted to enter the Big Brother house and also said that she wanted to prove everyone wrong about Romani people. During Week 5, Rigels called Ardit's face "very black".
===Violence in the house===
Another controversy this season was the use of physical assault and violence from the housemates. Jona expressed her feelings since Week 1 about Rigels and said she didn't want to have been paired with him to play the game. As a pair, Jona and Rigels had a lot of fights but their relationship reached a boiling point during Week 4, when Jona, furious that Rigles had eaten all her french fries, threatened to stab him with a knife, while holding the object in her hand and making several attempts to do so. While this was happening, none of the other housemates, who were watching the whole scene, attempted to stop Jona or grab the knife from her hand. Jona was then called to the Diary Room by the production team and she apologized publicly about her actions and said she had been in the heat of the moment and didn't have the nerves to put up with Rigels's games as she had not eaten for days. During the live show of March 14, 2014, Armand Peza, the panelist criticized Jona's actions and said she had still to make an apology to Rigels, but Rigels said that they had already settled into an agreement that would be the best for both. Other housemates such as Mikela, Violeta and Ardit were surprised that Jona wasn't ejected. Violeta then pointed out that Rigels was "the luckiest person" because Jona was seriously aiming to stab him.

[[File:Tunisia Flag.png|25px]] Tunisia | language = Arabic | executiveproducers = | director = | network = [[wikipedia:MBC 2 (Middle Eastern and North African TV channel)|MBC2]] | host = Razan Moughrabi | seriesrun = February 21, 2004 - March 2, 2004 }} '''Big Brother: The Boss ''(Big Brother: الرئيس)''''' ''(also known as '''Big Brother Arabia''')'' was a 2004 Arabic-language television show, based on the worldwide hit ''[[Big Brother (franchise)|Big Brother]]'', in which contestants live in a specially built house while competing for a prize. The show was aired on MBC 2 with a big prize $100 000, not won because of the cancellation. The show was filmed in the Amwaj Islands in Bahrain. It was hoped that the show would follow the success of such popular programs as [[wikipedia:Star Academy|Star Academy]], and the recent dating show "Al Hawa Sawa," but failed to do so, and instead the show gained major controversy in the countries it aired in. Many were offended by the fact that it featured six men and six women living together in one area due to gender segregation in Islam, despite staying in separate parts of the house, and the only way of communicating with each other was in open areas such as the kitchen and garden. The show began on airing 21 February, and was discontinued 11 Days later on 2 March to avoid more controversy in the Arab World, specifically, the Arabian Peninsula. During the first (and only) nominations Asjan, Bashara, Najwa and Shaza were nominated. However, an eviction never took place. ==The Big Brother House== The house was mainly segregated for the male and female housemates. Single-sex bedrooms, bathrooms and prayer rooms were provided and the only parts of the house accessible to both sexes were the kitchen and garden areas. Parts of the house (e.g. the women's bedroom) were monitored by female camera operators only. Five times a day, Big Brother would announce to the housemates the time for prayer. ==Series== {{Arabia Editions}} ==Cancellation== Producers decided to cancel the show, as there were many complaints from viewers, and complaints on Arab radio talkshows. The shows producers actually went into the house in person to inform the housemates that it was to be cancelled. Many of the Housemates were devastated at the news that they had to leave. Had the eviction gone ahead, Shaza would have been evicted with 65% of the vote. Bashara received 20%, Asjan received 10%, whilst Najwa received 5%. ==Trivia== *Big Brother Arabia is the first series in the history of Big Brother, to be cancelled and not have a winner. **It would be followed by the Big Brother series in the Balkans, when three housemates died in a car accident. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

}}'''''{{PAGENAME}}''''' is the fifteenth season of the [[Big Brother Australia (franchise)|Australian version]] of ''Big Brother''.

This season received an overwhelming amount of criticism from viewers and longtime fans due to its format, with many accusing the show of "selling out" and unfavorably comparing the show to ''Love Island'' and ''Married at First Sight''. Further criticism was aimed at its choice of casting, with many viewers and fans labelling the housemates as "Influencer Wannabes" and not real everyday people like earlier seasons. As a result of the negative criticism which lead to declining ratings, a planned fifth season on the Seven Network was ultimately cancelled despite audition applications initially being opened. It is widely regarded as the worst season of ''Big Brother Australia''.
==Background==
[[File:Australia15 HOL Logo.jpg|175px|thumb|right|Season logo for prospective "House of Love" theme]]

The controversy came to light after a video was posted on the internet showing them both in a bed. Under the covers, Daniel grabs the colleague who, apparently, did not react to his affections for being unconscious. A police investigation went to the house and opened a record of occurrence to hear those involved. [48] Daniel left the program on January 16 under the justification of "serious misconduct" by Rede Globo. [49] In addition to the movement it caused on the internet, the fact was publicized by the main print and television media in the country and also reached international repercussions, highlighting in publications such as the British newspapers Daily Mail and The Guardian and the Australian newspaper Sydney Morning Herald, which highlighted the critics against the station that the episode generated. ==Trivia== {{Brazil Seasons}} {{Season Nav}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:Brazil Seasons]]

A improvised house was assembled for the mothers and aunts. They stayed in the house until March 13.[13] On day 55, relatives had to vote for the housemate they want to win an immunity for week 8's nominations. Sol (Vanessa's mother) and Susi (Cássio's mother) voted for Clara. Ivone (Angela's mom) and Bel (Tatiele's mother) voted for Marcelo. Adriana (Clara's aunt) chose Vanessa. Márcia (Diego's mom) chose Cássio. Ledi (Aline's mom) voted for Diego. Leda (Marcelo's mom) and Zezinha (Valter's aunt) chose Angela. So, Clara, Marcelo and Angela tied with 2 votes each and Zezinha had the casting vote. She chose Angela to be immune. On day 57, due to Aline's eviction, her mother Ledi, who was the relative most popular among viewers, had to leave the house too. From the fifth week of the season, the public's vote became regional based. The candidate who achieves a simple majority of votes in each region of Brazil (Midwest, Northeast, North, Southeast and South) by internet gets a point. Also earn one point the candidate who obtains a simple majority of all votes by calls and SMS. Thus, there are six points in total: five per geographic region and another by SMS and telephone. In case of a tied score, the contestant with the most votes is evicted. The votes from outside is distributed equally among the five regions of Brazil. *'''Fake Eviction: '''Due to Alan's withdrawal, to maintain the program's scheduled schedule, there was no elimination in the third week of confinement. [[wikipedia:pt:Tadeu Schmidt|Tadeu Schmidt]] (2022-) | seriesrun = January 29, 2002 - }}'''Big Brother Brasil''' is the Brazilian version of the popular reality franchise ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== ===Overview=== Big Brother is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually 12-22 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ===Brazilian series=== The Brazilian version of Big Brother follows elements from both the original Big Brother version and the North American version. The series combines public interaction gameplay seen on many international versions while adding most of [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|American]] version's gameplay alongside it. Among the elements that the series shares with its American counterpart include the Líder (Head of Household), Paredão (Nomination Block) and Anjo (Power of Veto). ====Prova do Líder==== Prova do Líder (eng. Leader Competition) is the Brazilian version of the [[Head of Household]]. Every week, the housemates compete in the Prova do Lider wherein the winner of the challenge would be named as the Líder and would gain a power to select one housemate to become a nominee. Just like the HoH, the Lider will be given various perks throughout the week. These perks include special access to the Lider's own private suite and receiving photos or gifts from home, as well as, starting with [[Big Brother Brazil 20]], being allowed to choose which housemates they want to bring along to the VIP (Have). They may also get the chance to veto one or more housemates from participating in the next Prova do Líder. Also starting in BBB20, the Líder is rewarded with a party themed after them in the end of their tenure, named Festa do Líder (Leader's Party). ====Prova do Anjo==== Since [[Big Brother Brazil 3]], a weekly immunity challenge called ''Prova do Anjo'' takes place in the house, wherein the winner, called "Anjo" (Angel) gains a power to bestow immunity to a fellow housemate and save them from nominations. The immunity bestowal happens right before the nominations. While the Anjo usually has to chose someone else to save besides themselves most of the time, it's common for some weeks to have an auto-immunity benefit, which is only revealed to them during the bestowal ceremony, either before or after they announce the housemate they intended to immunize. [[Big Brother Brazil 7]] had a lottery after the bestowal ceremony that allowed one randomly chosen contestant to either veto or keep the immunity given by the Anjo, but this was discontinued in the season after, and exclusive to [[Big Brother Brazil 24]], the Anjo was auto-immune and also had the power to immunize someone else, but this perk was also abandoned in the following season. Along with the immunity perk, the Anjo is also gifted with the Almoço do Anjo (Angel's Lunch) perk, which allows them to invite two other housemates for a special meal in a private room inside the house, where the Anjo also receives video messages from home. ====Monstro==== Starting with [[Big Brother Brazil 8]], the Anjo of the week must also choose either one or two housemates to be the week's Monstro (Monster). This is the first time since ''[[Celebrity Big Brother Australia 1]]'' in 2002 that Australia has had a celebrity season of the show and the first time under the Channel 7 version. ==Background== ===Development=== [[File:Big Brother VIP Australia 2021 - First Look|thumb|250px|"First Look" promo of ''Big Brother Australia VIP 2021''.]] During Big Brother Australia's [[Network 10|Channel 10]] era, Big Brother Australia has produced its first celebrity edition back in 2002, with Australian viewers electing TV and Radio host [[Dylan Lewis]] as the winner. Despite a successful celebrity edition, no succeeding seasons were made until Channel 10 axed the Big Brother Australia franchise in 2008. When [[Nine Network]] revived the franchise from 2012 to 2014, various rumors have circulated regarding a new celebrity edition, although it never materialized until Nine decided to drop the franchise in 2018 and was picked up by the rival network, [[Wikipedia:Seven Network|Channel 7]] the following year. After the success of the [[Big Brother Australia 12|first Channel 7 season]], Channel 7 announced on March 30, 2021, shortly before the premiere of [[Big Brother Australia 13]] that a celebrity season of the show would air in late 2021. After 19 years, Channel 7 decided to produce a new celebrity edition under a rebranded name, ''Big Brother VIP''. Unlike Channel 10's ''Celebrity Big Brother'', ''Big Brother VIP'' followed the new game format used by Channel 7 seasons, and was also pre-recorded. {{cite web|url=https://7news.com.au/entertainment/big-brother-australia/big-brother-vip-set-to-launch-in-2021-featuring-some-of-australias-biggest-celebrities-c-2473966|title=Big Brother VIP set to launch in 2021 featuring some of Australia’s biggest celebrities|first=|last=|date=30 March 2021|publisher=7 News|language=English}} ===Casting=== For this edition's cast, Channel 7 has chosen a mix of Australian and foreign celebrities, featuring actors, reality TV personalities, athletes, politicians, and influencers in its lineup. April 2027 - }} '''Big Brother Canada''' is the Canadian version of the international phenomenon ''[[Big Brother]]''. It is based on the [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|American version]] of the franchise. ==Show History== [[File:BBCAN_Days_&_Episodes_Chart.png|thumb|right|250px|The amount of days and episodes per season.]] ''Big Brother U.S.'' has always been available to the Canadian audience since it premiered in 2000. Later in 2003, Quebec, the French province of Canada, decided to produce [[Loft Story Quebec (franchise)|their own version]] of ''Big Brother'' based on the French version called ''Loft Story''. After airing Loft Story through 2009, Quebec rebranded the series as ''Big Brother Quebec'' and later as ''Celebrity Big Brother Quebec''. Then in May of 2012, Shaw Media announced that ''Big Brother'' would come to Canada in 2013, and would be broadcast on [[Slice]]. Later Shaw announced that Live Feeds would be free on the ''Big Brother Canada'' website. It then premiered in February 2013. Due to being based on the American version of the series, the base format was identical, featuring a [[Head of Household]] who makes the [[Nominations|nominations]], a [[Power of Veto]] to potentially change those nominations, houseguests voting to [[Eviction|evict]], and a [[The Jury|jury]] deciding the [[Winners (Canada)|winner]] on finale night. After two successful seasons, Shaw Media decided that the show earned its spot on [[Global]]. A few weeks after the [[Big Brother Canada 5|fifth season]] finished airing, during June 2017, the show was announced to be on hiatus. Then, on July 20, 2017; Global announced that (due to overwhelming support from the fans) ''Big Brother Canada'' would be returning in 2018 for a [[Big Brother Canada 6|sixth season]]. In June 2024, soon after the conclusion of the [[Big Brother Canada 12|twelfth season]], after rumors that the show would not return in 2025, following its notable omission from Global's TV schedules during the 2024-25 upfronts, Corus Entertainment confirmed the cancellation of the show, due to a combination of factors including declining audience trends, a need for more sponsor support, and rising production and licensing costs. In June 2026, it was announced that [[wikipedia:Bell Media|Bell Media]] acquired the rights to produce new seasons of ''Big Brother Canada'' that would air on [[wikipedia:CTV Television Network|CTV]] and [[wikipedia:Crave (streaming service)|Crave]] starting in 2027. It was also announced that [[Andrea Bain]], from CTV's daytime talk show ''The Social'', would be taking over as host. New seasons would be filmed in Montreal, using the same house as the French-Canadian version in order to reduce production costs.{{cite web|url=https://www.bellmedia.ca/the-lede/press/bell-media-becomes-head-of-household-with-order-of-big-brother-canada-for-crave-and-ctv-and-acquisition-of-future-seasons-of-big-brother-usa-beginning-in-2027/|title=Bell Media Becomes Head of Household with Order of BIG BROTHER CANADA for Crave and CTV and Acquisition of Future Seasons of BIG BROTHER USA, Beginning in 2027|publisher=Bell Media|date=4 June 2026|accessdate=4 June 2026}} As of ''[[Big Brother Canada 12]]'', a total of 176 people have participated across 12 seasons. For ''[[Big Brother Canada 5]]'', 8 players from the first four seasons [[Returning Players|returned to played the game again]] against 8 new players, while ''[[Big Brother Canada 12]]'' featured two returning players against 12 new ones. This bubble, in fact, was a glass house that was in the mall Via Parque, in Rio de Janeiro, where four of the eighteen chosen were a week confined separately from the rest. At first, the most voted of the four members of the glass house would take the place of the first eliminated of BBB 9. However, on the day of the result of the most voted, in the program of January 21, 2009, a vote was held (Big Boss) where the public could choose the possibility of another participant of the glass house, the second most voted, joining the game. The option was well received by the public through the vote and, with 94% of the votes, it was decided that the 2 most voted, Emanuel and Josiane respectively, could join the house. * Another novelty was the wall that separated the house in two sides (A and B). A draw, held in the premiere program, defined which side would be each of the participants in the house. On Side A, half of the participants lived inside the house itself. On Side B, a room and a free area were available for the other participants. In the program of January 18, 2009, in which the first wall was built, this wall was removed. During the 5th week, a new "bubble" was created, this time in the outside (garden) of the BBB house, separating a glass two participants from the rest of the group. The two (André and Maíra Cardi) waited without knowing what would happen during the days that would be there, as well as the participants. The Big Boss of the Week was a vote for the public to decide whether or not the two would enter the house. The voting lasted five days, ending on a Sunday, February 15, 2009, where the entry of the two participants was approved by a vote of 59%. This season also saw an exchange between "Big Brother Brazil" and "Big Brother Africa". Current winner, the Angolan [[Ricco Venancio|Ricardo "Ricco" Venâncio]], 21, entered the house on February 28. He spent four days in the house and arrived at a Saturday party, which featured DJs and typical food from Angola. On the morning of March 3, Ricco left the house. * '''Walked from Leonardo '''- the guest Leonardo was sent to a white room together with Newton and Ralf, but Leonardo could not stand the pressure and asked to leave. * '''New Houseguests '''- André and Maira Cardi entered the house by popular vote. ==Housemates== {{BBB9 Progress}} ===Potential Housemates=== ====Glass House 1 Housemates==== {{BBB9 Potential Housemates}} ====Glass House 2 Housemates==== {{BBB9 Potential Housemates 2}} ==Nominations History== {{BBB9 Nominations History}} ==Have/Have-Not History== {{BBB9 Have/Have-Not History}} *During Weeks 1 & 2, Emanuel and Josiane were not in the house and were therefore not assigned a have/have-not status. *During Weeks 1, 2, 3 & 4, André and Maíra were not in the house and were therefore not assigned a have/have-not status. ==Game History== {{BBB9 Game History}} ==Trivia== {{Brazil Seasons}} {{Season Nav}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:Brazil Seasons]]

However the petition never did reach the goal of 15,000 signs, it received 12,500 in which started the ball rolling. The show is licensed by a foreign show of the same name, produced by [[Endemol]]. Croatian Big Brother holds the record for most male victories in a row since its inception. ==History== The license for the program was bought by RTL Television in mid-2004, and it started with its first season of the show that autumn. So far, 167 contestants, the so-called "stanari (eng. housemates)" of the Big Brother house, have participated in the show. When entering the house, housemates must comply with the house rules; house occupants can leave the house at any time without permission or be forcibly removed from the game if they have broken any rules, such as violent behavior. ==Production== ===House=== Big Brother house is located in Jadran film studio in Dubrava, part of the city of Zagreb. In the fifth season, the house was located in the movie city of Kantan, about forty kilometers west of Bangkok, the capital of Thailand. In 2011 and 2015, the show was filmed at home in Belgrade's Kosutnjak (regional Big Brother). After two regional seasons, Big Brother returned to Croatia in 2016. ==Series== {{Croatia Editions}} ==Presenters==

October 8, 2024 - }}'''Big Brother Bulgaria''' is the Bulgarian version of ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== Big Brother is a reality show based on the Big Brother series by Endemol. The show originates from the Netherlands, where in 1999 the very first season was aired. At present, the format is spread in a number of countries around the world. A group of people (called the Housemates) live together in an isolated house. 24 hours a day their life is recorded by hidden cameras in all the rooms in the House. They don't have TV, Internet, newspapers, even watches on their hands. The Housemates are completely isolated from the outside world. Every week, each one of them must enter the Diary room and nominate 2 of the other people for public eviction. The 2 or more housemates with most negative votes become nominated. For almost a week the TV viewers have to decide which of them to be evicted, voting via SMS or phone calls in past seasons, votes are now being cast through the "Nova Play" App. Every week the Housemates have a week task. Depending on whether they do their task successfully or unsuccessfully, their week budget is increased or decreased. During the final week, the viewers vote which one of the remaining people in the House to be the winner. He or she wins a big cash prize. ==Series== {{Bulgaria Editions}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

Sophie Rosentreter |prizemoney = 250,000 DM |nomberofhousemates = 13 |numberofdays = 102 |winner = [[John Milz]] |runnersup = [[Jürgen Milski]] |returnees = [[Zlatko Trpkovski]] ''([[Promi Big Brother 7|PBB7]])''

The show started with huge protests, where media institutions called for a prohibition because the show might violate the human dignity.https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=493099958246923 However, after a few weeks on air it became a runaway hit where housemates, most notably [[Zlatko Trpkovski]], became media sensations and quickly becoming celebrities. It was the first Reality Show in the country and started a revolution of the landscape of German Television which is why a [[Big Brother Germany 2|second]] and a [[Big Brother Germany 3|third season]] where started in less than a year. ==Background== === Development === Boris Brandt bought the format from John de Mol before its premiere in the [[Big Brother Netherlands (franchise)|Netherlands]]. Originally it was scheduled to air on ProSieben named ''Galileo – Das Experiment''.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zfklBpVVMjU After the initial success in the Netherlands, a German adaptation was quickly planned with RTL2 president Josef Andorfer buying the format while Rainer Laux was the delegated producer. Laux would eventually be in charge for every future German season of the format until 2010 and again from 2014 on.https://www.focus.de/kultur/kino_tv/interview-big-brother_id_4890498.html A first look at the house was revealed during a press conference on January 19, 2000.https://www.imago-images.de/st/0056898090?searchID=a15afe7e-4992-44ad-83aa-0563ff48045b === Hosts === The main host of the first season was Percy Hoven while Sophie Rosentreter was the co-host. === Airing & Shedule === The housemates moved in on the February 28, 2000. The launch was shown on March 1 with the first regular daily episode showing on March, which featured the events of the first two days. Daily recaps of one hour were shown from Monday to Friday and on Sunday at 8.15 pm. A weekly recap showed Saturdays and a two hour live was aired every Sunday which saw altered to cover the nominations or eliminations. === Theme Song === The theme song was called "Leb!" and was a cover from the same title [[Big Brother 1 (Netherlands)|song of the Dutch version]]. Performed by boyband ''Die 3. Generation'' the song benefitted from the hype the show created and topped the German single charts for 3 weeks. The B-Side was the song "Big Brother is ok!" which was recorded by the 8 housemates that were in the house during week 5. == House == [[File:DE1 House plan.jpg|thumb|House plan]] The house was located on the NOB studious in Cologne-Hürth and was a 1:1 replicant of the house that was constructed for the original show in the Netherlands. The so called "container" had a living area of 143 m2 and an additional outside garden. 24 cameras and 59 microphones recorded the life of the housemates. When entering the house, the housemates agreed to divide the bed rooms by gender, although that was not obligatory. A Chicken coop in the garden proved to be popular among one group of housemates to chat about the other half of the household. A weight bench in the backyard was provided for the housemates to remain in shape. The theme of the season was ''Back to Basic'' which is why housemates needed to chop wood if they wanted to use a small wood stove in the living room.

[[wikipedia:Vappu Pimiä|Vappu Pimiä]] was the host of the ''Big Brother Talk Show'' and [[wikipedia:Jani Toivola|Jani Toivola]] hosted ''Big Brother Extra''. This was the last series where Pimiä served as a hostess; the fifth season was the only series in which Toivola appeared.

==Twists==
*'''[[Rich and Poor House]]''': The twist of the season revolves around the division of the house where in the main house is called ''Paradise'' while another poorer area is called the ''Slums''. Housemates in Paradise get to live in the main house, have hot water 24/7 for bathing, plentiful of food and the power to nominate. Housemates in Slums get to live in a makeshift area, sleeping on the floor with their jackets as blankets, a garden hose to wash themselves in a roofless toilet, limited food (rice, sardines, porridge and pea soup).
*'''[[Head of House]]''': The concept of having a Head of House was first introduced in this season. Each week the housemate will compete in Head of House competitions where the winner will gain immunity as well as having the power to designate which housemates would stay on which side of the house.
*'''[[Housemate Exchange]]''': A chosen housemate would swap houses with another housemate from a foreign Big Brother Franchise for a week. [[Kätlin Laas]] lived in [[Pinoy Big Brother: Double Up]] house and swapped places with [[Cathy Remperas]] who also lived in Big Brother Finland house for a week.

After a short hiatus, the German broadcaster Sat.1 revived the show as '''Promi Big Brother''' 2013 which is a celebrity edition of the show still currently airing. In 2015 a civilian series of '''Big Brother Germany '''was aired, however, it did not return to air the following year. It later aired in February 2020 on Sat.1 and ended in May 2020. ==How it Works==

''Big Brother'' is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but are continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually fewer than 15 participants. The last housemate in the house at the end of the series typically wins a cash prize.

===Civilian Series=== The civilian series follows people from all walks of life under the watchful eye of Big Brother. Housemates live in the house for approximately three months with the hopes of being the last person standing and winning a monetary prize usually around 100,000 Euro. Starting with the fourth season twists and themes began to be introduced. The most famous of these twists was during season 5 when the program ran for 365 days and the winner walked away with 1 Million euros. Season 5 is the longest running Big Brother show world wide, and also was acknowledged by the Guinness Book of World Records as the longest running uninterrupted broadcast. === Celebrity Version ===

The celebrity edition of the show differs greatly from the civilian series that have been aired. The show follows a similar format to the civilian series except that it only lasts for about two weeks. The format is more fast paced due to the shortened time period, meaning that days 8-15 are all eviction shows with one or more housemates leaving the house per night, as voted on by the public. The Celebrities participating are playing for a 100,000 Euro prize which is ultimately awarded by the viewers during the live finale show.

==Twists==
*'''Housemate Rankings:''' The viewers will be rating each housemate via the Sat.1 app ranking each housemate out of 5 stars. These rankings will have a impact on the game determining the outcome of who will make decisions and ultimately the winner.
*'''Two Houses:''' The Big Brother compound consists of two houses this year. A log cabin and a glass house. The log cabin housemates will be provided with basic rations, supplies, and most importantly chickens. The glass house is a modern living space with monitors luxuries and more. The glass house housemates will be able to view their current ranking as well as be able to view comments posted by viewers in the app giving them vital information on how they are viewed by the public.
*'''Room of Truth:''' Each week a housemate will be chosen by the viewers via social media polls to enter the room of truth. Here the selected housemate will have to face comments from the audience as well as other surprises.
*'''Phase Two:''' On Day 15, Big Brother closed the Blockhouse moving all housemates in to the Glasshouse until further notice.

They could not participate in tasks, but still had the power to influence nominations. **[[Matthias Mangiapane]] stayed in the house during Week 1. He had the power to instantly nominate one housemate for eviction. **[[Emmy Russ]] stayed in the house during Week 2. She had the power to save-and-replace one of the nominees. **[[Cosimo Citiolo]] stayed in the house during Week 3. He had the power to save one nominee from eviction. **[[Gina-Lisa Lohfink]] stayed in the house during Week 4. She had the power to instantly nominate one housemate for eviction. **[[Janine Pink]] stayed in the house during Week 5. The '''American Big Brother House''' plays an important role in the series as it's the place where houseguests live together for a certain period of time. The house is actually located within a sound-stage studio lot inside the [[CBS|CBS Studio Center]] in [[wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]] near the Los Angeles River. The original one-story Big Brother House that appeared in the first five seasons was specially built on an empty back-lot. It then moved a few blocks away to CBS' Stage 18 and a specially-built backyard was added adjacent to the sound stage. The current house is a two-story house and has been in use starting from the sixth season up to the present. ==Original House== The original Big Brother house was used from [[Big Brother 1 (US)|Season 1]] until [[Big Brother 5 (US)|Season 5]]. It had a similar layout seen among early seasons of Big Brother internationally, and was based on the original Dutch house layout in the [[Big Brother Netherlands (franchise)|Netherlands]]. In contrast to the current house used in the show, the original house was slightly smaller in size and was a one-story house. In Season 2, the house introduced a [[Head of Household]] bedroom adjacent to the [[Diary Room]] and Living Room. January 22, 2017 - }} '''Big Brother Nigeria''', later known as '''Big Brother Naija''', is the Nigerian version of the popular television series ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== Big Brother is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. ===Retrieved From Africa Magic=== Big Brother is a reality game show franchise created by John de Mol of Endemol, originally broadcast in the Netherlands and subsequently syndicated internationally. As of 11 November 2016, there have been 387 seasons of Big Brother in over 54 franchise countries and regions. This is the second Big Brother Nigeria, the first airing in 2006. Housemates live together for a specified time in a specially constructed house that is isolated from the outside world. The Housemates vie to be the last person standing so that they can win the prizes Biggie has to offer. Housemates are closely monitored 24/7 on cameras through their various trials and tribulations, which is why Biggie’s eye is used in the logo: he is always watching. Housemates are required to nominate fellow Housemates for the weekly eviction show. The Housemate with the most votes is announced and the audience is invited to vote. Thereafter, the Housemate with the most votes will be evicted in a weekly show on Sunday evenings. The last person standing is declared the winner. Housemates have a daily meeting with Biggie in the Diary Room. During the Housemates’ all-important Diary Sessions, they are given daily and weekly tasks which are compulsory. These include Head of House challenges and Wagers. These tasks are designed to test Housemates’ teamwork abilities and community spirit. The Housemates’ positions in the house or weekly shopping allowance (to buy food and other essentials) are often at stake and this makes these tasks important; they are keenly contested as the aim of the game is to get as far as possible. Biggie always has something unique up his sleeve to challenge the Housemates to the limits of their capabilities, both mentally and physically. It is a tough game that brings out the best and the worst in contestants. There are many twists and turns along the way and the Housemates have to be at their best if they are to survive the full duration of the show. The Housemates have compulsory Diary sessions in which they are able to unpack their feelings with Biggie. These are almost treated as a confessional and this is the only time contestants can speak openly and frankly about their game and what is going on in the house. The return of Big Brother Nigeria follows the critical success of the second edition which saw aspiring hip-hop artiste Efe Ejeba winning the coveted N25 million prize money and SUV after almost three months of drama, intrigue, betrayal and entertainment in the Big Brother house. Speaking on Big Brother Nigeria’s return, the Regional Director, M-Net West Africa, Wangi Mba-Uzoukwu said: “Around the globe, the Big Brother format remains one of the most popular genres of entertainment and this is also the case in Nigeria. The edition of Big Brother Nigeria was one of the most successful reality shows not just in Nigeria, but around the continent with a record number of votes and many of the housemates going on to pursue careers in entertainment. We are delighted to have the show return for a third edition and cannot wait for our audiences to once again tune in to experience all of the exciting entertainment that the show is sure to provide.”https://africamagic.d

January 4, 2021 - April 4, 2025 }}'''Big Brother Netherlands''' is the very first ''Big Brother'' franchise. It created the format in which contestants live in an isolated house trying to avoid being evicted by the public with the aim of a prize at the end. This Endemol production set the rules for other versions of Big Brother. ==The Series== [[File:Big Brother 1999 House.jpg|thumb|225px|The very first Big Brother House.]] ===Creation of Big Brother=== The idea was born on Thursday, 4 September 1997 during a brainstorm session at John de Mol Produkties, an independent part of Endemol. Participants were John de Mol, Patrick Scholtze, Bart Römer and his brother, Paul Römer.[1] The idea called for a luxurious house with six contestants, closed for a year. The winner would receive 1,000,000 guilders. The working title was ''De Gouden Kooi (The Golden Cage)'' and the original concept was eventually realized as a reality show on Dutch television at the end of 2006. The group came up with the idea after the 1991 Biosphere 2 experiment in the Arizona desert, in which eight men and women discovered how hard it is to live together inside an airtight glass and steel geodesic dome that sought to replicate the Earth's environment. Big Brother alternated deprivation with excess. The format of Big Brother was also influenced by MTV's The Real World, which began in 1992 and originated the concept of putting strangers together for an extended period and recording the drama that ensued. The Real World had introduced "confessions" by housemates. Another pioneering reality format, the Swedish TV show Expedition Robinson, (produced in many countries as Survivor) which first aired in 1997, added to the Real World 's template the idea of competition, in which contestants battled were removed from the show until only one remained. The first version of Big Brother was broadcast in 1999 on Veronica in the Netherlands. In the first season of Big Brother, the house was very basic. Although essential amenities such as running water, furniture and a limited ration of food were provided, luxury items were often forbidden. This added a survivalist element to the show, increasing the potential for social tension. Nearly all later series provide a modern house for the contest with a jacuzzi, sauna, VIP suite, loft and other luxuries. In development, occupancy of the house was reduced to 100 days. An existing house was abandoned in favor of a prefabricated house. This made it possible to install "camera-cross", which allowed cameramen inside the house without being seen by the inhabitants. TVI launched the show and, since its beginning, it was a great success. ==The Series== ===Big Brother Format=== Contestants called "housemates" live together in a specially-constructed house that is isolated from the outside world. Housemates are voted out every week until only one remains and wins the cash prize. During their stay in the house, contestants are continuously monitored by live television cameras as well as personal audio microphones. August 29, 2011 - December 4, 2011}} '''Big Brother Norge''' is the Norwegian version of ''Big Brother''. It was aired from 2001 to 2003 on TV Norge for three moderately successful seasons. A new season of the programme was launched in late August 2011 on TV2 Bliss. ==How it Works== Big Brother is a reality show based on the Big Brother series by Endemol. The show originates from the Netherlands, where in 1999 the very first season was aired. At present, the format is spread in a number of countries around the world. A group of people (called the Housemates) live together in an isolated house. 24 hours a day their life is recorded by hidden cameras in all the rooms in the House. They don't have TV, Internet, newspapers, even watches on their hands. The Housemates are completely isolated from the outside world. Every week, each one of them must enter the Diary room and nominate 2 of the other people for public eviction. The 2 or more housemates with most negative votes become nominated. For almost a week the TV viewers have to decide which of them to be evicted, voting via SMS or phone calls. Every week the Housemates have a week task. Depending on whether they do their task successfully or unsuccessfully, their week budget is increased or decreased. During the final week, the viewers vote which one of the remaining people in the House to be the winner. He or she wins a big cash prize. ==Series== {{Norwegian Series}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

March 17, 2019 - December 15, 2019}} '''Wielki Brat''' is the Polish version of the international reality series, ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== Based on the original Dutch version created by Endemol, the show sees a number of "housemates", divided by gender, social backgrounds and geographical locations, locked up together in a house, where the viewing public can watch them twenty-four hours a day, and vote them out of the house as they choose. The housemates can visit the "Dairy Room" at any time during the day, either to talk to psychologists if they need to, talk to "Big Brother", or to nominate. The title is inspired by the George Orwell novel ''1984''. The novel tells of a Big Brother, head of the totalitarian state of Oceania that constantly monitors its inhabitants by the camera in an attempt to suppress their free will. The tag line of the novel is "Big Brother is watching you", which inspired the show, as it is Big Brother who now has total control over the situation in the house. The housemates live in a house 24 hours a day, bugged by numerous cameras and microphones which capture their every move. Every week the housemates participate in tasks that determine their food budget for that week, or could even affect that week's nominations. The overall goal is to be the final surviving housemate and claim the prize fund. A PlayStation game based on this version was released in 2003. ==Series== {{Poland Series}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

==Twists==
*'''American Format:''' Unlike the format of the previous seasons, this season would have elements of the American format of the game.
*'''Numéros:''' The Numéros were divided into two different housemates. They were the housemates that controlled the nominations for the week.
**'''Numéro 1:''' The Numéro 1 was the [[Head of Household]]. Numéro 1 was exempt from eviction and enjoyed certain luxuries. They were also required to nominate two housemates for eviction.
**'''Numéro 2:''' Numéro 2 was selected by Numéro 1. Despite being immune from eviction and enjoying certain luxuries, they were forced to sleep at the foot of Numéro 1's bed, lest they lose their power and privilege. In addition, Numéro 2 was required to choose a third housemate to nominate for eviction.
*'''Pouvoir de Véto:''' The Pouvoir de Véto (translated as the [[Power of Veto]]), would be held every week to save a nominated housemate. The winner of the Véto would have the right to veto a nominee and select the replacement.
*'''[[Food Competition]]:''' Each week the housemates would battle over what they would be allowed to eat in the house. The winners received desired food items, such as steak, bread, vegetables, and dairy, while the losers dined on [[slop]].
*'''Public vs. Housemate Evictions:''' Each week the housemates would either vote out the nominees themselves or a public vote would occur to vote a housemate out.
*'''Jury''': At the final eviction, the jury of previously departed housemates and the current housemates would vote out one housemate left out of the house.
*'''Grenade:''' Similar to ''[[Big Brother Australia 8]]'' after a housemate was evicted from the game, the evicted housemate will be given a power or punishment to give to one of the remaining housemates in the game.

Big Brother Sverige 8.head:
{{Series |image = Logo=[[File:Sverige 8 Logo 1.jpg|200px]]|-|Eye=[[File:Sverige 8 Logo.png|200px]] |version = Sweden |series = 8 |seriesrun = February 10, 2020 - May 18, 2020 |host = Malin Stenbäck |prizemoney = 1,000,000 kr |nomberofhousemates = 19 |numberofdays = 99 |winner = [[Sami Jakobsson]] |runnersup = [[Lennie Hansson]] |returnees = [[Julia Löfgren]] ''([[Big Brother Sverige 9|S9]])''

[[Victoria Klöfver Rama]] ''([[Big Brother Sverige 9|S9]])'' |executiveproducer = Joel Bendrik |channel = [[wikipedia:TV4 (Sweden)|TV4]] |previousseries = [[Big Brother Sverige 7]] |nextseries = [[Big Brother Sverige 9]]|video=[[File:Big Brother Sverige - Intro 2020 (TV4 - C More)|200px]]}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the eighth season of ''[[Big Brother Sverige (franchise)|Big Brother Sverige]]''. ==Background== ===Developments=== In September 2019, TV4 announced that Big Brother Sverige will be coming back on Swedish television after 5 years. Set to air in Spring 2020, the new season would be a fresh reboot of the original ''Big Brother Sverige'' series. With the new technological advancements in Big Brother internationally, the TV4 aimed to adopt the upgrades regarding the hit reality series. Fredrik Arefalk, the channel manager of TV4 stated that: ''“Big Brother revolutionized the world of television when it launched in the Netherlands 20 years ago and it is still going strong internationally. With today's technology and smartphones, "Big Brother" is more right in time than ever before and we are really looking forward to making a brand new and modern "Big Brother". The technical conditions for letting viewers follow and control what's going on in the house are on a completely different level today and we believe it will attract the young digital generation, but also a wider audience that has followed "Big Brother" before. "''{{cite web|url=https://www.expressen.se/noje/blogg/tvbloggen/2019/09/24/big-brother-sverige-tv4-cmore-sjuan-premiar-varen-2020/|title="Big brother Sweden" makes comeback in the spring of 2020: "On a completely different level"|date=24 September 2019|website=expressen.se|language=Swedish}} ===Casting=== According to Executive Producer Joel Bendrik, the casting for this season is a bit different to the previous seasons of Big Brother Sverige. The season's cast would have an age range within 20-30 years old, aiming to reflect the current generation of Swedish people along with different characteristics and personalities. ===Trailer and Logo Reveal=== [[File:Big Brother Sweden premieres in TV4 (Trailer 2020)|thumb|right|250px]] On January 22, 2020, the first trailer was released on the show's official social media pages. The trailer comes with the tagline; ''"100 days, 100 nights"'' indicating that the season would have a duration of 100 days. The official eye logo of the season was officially revealed in the trailer, adopting the new rebranded logo of the international Big Brother franchise. For this season, the eye has a yellow and pink color, with a camera lens as the eye lens of the logo. ===The House=== The Big Brother Sverige 8 house was built in Telestaden, a new real-estate property in Farsta, Stockholm. October 8, 2023 - }} '''Big Brother UK''' is the United Kingdom version of the popular international reality show ''Big Brother''. It was broadcast on [[Channel 4]] for its first 11 seasons before moving to [[Channel 5]] starting with ''[[Big Brother 12 (UK)]]''. The show was once again axed in 2018 before ITV bought the rights to the show in 2022, with ''[[Big Brother 20 (UK)]]'' being the first British series of Big Brother to air in almost 5 years of the show being axed by Channel 5. The series has received much critical acclaim over its run, with several housemates becoming notable media figures following their time on the show. The popularity of the main series has resulted in four spin-off series (''[[Teen Big Brother]]'', ''[[Big Brother Panto]]'', ''[[Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack]]'', and ''[[Ultimate Big Brother]]''), as well as a celebrity edition of the show which has become a staple in its own right. ==How it Works== [[File:BBUK Days Chart Civilian.png|250px|thumb|right|The amount of days per season (Civilian).]] [[File:BBUK Days Chart Celebrity.png|250px|thumb|right|The amount of days per season (Celebrity).]] [[File:BBUK Days Chart Spin-Off.png|250px|thumb|right|The amount of days per season (Spin-Offs).]] ''Big Brother'' is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually fewer than 15 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ===Civilian Series=== The UK version of the show largely follows the same format as the original Dutch version of ''Big Brother'' where each week the housemates will nominate two of their fellow housemates for eviction and the public will then vote to evict the two (or more) housemates who received the most nominations. Previously, Irish housemates have been allowed to apply for Big Brother, and have entered the Big Brother house, however the terms and conditions of ITV's reboot series application form stated only permanent residents of the United Kingdom were able to apply. What differentiates ''Big Brother UK ''from other versions of the show is not only its massive popularity but also its heavy reliance on twists. It is not uncommon for multiple twists to change the standard layout of the game each season, with past twists including the house being divided into Rich and Poor sides, housemates becoming "Power Housemates" and gaining special powers for the week, and housemates being fake evicted and moved into a secret house next door to the main house. It is not uncommon for housemates to move into the house after the series has already begun, and some of the tension on the show can come from the clash between people who have already been living in the house for a while and new people moving into the house. === Celebrity Version === The celebrity edition of the show contains a number of differences from the regular version of the show, although the core idea remains the same. }}'''Người giấu mặt''', translated into '''Big Brother Vietnam''', is the Vietnamese version of ''Big Brother''.

The show launched on VTV6's primetime block from November 12, 2013 and ended on January 14, 2014. Twelve strangers were originally introduced, with one more housemate introduced as a replacement housemate after one walked out of the competition.

VTV reportedly dropped the franchise and won't be able to return for its second season.

==Background==
After nearly 11 years, the idea of bringing Big Brother to Vietnam came into fruition through VTV6, the government-owned television broadcaster in Vietnam. and its production partner BHD.

It officially aired on VTV6 on November 12, 2013 where in 12 Vietnamese strangers were unveiled to the public and was sent to the Vietnamese Big Brother house.

With the prize of 2 Billion Vietnamese Dong (89500 USD), it was the largest prize a Vietnamese reality program ever had. According to BHD, the program is the most expensive ever to be produced by the said company with a production crew of 150 people and 12 international experts.
==How It Works==
===Vietnamese Series===
'''''Người giấu mặt''''' is a Vietnamese version of the ''Big Brother'' reality television show based on the Dutch television series of the same name originally created in 1997 by John de Mol's company Endemol. The show is based on a group of strangers, known as Housemates, living together twenty-four hours a day in the "Big Brother" house, isolated from the outside world but under constant surveillance with no privacy for five months more.

Big Brother Swap.head:
''This article is about the twist that appeared on Big Brother (US). For the international Big Brother Swap twist, see [[Housemate Exchange]].'' {{Twists |image=[[File:BB Swap.jpg|225px]] |description = One preexisting houseguest is replaced by a new houseguest. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} |seasonsappeared = ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]''
''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''}} The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a twist that appeared on ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]'' and is one of the opening night twists on ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. The core mechanic of the twist is that a preexisting houseguest is replaced by a new houseguest, typically triggered by a temptation or offer that creates a vacancy in the cast. ==Appearances== ===Big Brother 1 (US)=== After Week 9 of ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]'', it was revealed during the live eviction show that the six remaining houseguests would be offered $20,000 to walk from the game. If a houseguest accepted the offer, they would leave and be replaced by a woman named [[Beth Thieme]]. Ultimately, no one took the offer (including a subsequent $50,000 offer made later that night), and Beth did not enter the house. ===Big Brother 19 (US)=== On premiere night of ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', the sixteen houseguests were tempted with $25,000, with the warning that accepting it would unleash a personal consequence and a house-wide consequence. [[Kevin Schlehuber|One houseguest]] accepted the money and was instructed to throw the first Head of Household competition. When the Houseguests returned inside, the doorbell rang and [[Paul Abrahamian]] re-entered the house as a houseguest. Paul was granted the opportunity to save eight houseguests. The remaining eight competed for safety, leaving three houseguests nominated. The nominees then voted on whether their fate would be decided by house votes or a competition; by a 2–1 vote, they chose a house vote. By a vote of 8–3–2, [[Cameron Heard|Cameron]] was evicted, opening a spot for Paul. ==History== {| style="border: 1px solid; width: 55%; text-align:center; color:#000;" |- ! style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | Season ! style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | Week ! scope="col" style="text-align:center; background-color:rgb(149,159,253); color:#3a3a3a;" | Person Entering ! scope="col" style="text-align:center; background-color:rgb(250,128,114); color:#3a3a3a;" | Person Leaving |- ! style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 1 ! style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 10 | colspan="2" style="color:#FFFFFF;" | N/A |- ! rowspan=3 style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 19 ! style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 1 | style="color:#000;" | [[Paul Abrahamian]] | style="color:#000;" | [[Cameron Heard]] |} ==Trivia== *The Big Brother Swap from ''Big Brother 19'' is the first time in [[Big Brother]] history that a returnee re-entered the game as a Houseguest and was safe from eviction on premiere night. {{GameplayNav}} [[Category:Twists]] [[Category:Gameplay]] [[Category:Big Brother 1 (US)]] [[Category:Big Brother 19 (US)]]

Since its debut in 2005, Big Brother Thailand has run continuously with at least one season of the show airing each year, Big Brother was renewed for a 2nd season. ==Series== {{Thailand Editions}} ==Trivia== * [[Big Brother Croatia 5]] used the Big Brother Thailand house for the [[Foreign House]] twist of the season. Chris Roach}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a spin-off of the ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother U.S.]]'' franchise since ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]''. It shows live feeds from the [[Big Brother House/United States|Big Brother House]]. Unfortunately, it did not return in ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'' nor any season after, celebrity or civilian editions. ==Broadcast and features== The show covered events happening in the House during 9:00 p.m.–12:00 a.m. PT.[http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news.aspx?id=20070611cbs01 "CBS'S SUMMER OF "BIG BROTHER" ON-AIR (CBS), ONLINE (REALNETWORKS, CBS.COM AND THE CBS AUDIENCE NETWORK), ON THE PHONE (CBS MOBILE) AND NEW THIS SUMMER - ON SHOWTIME!"]. The Futon Critic/CBS. June 11, 2007. Retrieved April 4, 2008.[http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news.aspx?id=20080211cbs01 ""BIG BROTHER: 'TIL DEATH DO YOU PART" HERE...THERE..EVERYWHERE"]. The Futon Critic/CBS. February 11, 2008. Retrieved April 4, 2008 According to executive producer Allison Grodner, these three hours would be entertaining as "That's prime time for the ''Big Brother'' house. It's when our HouseGuests are most wide awake and having fun, talking about strategy and playing the game. People are going to see quite a bit."[http://www.tvsquad.com/2007/06/11/big-brother-after-dark/ Big Brother: After Dark, by Isabelle Carreau] TV Squad When the program debuted on Showtime 2, ''Big Brother: After Dark'' aired live seven nights a week from midnight to 3:00 a.m. Eastern (11:00 p.m.–2:00 a.m. Central) while a season of ''Big Brother'' is in progress. (Although it was tape delay on Showtime 2's West Coast feed, this was of little consequence as some major providers offered both coastal feeds of Showtime 2 as part of the service's multiplex tier.){{cite web | last = Donohue | first = Steve | title = Big Brother: After Dark Returns to Showtime | publisher = Multichannel News | date = January 8, 2008 | url = http://www.multichannel.com/article/CA6518192.html | accessdate = January 8, 2008 }} The show uses the same live feed footage available to Internet subscribers 24 hours a day throughout the season, though the show's producers choose the camera angles and scenes within the program. Every twenty minutes during the show, after a short promotional break showcasing Showtime's original series, a "scroll" was featured on the bottom of the screen to explain to viewers what events occurred that day prior to the start of the show. Due to the uncensored nature of the show, it was rated TV-MA-LS (for adult language and sexual situations) on Showtime 2. For the show's five-season run on Showtime 2, ''Big Brother: After Dark'' was the only first-run original program that was produced specifically for any of Showtime's seven multiplex channels (the bulk of the network's first-run original programming airs on the main Showtime channel, and is replayed on its various multiplex channels and on certain sister channels like Pop). The majority of the shows on ''Big Brother: After Dark'' are live with certain exceptions. During the [[Big Brother 9 (US)|ninth season]] of ''Big Brother'' the April 21, 2008, an episode was pre-recorded from earlier in the day due to an eviction and endurance competition still in progress at 9:00 p.m. PT/12:00 a.m. ET.Alison Grodner Productions, Endemol

{{nowrap|Endemol Shine North America}} |castphoto = [[File:BBOTT_Cast.png|200px]] |video = [[File:Big Brother Over the Top (BB19) Official Intro|190px]] |previousseason = [[Big Brother 18 (US)]] |nextseason = [[Big Brother 19 (US)]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the first digital season of ''[[Big Brother (U.S.)]]'' and the 19th season overall. During the ten weeks on [[CBS#Services|CBS All-Access]], America voted for various types of twists every week hoping to impact the game. However, because of the voting opportunities, the fan base was spread apart like never before with online campaigning rivaling the [[wikipedia:United States presidential election, 2016|2016 United States Presidential Election]]. After 65 days, the lone [[The Ballsmashers|Ballsmashers]] member remaining, [[Morgan Willett]] was crowned the winner with the most votes from CBS All-Access viewers over [[Late Night Jamboree]] alliance members [[Jason Roy]] and [[Kryssie Ridolfi]]. Although the season was widely regarded and many fans have asked for a second season, it seems highly unlikely. The season was consistently avoided in terms of mentions or references in an official form since its conclusion, even when ''Big Brother'' celebrated its [[Big Brother 20 (US)|20th season]] (Morgan and [[Alex Willett]] were in the audience for an episode but were not shown or mentioned on screen), its actual 20th anniversary in [[Big Brother 22 (US)|season 22]], nor its [[Big Brother: 25th Anniversary Celebration|25th anniversary special]]. After CBS All-Access rebranded into [[CBS#Services|Paramount+]] in 2021, all direct links to the season were removed from the website and its corresponding press website, but the official webpage with all the episodes and clips, alongside the official social media accounts still existed, up until late 2024, when they were removed entirely. [https://web.archive.org/web/20240520114454/https://www.paramountplus.com/shows/big-brother-over-the-top/ This link will take you to an internet archive of its former official Paramount+ page]. The season was finally mentioned in an official capacity during the [[Big Brother 25 (US)|25th season]] premiere, where a competition themed around "a multiverse where things are reversed" took place, and a headline shown in this multiverse stated that "BBOTT RENEWED FOR SECOND SEASON", seemingly confirming that in reality, the show will not be getting a second season and has effectively been cancelled. As of August 17, 2024, the season is no longer available for official viewing, and is now classified as lost media due to the lack of legal access to its content. ==Production Changes== *'''[[File:Big_Brother_Over_The_Top_Schedule_-_EMBED.jpg|thumb|''Big Brother: Over The Top'' Schedule]]Less Prize Money:''' Unlike the normal broadcast version, ''Over The Top'' featured a cash prize of $250,000. *'''No Event Blackouts 24/7:''' Unlike the normal broadcast version of the live feeds, the ''Over The Top'' live feeds had no blackouts during competitions, ceremonies, and evictions. *'''Shorter Season:''' Unlike previous seasons, this season lasted only 65 days, making this the second shortest season of the [[Big Brother (U.S.)|American version of Big Brother]].

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the seventh season of ''Bigg Boss (Hindi)''.

==Background==
The season was announced in July 2013 with Salman Khan returning as the host. The series lasted for fifteen weeks and 105 days. 

The theme of this season was Heaven and Hell where the housemates were initially divided into two separate sections of the house, one called "Heaven" and the other "Hell."

===Eye Logo===
The eye was revealed by the channel Colors in August 2013. It features colours of Red, Brown and Yellow. It is because of the theme of this season.

===The House===

===Heaven===
The heaven side of the house has a pool and a beach like feel and also has a portion that has a dome like ceiling designed to look like a skyline filled with clouds. The walls of the house are not only colorful but also have words like ‘crazy’ written on it with much flair. It also has a quote written on a wall that is the highlight of the living area. The house also includes a wash basin with a cycle. For the first time in the history of Bigg Boss, the house has a clock in the living room.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/salman-khan-bigg-boss-7-heaven-and-hell-concept-is-just-a-publicity-stunt/1168692/ |title=Salman Khan: Bigg Boss 7 'heaven and hell' concept is just a publicity stunt |publisher=Archive.indianexpress.com |date=15 September 2013 |access-date=30 April 2014}}</ref>

===Hell===
The hell side of the house has beds arranged on the floor but not much of a comfort to any of the contestants. The house is separated by a fence. There is one gate which is connected to the heaven side. Food is a big concern for the contestants as participants in this area do not have a kitchen. As per an announcement by bigg boss all the food is prepared by heaven living mates for themselves and for hell living mates. Also there is no demarcation between the bedroom and living area and will give the house a dormitory kind of a look. The toilets inside the hell half have only Indian style sitting and the water is to be filled manually and used for all daily chores from a tap planted outside.<ref name=":0" />

===Circumspection between Houses===
According to the concept of Heaven and Hell, and the boundary between two houses, Bigg Boss orders some strictures among inmates of both houses. With these orders, Inmates are unable to cross the boundary of each other places without the permission of Bigg Boss, No one can give anything from heaven side to hell or vice versa in any condition, but, they can share only food which is the basic necessity of both inmates and as hellmates have no kitchen and all the responsibility of food is of heavenmates.<ref name=":0" />

She has a responsibility for making inmates wake up on time, keep an eye on inmates tasks and their actions. It is the only new element that is common for both the houses.

==Background==
===Development===
[[File:Bigg Boss Double Trouble - Coming Soon|thumb|Bigg Boss 9 First Promo]]
The season was announced in July 2015. The season's promo released on 7 September 2015 featuring its host Salman Khan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/television/reality-tv/story/bigg-boss-season-9-promo-out-salman-khan-promises-double-trouble-for-contestants-261540-2015-09-07|title=Bigg Boss Season 9 promo out; Salman Khan promises 'double, trouble' for contestants|date=7 September 2015}}</ref>

The house theme mainly focuses on aesthetics to adapt to the underlying premiere twist for the ninth season which revolves around the housemates entering the house in pairs rather than as individual housemates.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bigg Boss 9: All you need to know about paired contestants!|url=http://www.abplive.in/tv/2015/10/11/article737762.ece/Bigg-Boss-9-Heres-everything-you-need-to-know-about-paired-contestants|publisher=[[ABP Live]]|date=October 11, 2015 |accessdate=October 13, 2015}}</ref>

===House===
The season's house pictures were revealed on 9 October 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/entertainment/bollywood/bigg-boss-9-house-pics-salman-khan-23841.html|title=Leaked: Inside pictures of Salman Khan's Bigg Boss 9 house|date=9 October 2015}}</ref> ''"The chalet-styled house, where contestants of the ninth edition of the reality TV show will compete for the coveted trophy and prize money, was designed by “Mary Kom” director Omung Kumar, said Deepak Dhar, managing director of Endemol Shine India, the producers of “Bigg Boss Nau”.''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.india.com/entertainment/bigg-boss-9-house-leaked-pictures-see-salman-khans-exclusive-double-trouble-bigg-boss-house-620523/|title=Bigg Boss 9 house leaked pictures: See Salman Khan’s exclusive ‘Double Trouble’ Bigg Boss house!|date=11 October 2015}}</ref> 

The house sections are replicated to depict places in history and around the globe. The exterior of the house is crafted to recreate the Garden of Eden.<ref>{{cite web|title=BB9 House which boasts grandeur and style|url=http://www.pinkvilla.com/tv/scoops/342887/bigg-boss-9-check-out-spectacular-house-which-boasts-grandeur-and-style#4|publisher=PinkVilla|accessdate=October 10, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sneak peek inside this year's Bigg Boss house|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/970119/sneak-peak-inside-bigg-boss-double-trouble-house/|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=October 9, 2015|accessdate=October 10, 2015}}</ref> It features a fortune teller machine and a wide canopy. The kitchen contains most of its sculptural and art pieces from the architecture of Santorini while the bathroom area follows a glitzy Las Vegas theme.<ref>{{cite web|title=BB9 Salman pics|url=http://www.indiatvnews.com/entertainment/bollywood/bigg-boss-9-house-pics-salman-khan-23841.html|newspaper=[[Times of India]]|accessdate=October 10, 2015}}</ref> The bathroom walls are lined with mirrors and most of the furniture is crimson.
