'''Bigg Boss 10''' is the tenth season of ''Bigg Boss (Hindi)''.

==Background==
===Development===
On the finale night of ''[[Bigg Boss 9 (Hindi)]]'', the season was announced and it was confirmed that the season will be open to civilians.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/television/reality-tv/story/bigg-boss-opens-doors-for-commoners-in-season-10-public-can-participate-in-the-show-as-contestant-winner-305164-2016-01-23|title=Bigg Boss opens its door to commoners in Season 10|date=23 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bollywoodbubble.com/bollywood-news/bigg-boss-season-10-opens-doors-to-commoners/|title=‘Bigg Boss’ season 10 opens doors to commoners|date=23 January 2016}}</ref> In February 2016, it was announced that Salman Khan will be hosting the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/salman-khan-to-host-season-10-of-bigg-boss/articleshow/50974640.cms|title=Salman Khan to host season 10 of Bigg Boss|date=13 February 2016}}</ref> The first promo was released on August 27, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/bigg-boss-10-promo-is-out-and-salman-khan-has-turned-astronaut/articleshow/53884157.cms|title=Bigg Boss 10 promo is out and Salman Khan has turned astronaut|date=27 August 2016}}</ref>

===House===
The house pictures were revealed on October 14, 2016 by host Salman Khan on Twitter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/television/bigg-boss-10-house-images-revealed-by-salman-khan-3083152/|title=Bigg Boss 10 house images revealed by Salman Khan|date=15 October 2016}}</ref> 

The house is themed to appear as a modern Indian palace with elements of mystique that invoke sentiments like vigour and positivity. The bedroom area features not only seven single beds, but also a massive bed. 7 contestants will take the single bed and the remaining will have to share a massive bed which has been placed against a wall. A first-time addition is a walk-in closet adorned with full-length mirrors to ensure that the contestants look their absolute best at all times. The seat of the confession room is a classic emulation of a King’s Throne covered in deep and glittery gold. With the walls covered in deep red, and rustic lamps suspended from the ceiling. The jail is splattered with gruesome material and promises to be as good as hell. Located in a corner in the garden area, the jail has two Iron Beds with dusty bedding. Aluminium utensils, an earthen water pot and an Indian-style washroom. The newest addition to the bathroom area this season, is a luxurious Jacuzzi placed in a corner which allows everyone a full view of the entire room. A pristine white Jacuzzi in a royal purple washroom adorned with Peacock graphics. The kitchen is the ultimate epitome of class and style. Its earthy tones and country design will bring a touch of home to this otherwise royal home. And this is extended to the dining table where a large curved table is set. All these elements are supported by the garden area which features a swimming pool, gym area and a specially-created Appy Fizz zone for the contestants to take a break from the daily tasks, making their Bigg Boss journey more enjoyable.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/Bigg-Boss-10-Sneak-Peek-into-the-royal-and-grand-house/photostory/54878634.cms|title=Bigg Boss 10: Sneak Peek into the royal and grand house|date=16 October 2016}}</ref>

[[Kani Thiru]] (2026-) | seriesrun = November 3, 2006 - }}'''Bigg Boss''' is the Indian version of the popular reality franchise ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== Big Brother is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are 10-17 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ==History== The idea for the show is said to come during a brainstorm session at the production house of John de Mol Produkties (an independent part of Endemol) on 4 September 1997. The first Big Brother broadcast was in the Netherlands in 1999 on the Veronica TV channel. It was picked up by Germany, Portugal, USA, UK, Spain, Belgium, Sweden, Switzerland and Italy the following year and became a world-wide sensation. Since then it has been a prime-time hit in almost 70 countries. The show's name comes from George Orwell's 1948 dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four. ==Franchises== ===Hindi=== {{Hindi Editions}} ===Kannada=== {{Kannada Editions}} ===Bengali=== {{Bengali Editions}} ===Tamil=== {{Tamil Editions}} ===Telugu=== {{Telugu Editions}} ===Marathi=== {{Marathi Editions}} ===Malayalam=== {{Malayalam Editions}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Television]] [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

After an abrupt ending to the [[Bigg Boss Malayalam 2|second season]] of the show, makers of the show confirmed that the third season of the show would air in February 2021. Asianet announced that the show would air on February 14, 2021, with the show running for 99 days, with the finale on May 23, 2021. However, when the [[The Impact of COVID-19 on Big Brother|COVID-19 pandemic]] hit India for its second wave, makers were adamant that the show would continue until its finale. Despite the cancellation of [[Bigg Boss Kannada 8|the eighth Kannada season]], producers decided to extend the show by two weeks, with the finale on June 6, 2021. On May 19, 2021, Asianet announced that the show would be temporarily suspended because eight crew members tested positive for COVID-19. Unlike the previous season, Asianet currently plans on resuming the show after all current housemates receive a negative COVID-19 test.{{cite web|url=https://www.filmibeat.com/malayalam/news/2021/bigg-boss-malayalam-3-shoot-is-suspended-contestants-shifted-to-a-hotel-314058.html|title=Bigg Boss Malayalam 3 Shoot Is Suspended; Contestants Shifted To A Hotel|date=19 May 2021|website=filmibeat.com|language=}} On May 24, 2021, Asianet confirmed that the contestants were going to be sent home, but the viewers would be allowed to select a winner out of the eight finalists.{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/malayalam/bigg-boss-malayalam-3-to-declare-the-winner-based-on-online-votes-8-contestants-reach-finale/articleshow/82900936.cms|title=Bigg Boss Malayalam 3 to declare the winner based on online votes; 8 contestants reach finale|date=24 May 2021|website=timesofindia.indiatimes.com|language=}} On July 25, 2021, Asianet announced that the finale would air on August 1, 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.asianetnews.com/entertainment-biggboss/artist-mohanlal-announce-bigg-boss-season-3-grand-finale-date-qwt6f6|title=ആരാകും ബിബി 3 വിജയി ? ഗ്രാൻഡ് ഫിനാലെ അനൗൺസ് ചെയ്ത് മോഹൻലാൽ|date=25 July 2021|website=asianetnews.com|language=Malayalam}} ==Background== ==Twists== *'''[[Project DNA]]''': [[Firoz Khan & Sajna Firoz|Firoz Khan]] entered the game with his wife, [[Firoz Khan & Sajna Firoz|Sajna]], on Day 8. Despite being nominated multiple times and constantly targeted, he repeatedly saved himself by winning critical Power of Veto competitions, but his relationship with Rachel and his competitive threat level kept him under constant pressure. After Rachel’s eviction, Brendon briefly gained traction by winning Head of Household and attempting to regain control of the game, but he remained a primary target in the midgame. Ultimately, a [[Double Eviction]] in Week 7 resulted in him being evicted during the second half in a unanimous 3-0 vote. He placed 6th and was the 4th member of the [[jury]]. On [[Big Brother 13 (US)|''Big Brother 13 (US)'']], Brendon came back into the house alongside Rachel as a part of the [[Dynamic Duos]] twist. He and Rachel joined the [[Veterans]] alliance with the other veteran players. In Week 4, both Brendan and Rachel were nominated by HoH [[Daniele Donato]] after she turned on the Veterans alliance. Brendon won the PoV but chose to use it on Rachel; he was then evicted in a 5-2 vote. However, he returned the next week after receiving the most votes from America to come back and defeating [[Lawon Exum]] in a sudden death competition. In Week 6, however, Daniele once again won HoH and [[Backdoor|backdoored]] Brendon, sending him home in a 5-1 vote. On ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', Britney made close relationships with [[Lane Elenburg]], [[Monet Stunson]], and [[Ragan Fox]], while getting into a rivalry with [[Brendon Villegas]] and [[Rachel Reilly]]. However, she was infamously unaware that she was helping to push the agendas of the secret dominant alliance, [[The Brigade]]. At the final four, she became the consensus target for being the only non-Brigade member left. After failing to win the [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]], the Brigade revealed the existence of their alliance and her imminent eviction to a shocked Britney, with [[Enzo Palumbo]] casting the sole vote to evict her. She placed 4th and was the 6th member of the [[The Jury|jury]]. On finale night, she won the [[America's Favorite Houseguest]] award. Britney returned on ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'', as a [[Coach]]. Although initially in a minority position as she only had one player left in [[Shane Meaney]], she was able to pull through with her excellent social positioning with the rest of the house. However, when the coaches were allowed to enter the game as players in week 3, Britney became a key member of [[The Quack Pack]] alliance, forming strong relationships with [[Danielle Murphree]] and [[Ian Terry]]. Her game came to an end at the final eight when [[Dan Gheesling]] managed to miraculously get himself off the block at the Power of Veto ceremony by revealing [[Ian Terry]]'s duplicity to Dan's nemesis [[Frank Eudy]]. As Ian was safe for winning a second veto, Dan convinced Frank to target Britney as collateral damage instead, in an attempt to weaken Ian and eliminate a huge strategic threat. She was evicted in a 4 to 1 vote, with Ian being the sole vote to keep her. She placed 8th and was the second member of the jury. On ''Reindeer Games'', Britney quickly made amends with [[Nicole Franzel]], her friend with whom she had a falling out with outside the game, and forged an unbreakable alliance with her, along with ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)|Big Brother 16]]'' contestant [[Frankie Grande]]. ''"Only CBS"'' | website = [http://www.cbs.com/ cbs.com] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the American television channel that broadcasts the [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|American]] version of ''[[Big Brother]]''. ==History== '''CBS''' (an initialism of the network's former name, the Columbia Broadcasting Services or System) is an American English language commercial broadcast television network that is a flagship property of CBS Corporation. The company is headquartered at the CBS Building in New York City with major production facilities and operations in New York City (at the CBS Broadcast Center) and Los Angeles (at CBS Television City and the CBS Studio Center). CBS is sometimes referred to as the "Eye Network", in reference to the company's iconic logo, in use since 1951. It has also been called the "Tiffany Network", alluding to the perceived high quality of CBS programming during the tenure of William S. Paley. It can also refer to some of CBS's first demonstrations of color television, which were held in a former Tiffany & Co. building in New York City in 1950. The network has its origins in United Independent Broadcasters Inc., a collection of 16 radio stations that was purchased by Paley in 1928 and renamed the Columbia Broadcasting System. Under Paley's guidance, CBS would first become one of the largest radio networks in the United States, and eventually one of the Big Three American broadcast television networks. In 1974, CBS dropped its former full name and became known simply as CBS, Inc. The Westinghouse Electric Corporation acquired the network in 1995, renamed its corporate entity to the current CBS Broadcasting, Inc. in 1997, and eventually adopted the name of the company it had acquired to become CBS Corporation. In 2000, CBS came under the control of Viacom, which was formed as a spin-off of CBS in 1971. In late 2005, Viacom split itself into two separate companies, and re-established CBS Corporation – through the spin-off of its broadcast television, radio and select cable television and non-broadcasting assets – with the CBS television network at its core. CBS Corporation is controlled by Sumner Redstone through National Amusements, which also controls the current Viacom. CBS continues to operate the CBS Radio network, which now mainly provides news and features content for its portfolio of owned-and-operated radio stations in large and mid-sized markets, and affiliated radio stations in various other markets. The television network has more than 240 owned-and-operated and affiliated television stations throughout the United States. ==Services== On October 28, 2014, CBS launched '''CBS All Access''', a subscription streaming service offering access to past and present CBS shows. Priced at $5.99 per month ($9.99 without commercials), it became the first over-the-top (OTT) offering from a U.S. broadcast network. The service was available on platforms like Roku and Chromecast and included live programming from local CBS affiliates in 124 markets. CBS All Access allowed subscribers to watch recent episodes of CBS shows the day after they aired, along with complete back catalogs and classic series from CBS's library. Houseguests need to maneuver those eggs one by one to a certain destination while using their fingers. The first player to do so wins the competition. On ''[[Big Brother 18]]'' after maneuvering the egg instead of placing the egg to its slot houseguests needed to roll their eggs down the plank with the aim of knocking down three letters (H, O, and H). ==History== ===United States=== The competition was first used on ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)|Big Brother 11 (US)]]'' as a [[Power of Veto]] competition. Houseguest [[Kevin Campbell]] won this competition, winning his first PoV of the season. On ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' this competition returned as a [[Head of Household]] competition. It was the only time when Christmas ornaments were used instead of eggs. [[Hayden Moss]] was the first one to put all 18 ornaments and a star in their slots, winning his third HoH. The competition later appeared on ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]''. Houseguest [[GinaMarie Zimmerman]] won the competition, winning her second HoH of the season. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]''. Houseguests [[Cody Calafiore]] and [[Frankie Grande]] won the competition, winning their first and second HoH, respectively. However, Frankie was later on dethroned during that Week's [[Battle of the Block]] The competition reappeared the following season, ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]'', during Week 12. Houseguest [[Vanessa Rousso]] won the competition, winning her fourth permanent HoH of the season, while [[Liz Nolan]] won the luxury portion of the competition. In its next appearance, ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', houseguest [[Victor Arroyo]] won the competition, winning his third HoH of the summer. In its most recent appearance, ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'', houseguests [[Analyse Talavera]], [[Christie Murphy]] and [[Jackson Michie]] were voted into this competition via the America's Field Trip twist. Jackson ended up winning the competition and granting himself immunity for the week, while Analyse and Christie faced off to avoid being nominated. Analyse beat Christie, saving herself from the block but earning a punishment for losing, while Christie was nominated for eviction. ===Canada=== The competition was first used on ''[[Big Brother Canada 1]]''. After a certain amount of time, a barrier will drop, allowing the house guests to attempt to roll a ball towards bowling pin shaped targets on the other side. After a certain amount of time, the barrier will rise again, requiring the house guest to repeat the process. ==History== Originally appearing as a PoV competition in ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]'', it was won by [[McCrae Olson]], who was on the block against his [[showmance]] [[Amanda Zuckerman]]. Returning two years later on ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]'', history repeated itself, as [[Austin Matelson]] won this PoV competition after being nominated alongside his showmance [[Liz Nolan]]. Another two years later for ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', the competition was used as a [[Temptation Competition]], which was then by [[Mark Jansen]], who gained immunity for the week, while [[Jason Dent]] was nominated for coming in last place. On ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)]]'', it was used as an HoH competition, where [[Ross Mathews]] won. The physical aspect of this challenge caused [[Omarosa Manigault]] to have an asthma attack, requiring her to leave the house for a while to seek medical attention. In honor of ''[[wikipedia:Super Bowl LIII|Super Bowl LIII]]'', the competition was given a football theme as opposed to a bowling theme on ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2 (US)]]'', however the rules were essentially the same. Instead of rolling a bowling ball to knock down four pins, the players had to kick a giant inflatable football through a field goal three times. [[Natalie Eva Marie]] won her first PoV, making her the first female to win this competition. On [[Big Brother 23 (US)|''Big Brother 23 (US)'']], it was used as a PoV competition, with a slightly different format. Players were given a three digit code and were tasked to knock down the numbered pins not shown in the code. '''Bolshoy Brat ''(Большой брат)''''' ''(English: Big Brother)'' was the Russian version of the reality show ''[[Big Brother (franchise)|Big Brother]]'', and was produced by Endemol. Unlike most of the other countries the franchise aired in, ''Bolshoy Brat'' had only one season in Russia, with no plans for a second season.

==How it Works==
In the show, contestants called "housemates" live together in a specially-constructed house that is isolated from the outside world. Housemates are voted out (usually on a weekly basis) until only one remains and wins the cash prize. During their stay in the house, contestants are continuously monitored by live television cameras as well as personal audio microphones.

Each week, contestants anonymously nominated one contestant for eviction. The contestants with the most nominations were nominated for eviction. The public voted for who they wanted to keep on the show. The contestant who received the fewest votes was evicted.

Brittany’s game centered around her close Final Two partnership with [[Michael Bruner]], while she initially struggled socially before eventually joining [[The Leftovers]], which dominated the house and eliminated her former [[Girls Girls]] allies. Despite being frequently targeted due to weaker social bonds, she repeatedly survived eviction thanks to allies winning competitions or bigger threats being present, though her position collapsed during the Week 9 [[Double Eviction]] when Michael exposed her multiple endgame deals in a failed attempt to save himself, leaving her isolated after his eviction. From that point on she was consistently targeted but briefly saved herself with a crucial Week 10 veto win, though her attempts to flip the vote against [[Taylor Hale]] and keep [[Alyssa Snider]] failed. At the Final Four, with Taylor being the Head of Household and [[Monte Taylor]] winning the final Power of Veto, Monte cast the sole vote to evict Brittany as he had a better connection with [[Matt Turner]] and deemed Brittany as a threat to his pathway to the end. On finale night Brittany voted for Taylor, contributing to Taylor’s historic win. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

If the housemate received all 3 votes to stay, they would automatically advance to the Top 15. If they received 1-2 votes to stay, they would be placed "on hold," where their fate in the game would be determined later on in the season. If they did not receive any votes to stay, they would be automatically evicted. *'''Selection by Competition''': **During the second portion of the game, the housemates put on hold competed in a series of challenges. The winner of each challenge would enter the Top 15. Once the Top 15 was determined, the remaining housemates on hold would be evicted from the game. **During the third portion of the game, the 15 contestants continued competing in challenges. Each episode, the jury selected the worst performing housemates. If a competitor is selected as a worst performing housemate twice, they would be automatically evicted from the game. The remaining contestants after 15 episodes would enter final fourth phase of the game. *'''Selection by Viewers''': During the fourth portion of the game, the viewers voted for the housemates that they wanted to enter the following season. The six contestants that received the most votes would become official ''[[Bigg Boss Telugu 9]]'' housemates. The selected contestants would not be revealed until the ''[[Bigg Boss Telugu 9]]'' premiere. ==Housemates== {{Agnipariksha Progress}} ==Status History== {{Agnipariksha Status History}} ==Voting History== {{Agnipariksha Voting History}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{India Seasons}} {{Season Nav}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:India (Telugu) Seasons]] [[Category:Online Exclusive Seasons]] [[Category:Pre-Recorded Seasons]]

'''Carol Michelle Adler''' (née '''Journey''') was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]''.

Carol began the game with a target on her back as one of the few houseguests with [[rivals]] in the house. After [[Kail Harbick]] won the first [[Head of Household]] of the season, she targeted Carol due to their weak bond and Carol being one of the first two out of the Head of Household competition. Later, Kail nominated Carol alongside [[Amber Siyavus]]. After failing to win the [[Power of Veto]], Carol became an easy consensus target, only really having [[Jen Johnson]] on her side. Ultimately, Carol was evicted by a vote of 10-1, placing 14th.

==='''Biography'''===
Carol Michelle Journey (born March 3, 1986) was a student from Lawrence, Kansas, born and raised in Haysville, Kansas. Carol attends the University of Kansas and is part of their dance team. She is the daughter of Kansas State Senator Phil Journey.

}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the highly controversial fifth season of ''[[ Big Brother UK (franchise)|Celebrity Big Brother]]''. It saw 12 celebrities (as well as 2 non-celebrities) living together in the Big Brother house, participating in tasks and facing the threat of being nominated by their fellow housemates or evicted by the public.

This series caused worldwide controversy due to the actions of housemates Jade, Jo, and Danielle, who were accused of bullying and displaying racist behavior towards fellow housemate Shilpa Shetty. The public outcry caused as a result of this led to UK broadcasting committee Ofcom receiving the largest number of public complaints caused by a television show.
==Racism Controversy==
''Celebrity Big Brother 5'' was the recipient of a large amount of controversy and public complaints due do a number of incidents of racist behavior by several housemates towards Indian actress and fellow housemate Shilpa Shetty. The majority of these complaints were directed towards Jade Goody, Jo O'Meara, and Danielle Lloyd, though Jack Tweed and Jackiey Budden also received fire from the public. Among other instances were Jade referring to Shilpa as "Shilpa Fuckawallah" and "Shilpa Daroopa" and Danielle calling Shilpa a "dog" and claiming that she should "fuck off home".

By January 20 Ofcom had received 44,500 complaints from viewers about the incidents, while Channel 4 had received an additional 3000 complaints. Channel 4, which had initially referred to the events as "girlish rivalry" later admitted that bullying and racism were definitely present within the house. However, they continued to air instances of racism on the show, stating that the social dynamics of the house were a part of its narrative and viewers had the right to see events aired as accurately as possible.

In response to the controversy, a number of British political officials such as Leicester East MP Keith Vaz, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, and London mayor Ken Livingstone made statements condemning the racist behavior in the house. The Indian government stated they would take "action as required" in regards to the events. Former Chairman of Channel 4 Vanni Treves called for the station to cancel the show, despite the fact that ''Big Brother'' was Channel 4's most financially successful program. Further, several of ''Big Brother's'' sponsors and advertisers either pulled their sponsorships or cancelled their advertisement deals with the show.

Jade Goody, seen as the "frontrunner" of the racist incidents in the house, received the majority of backlash from the public. Her brand of perfume, ''Shh...'', was pulled from store shelves and book publisher HarperCollins cancelled plans to publish the paperback version of Goody's autobiography. Jade also received a number of death threats, and no audience was present at her eviction to prevent any attacks against her.

* '''Unmade Beds:''' Shortly after entering the house, Big Brother informed the housemates that two bedrooms would be available to them: Bedroom 2 would have the beds made, and Bedroom 1 would have unmade beds. The housemates, assuming that unmade meant not having the sheets or blankets on the mattress, entered Bedroom 1 only to discover that the beds were literally unmade, meaning all the parts to make up the frames of the beds were laid out but not put together. The housemates would have to construct the three beds before being able to sleep in them.

Like the regular version of ''[[Big Brother (UK)]]'', the show featured a number of strangers living in a house together in complete isolation, having to nominate each other for eviction with the public voting on who to evict. Unlike the regular version of the show, however, the six housemates living together were notable celebrities, with the prize money going to charity rather than to themselves. This season, all money raised was given to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief Comic Relief], with the season finale being held on Red Nose Day 2001. ==About== ''Retrieved from Comic Relief''
Celebrity Big Brother is the result of an incredible alliance between Comic Relief, Channel 4, BBC and Bazal (part of Endemol Entertainment UK) to raise money for Red Nose Day 2001, on 16th March. The week-long TV special will be made by Endemol and, uniquely, programmes will be broadcast on both Channel 4 and BBC ONE. The six celebrity housemates taking part in this special version of Big Brother will not receive fees of any kind and money raised from the voting lines will go to Comic Relief, as will the format fee for Endemol. The celebrities entered the Celebrity Big Brother house on Friday 9th March, and the final eviction will take place as part of BBC ONE's Red Nose Day on Friday 16th March. Conditions inside the house will be comfortable but basic, with simple food supplied and a small additional budget. As in Big Brother, the stars will be required to complete tasks, but this time the tasks will be daily.{{cite web|url=http://web.archive.org/web/20010418164818fw_/http://www.comicrelief.com:80/bigbrother/information/index.html|title=Information|publisher=Comic Relief|date=9 March 2001|accessdate=27 September 2018}} ==Twists== * '''Live Nominations:''' Each housemate was required to make their nominations live during the launch episode, moments after meeting each other. Back after the summer ended, co-producer Caroline Davies left the show. She would be replaced with Richard Greenwood, who worked with ''Big Brother's Bit On the Side'' Presenter [[Rylan Clark]].<ref>http://www.bbspy.co.uk/cbb19/news/1205/new-executive-producer-for-celebrity-big-brother-2017-all-stars-early-january-launch-confirmed</ref> Later after a production meeting, the producers decided to change the size of the beds in the new house. ==Twists==
*'''[[Returning Players|All-Stars vs. New Stars]]:''' New Housemates will compete alongside popular past Housemates.<ref>http://www.bbspy.co.uk/cbb19/news/1205/channel-5-confirms-all-stars-new-stars-theme-for-celebrity-big-brother-2017-reveals-new-comic-book-eye-logo</ref>
*'''Producers' Editing Out:''' The All-Stars and New Stars were separated upon entering. The All-Stars were sent into the producer's room (''previously the Others House'') and the New Stars were sent into the Main House. The All-Stars were then tasked with ''Editing Someone Out''. After five New Stars are edited out, it was announced that they could not nominate in the first round of nominations. The two stars that were not edited out, [[Angie Best|Angie]] and [[Jamie O'Hara|Jamie]] had to save four housemates from eviction leaving [[James Cosmo]] for the first eviction.
*'''Late Entrants:''' Multiple additional housemates entered after Day 1. [[Jedward Grimes|Jedward]] entered on Day 4 and [[Chloe Ferry|Chloe]], [[Jessica Cunningham|Jessica]], and [[Kim Woodburn|Kim]] on Day 11.
*'''Shock Eviction:''' On Day 11, the remaining 12 housemates were taken next door to "Hell". They were then joined by three new housemates: Chloe, Jessica, and Kim. They were then instructed to vote for the "dullest housemate". Austin received three votes, the majority, and was evicted from the house.
*'''Weekend In Hell:''' After Austin's eviction, [[Coleen Nolan|Coleen]], [[Heidi Montag & Spencer Pratt|Heidi & Spencer]], [[James Jordan|James J]], [[Jasmine Waltz|Jasmine]], Jedward, and [[Stacy Francis|Stacy]] were banished to "Hell" to fight for survival. After three different tasks and housemates "escaping Hell" and then "banished to hell" Heidi & Spencer, James C (who replaced Jedward), and Jasmine were left for the housemates in the "Land of the Living" (Main House) to unanimously evict one of the remaining housemates. Camp Director.head:
{{twists |image = [[File:BB21 Camp Director.png|225px]] |description= One houseguest would have the power to banish four houseguests for eviction. |seasonsappeared= ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'' |countriesappeared = {{United States}} }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a twist on ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''. ==Press Release== ''Retrieved from CBS.com''
==History== On Night One, the houseguests had to elect a "Camp Director" to rule over the house. The winner would have the power to banish four houseguests to the Hit The Road competition where the loser would be evicted from the house. The majority of the house voted for [[Jackson Michie]], making him the Camp Director. Jackson chose to banish [[Cliff Hogg III]], [[David Alexander]], [[Jessica Milagros]], and [[Kemi Fakunle]]. David lost the competition and was the first houseguest evicted from the house. ==Trivia== [[Category:Twists]] [[Category:Big Brother 21 (US)]]

Camp Comeback.head:
{{twists
|image = [[File:Camp Comeback.png|225px]]
| description= Evicted houseguests get to stay in the house, with one getting a permanent stay.
|countriesappeared = {{United States}}
| seasonsappeared= ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''
}}'''Camp Comeback''' is a twist introduced in ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'' where the first four evicted houseguests remained in the [[Big Brother House]], with one evicted houseguest earning their way back into the game.

Although the evicted houseguests are still allowed to remain in the house and play the social game, they must wear a camper's uniform and sleep in a room with [[Have-Not]]-like living conditions, although they were free to eat whatever they wanted. In addition, they are ineligible to participate in competitions and ceremonies and instead must watch and listen from a small black and white TV in the Camp Comeback room. However, they are allowed to be present at the live evictions.

After [[Ovi Kabir]] was evicted on Day 15, [[David Alexander]] re-entered the house after being evicted on Day 1 and they entered Camp Comeback together. [[Kemi Fakunle]] joined them on Day 23. On Day 30, [[Cliff Hogg III]] was evicted and the four immediately battled to get back into the main game, with Cliff returning, sending the other three home for good.
==Trivia==
* Camp Comeback can be described as ''Big Brother's'' version of ''Survivor's'' [[w:c:survivor:Edge of Extinction (twist)|Edge of Extinction]] twist.
* After the twist ended, the Camp Comeback room became the Have-Not room for the rest of the season.
* The twist was the center of much controversy during ''Big Brother 21'', as the first three people sent there were people of color ([[David Alexander|two African]]-[[Kemi Faknule|American contestants]] and [[Ovi Kabir|one of Bangladeshi descent]]), all evicted by Caucasian-American contestants. The controversy arose when the [[Cliff Hogg III|only Caucasian-American person]] in Camp Comeback was the person to return, eliminating the three minorities all at once.

The two HOHs had to agree to nominate two people together. If a consensus was not reached, the two HOHs would instead become the two nominees. *'''Hidden Votes''': Starting this season, during evictions, the vote count was not revealed to the housemates. *'''The Storm''': Every week, there were tasks that could cause one housemate to either to lose their vote or gain an additional one. *'''Chain of Safety''': On Day 15, there was a [[Double Eviction]]. However, unlike normal double evictions, the evictee was determined by a "Chain of Safety" selection process. Beginning with the winner of the immunity challenge, each housemate had to select another housemate to save until one person was left unselected, who would then become nominated. This was followed by a second safety chain, with the second housemate left unselected also being nominated. The two nominees had to compete against each other in a head-to-head duel to determine who was eliminated. The winner of the duel received immunity for the following week. *'''Temple of Crystals''': This season, contestants attempted to collect crystals throughout the game. Insulated by both [[The Pentagon]] and [[The Collective]] alliances, Cedric was able to build strong social connections, which allowed him to be safe from nominations. As he became the third Head of Household, it was initially a straightforward week when he targeted social pariah [[Angela Murray]], but easily crumbled at the hands of [[Tucker Des Lauriers]] who won the veto and saved Angela, instead of himself, because of Tucker's pure mistaken belief that [[Quinn Martin]] was going to be the replacement nominee in an attempt to flush out the [[Invisible HOH|Deepfake HOH]] advantage Quinn won. This ignited an intense rivalry between Cedric and Tucker, with both men openly targeting each other. When Cedric's ally Quinn hijacked Angela's Head of Household as he activated the Deepfake HOH, he asked Cedric to be the pawn with Tucker as the main target, which Cedric agreed to. This proved to be a fatal error as after Tucker won the veto to save himself and secondary target [[Makensy Manbeck]] also won safety via the AI Arena competition, his Collective allies [[Kimo Apaka]] and [[T'kor Clottey]] defected at the last minute in an attempt to defuse the power structure in The Pentagon, resulting in Cedric's unexpected eviction. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''
'''Age:''' 21
'''Hometown:''' Running Springs, CA
'''Current City:''' Boise, ID
'''Occupation:''' Former Marine
'''Why did you want to come on ''Big Brother''?'''
I want to compete on ''Big Brother'' or my siblings. Everyone tells you that you can do what you want. But when you see your big brother competing on ''Big Brother'', [Laughs.] it kind of adds. You could really do whatever you want. So I want to instill that into my siblings as much as I can, at the end of the day, what's most important to me isn't money or lying to people in the house. It's my family. So if I have to do that, then that's what you have to do. '''Why will you win ''Big Brother''?'''
I'm gonna win ''Big Brother'' because of my ability to adapt to any situation. I'm a people person, and a lot of the game that people overlook is a social game. Once you're out, you're gone. If you get backdoored, you're gone. But if you're likable and people mess with you, it's all social. Not to mention, you gotta throw a little competition in there when you need it. Sometimes you can't rely solely on the social. So I think I'm just the most well rounded player in the house. I'm young, 21, still got that good energy to brighten everyone's day. And I think a lot of people are gonna mess with that. My social game is gonna take me far. And then when I can't go any farther on my social game, that's when mental and physical challenge wins come in. '''What's your strategy going into the game?'''
It's kind of hard, because it's always changing. The dynamic in the house is always flip-flopping. People are going in, going out, alliances change. People get backdoored

[[Big Brother Canada 9]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]], [[Re-Entry Competition|Re-Entry]], and [[Second Chance Challenge]] competition, similar to [[Perfect Shot]] and [[Ball Roll]]. ==Rules== This competition has two variations/parts: #Players must roll one ball at a time up a ramp and land a certain number on a flat platform in the fastest time. #Players must knock a certain number of balls off the platform in the fastest time The exact format varies in each appearance. On ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'', the houseguest had to land three balls in the holes on the platform. There were 3 heats of six; the top three from each heat advancing to the next round until there was a winner. This format would appear in [[Big Brother Canada 9]], replacing the slots with a flat landing atop a ramp. In ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'', the competition played out over two rounds: #The houseguests had to knock ten silver balls off of the flat platform by their respective balls up the ramp one at a time. The two fastest houseguests advanced to the next round. #The two remaining competitors are given ten balls. On Julie's command, the houseguests try to land as many of these on the platform, with only one shot with each ball. On ''[[Big Brother 25 (US)]]'', the format was slightly altered to incorporate a knockout element: #Instead of a flat platform, the end of the ramp had targets featuring the competing houseguests' [[BB Comics]]. Each player had three targets. #One at a time, the houseguest will call out which houseguest's target they would like to hit. #If the player hits they target they called out, the hit counts. #If they hit a target they did not call out, the hit does not count and the target is reset. #Once all of a player's targets are down, they are out. The last houseguest standing wins the competition. On ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'', it worked as follows: #The players rolled one balls of their respective colors at a time up the ramp, trying to land on the flat platform. #Once a player has five balls on the platform, they use the silver balls to knock off their colored balls off the platform. #The houseguest who completes this and buzzes in first wins the competition. On ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'', the format was slightly altered: #The houseguests rolled one gold orb at a time up the ramp, trying to land it on the platform. #If they land a ball or it fall off the platform, the houseguests must go under the bar to retrieve another orb. #If it rolls back down the ramp, the play can roll it again. #The first houseguest to land 5 orbs and buzz in wins the competition. ==History== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'', where [[Enzo Palumbo]] won his first ever Head of Household. The next appearance occurred on [[Big Brother Canada 9]] as the Re-entry competition following the fake [[Double Eviction|double eviction]]. }}The '''Diary Room''', also known as the '''Confession Room''' or '''Confessionario''', is a special confessional room inside the Big Brother house where the [[housemates]] ''(houseguests in US & Canada) ''can have a private conversation with [[Big Brother (person)|Big Brother]] about their daily thoughts and emotions regarding the different events that have taken place inside the house.

Every day, the houseguests are called in individually to the Diary Room to voice out all of their thoughts about the day. Still, the houseguests can also voluntarily enter the Diary Room if they feel the need to converse or seek advice from Big Brother without having the presence of fellow housemates. Further, the room is the only place inside the house where the houseguests can communicate with Big Brother, and one or more houseguests may be called in by Big Brother to give information on various tasks and announcements.

Importantly as stated in the [[Big Brother Rule Book|rule book]], conversations inside the Diary Room must never be shared with anyone unless told by Big Brother to do so.

== North American Series ==
[[file:Jordandr.jpg|250px|thumb|right|[[Jordan Lloyd]] having her confessional moment inside the Diary Room.]]

In the American and Canadian versions, the Diary Room ''(abbreviated DR)'' is where the [[Housemates|houseguests]] would talk to the camera, express their emotions and explain their strategy to the viewers. After every major house events such as challenges and nominations, the houseguests would be called into the DR to answer questions from the producers in order to help narrate the story and explain to the viewers what is going on in the house. 

In addition, the houseguests also go to the Diary Room when voting for eviction during the Live Eviction Nights where the host [[Julie Chen-Moonves]] (or [[Arisa Cox]] in the Canadian version) presides the voting. The Diary Room is a key feature of the Big Brother House and is featured regularly in every episode. 

In contrast to its international counterparts, the appearance of the Diary Room in the American series only has a small chair and a backdrop that changes occasionally whilst the rest of the house décor is being changed.

In the [[Big Brother (U.S.)|American version]] specifically, the houseguests are shown footage from their competitions and talks with other house guests to help them remember more vividly what happened and/or why they said what they said. They are also asked to speak loud and clear so they show more enthusiasm in the diary room. The houseguests are allowed to redo or repeat what they said if they want to make a better statement in the diary room.

===Uses of Diary Room in the US & Canadian versions===
*'''Answering Questions:''' Houseguests are called to the Diary Room at different times throughout the day. Once they enter the Diary Room, they may be asked certain questions to help narrate competitions or key events throughout parts of the episode. A reason for this is to explain to viewers what is going on at that given moment to make sure they are following the show correctly.

*'''Eviction Voting:''' On eviction nights, houseguests are called to the Diary Room to "cast their vote to evict". At this time, [[Julie Chen-Moonves]] or [[Arisa Cox]], depending on the country, communicates to the houseguests via the Diary Room.

*'''Houseguests' Goodbye Messages:''' At the end of eviction interviews, the evicted houseguest is played messages from their fellow houseguests in order to say goodbye to them. These messages are recorded in the Diary Room on the day of the eviction.

It was then reintroduced with greater power in ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' - if the winner chooses to use it, ''they'' will name the replacement nominee rather than the Head of Household. It was awarded to [[Matt Hoffman]] as a gift from [[Pandora's Box]] in Week 5. A week later, when he was up for eviction due to being nominated by [[Brendon Villegas]], he used it on himself and nominated [[Kathy Hillis]] as the replacement. Kathy was then evicted in a 5-0 vote against [[Lane Elenburg]]. The Veto returned in ''[[Big Brother 28 (US)]]'' as one of the powers to be granted from the BB Time Capsule. [[Rick Devens]] entered the Time Capsule in Week 3 and chose the space that held the Diamond Veto. He was able to use it for the following six veto ceremonies. ''[[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 6]]'' }}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a special power given to a houseguest. It allows the holder to remove up to two nominees from the Nomination Block and replace them with up to two other houseguests other than the [[Head of Household]] (except in [[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 6]]) and the [[Power of Veto|Veto]] holder. It is similar to the [[Diamond Power of Veto]], except the holder can remove both nominees from the Block, as opposed to just one. The Coup d'Etat first appeared as a prize in ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]'', but it was ultimately not used, due to a violation of rules. The power appeared once again in ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)]]'', and the holder was chosen by America. The Coup d'Etat has also appeared in ''[[Big Brother Canada 3]]'', but its name was not referenced. A weaker power that still overtakes an existing HOH's reign and changes their nominations has been seen as a variation of the [[Invisible HOH]] twist, keeping the usurper anonymous and allowing the nominees a chance at the Veto. =={{PAGENAME}} Holders== ==='''Mike Malin'''=== During Week 6 of Big Brother: All-Stars, the houseguests were told by [[Julie Chen-Moonves]] that they would be competing for a "mystery power". Throughout the following week, the houseguests were given various clues to a common Big Brother phrase. [[Mike Malin]] was the first houseguest to correctly guess the phrase, "You reap what you sow". Mike was given three weeks to use the power before it would expire. However, he chose not to use the power in the first two weeks and became the HOH in the third week, so he never used it. It was later revealed that he had broken the rules by telling [[Will Kirby]] that he won the power in between the first two weeks, so production ended up taking it away from him, meaning he was ineligible to use it in the second or third weeks, even if he hadn't been HOH. This information never made air and was never acknowledged by production.https://www.realityblurred.com/realitytv/2006/08/big-brother-7-mike_boogie_coup_detat/ ==='''Jeff Schroeder'''=== Shortly after [[Casey Turner]]'s eviction in ''Big Brother 11'', it was announced to the house that America would be selecting one houseguest to receive a special power. [[Jeff Schroeder]] was chosen by America to receive the Coup d'Etat. He was given two weeks to use the power before it would expire. During the first week, Jeff chose not to use the Coup d'Etat. The following week, Jeff used the power to overthrow [[Chima Simone]]'s nominations ([[Russell Kairouz]] & [[Lydia Tavera]]). {{twists |image = [[File:Den of Temptation Logo.PNG|225px]] | description= One houseguest will be given a temptation in order to change up the game. | seasonsappeared= ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'' |countriesappeared={{United States}}}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the main twist of ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. For the first three weeks, America will vote for one houseguest to enter the {{PAGENAME}} in order to face a dilemma that could impact their game. ==Press Release== ''Retrieved from CBS.com''
Starting on Sunday, July 2 at 8/7c, the Houseguests will discover the Den of Temptation, a room that holds yet another enticement that, if accepted, will potentially unleash a game-breaking consequence upon the entire house. Even better, America will get to vote for the Houseguests they want to send into the Den of Temptation, which lets fans influence the game in spectacular ''Big Brother'' fashion. "Temptation has always been a part of ''Big Brother'' but this summer we are testing the Houseguests like never before," said Rich Meehan, Executive Producer, ''Big Brother''. "There are so many different paths the game could take this season depending on what the Houseguests choose to do. With so many unknowns, we are excited to see how it all plays out." ==Description== America will vote on which Houseguest they would like to send into the “Den of Temptation” to be enticed by a potentially game-changing offer. But it’s always a game of risk vs. reward, as every temptation will unleash a consequence on the house. The concept of taking a prize and getting a punishment onto the house is similar to [[Pandora's Box]], and the voting requirements that once you are voted into the Den once you cannot be voted in another time is identical to the [[America's Care Package]] voting requirements. ==List of Temptations== |-|Week 1=
'''"The Pendant of Protection"'''
"The winning Houseguest will be tempted with the Pendant of Protection. If they accept they will be protected from being nominated or evicted for the next three evictions, but remember-every temptation comes with a consequence!" This temptation was won by [[Paul Abrahamian]]. He ended up getting nominated by [[Cody Nickson]] during Week 1, but the Pendant saved him from going on the block, leading Cody to have to nominate [[Christmas Abbott]] instead of Paul. The curse was randomly given to [[Ramses Soto]], where he had to nominate himself as a special third nominee at one of the next three nomination ceremonies. |-|Week 2=
'''"Ring of Replacement"'''
"The winning houseguest will be tempted with the Ring of Replacement, which will give them the power to play in any Veto Competition they want this summer! If they’re not one of the six houseguests playing, they can swap places with one of the three players chosen by random draw. The Ring of Replacement can only be used once, but remember, every temptation comes with a consequence." This temptation was won by [[Christmas Abbott]]. She used it during Week 6 to take Cody's place in the Veto competition. However, due to her broken foot and the [[OTEV|type of competition that was being played]], she was not allowed to play, essentially meaning the temptation was wasted. Christmas selected to give the curse to Cody, [[Jessica Graf]], and [[Jason Dent]], where they had to dress up as "Ve-toads" (frog costumes) for the week and can only move around by hopping, and can only stand/sit on lily pads placed in every room. |-|Week 3=

[[Tommy Bracco]] |Days = 79 |OtherPrizes = |TwitterUserName = |InstagramUserName = christie.murph |}}'''Christie Lynn Murphy ''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''. Christie was a major force in the game, known for her pre-existing relationship with [[Tommy Bracco]], emotional gameplay, faith-driven “manifestation” strategy, and strong strategic influence. He also appeared on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]''. In ''Big Brother 12'', Enzo became well-known for his use of his moniker "the meow-meow" and was the founding member of [[The Brigade]]. Enzo played a social, under-the-radar strategic game early on, focusing on long-term positioning rather than being an immediate target. While he rarely won competitions in the early and middle stages, he maintained strong loyalty within his alliance and consistently avoided becoming a primary eviction threat as the Brigade systematically controlled votes. As the he reached the endgame, Enzo continued relying on alliance strength and timing, ensuring that more visible threats were removed ahead of him, and his allegiance to the Brigade helped him make it to the final three. Enzo ultimately placed 3rd after [[Hayden Moss]] cast the sole vote to evict him, thus making him the seventh and final member of the [[jury]]. In ''Big Brother 22'', Enzo found himself in a comfortable position as an affiliate of [[The Committee]] alliance. He was particularly close with Committee members [[Cody Calafiore]] and [[Memphis Garrett]], having a final 3 deal with them called the Wise Guys, and a final 2 alliance with Cody called [[The Root]]. He proved to be better in competitions this time around, winning 2 HoH's, 1 PoV, and 1 Safety competition. He overall made very safe moves, nominating obvious target Kaysar, and also keeping [[Nicole Franzel]] over [[David Alexander]] in final 8. He made it to the final three without being nominated. After Cody won the final HoH, he brought Enzo to the final two. He had a dislike towards [[Kaysar Ridha]] and successfully got him evicted in Week 4, and clashed with [[Janelle Pierzina]] over their conflicting personalities, but developed friendships with [[Bayleigh Dayton]], Nicole F, [[Christmas Abbott]], [[Daniele Briones]], [[Da'Vonne Rogers]], including stronger ones with Cody, [[Tyler Crispen]] and [[Memphis Garrett]]. However, Enzo's subtle game wasn't respected for Cody's dominant and aggressive game, and he gave poor answers to the jury's questions. This caused him to finish second to Cody in a unanimous 9-0 vote, making Enzo the second ever houseguest to receive 0 jury votes, after Memphis. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | BB12= ''Retrieved from CBS.com''

{{Houseguest |Image=BB7=[[File:BB7 George Large.webp|250px]]|-|BB1=[[File:George.png|250px]] |name=George Allen Boswell |nickname=Chicken George |birthdate = {{Birth date and age|1958|09|29|mf=yes}} |hometown = Rockford, Illinois |occupation = Youth Counselor |ProfileInputAnyText = Yes |Season2=7 (US) |Place2=5th |Votes2=3 |Alliances2= |Loyalties2= |HOHs2=1 (Week 7) |Nominations2=4 (Week 3, Day 49, Week 8 & Day 60) |Vetos2= 1 (Week 3) |Days2=60 |OtherPrizes2= |Currently=Jury Member |Currently2=Jury Member |Season=1 (US) |Place=5th |Votes=51% of America |Alliances= |Loyalties= |Nominations=2 (Weeks 8 & 11) |NominationsReceived(BB1) =9 |Days=79 |OtherPrizes= |Currently1=Banished |FacebookUserName = george.boswell.39 }} '''George Allen Boswell''' (better known by his nickname '''Chicken George''') was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]''. On ''Big Brother 1'', George became a fan favorite due to his goofy personality, kind nature, and dedication to caring for the house's chickens, earning him the nickname "Chicken George." He appeared to be in a good position until controversy arose when his family campaigned for other popular houseguests to be banished in an effort to help him stay in the game. After the houseguests learned of the situation through outside information, George considered [[Walking|walking]] and encouraged others to leave with him, but nobody followed through. The controversy damaged his standing in the house, and George was ultimately banished on Day 79, finishing in 5th place. In the early days of ''Big Brother 7'', George was often ridiculed and dismissed as a minor resident of the house. He was nominated as the target by [[Head of Household]] [[James Rhine]] in Week 3, but he saved himself by winning the [[Power of Veto]]. As time passed, however, he began gaining recognition as a potential threat due to his under-the-radar personality. He was ultimately evicted during the second half of the fast forward week by a 2-0 vote after the intended target, [[Erika Landin]], won the Power of Veto. He finished in 5th place and became the fifth [[jury]] member. He voted for [[Mike Malin]] to win. ==Biography== ===''Big Brother 1 (US)''=== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''George Allen Boswell Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from webcenter.bigbrother2000.aol.com''
Born in Rockford, Illinois on September 29, 1958, George is the eldest male of the Big Brother House Guests. He runs his own roofing company, Raincoat Roofing. He has been married for 22 years to the mother of his three children, ages 7 to 17. George spends much of his leisure time volunteering for Rockford's Jefferson High School Fans Association. He likes to relax at two of his town's Italian eateries - Dom's Pizzeria and Linos. But when the mood hits for a burger, George opts instead for one of the local Beef-A-Roo restaurants. For a laugh, George likes the offbeat style of John Belushi and Dan Akroyd, ranking "The Blues Brothers" as his all-time favorite movie. {{Houseguest |Image=[[File:Eddie1.jpg|250px]] |name={{PAGENAME}} |birthdate = {{Birth date and age|1979|02|24|mf=yes}} |hometown = Commack, New York |occupation = Student |ProfileInputAnyText = Yes |nickname= |Season=1 (US) |Place=1st |Votestowin=59% of America |Alliances= |Loyalties= |Nominations=4 (Weeks 8, 10, 11, & 12) |NominationsReceived(BB1) =17 |Days=88 |OtherPrizes= |Currently=Winner |SocialMediaInputAnyText= Yes |TwitterUserName =TheEddieMcGee |YoutubeUserName =Don'tTurnAround |Currently1 = Winner |FacebookUserName = eddie.mcgee.58 |InstagramUserName = eddieofny}} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the [[Winners (US)|winner]] of ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]''. Eddie was known in the game for being blunt and outspoken and being one of the only houseguests who would openly talk about his desire to win the money. He also played a strong social game, earning respect from both his fellow houseguests and the viewing public through his positive attitude, resilience, and ability to build relationships across the house. Despite being marked for banishment several times throughout the season, he consistently survived public votes and avoided becoming a major target among his peers. As larger controversies and conflicts unfolded around other houseguests, Eddie maintained his likable image and steady position in the game. Eddie became the first winner in ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother U.S.]]'' history after defeating [[Curtis Kin]] and [[Josh Souza]], receiving 59% of [[America's Winner|America's Vote]] and winning the $500,000 grand prize. His victory was largely attributed to his likability, unapologetically blunt personality, and inspiring story of overcoming the loss of his left leg to cancer during childhood, which made him an important source of representation for amputees on a national scale. Despite ''Big Brother 1'' having a completely different format from the rest of the series, Eddie is arguably the first houseguest in ''Big Brother U.S.'' history to display any sort of active strategic savviness in regards to how he nominated and who he built close relationships with to get him further in the game. ==='''Biography'''=== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from webcenter.bigbrother2000.aol.com''
Born in Manhasset, New York on February 24, 1979, Eddie is, at age 21, the youngest of the Big Brother House Guests. A student at the University of Texas, Eddie is on a wheelchair basketball scholarship and once coached a kid's basketball team. A cancer survivor, Eddie's proudest accomplishment is teaching children that being disabled doesn't mean that you can't live a rewarding life. Eddie is a good guy to have around the house. His favorite pursuits include landscaping and home-improvement projects. He's also an avid basketball fan, (so maybe he'll find time for a little one-on-one with housemates William and Josh). Maybe there's a hint of the romantic in Eddie, since he counts the Candelight Diner in Commack, New York among his favorite restaurants. Still, he's equally happy with burgers and fries from the local White Castle, and is always up for a Big Sloppy from Commack's Miami Subs. As for books and movies, Eddie's tastes can best be described as eclectic. The best films hes ever seen range from the SCTV-inspired silliness of "Strange Brew", to the dramatic magnetism of "The Shawshank Redemption" (also a favorite of housemate Josh's), to the dark intensity of "American History X". Similarly, Eddie's interest in such literary classics as Jules Verne's "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea", Robert Louis Stevenson's "Treasure Island", and William Shakespeare's "Hamlet", is offset by his appreciation for a well-told horror story like Stephen King's "It". He would later return in ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]''. On ''Big Brother 2 (US)'', Will was known for his [[Chilltown|friendship]] with fellow housemate [[Mike Malin|Mike "Boogie" Malin]] and his [[Showmance|showmance]] with [[Shannon Dragoo]]. Even though he drew the ire of many of his fellow houseguests and was nominated four times through the season, Will was able to stay in the game with the help of his charismatic personality, clever social maneuvers, and over the top strategies, making the target on his back so big that he was able to hide in plain sight. While he failed to win the final Head of Household, he was taken to the final 2 by [[Nicole Nilson Schaffrich]]. At the end of the jury questionnaire, Will rubbed many of the [[Jury|jurors]] the wrong way with his final jury speech. Despite this, most of the jury respected Will's game, and he won the $500,000 grand prize by a 5-2 [[Jury|jury]] vote over Nicole. On ''Big Brother 7 (US)'', Will entered the house with a huge target on his back due to being the only winner in the game. However, with the help of fellow ''Big Brother 2'' housemate and "Chilltown" member Mike "Boogie", Will was able to manipulate other houseguests (most notably his new showmance parter [[Janelle Pierzina]]) and managed to get rid of big names like [[Howie Gordon]], [[James Rhine]], and [[Danielle Reyes]] just to name a few. Will's ultimate demise was during the final 4 when [[Erika Landin]] and Janelle caught onto Chilltown's schemes. Since Mike "Boogie" was the HOH of that week and could not be evicted, Janelle, the Power of Veto holder of that week, casted the sole vote to evict Will from the house, making him the 6th member of the jury. ==History== ===Creation=== The Four Horsemen was created on the first day of ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]'' by [[Jase Wirey]] and [[Scott Long]]. ===Early Dominance=== After Jase won the first [[Head of Household]] competition, the alliance seemed to be in a powerful position. However, Jase and Scott’s behavior would make the, very big targets for the opposing [[Pinky Swear Alliance]]. Despite this, the alliance was able to unanimously evict [[Mike Lubinski]], who was openly going after the alliance. The following week, affiliate [[Marvin Latimer]] won Head of Household and the alliance aided in taking out [[Lori Valenti]]. ===Downfall=== During the first few weeks of the game, Jase and [[Holly King]] had become a [[showmance]], however, this would cause friction in the alliance as the rest of the alliance didn’t trust Holly. Along with this, conflict between Jase and Scott started to arise because of Holly due to their mutual liking of her. After Drew won Head of Household in week three, he put Holly on the block as the target with the goal of creating peace in the alliance. However, what the alliance didn’t account for was that Holly was a loyal and vital number for the alliance. Despite Jase’s pushes to keep Holly, she was evicted in a 7-1 vote later that week. Also this week, both Jase and Scott participated in a heated public argument with [[Diane Henry]]. After Diane won Head of Household in week four, Diane put Jase and Scott on the block and ultimately Scott was evicted that week. After [[Nakomis Dedmon]] won Head of Household, the entire house excluding Jase and [[Michael Ellis]] created a plan to [[backdoor]] Jase. After Drew won the [[Power of Veto]], he sealed Jase’s fate as he used the veto allowing Nakomis to put Jase up and evict him in a 6-1 vote. ===Revival=== Despite Drew’s defection and their low numbers, Drew and Michael were able to reconnect and work together in the game. ===Victory=== Using their relationships and the breakup of the majority alliance, Drew and Michael were able to make it to the final two together where Drew won in a 4-3 vote. ==Trivia== *The Four Horsemen had no members in the jury. {{BB5 Alliances}} [[Category:Alliances]] [[Category:The Four Horsemen]] [[Category:Big Brother 5 (US) Alliances]] [[Category:Big Brother 5 (US)]]

''[[Big Brother 24 (US)]]'' }}'''Dynamic Duos''' was a twist on ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]''. It was reintroducted on ''[[Big Brother 24 (US)]]'' under the name of '''Festie-Besties'''. On ''Big Brother 13 (US)'', in addition to the eight original houseguests, three pairs of returning players were introduced into the house as Dynamic Duos: [[Jordan Lloyd]] and [[Jeff Schroeder]], [[Rachel Reilly]] and [[Brendon Villegas]], and [[Dick Donato]] and [[Daniele Briones]] went into the house to compete for the grand prize. The eight new houseguests were allowed to get to know one another and form their own duos. When a houseguest won the [[HOH|Head of Household]] competition, their partner also received immunity from eviction. The HOH nominated a pair for eviction, rather than two individual houseguests. Houseguests could also receive a [[Golden Key]]; this was given to the remaining member of the nominated pair that survived an eviction vote or lost a partner due to an expulsion or voluntary exit. A Golden Key guaranteed this houseguest a spot in the top ten and immunity from all challenges and eviction. However, the recipients of a Golden Key were still required to vote to evict during the live [[eviction]] shows. A similar twist was introduced in ''Big Brother 24 (US)'' at the end of Week 2 under the name, Festie-Besties. The remaining houseguests paired up immediately after they lost during the Week 3 HOH competition. The mechanics remained much the same as in Season 13 with one main exception: instead of receiving a golden key, the surviving houseguest after the eviction had the power to join one of the remaining pairs of "Festie-Besties" to form a trio and were not given immunity until [[The Jury|jury]] while the twist was active. If a Festie-Bestie wins POV, their partner also wins the veto. ==The Dynamic Duos== {{BBUS13 Duos}} ==Festie Besties== {{US 24 Besties}} [[Category:Twists]] [[Category:Duos]] [[Category:Big Brother 13 (US)]] [[Category:Big Brother 24 (US)]]

{{Philippines}}}}'''Double Evictions''' are a special event on Big Brother where two houseguests are evicted in the same week. This often involves speeding up the game by having the [[Head of Household]] competition, [[Nominations|nomination]] ceremony, [[Power of Veto|veto]] competition, veto ceremony, and [[eviction]] all held within the span of 2-3 days or happening in a single night. The first Double Eviction occurred during ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)]]''. ==Types of Double Eviction== ===Two Evictions in One Week=== *Often, the HouseGuests will compete for HOH following the previous eviction and then the new HOH will immediately nominate two people for eviction during the live show. The next day, they will compete in the POV and have the next eviction within the next two or three days. This was first seen in Big Brother 5. ===Two Evictions in One Day=== *Fast Forward evictions are more fast paced. In the [[Big Brother Canada (franchise)|North]] [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|American]] format, the HouseGuests are informed of the Fast Forward immediately before or after an eviction. Someone is crowned the new HOH, and he or she only has the ad break to name his or her nominees. The POV competition is usually short due to being performed live. The Veto ceremony is also held live, and then another eviction occurs all within one hour. In ''Big Brother US'', this is the most typical variation. This eviction first occurred in [[Big Brother 7 (US)|''Big Brother 7 (US)'']]. This format is used and enhanced for a [[Triple Eviction]] (first seen on [[Big Brother Canada 3|''Big Brother Canada 3'']]), where two people leave during the second eviction of the night. *In the International Format, Double Evictions are done in one night. The double eviction typically determines their evictees through who among the nominees received the two lowest save votes or in some seasons the top two highest evict votes. The announcement may vary, both nominees can be announced as evicted at the same time but in most seasons, the announcement is usually done by evicting the nominee with the lowest vote first and then interrupted only by a commercial gap before evictng the second nominee with the second lowest viewer votes. ===Eviction by Pairs=== *In [[Big Brother 9 (US)|''Big Brother 9 (US)'']], there were 16 HouseGuests who competed in pairs. For the first two weeks, they were evicted in said pairs. The twist returned in the first week of [[Big Brother Brazil 23|''Big Brother Brazil 23'']]. ===Instant Eviction=== *On ''Big Brother Canada'', there are instant evictions. This is a variation of the "two evictions in one week" but houseguests are given a few minutes warning before the upcoming eviction. }}An '''ejection '''(or '''expulsion''')''' '''is the removal of a Big Brother houseguest by means of production via the Diary Room, bypassing the typical eviction process. A houseguest is ejected when they have repeatedly broken critical rules or have jeopardized the safety of the other houseguests due to their behavior. A houseguest is usually warned for repeated unacceptable behaviors before being expelled.

In the U.S., houseguests who are expelled during the jury stage are not allowed on the jury, and their votes are determined by a poll. Expelled houseguests are ineligible to win the [[Fan Favorite Award]] and are banned from attending the finale.

In the Philippines, the term '''Forced Eviction''' is used. The housemates typically receive a "forced eviction" if they violated major [[Big Brother Rule Book|house rules]] or received violation strikes three times.

Global.head:
[[File:Global.png|thumb]]
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is one of the major broadcast television networks in Canada, owned by Corus Entertainment. From 2015 to 2024, it was the home of ''[[Big Brother Canada (franchise)|Big Brother Canada]]'', the country's English-language version of Big Brother. Global has also aired ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother US]]'' from its inception in 2000 up until 2026.

Starting in 2027, both ''[[Big Brother Canada (franchise)|Big Brother Canada]]'' and ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother US]]'' began airing on rival network [[wikipedia:CTV Television Network|CTV]].

In addition to BBUS, Global is the Canadian home of several other [[CBS]] programming brands, including Survivor, NCIS and The Late Show.
==Association with Big Brother==
===Big Brother U.S.===
Global aired every season of BBUS from 2000 to 2026, except [[Big Brother: Over The Top]], which was exclusive to CBS's video on demand platform CBS All Access. In 2026, it was announced that [[Big Brother 28 (US)]] would be the final season carried by Global.
===Big Brother Canada===
Big Brother Canada (BBCAN), the first English-language adaptation of the Big Brother format in Canada, began on Global's sister network [[Slice]] in 2013.

After the first two seasons of the show proved successful, it was announced in 2014 that BBCAN had been renewed for its [[Big Brother Canada 3|third season]], and would move to Global, where it has remained since.

On June 1st, 2015, Global renewed BBCAN for its [[Big Brother Canada 4|fourth season]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624042232/http://www.shawmedia.ca/Media/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?pressReleaseId=6442462338|title=Global delivers super-charged slate of new series and returning primetime hits this fall|publisher=Shaw Media (archived)|date=24 June 2015|accessdate=4 March 2018}}</ref>. During this season, Global also premiered select episodes of the spin-off [[Big Brother Canada Sideshow|Big Brother Canada Side Show]], which usually aired on Slice. On June 7, 2016, Global renewed BBCAN for its [[Big Brother Canada 5|fifth season]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://canada.bigbrothernetwork.com/big-brother-canada-5-season-ordered-for-2017/|title=Big Brother Canada 5 Season Ordered For 2017|publisher=Big Brother Network|date=7 June 2016|accessdate=4 March 2018}}</ref>.

On June 5th, 2017, just a few weeks after season five concluded, Global announced that it would be putting BBCAN on 'hiatus'. A media statement from the network insisted: "Global remains the broadcaster for Big Brother." Following a backlash from fans and viewers, Global announced on July 21st, 2017 that it had reversed its decision, and the show was no longer on hiatus. BBCAN returned for its [[Big Brother Canada 6|sixth season]] on March 7th, 2018. On June 5, 2024, soon after the conclusion of the [[Big Brother Canada 12|twelfth season]], the show was once again put on hiatus.<ref>https://brioux.tv/blog/2024/06/05/big-brother-canada-fails-to-make-the-2024-25-cut-at-global/</ref> A few weeks later, on June 27, BBCAN and Global announced that the series would not return for a thirteenth season.<ref>https://twitter.com/BigBrotherCA/status/1806410238972641428/</ref>

It was played during the opening and closing credits of each episode. ===The House=== The studio was located in Soto del Real, Madrid. 29 cameras and 60 microphones recorded the events in the house. The house was 160 square meters with two bedrooms, a kitchen, a dining room, living room, storage room, a bathroom and a sound-proofed diary room. The interior design was dominated by pastel colors to create a homely atmosphere. Archetypical paintings from Spain decorated the walls such as "''Las mil y una noches"'' by Henri Matisse. Outside the house they could enjoy a garden with a heated swimming pool and an orchard with an extension of 280 meters. Two control rooms have also been set up. The digital audio room and parallel to this, in the production control, 38 television monitors control everything that happened inside the house. There were two editing rooms and four mini-controls in parallel. The traveling tracks that ran along the house, which were filmed with five cameras, were approximately 200 meters long. Sixteen filmmakers worked to ensure that everything runs smoothly. Some 40,000 meters of cable have been used to cover the entire infrastructure of the house. ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'' |countriesappeared = {{United States}} }}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a variation of the [[Power of Veto]] where two different houseguests win the Power of Veto in the same week. The [[Secret Power of Veto]] originated as an anonymous variation of this twist. ==History== ===Big Brother 14 (US)=== Originally known as the Golden Ball of Veto, it was introduced in Week 7 of ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'' after [[Frank Eudy]] opened Pandora's Box. Including the typical Power of Veto won by competition, a Golden Ball of Veto could be received by winning it in a claw game. The Golden Ball of Veto was won by [[Ian Terry]], who was unable to play in that week's Veto competition as he already had a Veto. He did not use it during that week's Veto Ceremony. [[Jenn Arroyo]] then won the actual Veto competition and used it on [[Dan Gheesling]]. ===Big Brother: Over The Top=== The name was changed to Double Power of Veto and was seen as a choice for [[America's Care Package]] during Week 3 of ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]''. At the [[Power of Veto]] competition, two Vetoes would be won, rather than the one. It was selected by [[Scott Dennis]], and the two Veto winners were [[Alex Willett]] and [[Justin Duncan]]. Alex did not use hers, while Justin chose to use his on [[Kryssie Ridolfi]]. ===Big Brother 19 (US)=== It was an option during the [[Tree of Temptation]] twist during ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'' but no one ended up randomly selecting it power and it went unused. ===Celebrity Big Brother 2 (US)=== It returned again in the first eviction cycle of ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2 (US)]]''. After [[Ricky Williams]] won the first POV competition and decided not to use it, it was revealed that [[Anthony Scaramucci]] was a Fake HouseGuest, and was giving the remaining HouseGuests a second chance at the POV. Since Ricky already won one, he was safe and could not play in the second competition, dubbed Mooch's Veto, which was then won by [[Kato Kaelin]], who took [[Tom Green]] off the block. ===Big Brother 23 (US)=== Returning once again in ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'', the Double Power of Veto was part of the "High Roller's Room" twist. If a houseguest was willing, they could bet 50 BB Bucks on one of the six Veto players. If one of those six won the PoV competition, the person who bet on them would receive a second Veto, even if they played in the competition and originally lost. If no player had anyone bet on them, there would not be a second Veto unleashed if they won the competition. HOH [[Kyland Young]] ended up playing and losing the competition, but since he bet on [[Alyssa Lopez]], who ended up winning, he earned himself the second Veto. Kyland then chose to remove his nominee, [[Claire Rehfuss]], from the block, and replaced her with [[Britini D'Angelo]]. Alyssa then had the final say and could save either Britini or Kyland's other nominee, [[Derek Frazier]], but she chose to respect Kyland's wishes and leave his new nominations in place. ===Big Brother 25 (US)=== In ''[[Big Brother 25 (US)]]'', the twist returned and was called the "BB Power of Multiplicity", as part of "BB Comic-Week". Two separate Veto competitions were held, and everyone was allowed to participate in the first one. The winner of the first Veto would then sit out of the second, while everyone else competed again. [[Jag Bains]], whose HOH reign was anonymous due to the "[[Invisible HOH|BB Power of Invisibility]]", ended up winning the first Veto competition, while [[Blue Kim]], one of his nominees, won the second. [[Rockstar Lantry]] |TwitterUserName = fessyfitness |InstagramUserName = fessyfitness |HackerComp=0 | thechallenge = {{otherfandom|thechallenge|Faysal_Shafaat}} }} '''Faysal Shawn "Fessy" Shafaat'''{{cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Big_Brother_20_houseguests_(U.S.)|title=List of Big Brother 20 houseguests (U.S.)|publisher=Wikipedia|accessdate=14 July 2018}} was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''. Known for his [[showmance]] with [[Haleigh Broucher]] and being strategically clueless, Faysal was a member of the crumbling [[FOUTTE]] alliance, was blindsided and left out of nearly every vote, and never knew what was going on. Throughout the season, he was attracted to Haleigh, and while Haleigh initially rejected his advances she eventually accepted and the two became a couple. He was often manipulated by his close ally [[JC Mounduix]]. After becoming the HoH in week 8, he was manipulated by JC into targeting his ally [[Scottie Salton]]. Scottie was evicted under his HoH. However, this was fatal as the following week both he and Haleigh were betrayed and nominated, and he was evicted in a 4-1 vote. He came in 9th place and became the third member of the jury.
