Frenchie started his game on a high note, becoming captain of the [[Jokers]] team, drafting his group, and winning HoH. Frenchie spent the first couple of days shifting through his nomination options, all while making promises to various houseguests to keep them safe. He settled on targeting a “meathead” boot, but the plan shifted multiple times after [[Christian Birkenberger]] won the Wildcard competition and [[Derek Xiao]] won the Power of Veto. Frenchie eventually settled on going after [[Travis Long]], who he promised to keep safe in the very first minutes of the game. His disastrous HOH reign damaged his credibility and led to distrust from multiple sides of the house. After forming and then exposing [[The Slaughterhouse]] alliance, he became the primary target under [[Kyland Young|Kyland Young’s]] HOH, where he was nominated alongside [[Britini D'Angelo]]. Unable to win safety or regain trust through last-minute deals, Frenchie was evicted in a 11–1 vote, finishing 15th place. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''Brandon "Frenchie" French Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | Brandon “Frenchie” French
Age: 34
Hometown: Camden, Tennessee
Current City: Clarksville, Tennessee
Occupation: Farmer Three words that describe you: Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious, compassionate, and exuberant. Favorite activities: “Yes” days with the kids, fishing, playing with the baby animals, and grilling out. Who are your favorite Houseguest duos?
Definitely Britney Haynes and Rachel’s hair extensions! What are you most excited about living inside the Big Brother house?
Living out my dream of being here. I learned life is way too short with the passing of my son so just being able to live out this dream. I’m here to WIN, not to get famous! What do you think will be the most difficult part about living inside the Big Brother house?
For me it’s being away from my kids and the farm. What is your favorite past moment on Big Brother?
Dan’s funeral on my daughter’s birthday was legendary! What is your strategy for winning the game?
Building relationships with everyone, not just your alliance. Being a farmer, no two days are the same. You never know what to expect. I always have to evolve and change gameplans on a daily basis and I have got really good at it. Set strategies are overrated and crumble, so my lifestyle fits perfect with the Big Brother house. My lifes motto is…
“You will always go through rocky times, but together we can crush those rocks into fine sand and create our own paradise!” What would you take into the house and why?
A picture of my son who passed away because it motivates me like no other. A fishing pole because it would be fun catching other Houseguests from the HOH balcony lol, a voice recorder because everyone in that house lies and then I’d have proof of what was said. Fun facts about myself:
-At 13 I won the NFL national punt pass and kick competition.
-We have a two-time grand national champion show bull that lives better than most humans.
-I’m a proud member of the NAACP.
-I’m prior military.

Vibrant and often outrageous with her antics, Felicia connected early with second-oldest houseguest [[Cirie Fields]] and together, they formed the [[Bye Bye Bitches]] alliance. Her gameplay took a serious turn when she won the Week 3 [[Head of Household|HOH]] competition and [[Backdoor|backdoored]] a belligerent player in [[Hisam Goueli]], despite his loyalty to her. In spite of her strong start, Felicia's alignment with Cirie caused her to be used as a [[pawn]] and was nearly evicted in Week 6 prior to the house flipping against [[Izzy Gleicher]], and without any influence or physical prowess, Felicia became an outsider to the soon-dominant [[The Mafia (BB25)|Mafia]] alliance. Felicia is the first woman over 60 to compete on ''Big Brother''.
'''How does it feel to be on the 25th season of ''Big Brother''?'''
Well, I'm excited, I'm actually a little nervous because I thought, "It's the 25th season, they're going to do some crazy stuff, something we haven't seen before." I'm sure there's going to be all kinds of surprises, they say, "Expect the unexpected. "Well, for the 25th season, I'm assuming there's going to be a whole lot of that. So I'm excited to be a part of it, but a little nervous about what all of that unexpected could possibly be. '''What twists do you think are happening in ''Big Brother 25''?'''
I can't even imagine what they're going to do. I believe they're going to bring in some old stuff, some new stuff, a combination is tough. And I've racked my brain thinking, "What are they going to do?" It's the 25th season, so I know it's gonna be crazy. And I'm just ready for whatever they throw at us. I think it's going to be exciting, and I can't wait to be a part of it. '''Why did you decide you wanted to play ''Big Brother''?'''
I think part of the reason why I wanted to be in the ''Big Brother'' house is to prove to myself. I've always looked at myself as a people person, as a social person, as a relationship person. And this is going to let me know if how I've always seen myself is how other people see me. I believe I know how to strategize and play all the little different things you need to do to get to the end. So I'm going to see if how I see myself, other people see me, and will it carry me to the end? I know my age and experience is going to be an advantage for me. I'm hoping it's not looked at as a disadvantage to the 20- and 30-somethings in the house. But I genuinely connect with younger people very easily. '''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' Outgoing, fun — which is kind of a boring word, and unpredictable.
'''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' Dude, it’s so fun to be on ''Big Brother''! I’m so excited. I’ve watched this show since I was eight years old, and my mom learned how to speak English watching the show. So it’s actually just bizarre. I feel like I’m living in a fever dream.
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I’ve been watching ''Big Brother'' since I’ve been eight. And I’m kind of like a hybrid [fan]. I’m a casual fan, because I watch all the episodes. But I do like to dabble in the live feeds. So don’t kill me if I’m not the biggest fan watching the live feeds! But I like to say I’m a hybrid fan. I’m gonna classify a new one.
'''What’s your biggest strength?''' I would say my biggest strength is connecting with people. I mean, my job, I sit there with patients, and we just connect. And I feel like at the end of it, I just made a new friend. So I’m going in there, hoping that I could just make 15 new friends. And I feel like that’s going to help me pull on the heartstrings a little bit.
'''What’s your strategy going into the house?''' I don’t love the question of what your strategy is going to be. Because I feel like every season you have to know who’s going to be there. I have no idea who’s going to be there, and it has to adapt. So I would say my strategy going in there is just going to be fluid. Do I have to win competitions, or is it going to be a big guy winning everything? Do I have to be more of a social guy, because everyone doesn’t like me? So I think I’m gonna do a little bit of both. I don’t feel like you should classify yourself into one avenue of that. So I’m gonna read the room, and that’s what I’m gonna try to do best.
'''What are you going to bring to ''Big Brother'' that we’ve never seen before?''' What would I bring to the show that people have never seen before is my awesome hair routine. I don’t think you guys are ready for this! I’m gonna be upside down, hanging off the bed. And I’m gonna classify a new style. We’re gonna call it the “Drewth,” and everyone’s gonna be rocking after the show. So just get ready for it. It’s gonna be the new TikTok haircut.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' The biggest misconception people have about me when they first meet me is, “This guy’s just a beach bum who doesn’t have a lot of brains.” But I actually graduated college with summa cum laude. I mean, I don’t really know what that means, but I know it means I’m smart. So people aren’t ready for all the brain behind this hair!

Jorge Rial returned to front the show after doing so during the 3 successful seasons that aired in 2007. ==Twists== The following twists happened during this series of ''Gran Hermano''. *'''Series Duration''': running for a total of 141 days, it became the longest series produced within the Americas at the time. It was later surpassed by its successor series, '''''[[Gran Hermano Argentina 7|Gran Hermano 7]]'''''. *'''Repechage''': On Day 50, [[Juan Migliavacca|Juan]] left the House, since he wanted to go back to his studies and during his stay, he repeatedly announced his intentions of leaving. After [[Cristian Urrizaga|Cristian U.]] walked out of the House on Day 58, a repechage process began on Day 62, and the two housemates that decided to leave voluntarily were also asked to be part of this process. At the end of Day 62's live nominations show, only Juan decided to stay out of the repechage and evicted housemates [[Rocío Gancedo|Rocío]], [[Ariana Fiorentino|Ariana]], [[Leandro Pigó|Leandro]], [[Natalí Kessler|Natalí]], [[Christian Yáñez|Christian Y.]], [[Emiliano Boscatto|Emiliano]], and [[Gisele Marchi|Gisele]] with walkee Cristian U. were put up for a public vote to see who will be the two returning, it was announced that Cristian U., Emiliano, Gisele, and Rocío were the elected ones to go back in with the final decision to be revealed on Day 64's live eviction show. The nominations system drastically changed during this series, as ''Las Cartas'' (or ''The Cards'' in English) were introduced this series. ''GH2011 ''kept the fulminant nomination introduced in ''[[Gran Hermano Argentina 4|Gran Hermano 2007]]''. Also, housemate could automatically nominate themselves for eviction, if they wished to do so. Before casting their votes every week, each housemate inside the Diary Room had to pick one of the available cards, and then they would cast their nominations. And these were the following: *''Your Votes Are Worth Double'': if picked, the housemate's votes during that round of nominations would be worth double the regular amount. Thus they would award 4 points for their first pick and 2 points for their second pick. *''Send Half Your Points'': whoever had this card, they would choose 1 of their fellow housemates who would end up receiving half of the awardee's points plus whatever points they accumulate on their own. *''Mutual Agreement'': this card will be picked by two different housemates, whoever gets them must pact their nomination votes for the week, and if the end they vote differently, their votes will be annulled and they'll receive a punishment. *''Immunity'': the recipient of this card was automatically immune for that week's nominations. *''The Spy'': the recipient would have to guess which two housemates got the Mutual Agreement cards for the week, if successful, the nominations of those two housemates would then be annulled and the recipient of the Spy card would have cut by half their nomination points for the week. *''Save A Housemate'': the recipient would be awarded to save a housemate from that week's nominations, including themselves; before they can make their decision, they'l

However, along with the duos, two groups will play in trios. This would be in affect from weeks 1-6. Starting on week 7, the housemates would play the game individually. *'''Different Nomination Format''': For the nominations during weeks 1-6, the housemates would nominate as duos, be nominated as duos, and be saved as duos. Once the housemates were nominated, they would be individual housemates, with the viewers only voting to evict one housemate. *'''Different Nomination Points''': For the nomination points from weeks 1-6, the first duo nominated would receive three points, and the second duo nominated would receive one point. Starting on week 7, the housemates would follow the regular GH nomination format. *'''Swap Power''': Along with immunity, the HOHs will receive the power to save one of the nominees and nominate another person. *'''Temporary Leaving''': On day 17, [[Irene Rosales]] had to temporarily leave the house. Her partner, [[Kiko Rivera]], would still make the nominations for her, and she could still be nominated with [[Kiko Rivera|Kiko]]. *'''Individual Nominations''': After [[Yurena Seisdedos]] was evicted from the game, her partner, [[Juan Miguel Martínez]], was left alone in the game, meaning that he could still nominate the other groups, but they would nominate him individually. **'''New Pairs''': After two housemates were left alone as individual housemates, they would be combined into a single pair. *'''Repechage''': On day 45, all of the previously evicted housemates (meaning that [[Julio Ruz]] would not be in this due to his ejection), would all go against each other in the viewers' votes to determine which one of them would re-enter the game. ==Housemates== {{Spain Duo 1 Progress}} ==Nominations History== {{Spain Duo 1 Nominations History}} ==Game History== ==Trivia== ==Ratings== {{Spain Duo 1 Ratings}} ==External Links== {{Spain Seasons}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:Spain Seasons]] [[Category:Seasons with Returning Contestants]] [[Category:Seasons with Evicted Contestants Returning]]

[[wikipedia:Simona Ventura|Simona Ventura]] (2025) | seriesrun = September 14, 2000 - }}'''Grande Fratello''' is the Italian version of the reality television franchise Big Brother, begun in September 14, 2000, and which has gone on to become a cultural phenomenon in Italy. ==Italian Series== Based on the original Dutch version created by Endemol, the show sees a number of "housemates", divided by gender, social backgrounds and geographical locations, locked up together in a house, where the viewing public can watch them twenty-four hours a day, and vote them out of the house as they choose. The housemates can visit the "confessional" at any time during the day, either to talk to psychologists if they need to, talk to "Big Brother", or to nominate. The title is inspired by the George Orwell novel ''Nineteen Eighty-Four''. The novel tells of a Big Brother, head of the totalitarian state of Oceania that constantly monitors its inhabitants by camera in an attempt to suppress their free will. The tag line of the novel is "Big Brother is watching you", which inspired the show, as it is Big Brother who now has total control over the situation in the house. The housemates live in a house 24 hours a day, bugged by numerous cameras and microphones which capture their every move. Every week the housemates participate in tasks that determine their food budget for that week, or could even affect that week's nominations. The overall goal is to be the final surviving housemate and claim the prize fund. A PlayStation game based on this version was released in 2003. ==Popularity== The program has broken several records, including exceeding a 50% share of the ratings (with peaks of 60% during season one). The fifth season recorded a decline in ratings which was put down to both the competition from rival reality television shows and the season's poor and hasty production. By the ninth season, the show recorded increasing ratings which took the program back to its original popularity. Despite a decline in viewing figures over the years (especially in the twelfth season), Grande Fratello is still one of the most successful reality shows in Italy. ==Seasons== {{GF Editions}} ==Italy== {{Italy Ratings}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

September 14, 2023 - }}'''Gran Hermano''' is a reality television series broadcast in Spain on Telecinco produced by Endemol. It is part of the Big Brother franchise first developed in the Netherlands. ==The Series== ===Format=== Based on the Original Dutch Version created by Endemol, the show sees a number of different Housemates, divided by gender, social backgrounds and geographical locations locked up together in a House, where the viewing Public can watch them twenty-four hours a day, and vote them out of the House as they choose to. The housemates live in isolation from the outside world in a house custom built with everyday objects, like fridges and a garden. The house also includes cameras and microphones in most of the rooms to record all of the activity in the house. The only place where Housemates can be away from the other contestants is in the Diary Room, where they can confess their true feelings. The winner is the last contestant remaining in the house, and receives a large cash prize. Housemates are evicted weekly throughout the show by the viewing public. The show's name comes from George Orwell's 1948 novel 1984, a dystopia in which Big Brother is the all-seeing, omnipotent leader of Oceania. The Gala (''Eviction & Nomination Show'') is presented by Mercedes Milá on Thursdays, the weekly Debate show is presented by Jordi González on Sundays with main highlights from the previous day being shown daily, and for ''Gran Hermano 16: Última hora (last minute)'' is presented by Jordi González on the set and Lara Álvarez from the editorial office on Tuesdays. Gran Hermano became an instant success reaching over ten million on its first two seasons. It has had a total of eighteen completed main seasons, seven celebrity seasons, and five spin-off seasons. After the seventh VIP season was completed, Telecinco announced that Gran Hermano would be axed after a controversy from the eighteenth civilian edition of the show. ==Seasons== As of January 2026, 37 editions of the show have aired (20 regular seasons, 8 VIP seasons, and 9 spin-off seasons). {{GH Editions}} ==Trivia== * [[Mercedes Milá]] was the host of the show for the first two series before leaving to be replaced by Pepe Navarro. However, viewers felt Mercedes gelled with the format and made the show her own, and she was brought back the next series. * When Mercedes Milá left for the first time, Carlos Sobera, the host of the local ''Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?'', was offered the job yet turned it down, simply due to seeing Mercedes as irreplaceable. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

{{United States}} }}The '''Head of Household''' (abbreviated ''HOH'') is the position of supreme power and control in the ''[[Big Brother House]]''. ==Background== The Head of Household is the contestant that is in charge of the ''[[Big Brother House]]''. Each week at least one contestant is chosen by a competition in order to determine the final nominations for the week depending on the country's format. Each contestant is eligible to win the Head of Household multiple times in one season, however, the twist is always finished when the finalists are determined for the season. It was first established in 2001 in the United States to make the show's format more similar to [[CBS|CBS's]] other reality powerhouse at the time, ''Survivor''. Just months later, it was introduced as the main structure in the Brazilian version when it was launched in January 2002. Over time, it was introduced to multiple franchises around the world. Some franchises have introduced a variant of the format has been called [[Head of House]]. While the overall concept is similar, the main difference is the the Head of Household is determined through a competition and has an effect on the gameplay elements to the show, while the Head of House's responsibilities mostly include determining house rules and chores. ==Format by Country== ===United States & Canada=== The Head of Household is determined by a competition each week during or after the live show. The Head of Household is free from the threat of eviction. They receive perks, such as getting their own private bedroom, but they are also faced with the decision of nominating two houseguests for eviction and putting up a replacement nominee when the [[Power of Veto]] is used. Usually, the previous Head of Household is not eligible to play in the subsequent Head of Household competition, and thus, cannot be Head of Household twice in a row (unless the houseguests are down to the final three). [[File:HOH Statue.png|thumb|219x219px|A Head of Household Logo outside in the backyard (US version) that is often used in promotional material.]] ====Head of Household Competition==== Each week, all houseguests, except the outgoing Head of Household, compete in the HOH Competition. The final three is the only time that an outgoing Head of Household can win consecutive HOH competitions or if a certain twist happens. HOH competitions mainly fall into one of three major categories - listed below - though some competitions include elements of more than one category. During ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]'', the competition was called the '''Jingle Bell Brawl''', however the power earned from the competition remained the same. The competition can be played individually, or in pairs or teams, and the power can be won in back-to-back weeks. =====Quiz Competition===== [[File:Hoh quiz.jpg|thumb|250px|''[[Big Brother 14]]'' HouseGuests compete in a quiz HOH competition.]] Quiz competitions are fairly short and are usually shown during the live show. Questions range from events in the house to comments from previously evicted houseguests. The houseguests line up, each getting their own booth, and are unable to see each other. ''[[Big Brother Canada 1]]'' - ''[[Big Brother Canada 12]]''}} A '''Have-Not''' is a HouseGuest that has to eat slop in addition to foods voted on by America, sleep in the Have-Not Bedroom, and take cold showers. The alternative is a [[Have]]. The status of Have or Have-Not was determined in the weekly [[Have/Have-Not Competition]] up until ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]''. From ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', the [[Head of Household]] would typically choose the Have-Nots. A HouseGuest may be exempted from being Have-Not by earning a Never-Not Pass, or pulling the Have-Not Escape in ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. On ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 24 (US)]]'', the outgoing Have-Nots would choose a houseguest to replace them the following week. The twist did not appear any of the American celebrity Big Brother seasons. In Week 6 the twist was introduced to ''[[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 2]]''. Called "The Condemned" in French, The Condemned had to sleep on camp beds in a small room as well as take cold showers and eat only slop. The 2 nominated houseguests, along with 2 houseguests selected by the HOH would be "Condemned". ==Trivia== * ''[[Big Brother Canada 3]]'' houseguest [[Brittnee Blair]] and ''[[Big Brother Canada 6]]'' Martinez]], and ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'' houseguest [[Scottie Salton]] hold the record for being a Have-Not the most weeks in a single season in the US version, a total of four times. ** Mark was technically a Have-Not five times, but he had won the Have-Not Escape once, ending his Have-Not early that week. * ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' houseguest [[Lane Elenburg]], ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'' houseguests [[Chelsie Baham]] and [[T'kor Clottey]], and ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'' houseguests [[Keanu Soto]] and [[Kelley Jorgensen]] are the only houseguests to make it to the end of the Have-Not During the early stages of the game, Hayden was targeted for being in a [[showmance]] with [[Kristen Bitting]], but he quickly adopted a low-profile strategic style by joining [[The Brigade]] alliance, which secretly controlled much of the game by agreeing to target outsiders while avoiding suspicion. Throughout the season, Hayden mostly stayed under the radar while his alliance systematically eliminated major threats and he timed his competition wins for crucial moments late in the game. In the endgame, he increased his comp performance, won key competitions including the final Head of Household, and used it to secure his position in the final two against [[Lane Elenburg]]. {{Template:Series |image = [[File:HaAh HaGadol Logo 2018.png|200px]] |version = Israel |series = 9 |seriesrun = May 5, 2018 - September 1, 2018 |host = Ofer Shechter
Asi Israelof
Liron Weizman |nomberofhousemates = 27 |numberofdays = 120 |prizemoney = ₪1,000,000 |network = [[wikipedia:Channel 13 (Israel)|Reshet]] |winner = [[Israel Ogalbo]] |runnersup = [[Eliav Rachamin]] |numberofepisodes = 42 |viewership = 0.50m |share = 17.8% |previousseries = [[HaAh HaGadol 8]] |nextseries = [[HaAh HaGadol 10]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the ninth season of ''HaAh HaGadol''. ==Background== ''Retrieved from Hebrew Wikipedia''
The new franchisee "network" decided to turn towards healthy and therefore stop display of tobacco in the cigarettes an important center for the home. The contestants will smoke in small cells that fit only one person and will not be photographed. The production explained the move in an effort to prevent cigarettes from being turned into a focus for teenagers who watch the program and the contestants start smoking because their stay at home is around the cigarettes. With the transition of format to the network, Yoram Zack - "Big Brother" (the program's editor) was replaced by a large sister - Ravit Lior-Mandel, a change that expresses in her female voice and a demand to address the "big brother". Three weeks later, however, she decided to step down from her position in the wake of low ratings against competitors from Keshet 12 and also for personal reasons, and was replaced by Ro'i Oz. Oz was himself "Big Brother" in the first three weeks of the first season , before Zack inherited his role and contributed to the success of the program in Israel. For the first time in the history of Big Brother, the opening event was divided for two consecutive days. On the first day, 10 residents entered, who were told that no more residents would enter that evening. However, the other residents who had not yet entered entered the next day, and the residents who had already entered were in a separate suite when the other residents entered. In addition, the "first day residents" chose to grant one of the "second day residents" - Liron - immunity already in the first dismissal.{{cite web|url=https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/האח_הגדול_עונה_9#על_העונה|title=האח הגדול עונה 9|publisher=Hebrew Wikipedia|accessdate=17 June 2018}} ===The House=== Israel9 House 1.jpeg Israel9 House 2.jpeg Israel9 House 3.jpeg Israel9 House 4.jpeg Israel9 House 5.jpeg Israel9 House 6.jpeg -Israel9 House 7.jpeg ==Twists== ==Housemates== {{Israel 9 Progress}} ==Nominations History== {{Israel 9 Nominations History}} ==Game History== ==Trivia== ==References== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 6pt; width: 100%;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a; font-size: 8pt;" | References |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" |{{Reflist|2}} |} ==External Links== * [http://www.reshet.tv/entertainment/the-big-brother Official Site (in Hebrew)] * [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HaAh_HaGadol_9 Wikipedia Page] {{Israel Seasons}} {{Season Nav}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:Israel Seasons]] [[Category:Seasons with Returning Contestants]] [[Category:Seasons with Evicted Contestants Returning]]

[[wikipedia:Kevin Rubin|Kevin Rubin]] (2026) | seriesrun = September 1, 2008 - }}'''HaAh HaGadol''' is the Israeli version of the popular reality franchise ''Big Brother''. ==How it Works== Big Brother is a reality television show in which a group of people live together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are 10-17 participants. The housemates try to win a cash prize by avoiding periodic evictions from the house. ==History== The idea for the show is said to come during a brainstorm session at the production house of John de Mol Produkties (an independent part of Endemol) on 4 September 1997. The first Big Brother broadcast was in the Netherlands in 1999 on the Veronica TV channel. It was picked up by Germany, Portugal, USA, UK, Spain, Belgium, Sweden, Switzerland and Italy the following year and became a world-wide sensation. Since then it has been a prime-time hit in almost 70 countries. The show's name comes from George Orwell's 1948 dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four. ==Editions== {{Israel Editions}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Franchises}} [[Category:Television]] [[Category:Big Brother Versions]]

Hacker Competition.head:
{{Competition
|image = [[File:H@cker.jpg|225px]]
|description = The winner of this competition gains the ability to anonymously replace one of the two nominees selected by the HOH (however, they can choose not to), nullify one eviction vote, and select the player of their choosing to compete in the Veto competition.
|seasonsappeared = [[Big Brother 20 (US)]]
|countriesappeared = {{United States}}
}}The '''Hacker Competition''' is a new twist that was in play during ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''. The winner of the competition (played after the [[Nominations|nomination ceremony]], but before the [[Power of Veto|Power of Veto competition]]) gained the ability to anonymously do the following:
*Remove one of the two selected HOH nominations and replace them with another of their choosing OR discard and keep the nominations the same, similarly to the Power of Veto.
**Since the HOH controls the replacement nominee, the nominee that the Hacker removes is still eligible for renomination at the Veto Meeting, as long as they do not also win the Power of Veto.
*Choose one player to compete in the Power of Veto competition.
*Block one player from voting at the Live Eviction.
==History==
===Week 6===
[[File:Week 6 Hacker.jpg|250px|right|thumb]]
After Rachel's blindside eviction over Brett, this twist was revealed to the Houseguests. Angela formulated a plan to use this power, alongside her alliance, to nominate Scottie and Rockstar so that Bayleigh wouldn't feel threatened enough to use her Identity Theft Power App, and win the competition to save Scottie or Rockstar, and put up Bayleigh as the intended target anonymously. This way, Bayleigh wouldn't use her Power App to take over Angela's HOH reign, and they could target her per usual. This plan was foiled, however, when Haleigh won the power for the week, thus eliminating any chance of a member of the other side of the house winning and blindsiding her alliance. Haleigh decided to take Scottie off the block to keep her power a secret, as most would expect her to save Rockstar, and put up Tyler in his place, as Haleigh knew of him playing both sides of the house, wanting to make a big move and get rid of who she believed was the best player in the game. Haleigh also decided to throw the other side of the house off by placing Kaycee in the Veto competition, since she never played in a POV before, so it was an easy choice. Later on, after Angela won the Power of Veto, Haleigh's first hack of the game was made void, as Angela decided to use the Veto on Tyler and nominate Bayleigh for eviction. However, Tyler wasn't free from the Hacker yet, as Haleigh also decided to cancel his eviction vote that week.

===Week 7===
[[File:Week 7 Hacker.jpg|250px|right|thumb]]
After Bayleigh's near-unanimous eviction over Rockstar, the twist was do or die for both sides of the house; [[Level Six]] vs. [[The Hive]]. Both sides needed to win this competition and the Veto in order to control the week. Haleigh, the new HOH, nominated Angela and Kaycee, with the intent of keeping the nominations the same for the Hive. However, Level Six formed a plan to keep all of their last four members in the game, so when Kaycee won the competition, she took herself off the block and put up Rockstar for the second week in a row. Kaycee then chose to pick Tyler to play in the Veto, and he ended up winning, giving Level Six control of the game once again. He then Vetoed Angela off the block. Haleigh then nominated Kaycee for the second time in one HOH reign, a Big Brother first. However, Level Six had control over the votes, and Kaycee then decided to cancel Faysal's vote, making her final act of Hacking for the week, and ending the Hacker twist for the summer.

Hannah began the game on the [[Aces]] team, where she resisted [[Brent Champagne|Brent Champagne's]] showmance attempts and helped lead the effort to evict him while forming a strong bond with teammate [[Derek Xiao]] that became strategic as they became the last two Aces remaining. She later emerged as a target after [[Sarah Beth Steagall]] pushed [[Christian Birkenberger]] to consider her a stealth threat during his HOH, but she survived by positioning herself as a pawn. Fully loyal to [[The Cookout]] after Week 4, she notably convinced Derek X. not to play in Chopping Block Roulette despite a backdoor plan against him, and reached the Final 6 believing she was safe under a Final 3 deal with [[Tiffany Mitchell]] and [[Kyland Young]]. However, Kyland’s HOH exposed his preference for [[Xavier Prather]], leading to Tiffany and Hannah’s nomination. Hannah survived that eviction but was targeted again in the second Double Eviction, where [[Azah Awasum]] nominated her next to Xavier. However, after Xavier won the veto, he and Kyland voted to evict Hannah in a 2-0 vote. '''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' Being on ''Big Brother'' feels like a surreal experience, something that you would have never have dreamed of. It feels like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. And what better show to be on than ''Big Brother''?!
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I actually haven’t been a long-term ''Big Brother'' fan. Growing up, TV was a privilege. So it was up until recently that I started watching. And now I’ve watched like 10 seasons.
'''What’s your biggest strength and your biggest weakness?''' My biggest strength is probably my heart. I think that I will always stand true to good alliances that are showing me who they are, and then what they bring in the table. But my biggest weakness is again going to be my facial expressions, and how true and honest I am. You call a spade a spade, so we’ll play that game.
'''What’s your strategy going into the house?''' My strategy is to come in and not only just be friends with people, but a lot of people, after being sequestered for X amount of days, just want to be heard; they want to talk. So I’m going to do a lot of listening. I make friends with a fly on the wall, as it is. So I think it’d be a good strategy to come in, kind of listen, kind of be everyone’s friend, but kind of turn up the noise a little bit as the days go on, and kind of see where that gets me.
'''What are you going to bring to ''Big Brother'' that we’ve never seen before?''' Something that I will bring [to] the show that you’ve never seen before is true brutal honesty with good integrity. I feel like a lot of people play a big game where they want to be the center of the show, and they say things they don’t truly mean. But I think a lot of the things that will come out of my mouth are very honest. And I think I’ll probably think about it a little bit more than what I say, but just brutal honesty. And maybe a little bit of drama, but in a good, fun, clean way. We’ll see.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' The biggest misconception I would say that people have of me is I’m intimidating. Some of it’s a little bit true. I come with a full leg sleeve. I’m also like 5’9”, so I would imagine that’d be a little intimidating. But once you get to know me, peel back some layers, I’m just a big bubbly person that doesn’t shut up. [''Laughs''.]
'''Are you a hero or a villain?''' I don’t feel like I’m always everyone’s cup of tea, but I’m fun to be around. I’m not saving anyone, but I think I will bring enough to the table that can maybe do a mix of both the hero and the villain side.
'''Do you have a secret you plan on keeping about yourself in the game?''' I do not have a secret that I am withholding.

In ''Big Brother 6 (US)'', James entered the house as [[Sarah Hrejsa]]'s boyfriend and secret partner, and attempted to lay low. Despite initially being a member of the [[Sovereign Six]], he got caught trying to play both sides to save himself and Sarah, which made his alliance distrust him. His alliance officially turned on him week 5, when his ally and [[Head of Household|Head of Household,]] [[Howie Gordon|Howie Gordon,]] nominated him and Sarah after being miraculously convinced by [[Maggie Ausburn]] to do so. Although James would win the [[Power of Veto]], Sarah would be evicted later that week, leaving James all alone. Despite being alone and the obvious target, James would remain safe for the next few weeks because both sides were going after each other. As such, James would choose to stay closer to the middle of the two sides of the house, [[Social Strategies#Floater|float]] , and forge an alliance with [[Ivette Corredero]]. A massive competition threat, James would win four different POVs during the season, breaking the record for most POV wins at the time. However, this obvious capability, along with never being able to win an [[Head of Household|HOH]], would ultimately lead him to getting [[Backdoor|backdoored]] in Week 8 by a unanimous 4-0 vote, placing 7th and becoming the third member of the [[jury]]. In ''Big Brother 7 (US)'', James was part of the Sovereign Six (now the Season Six alliance) during their initial streak of HOH wins. However, after Janelle's decision not to nominate [[Chilltown]] member [[Will Kirby]] during Week 4, James, outraged that Janelle wasn't playing for the alliance's best interest, betrayed the alliance and became a part of [[the Legion of Doom]] alliance along with Will, [[Mike Malin]], and his closest ally [[Danielle Reyes]] to get rid of Janelle, although he did initially deceive Janelle into believing he was still with her. He was nominated during the first half of the [[Double Eviction]] but saved himself by winning the POV. During the second round of the Double Eviction, however, he was betrayed by Will and Mike due to the former's distrust of him, leading to him being nominated again and then evicted in a 3-1 vote. Once again, he came in 7th place and became the third member of the jury. James formerly held the record for the most Power of Veto wins with 4 in ''Big Brother 6 (US)'', but the record would be broken by his Sovereign Six ally [[Janelle Pierzina]] the following season in ''Big Brother 7 (US)'' when she won 5 Power of Veto competitions. == Biography == James Rhine (born December 6, 1975) is a Loss Prevention Manager from Miami, Florida. ==Player History - ''Big Brother 6 (US)'' == ===Competition History=== {| style="border: 1px solid; width: 55%; text-align:center;" |- | rowspan="3" style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a; width:30%" | '''Week 1''' | style="color:#3a3a3a; background-color:#9966CC; width:35%" |

{{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (also known as '''Do or Die Competition''' and '''Santa's Showdown''') is an [[Eviction Competition|elimination challenge]] where the loser is either automatically evicted or nominated for an immediate vote. It premiered during ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)|Big Brother 14]]''. The competition put [[Team Britney|fo]][[Team Janelle|ur]] [[Team Boogie|te]][[Team Dan|ams]] against each other so that they could fight for Head of Household and to keep their status in the game. [[Team Britney]] finished in the competition first and team coach [[Britney Haynes]] chose [[Willie Hantz]] to be the first Head of Household. [[Team Dan]] finished in last, forcing team coach [[Dan Gheesling]] to evict one of his team members, he chose to evict [[Jodi Rollins]]. During ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)|Big Brother 18]]'', the Hit the Road competition was turned into a three-part competition that put the three remaining teams, [[Freakazoids]], [[Category Four]], and [[Big Sister]], against each other to stay in the house. After all three competitions, [[Glenn Garcia]] of [[Freakazoids]] was the first person evicted from the house. During ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'', it was dubbed the '''Do or Die''' Competition. [[Morgan Willett]] and [[Justin Duncan]] competed in it, after being nominated by HoH [[Jason Roy]], and Justin ended up being the last person evicted after losing the competition, named "End of the Road." During ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)|Big Brother 19]]'', the eight houseguests not saved by [[Paul Abrahamian]] had to compete for safety. If they dropped, they received an apple and had a 50/50 chance of being deemed safe. The winner was automatically safe and joined those saved by Paul. During ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)|Big Brother 21]]'', the sixteen houseguests must vote for a [[Camp Director]], who would receive unprecedented power. This houseguest would be able to banish four houseguests and make them compete in a challenge. The three winners would re-enter the game, while the loser would be the first houseguest evicted from the game. A Hit the Road competition was planned for ''[[Big Brother 24 (US)|Big Brother 24]]'' in conjunction with the Backstage twist, however due to [[Paloma Aguilar]] walking from the game, the twist was cancelled. The houseguest voted by the house was set to compete in a duel against one of the Backstage houseguests who was not saved by America, with the loser being permanently evicted. The would-be competition was then incorporated into the first part of the following HOH competition. During ''[[Big Brother 25 (US)|Big Brother 25]]'', the two previously-evicted houseguests in the [[Double Eviction]] were brought back as [[The Walking Dead|BB Zombies]] to compete in a two-part competition. The winner of the first part would be able to decide who would compete in the second part. That houseguest would return to the game if they won and would officially be evicted from the game if they lost with the other houseguest returning instead. During ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]'', this competition was the main elimination format of the season instead of eviction voting. Every episode ended with at least two contestants facing off in "Santa's Showdown", where one would be eliminated from the game upon their defeat. Each houseguest also has a number of objects with different weights. # The goal of this competition is to hang all of the objects on the mobile. However, they must be balanced properly or the mobile may tip. # The first houseguest to get their mobile properly set up without anything touching the ground, and then hit a button will win this competition. ==History== This was first used as a Power of Veto competition on ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]''. In honor of former houseguest [[Britney Haynes]]' pregnancy, it had a baby theme, with the houseguests attempting to hang stuffed animals from a baby's mobile. It was won by [[Jeremy McGuire]]. It was again used as a Power of Veto competition on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', this time with a space theme. The goal was to hang a number of different planets to create a planetary display. It was won by [[Devin Shepherd]]. The next time this competition was used was on ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', this time as a Head of Household competition. Rather than the entire house participating, only one member from each of the two teams that won the previous part of the HoH competition competed: [[Paul Abrahamian]], and [[Cody Nickson]]. In keeping with the "Garden of Eden" theme used throughout this week, the two had to hang apples from a tree. In the end, Cody narrowly beat out Paul to win Head of Household. It returned as a Power of Veto competition on ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'', with an underwater theme. The goal was to hang up all of their sea creature stuffed animals onto the mobile, and [[Jackson Michie]] managed to win. In ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'', it was instead used as a Safety Suite Competition, and the rules were a sligthtly altered. Instead of being the first one to balance various weighted objects on a mobile and hit their button, the houseguests instead had to balance various weighted objects on an unstable table, and since they competed individually, they had to do so in the fastest time to win. [[Christmas Abbott]] completed this task in the fastest time, and she chose [[Ian Terry]] to be her Plus One, granting them both safety for the week. ==List of the ''In The Balance'' Competitions== ===United States=== {|class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week/Episode ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! colspan=4 style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Winner(s) |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 15 | rowspan="2" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 2 | rowspan="2" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | Power of Veto | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "In the Balance" | colspan=4 style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" |

A special version of this competition dubbed the [[Temptation Competition]] debuted in ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]] ''and the [[Safety Suite Competition]] debuted in ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. ==History== A special kind of Immunity Challenge was introduced in ''[[Pinoy Big Brother: All In]]'' which is a [[Nomination Competition|nomination competition]] to determine the weekly nominees who will face eviction. During ''[[Pinoy Big Brother 2]]'', the competition was dubbed as the [[Ligtask Challenge|Ligtask Games]] where each week, a winner would have immunity for the following week. Current Weekly Nominees were also eligible to compete for Immunity, but in the event they win immunity, it would only take effect for the following week, thus it won't save them from facing eviction in the current week. If ever a current week's nominee who won immunity was evicted, the runner-up of the Ligtask Games will automatically gain the immunity for the following week. During ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', the four teams competed in the first ever immunity challenge. The winning houseguest would win for their team, and the whole team would not have to compete in the series of [[Hit The Road]] competitions. During ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'', [[Justin Duncan]] received [[America's Care Package]], which allowed him to win immunity for the week if he succeeded in a competition. During ''[[Big Brother Canada 5]]'', the houseguests were divided into pairs. Whichever pair survived the longest in the challenge would win immunity for the week. Between the two of them, one would have to be the first [[Head of Household]]. During ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', the houseguests were split into two groups of eight. Both groups would participate in separate Punishment Competitions, and the two winners of those competitions would then compete against each other for immunity. The winner then had to grant immunity to half of the house, leaving the other half to play in HoH and be nominated for eviction. The house was split into four groups of four, based on the groups that they entered the house in. During ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2 (US)]]'', during the [[Double Eviction]], a twist was unleashed which allowed one houseguest to win immunity and be safe. During ''[[Big Brother Canada 7]]'', after [[Wildcard Contestants|Canada's Asset]] was voted into the house, they had to complete a task of forming three separate Final Two deals in order to earn immunity and a spot in the game. If they didn't complete the task in 24 hours, they would be instantly evicted. In [[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 6]], TD Insurance sponsored an immunity room. The evicted houseguests of Weeks 4-7 (excluding the Horror at the Ball evictee) were allowed to select someone to get a chance at immunity for the following week. ==List of Immunity Competitions== ===United States=== {| style="width: 18em; border: 1px solid; width: 60%; text-align:center;" |- style="background-color:#

{{Argentina}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (sometimes called '''Hide and Seek Veto''') is a recurring [[Power of Veto]], [[Luxury Competition|Luxury]] & [[Head of Household]] competition. ==Rules== Each houseguest will receive a Power of Veto card and, one at a time, will go into the house to hide it somewhere. After everyone has hidden the Veto card in a spot, the players will go in one at a time to search for the Veto for a select period of time. Once a card is found, it will be placed on a board until all cards, except one, are found. Once the cards are on the board, the host will reveal the names that are inside. The houseguest whose name is not revealed will win the POV. While waiting in between turns, the houseguests are in a soundproof booth wearing headphones, so they can't communicate to one another during the duration of the challenge. ==History== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]'', during the first week. [[Daniele Donato]], eventual runner-up, won her first POV competition of the summer. After a hiatus, the competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', as a luxury competition, which was won by Britney Haynes in Week 9. Following another hiatus, it reappeared again on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', during Week 12, as the first and only luxury competition of the season. [[Hayden Voss]] won the competition for himself and [[Victoria Rafaeli]], winning them both $5,000 each. From this season onward it appeared annually. The next season, the competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]'', during Week 10. [[James Huling]] won the competition, securing his second POV win of the season. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', the competition appeared once again, during Week 7. [[Paulie Calafiore]] won the competition, winning his third Power of Veto of the summer. It appeared again in ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', during Week 9. [[Jason Dent]] won the competition, securing his third POV win of the season. Following the annual appearance schedule, the competition appeared in ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', during Week 8, where it coincided with the [[Zingbot Competition]]. [[Brett Robinson]] won it as his first competition, and thus his first POV, of the season. It appeared once again in ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'' during Week 10. [[Tommy Bracco]] won the competition, securing his second POV win of the season. It returned in ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' after a hiatus during Week 5. [[Sam Bledsoe]] |TwitterUserName = |InstagramUserName = jcmounduix }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' (born '''Joseph Charles Monduy'''){{cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Big_Brother_20_houseguests_(U.S.)|title=List of Big Brother 20 houseguests (U.S.)|publisher=Wikipedia|accessdate=25 June 2018}} is a contestant on ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''. A controversial houseguest, JC was a skirt voter in the [[Level Six]] Alliance. He would often play both sides between [[Level Six]] and the rival [[FOUTTE]] alliance, was particularly close with FOUTTE member [[Faysal Shafaat]] and Level Six member [[Tyler Crispen]], and managed to manipulate several houseguests, particularly Faysal. An aggressive player, Jackson set himself well for the majority of the pre-jury phase by aligning with [[Jack Matthews]], forming a showmance with [[Holly Allen]], and being a part of two alliances. In Week 5 however, a huge blowup caused all of Jackson's allies except Holly to turn on him. The following week, Jackson and Jack were nominated, but Jackson survived eviction. Following that, he managed to go on a competition run, winning 4 HoHs, 4 PoVs, and America's Field Trip throughout the season, while also forming a final four alliance with Holly, [[Cliff Hogg III]], and [[Nicole Anthony]], all of which allowed him and Holly to be in control for the rest of the season. At the final five, he convinced Cliff and Nicole of a lie that [[Tommy Bracco]] was targeting them, saving his showmance, Holly. His competition wins and strong gameplay eventually won him the game over Holly in a 6-3 vote. It is a variation of the [[Giddy Up]] competition. ==Rules== This competition involves players either stacking objects or building a puzzle while needing to refill their timer. In ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'', this competition was played in teams; each team assembling a puzzle while swapping teammates to reset their timer to 25 seconds, and the winning teammate who placed the last piece of the puzzle became HOH. In ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]'', this competition was the third stage of the final competition, and since it was a head to head match between the Final Two, there was no timer element required. In ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'', the rules were simplified and the houseguests were given one hour to stack as many objects as they wanted to. {{United_States}} }}The '''Invisible [[Head of Household]]''' (also known as the '''Secret HOH''', '''Anonymous HOH''', and '''BB Power of Invisibility''') is a twist first introduced in ''[[Big Brother Canada 9]]'', which hides the HOH's identity from all other houseguests. A variant of this power where a different individual dethrones the HOH and anonymously steals their power was first introduced in ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', known as the '''Identity Theft Power App'''. Another name for this power would be the '''Deepfake HOH'''. These variants are similar to the [[Coup d'Etat]], with the key difference being that the usurper remains anonymous (unless they reveal themselves) and overtakes the entire week, while still allowing for the new nominees to compete in a Veto Competition, whereas a Coup d'Etat is publicly activated on live eviction night, moments before the voting begins. ==How it Works== ''Retrieved from Global''
Whoever won this week’s HOH Competition on Friday is the Invisible HOH and will make their nominations in secret and can play not only in this week’s Veto Competition but next week’s HOH Competition as well. However, they were still unable to cast an eviction vote.https://www.bigbrothercanada.ca/news/invisible-hoh-causing-chaos-confusion/ In ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'' during Week 8, houseguests had an opportunity to spend 250 BB Bucks to play for the right to flip the Coin of Destiny. The winner would call the coin toss, and if they called it correctly, they would anonymously dethrone the reigning HOH and their nominees would be taken off the block, eligible to go back up again. ==History== ===Big Brother 20 (US)=== In week 3, [[Bayleigh Dayton]] was the most trending houseguest at that point, and she got to select a Power App in the [[BB App Store]]. She chose the "Identity Theft" Power App, which would give her the power to "steal the HOH's identity" and anonymously control their nominations. However, that is where the power ends; the proper HOH still gets to play in the Veto Competition, name a potential replacement nominee, and cast a potential tiebreaker vote, while Bayleigh would cast a traditional eviction vote (so long as she was eligible). Bayleigh had until the Final 8 to activate the power, but news of her power spread throughout the house and ended up causing her eviction at the Final 11, so she never got to activate it. ===Big Brother Canada 9=== In week 5 of ''Big Brother Canada 9'', houseguests had to count falling rocks and whoever was the closest would win HOH. Temptations were provided for houseguests to choose from such as: * Resetting the count to receive a letter from home. For being the furthest away from the count, [[Tina Thistle]] eventually took this offer to receive her letter. * Winning a slop pass by turning around the longest. Only [[Tera Gillen-Petrozzi]] and [[Victoria Woghiren]] took this offer with Victoria winning the slop pass. * Eating in a feast if three of them turned around for a minute. However, nobody took this offer. The competition ended with Tera and Victoria tying so a tiebreaker secretly were done, which Victoria eventually won and marked her second HOH reign. '''Age:''' 45
'''Hometown:''' Minneapolis, MN
'''Current City:''' Seattle, WA
'''Occupation:''' Geriatric Physician
'''How does it feel to be on the 25th season of ''Big Brother''?'''
I am beyond thrilled to be on ''Big Brother'' season 25. This is a historic milestone, which means that this game is going to be more competitive, the house's going to being more interesting, and it's going to blow people out of the water. And I'm so thrilled to be part of something so big. '''Why did you decide you wanted to play ''Big Brother''?'''
The reason I wanted to be in the ''Big Brother'' house was that I work with older adults every day, and you are not guaranteed another day. If you live to be 100 years old, you only get 36,500 days to live. And most people only live into their 70s, which is around 27,000 days. I wanted to make sure that every day that I lived mattered and counted, and I was living it to its full potential, going on adventures, and experiencing new things. '''What are your thoughts on [[Julie Chen-Moonves|Julie Chen Moonves]] as a host?'''
I think that Julie is an iconic person in the show because she has been with the show, from its very inception. She has a background in actually interviewing people and had sort of a career prior to starting ''Big Brother''. She consistently comes back and her outfits get more and more fierce every year. And I think that the questions in the probing and the conversations that we're having are a lot more meaningful. We're talking a lot about race now and what it means to basically develop an alliance and what it means to move dynamically in this new climate. And I think she's a great guide for all of that. '''What is your strategy going into the game?'''
So my strategy for the ''Big Brother'' game is to find someone who's conscientious and agreeable to be my ride-or-die. I want them to be someone who is good at keeping their emotions in check, and someone who's intelligent and sort of maneuvering strategically. Then the two of us will sort of maneuver to create two fashioning groups that basically get split, while we sort of live in the middle and then are able to sway the vote based upon the dynamics of what is happening, never allowing either side to get too powerful. I think that one of the problems that has happened in past seasons is people ride or die is not that competitive and not that good at winning, and then you watch the two of them sort of fumble at the end.

JANKIE.head:
{{Template:Personnel |Image = [[File:BB26 Jankie.jpg|250px]] |nickname = |birthdate = {{Birth date and age|2024|9|12|mf=yes}} |hometown = Los Angeles, California |occupation = JANKIE World Twist |yearsactive = 2024 |Currently = Winner }}The ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother]]'' "'''J'''unior '''A'''rtificial '''N'''euro-'''K'''inetic '''I'''ntelligence '''E'''ntity", aka '''JANKIE''' is the secondary antagonist of ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'', who unintentionally tortured the Final 8 houseguests during the "JANKIE World" twist in Week 9. At the start of Week 10, he was deleted by his creator [[AINSLEY]] for being "too fun." However, after her defeat during the season finale, he was revived, and production teased that he may return in future seasons.https://ew.com/big-brother-producers-franchise-future-jankie-taylor-hale-exclusive-8747397 However, according to [[Julie Chen-Moonves]], he is not slated to appear during ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]''.https://ew.com/julie-chen-moonves-addresses-long-term-future-big-brother-host-11766994 He is voiced by '''[https://m.imdb.com/name/nm4665656/ Chris MacEwan]''', a regular member of the ''Big Brother'' crew, primarily working as a tape librarian. ==History== During Week 9 of ''Big Brother 26'', JANKIE initiated the "JANKIE World" twist, effectively transforming the backyard into a carnival-themed, highly controlled environment where the Final 8 houseguests were forced to live for an entire week. Houseguests endured numerous challenges and restrictions including: * Sleeping on uncomfortable cots outdoors, with only portable toilets available. * Limited food options restricted mainly to pizza and ice cream. * Compulsory participation in dance parties and sing-alongs to JANKIE’s catchy theme song multiple times a day. * Harsh environmental conditions including extreme heat and constant bright carnival lighting which disrupted sleep. * No privacy or traditional social gameplay spaces, which severely impacted usual strategic discussions. Despite the oppressive conditions, the twist featured two Power of Veto competitions – the traditional veto and a special "[[Double Power of Veto|JANKIE Veto]]." [[Angela Murray]] won the veto and used it to save [[Kimo Apaka]], which led to [[T'kor Clottey]]’s nomination replacement and eventual eviction. JANKIE's theme song went:
''"J-A-N-K-I-E, Jankie, Jankie, you love me
J-A-N-K-I-E, Jankie, Jankie, let's party
Ice cream, dancing, so much fun
Jankie, Jankie, #1
Candy, Pizza, Never ends
Jankie, Jankie, our best friend"'' AINSLEY decided to delete JANKIE at the start of Week 10 for being "too fun." He resurrected during the finale and it was described as an funny moment and that possibly hinted at possible appearances in future seasons. However, it has been confirmed by Julie Chen-Moonves that JANKIE will not appear in ''Big Brother 27''. ==Trivia== * JANKIE’s voice actor, Chris MacEwan, had previously voiced the narrator of the [[Whacktivity Competition]] and various camp-themed twists during ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''. * The "JANKIE World" twist lasted exactly seven days, during which houseguests faced no escape from mandatory carnival-themed activities. * Official JANKIE merchandise, including t-shirts and hats, were released due to significant fan demand online. * The twist significantly disrupted normal Big Brother strategy as houseguests were confined to the backyard, severely limiting private conversations. ==Gallery== File:BB26 Jankie.jpg|JANKIE File:BB26 Jankie World.jpg|JANKIE World File:BB26 Jankie Death.jpg|JANKIE being deleted by [[AINSLEY]] File:BB26 Jankie Memorial.jpg|Memorial for JANKIE File:BB26 Jankie Missing Poster.jpg|Missing poster for JANKIE posted on the ''Big Brother'' Instagramhttps://www.instagram.com/p/DBE77nnTdKQ/ File:BB26 Jankie Revival.jpg|JANKIE being revived following AINSLEY's deletion File:BB26 Jankie Finale.jpg|JANKIE singing hi

She began hosting when the series premiered in 2000 with ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]'', and from ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]'' onward has served as the sole host of the franchise.{{Cite web |title=Julie Chen Talks Hosting Big Brother For Over 20 Years |url=https://www.etonline.com/julie-chen-reflects-on-20-years-of-big-brother-exclusive-148372 |website=Entertainment Tonight |date=February 12, 2020 |access-date=August 20, 2025}} Notably, Chen-Moonves was absent from hosting duties only during the 2023 spin-off ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]''.{{Cite web |title=Big Brother: Reindeer Games – Everything to Know |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/tv/2023/12/11/big-brother-reindeer-games-cast-rules/71873291007/ |website=USA Today |date=December 11, 2023 |access-date=August 20, 2025}} Throughout her tenure, Chen-Moonves has become strongly associated with the show's culture and fandom. She is known for her signature phrase “but first,” often used to transition into key segments of the broadcast.{{Cite web |title=Julie Chen’s Iconic “But First” Is The Heart Of Big Brother |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/big-brother-julie-chen-moonves-interview-1235028826/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |date=July 7, 2021 |access-date=August 20, 2025}} Her precise delivery and stage mannerisms have led fans to affectionately nickname her the "Chenbot," a moniker that has become a long-running in-joke among viewers.{{Cite web |title=Big Brother Fans Explain The Origins of the “Chenbot” Nickname |url=https://ew.com/tv/big-brother-fans-julie-chen-chenbot-nickname/ |website=Entertainment Weekly |date=August 19, 2019 |access-date=August 20, 2025}} Over the years, her consistency as host has been credited with anchoring the franchise, even as the format and audience evolved. Outside of ''Big Brother'', Chen-Moonves previously co-hosted the daytime panel show ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Talk_(talk_show) The Talk]'' before resigning in 2018.{{Cite web |title=Julie Chen Steps Down From The Talk Amid Husband Leslie Moonves’ Exit |url=https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/julie-chen-leaving-the-talk-1202946242/ |website=Variety |date=September 18, 2018 |access-date=August 20, 2025}} She is married to media executive [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Moonves Leslie Moonves], the former president and CEO of [[CBS|CBS Corporation]]. ==Biography== ''Retrieved from CBS'' BB22= Julie Chen hosts the hit summer reality series Big Brother, now in its 22nd season on CBS. Chen was one of the original hosts of The Talk, serving as host and moderator from 2010 to 2018 for the Daytime Emmy Award-winning talk show that examines topical events and contemporary issues through the eyes of five female hosts. Chen served as Special Contributing Anchor of CBS News' weekday morning broadcast "The Early Show" from 2010 to 2011, and co-anchor from 2002 to 2010. Prior to that, she served as the news anchor of "The Early Show" and anchor of the "CBS Morning News," the CBS Television Network’s early-morning, half-hour broadcast, beginning Nov. 1, 1999, when "The Early Show" debuted under that title. Chen covered several major news stories for "The Early Show," including the war in Iraq

The Jury.head:
{{gameplay | image = Big-Brother-Jury.jpg | description = The group of evicted houseguests who determine the winner of a season. | seasonsappeared = Every season except ''[[Big Brother 1 (US)]]'', ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'', ''[[Big Brother Canada 8]]'' and ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]''}} '''The Jury''' is a crucial element of the ''Big Brother'' game, introduced in ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]''. It plays a pivotal role in determining the [[Winners (US)|win]][[Winners (Canada)|ner]] of each season. Initially, all evicted houseguests voted for the winner until ''[[Big Brother 4 (US)]]'', when the Jury was reduced to the final seven evicted houseguests. This change was implemented after ''[[Big Brother 3 (US)]]'', where [[Danielle Reyes]]'s [[Diary Room]] confessions influenced the jury vote, leading to the introduction of the Jury House for sequestering jury members. The composition of the Jury typically consists of the last seven or nine evicted houseguests, excluding the Final 2. Houseguests who [[Walking|walk]] or are [[Ejection|expelled]] from the game are ineligible to serve as jurors. In cases where an even-numbered jury occurs, whether intentional or not, [[America's Winner|the viewing audience receives one jury vote]] to avoid ties. In spin-off seasons, variations have emerged. ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'' and ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]'' featured no jury; instead, winners were determined by audience votes and competitions, respectively. Conversely, all three seasons of ''Celebrity Big Brother (US)'' returned to the original format where all evicted houseguests served as jurors but returned home instead of being sequestered. The Canadian version of ''Big Brother'', known as ''[[Big Brother Canada]]'', has experimented with various jury formats since its inception. It originally started with a seven-member jury but began implementing twists and changes to the jury size and format starting with ''[[Big Brother Canada 2]]''. Notably, ''[[Big Brother Canada 4]]'' was planned to feature a traditional nine-member jury but had to include a public vote due to a houseguest walking from the game. Additionally, due to the [[The Impact of COVID-19 on Big Brother|COVID-19 Pandemic]], ''[[Big Brother Canada 8]]'' was discontinued prematurely, resulting in no jury or winner being crowned. ==Current Jury== These were the Jurors of ''[[Big Brother 28 (US)]]'': {| class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 8pt;" | {| align="center" | [[File:US28 Small LaTrice.jpg|50px|link=LaTrice Verrett]] | align="left"| '''[[LaTrice Verrett]]'''

'''Joseph "Joe" Barber II''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]''. 

Joe entered the house where he soon found out he would be competing with his ex-boyfriend [[Dustin Erikstrup]]. Immediately upon hearing this, Joe tried to convince the other houseguest to target the [[rivals]] after their week of safety was up. In week 2, [[Jen Johnson]] won [[Head of Household]]. While Joe didn’t have the best relationship with her, Jen was set on targeting the duo of [[Dick Donato]] and [[Daniele Briones]]. After Daniele won the [[Power of Veto]], Jen nominated Joe as a [[pawn]], but Dick had backing from the [[Late Night Crew]], still Joe continued to campaign hard, even convincing [[Kail Harbick]] to keep him. Despite Kail’s attempts to convince her [[Mrs. Robinson Alliance|alliance]] to keep Joe, she was unsuccessful and thus Joe was evicted by a vote of 9-1, placing 13th.

== Biography ==
Joseph Barber II (born September 28, 1983) is a receptionist from Chicago, Illinois. He is openly gay.

{{United States}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (sometimes referred to as '''Jury Questions''' or '''Scales of Just Us''') is a recurring [[Head of Household]] competition in ''Big Brother''. It is typically used as the third part of the Final HOH competition of the season. This competition determines who becomes the Final HOH, securing them a spot in the Final 2, to face the jury themselves. ==Rules== The houseguests are asked a series of questions about the [[Jury]]. Typically each question is to finish off an open-ended statement made by one of the jurors. The houseguests answer either "A" or "B" for one of two possible endings. If they are right, they receive a point. This continues for all the jurors; the houseguest with the most points wins the final HoH of the season. On ''[[Big Brother Canada]]'' the questions have a different format and are based on the facts about jurors like the order of events, days, things they did during the season etc. The [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|American version]] adopted this format starting with ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', and have stuck with it ever since. In the United States, this competition was usually held in the living room. From season 15 onwards, the competition was held in the backyard. Starting with season 22 it would typically be held in the basement set, though sometimes it would remain in the backyard. In Canada, it always took place in the backyard. If there is a tie, then the houseguests will take out a chalkboard and be asked a question about an amount of something, whether it be time or an object. Whoever has the closest number without going over wins. If both go over, whoever has the closest number wins. ==History== ===United States=== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 3 (US)|Big Brother 3]]'', where eventual winner [[Lisa Donahue]] beat [[Jason Guy]]. A year later on ''[[Big Brother 4 (US)|Big Brother 4]]'', [[Robert Roman]] won this competition against [[Alison Irwin]] and [[Erika Landin]] securing a spot in the final three. A year later on ''[[Big Brother 5 (US)|Big Brother 5]]'', eventual winner [[Drew Daniel]] won this competition against [[Michael Ellis]]. The competition appeared once again on ''[[Big Brother 6 (US)|Big Brother 6]]'', where eventual runner-up [[Ivette Corredero]] defeated [[Janelle Pierzina]]. The following season, ''[[Big Brother All-Stars]]'', eventual winner [[Mike Malin]] beat [[Erika Landin]], securing a spot in the final two. The season after, ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)|Big Brother 8]]'', eventual winner [[Dick Donato]] defeated [[Zach Swerdzewski]]. Appearing once again on ''[[Big Brother 9 (US)|Big Brother 9]]'', eventual runner-up [[Ryan Quicksall]] beat [[Adam Jasinski]], locking his spot in the final two. On ''[[Big Brother 10 (US)|Big Brother 10]]'', eventual winner [[Dan Gheesling]] defeated [[Memphis Garrett]]. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)|Big Brother 11]]'', eventual winner [[Jordan Lloyd]] beat [[Kevin Campbell]], ensuring her safety going into the final two. Appearing once again on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)|Big Brother 12]]'', eventual winner [[Hayden Moss]] defeated [[Lane Elenburg]]. On ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)|Big Brother 13]]'', eventual winner [[Rachel Reilly]] beat [[Porsche Briggs]], gaining a seat in the final two. On ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)|Big Brother 14]]'', eventual winner [[Ian Terry]] defeated Dan, who played this competition once before. He helped initiate and later revive [[The Collective]] alliance, initially unaware that [[The Pentagon]] was its core structure, while also forming a strong Final 2 bond with [[Tucker Des Lauriers]] and a close working relationship with [[Quinn Martin]] that influenced key power shifts, including a vote flip that sent [[Cedric Hodges]] home. After Tucker’s eviction, Joseph briefly stayed safe through shifting loyalties, but his position collapsed when Quinn shortsightedly named him a replacement nominee following a miscommunication with [[Leah Peters]]. With growing distrust over his outspoken gameplay and endgame positioning, Joseph was ultimately evicted in a 4-3 vote after a last-minute flip from [[Makensy Manbeck]] and [[Chelsie Baham]]. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

'''Why did you want to come onto ''Big Brother''?'''
I want to compete on ''Big Brother'' because I have consumed a disgusting amount of reality TV over 30 years of life. I love this genre. I love ''Big Brother'' so much. I'm also just a competitor in my daily life, playing poker and things like that. And this is the most high stakes poker tournament you can be in. The pressure's on, there's a lot of money on the line. And I love that feeling. '''Why will you win ''Big Brother''?'''
I'm gonna win ''Big Brother'' because I feel like in each of the categories, strategic, social, physical, I'm good enough in all them. But not super overbearing to where people will notice how good I am at any of those categories, and I'll be able to sneak up on them. '''What's your strategy going into the game?'''
My general strategy going into the ''Big Brother'' game is going to be to kind of play coy at first. I'm not going to tell people that I'm a huge fan of the show, which I totally am, so that they don't see me as a threat. I'm going to try to just be low-key. But then, when I see my moment, go all in and make the big move when I see that it's open. '''How will you make your mark this season?'''
I'll make my mark in the ''Big Brother'' house just by being myself, just being by honest and open. I feel like, nowadays, people are very mindful of what they say. And I'm not a bad person, so I know I'm not going to say anything too crazy that'll get me in trouble. I'm just going to be authentic and be myself, and also play the game hard and try not to play scared. I feel like a lot of people play scared nowadays, and that's not how I intend on going about this. '''What excites you most about playing ''Big Brother''?'''
What I'm most looking forward to about being in the ''Big Brother'' house is honestly just chilling, just obviously playing the game and everything. But those moments where I'm just alone, chilling in the pool and just being like, "Holy crap. I can't believe I'm actually on this show." Those are the moments I'm really looking forward to. ''

'''What’s your reaction to getting to play ''Big Brother''?''' It feels incredible, alright?! I’ve been on edge, on my seat for the last few months at this point – well, I guess month and a half. But it’s incredible. I mean, if you had told me a year ago today, when I was celebrating the Fourth of July in Idaho, that I’d be now sitting in the ''Big Brother'' Diary Room talking to you, I would tell you, there’s no way that was the case. And especially like younger me, Jimmy, who was watching [[Big Brother 16 (US)|BB16]] 10 years ago, shortly after coming out, and shortly after having my my parents lose our house. If you had told me, flash forward 10 years, the 25th anniversary of the show, I’d be sitting right here, I wouldn’t have believed you. And I am so excited to be here. It’s insane, and I’m ready for this summer of twists and turns. I can’t wait to see what’s ahead in store for us. '''Why will you win ''Big Brother''?''' I’m gonna win ''Big Brother'' because I have a strategy background. Professionally and personally, I come from a world where manipulation and understanding who you want to get something from and when you want to get it is key. And I come into the house with a strong amount of self-awareness. I know what I need to say, I know who I need to say it to, and I know exactly what I need to do to win. I’m ready to put my chips on the board. I’m ready to show my cards, and I’m just ready to play and ready to play to win. I’m not here for the experience, okay? Some people come into the ''Big Brother'' house for the experience. But I am here to win because that $750,000 check is gonna have my name on it. [''Laughs''.] I’ve been manifesting it for weeks now. I’ve been seeing myself walk out of that onto that stage, seeing [[Julie Chen-Moonves|Julie Chen]]. For some reason, the confetti is purple to me, so I’ve been seeing that. I’m excited for everybody else to see it, too. But I have the smarts. I have the social game, and I know what it takes to win competitions, and when you need to win competitions. I know how to play people, and I know how to manipulate them. But at the end of the day, I also know how to build relationships with and create friends.

When [[Jeff Schroeder]] won the Week 7 HOH, Kevin and Natalie successfully convinced Jeff and [[Jordan Lloyd]] to turn against [[Russell Kairouz]] by forming a fake final four deal with them. After winning Head of Household at the Final Five, Kevin orchestrated Jeff's eviction, then won the final Power of Veto at the Final Four and cast the sole vote to evict [[Michele Noonan]]. Reaching the Final Three alongside Natalie and Jordan, Kevin won the first part of the final Head of Household competition but lost the final round to Jordan, who then evicted him on Day 73. He placed 3rd and became the sixth member of [[the Jury|the jury]]. In ''Big Brother 22 (US)'', Kevin found himself as an outsider, that was often nominated, and he ended up being nominated 5 times. On one occasion, he came off the block by winning the POV, and on another occasion, he came off the block thanks to his ally [[Da'Vonne Rogers]] using the POV on him. In Week 8, HOH [[Cody Calafiore]] nominated him and [[David Alexander]]. Both stayed on the block when they did not win the POV.
