{{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (also known as '''Turnover''') is a recurring [[Power of Veto]], [[Battle of the Block]] and [[Head of Household]] competition. ==Rules== Houseguests all pick a tile to start on and flip it over. They must then take one step in any direction and flip over the tile. That tile is out of play and houseguests cannot step on that tile ever again. Houseguests continue until they can no longer take a step in any direction. When that occurs, the houseguest is out of the competition. Starting from [[Big Brother 6 (US)|Big Brother 6]], one rule was upgraded, with players must move in an L-shape route(either move two steps vertically then 1 step horizontally, or two steps horizontally then 1 step vertically) and flip over the tile they reach, other rules remained. This process continues until one person is left standing. That person wins the competition. ==History== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 3]]''. Houseguest [[Chiara Jude Berti]] won the competition, winning her first PoV of the summer. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 6]]''. Houseguest [[James Rhine]] won the competition, winning his second PoV of the season via HoH [[Kaysar Ridha]]'s plan. James' win led to an iconic moment in ''Big Brother'' history, when Kaysar informed nominee, and eventual season winner, [[Maggie Ausburn]] that James winning didn't seal her fate, but rather [[Eric Littmann|her partner's]] fate. Reappearing on ''[[Big Brother 16]]'', the competition was now a Battle of the Block competition. Houseguests [[Amber Borzotra]] and [[Jocasta Odom]] won the competition, meaning they were safe for the week. Due to his legacy with this competition, Kaysar returned to host it after his eviction on ''[[Big Brother 22]]'', where it was used as a Head of Household competition, won by [[Enzo Palumbo]]. ==List of ''Knight Moves'' Competitions== ===United States=== {|class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! colspan=2 style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Winner |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 3 | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 4 | rowspan="2" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | Power of Veto | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "Turnover" | colspan="2" style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);"|

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the first season of ''[[Loft Story France (franchise)|Loft Story France]]''. Slightly remodeled, the show became a runaway success and changed French television forever.  

==Background==

=== Development ===
To fit the interest of the French market better, the original concept of ''Big Brother'' was slightly remodeled to a dating-show. In a casting call applications where asked if they were looking to find love and had to be single aged between 18 and 35. The title was meant to remind of the term of ''Love Story.''

=== Hosts ===
The main host of the show was Benjamin Castaldi, the grandson of Academy-Award-winning-actress Simone Signoret. The show marked the start of his career. Marie Guillaumond was the co-host who would escort the contestants to the loft.

=== Casting ===
Out of 13.000 applications 11 contestants were chosen that were supposed to display different parts of the french society and stereotypes: Loana, was working as a gogo-dancer in a nightclub in Nice, Aziz the security guard in a Casino, Laure the fashion victim from Paris with a bourgeoise background, Philippe, the young intellectual loving the nature or Delphine, the down to earth-farmer.

== The House ==
[[File:LSFrance1 Houseplan.jpg|thumb|Floorplan of the Loft]]
The loft had a size of 225  <abbr>m2 with an additional</abbr> 380 m2 garden that was built on a parking lot of the studio 103 in La Plaine Saint-Denis. As most other Big Brother-houses during that time, it was furnished by Ikea while the colors that were used for the decoration were inspired by the pop-art-work of Andy Warhol.

== Controversies ==
The show sparked several controversies the weeks after its initial release. 

=== Sex Scene in Pool ===
Because of the French media law, the housemates were not allowed to be filmed drinking alcohol or smoking as well as having sexual intercourse. This became a conflict when on the broadcast of April 28 2001, Loana and Jean-Édouard had sex in the pool. After a few moments the livestream switched off. The scene was edited so that in the daily broadcast only a kiss between the two was featured. However, due to the M6-Site being hacked, the full footage was leaked.

=== Protests ===
Protests happened in front of M6s studios that got quite heated resulting in people from the production company hiring additional security guards.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/1341239.stm BBC: Loft Story under siege]</ref>

=== Loana and her Baby ===
[[File:LSFrance1 Paris Match.jpg|thumb|The notorious cover of ''Paris Match.'']]
One housemate in particular has been the subject of most controversies: While being in the house it was discovered that 23-year-old Loana gave birth to a child in 1998. This was a breach of rules as all contestants were not allowed to have children. However, because she did not held custody for the child, Loana was not removed from the house. Being aware that the scandal would break out soon, the production tried to do damage control and asked Loana if she would issue a statement about the situation from inside the Loft, which she declined. She had given permission to interview her mother instead but clearly permitted to show any pictures of her baby, because the father of the child was not aware that the baby had in fact survived the pregnancy. }}'''Loft Story''' is a slightly re-tooled version of the Dutch-created ''Big Brother'', toned down slightly for the French market by production company ''Endemol''.

The initial French Loft Story inspired the creation of a similar show of the same name in Quebec. The famous eye logo is used by both Loft Story versions. It evokes the voyeuristic eye of the television viewer as she or he watches the Lofteurs live in front of the cameras. Some of them get gradually voted off the show by viewers on their phones and the last couple win a house. It caused great controversy in France and the house was attacked by protesters.

The series never returned after the second season. 5 years later, another French version of Big Brother was aired, ''[[Secret Story France (franchise)|Secret Story]]'', with a new format to suit the French market. 
==The Series==
===Format===
The format for the show was loosely based on the original Big Brother show where contestants must live in a confined quarters and are encouraged to find a partner in order for them to win a house.

===Criticisms===
Loft Story became a craze when it was screened, but as it went on, it became extremely criticized, mocked and belittled by the media: the premise of ordinary young people being filmed most of the time in a cozy loft (and letting themselves out, they got a reputation of being stupid), being voted off by people on phones and getting to win money at the end, got it called high-rate "garbage tv".

Loft Story is considered to be the precursor of reality shows in France where the contestants get voted off by viewers.

Like other Big Brother-style programs, the show's sexual content was criticized as several contestants were seen having intercourse on camera.

Twelve participants from previous seasons will come back to replay the game. Six candidates will be chosen by the production and six will be chosen by the public. The production announced the biggest prize in the history of Loft Story . Season 6 started in 2009 and it was announced that it would be the last edition of Loft Story at TQS. ===Principles=== Several modifications to the principles were made from the second season. The hot water is no longer rationed as it was during the first series, the production attempts to direct the adventures of lofters and intrigues by causing situations that improve the television show (like a treasure hunt, tests and riddles). The second series also sees the "loft master" who plays a more pro-active role by being himself a character in its own right. For the fourth season, changes were made in the loft (decorative changes and new rooms: lounge and boss room) and the decor of the shows was changed. ===The House=== For the first season, the loft and studio of the Sunday program were located in two separate buildings in the borough of Saint-Hubert in Longueuil . The competition re-appeared in [[Big Brother 26 (US)]] as the Week 3 [[Power of Veto]] competition. [[Tucker Des Lauriers]] won the competition, winning his first POV of the summer. He would go on to use the POV on [[Angela Murray]] instead of himself in an attempt to [[Quinn Martin]]. This competition was featured again as the Week 3 POV competition in [[Big Brother 27 (US)]]. ==History== Christian won the first competition of the season, apart of the live move in, becoming one of the four winners that later became Team Captains. He was the first member of Team Kings and selected three fellow houseguest (2 girls and 1 guy). ===Rocky start (Week 1)=== Team Kings lost the first HOH competition of the season, which resulted in the entire team being [[Have-Not]]s for the first week. In week 1, Christian won the new [[Wildcard Competition]] twist, which resulted him immunity from nominations for the week. As part of the new twist, Christian accepted safety for the week, after being led on that he is being considered a threat to others by Sarah Beth in a team meeting before the competition. Also both Alyssa and Sarah Beth in that same meeting, mentioned that the [[Head of Household]] (HOH), [[Frenchie French|Frenchie]] came up to them about being safe from being [[Nominations|nominated]]. After winning the Wildcard Competition, Christian accepted the safety for the week and which resulted him on deciding another houseguest to be immune from nominations. He chose Xavier, believing that since the ladies in team are allegedly save from the hearsay in the meeting earlier, that it would be in the best interest for the team to choose the remaining teammate for safety. During the nomination ceremony, Frenchie nominated Alyssa for [[eviction]], due to her close ties to Christian (as Christian was the true intended target to evict from Frenchie). Alyssa is the first teammate from the team to be nominated. In the [[Power of Veto]] (POV) competition, Alyssa was the only one from the team to compete. She did not win the POV, nor was chosen to be taken off the block by the POV holder, [[Derek Xiao|Derek]]. Alyssa survived the first eviction of the season, by a vote of 11-2. All members of team Kings, voted in favor of keeping Alyssa in the house. After the first week Sarah Beth, won the second Wildcard Competition, and had the ability to switch teams. Kyle was known for making key power-shifting moves that benefited both his game and his showmance with [[Alyssa Snider]]. After learning from Alyssa about a [[Old Skool|secret alliance]], he shared the information with [[The Pound]] and helped form [[The Leftovers]], which went on to dominate the game and eliminate many outsiders, putting him in a strong position. However, when [[Taylor Hale]] won Head of Household in Week 6 and stated she would not nominate [[Jasmine Davis]] since she was the only other Black woman in the house, Kyle expressed fear of a potential alliance forming among the minority houseguests, referring to it as the “Cookout 2.0” (in reference to [[Big Brother 23 (US)|last season’s]] [[The Cookout|Cookout]]), and relayed his concerns to allies [[Michael Bruner]] and [[Brittany Hoopes]]. During the Split House Double Eviction, he betrayed The Leftovers by exposing the alliance to Alyssa and [[Terrance Higgins]], leading to [[Joseph Abdin|Joseph Abdin's]] eviction and the creation of a short-lived counter-coalition, [[The Afterparty]]. After Michael won the Week 8 Power of Veto competition, he and Brittany decided to reveal Kyle's concerns of a potential “Cookout 2.0” alliance to the entire house, leading to HoH [[Matt Turner]] putting Kyle on the block as the replacement nominee. Kyle was later evicted unanimously by a vote of 5-0. On finale night, he cast his vote for Taylor to win the game. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''
'''Age:''' 29
'''Hometown/Current City:''' Bountiful, Utah
'''Occupation:''' Unemployed '''What’s the best advice you received before coming out to play?'''
The best advice I received has gotta be from my mom. She said, "Just be yourself. Everybody else has already taken." So going into the Big Brother house, I'm just going to be as genuine, as nice, and as goofy as possible. (Laughs.) '''What do you think people will perceive you as?'''
I think when people first see me, they're gonna see this 6'3" Ken doll-looking guy. They might think I'm a dumb blonde. But hopefully, as they get to know me, they realize I'm a genuine guy that wants to play the game of Big Brother. '''What types of players would you least want in your alliance?'''
So I'm a very chill guy. I don't like conflict. And I think the type of person that I'm going to butt heads with most are those Type-A dominant personalities that want to rule the house and dictate what happens in the alliance. Those are the people that I'm going to try and distance myself from, and hopefully not get in too many fights with. '''What’s something the other houseguests may dislike about you?'''
So I'm the type of person that always makes light of every situation. If there are fights and quarrels, I'm the type of guy that tries to make a joke and make people laugh to feel better. That might rub people the wrong way when people are trying to play the game hard and be very serious. I'm definitely a goofy guy. And hopefully, my jokes won't rub people the wrong way.

Her [[Phalanx 5]] alliance crumbled once supposed ally, first [[Head of Household|HOH]] [[Reilly Smedley]], blindsided Kirsten by not saving her after being pitched as an easy target by much of the house. On eviction night, she was evicted by a 13-0 vote, placing 16th. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''
'''Age:''' 25
'''Hometown:''' Orlando, FL via Dominica
'''Current City:''' Houston, TX
'''Occupation:''' Molecular Biologist
'''How does it feel to be on the 25th season of ''Big Brother''?'''
This is the historic 25th Ssason of ''Big Brother''. I'm 25. It feels like the stars are aligning for me to win this. '''What twists do you think are happening in ''Big Brother 25''?'''
The 25th season of ''Big Brother'', I feel like they're going to make everything 25 times as hard, to be honest with you. But I think it's also going to be a little bit of a bigger reward. We'll see if I'm right. I am not a psychic. But if the prize was bigger, because it's the 25th season, don't say I didn't tell you. '''Why did you decide you wanted to play ''Big Brother''?'''
This is a crazy opportunity. And I deserve to win. I came to this country as a little girl chasing the American dream with my family. And I've seen them work and struggle. For that reason, I took myself from somewhere where we didn't really have a lot to having everything that I need to get by. I think, right now, it's more important to me to help those who are around me get to okay places and be able to live a happier and more comfortable life here in America. So I definitely want to help my family members and some people overseas who don't have some of the stuff that we have here. '''What's your experience watching ''Big Brother''?'''
I always watched ''Big Brother'' a little bit as a kid, and I just thought it was so funny seeing people in the Diary Room saying whatever they wanted to say on national TV. '''What are your thoughts on [[Julie Chen-Moonves|Julie Chen Moonves]] as a host?'''
Julie has the most soothing voice. She could say the most negative thing ever, and you'd still be okay with it just because her voice calms you down. I think that's important. '''What is your strategy going into the game?'''
My strategy going into ''Big Brother'' is aligning with the strong people right off the bat. I need a strong alliance out of the gate, and we're going to steamroll the other alliances. '''How much will you hide about yourself during your time in the house?'''
The one thing I'm going to keep a secret from the house guest is my background as a cell and molecular biologist. I'm going to tell them I'm a swimsuit designer because I don't need them knowing that I'm too smart. I don't need a target on my back. '''Why will you win ''Big Brother 25''?'''
I'm going to be the winner of ''Big Brother'' season 25 because I don't take no for an answer. I never give up, and I'm 10 steps ahead of everyone's game. They won't even know it.{{cite web|url=https://parade.com/tv/big-brother-25-cast-photos-interview

After forming a friendship with [[Matt Hardeman]], Kenney quickly realized the hardships of playing the game and decided to give up his game for Matt, though Matt was ultimately evicted. Thereafter, he continually expressed his desire to be evicted for missing his family, which was met with chastise and ridicule by his fellow houseguests. His wish was finally granted when [[Cedric Hodges]] nominated him and he was evicted during week 3. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''
'''Age:''' 52
'''Hometown:''' Boston, MA
'''Occupation:''' Former undercover cop
'''Why did you want to come onto ''Big Brother''?'''
Competing on ''Big Brother'' started off with Derrick. I watched [[Derrick Levasseur|Derrick]], I think it was [[Big Brother 16 (US)|Season 16]], a police officer from the New England area. He went in there. He was able to hide his identity and become a big winner. And, at the end of the day, my wife was super involved in ''Big Brother'' with all her friends. And that's kind of how I got into ''Big Brother''. I wanted to have conversations with her, and I did win her over eventually. Now I'm married; I got two kids. But what better way to impress my wife, who was probably the biggest ''Big Brother'' Fan of all times [than] to come home with the $750,000? '''Why will you win ''Big Brother''?'''
When it comes down to the end of the game, I am finally going to be a person who is older and wins this competition outright. '''What's your strategy going into the game?'''
My strategy in this game is going to be very complex, because I'm going to take it week by week. I'm going to try and come in the middle of the pack at the beginning, try and fill out everybody. I think I'm a person who can read people very well. I know coming into the game the first week or two, people aren't their true selves. They're not comfortable with everybody. But as people get more comfortable, their real feelings are going to come out. That's when I will really start amping up my game and trying to pit people against each other, trying to figure out where I'm going to fit in in the house. Clearly, I want to make a strong alliance at some point. Older people tend not to get into those alliances right away. But I think that I can convince some people to bring me along. I'm a pretty persuasive person. And that's kind of how I'm going to go with it, week by week. '''How will you make your mark this season?'''

Unfortunately for Lisa, she voted in the minority to keep [[Matt Hardeman]] in the game, further putting herself into an unfavorable position. I'm gonna find ways to connect with new people, stimulate interesting conversations with them, and, of course, serve them up, maybe some avocado toast, and that's going to make my mark in the game towards the beginning. And then some more opinionated strategy is going to come out.

[[Tamar Braxton]] won the Safety Competition after having the closest number to how many living statues were in the house. [[Lolo Jones]] won the Head of Household competition after finding the closest number to the living statues that remained in the house. '''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' Absolutely fantabulistic fantastic! [''Laughs''.]
'''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' Oh my gosh, it feels so amazing to be on ''Big Brother''. I’m still pinching myself. I cannot freaking believe it. I’m so excited. I’m ready to get this game going!
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I have been watching ''Big Brother'' since the [[Big Brother 2 (US)|second season]]. I was really heavy and hot into it for many, many years. I used to watch the overnights, the live feeds. I mean, I was in it. And then, I fell off a little bit. And now, for the last couple years, I’ve been back into it, and now I’m in it myself! What?! [''Laughs''.] I’m so stoked!
'''What’s your strategy going into the house?''' I’m a real social game player, because of the fact that I have never met a stranger. I’m always very vested in people, and I have a very big discerning spirit. So I’m really social, but I really think I’m gonna surprise a lot of people, because I’m very physical as well. So, try to put me on the block, I’m getting off with a [[Power of Veto|Veto]] win. Try to get me out of the house, I’m coming out with a [[Head of Household]] win. So I’ve got little different things that I’m going on. But you never really know until you get in there and you see who else is in the house, how you got to work it. I’m playing like football. You know calling an audible? I’ll call an audible in a second.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' The biggest misconception people have about me when they first meet me is that I’m not as down-to-earth as I am. Because they see me when I walk in, I’m always pulled together, I’m always cute. I’ve always got my little makeup on, cute little outfit, and they probably think I’m a little snooty. But I am the least snooty person you would ever want to be in your life. I am so down to earth, I’m from a country town, so I’m a country girl; I’m very, very sweet. So that’s one of the things I think they’re very surprised at: How nice I am. I can be a bitch though, but anyway… [''Laughs''.]
'''Are you a hero or a villain?''' Oh my gosh! By nature, I’m such a hero. I am so much more a hero than I am a villain. However, I do have that side that if you really push me, I can definitely bring out some devilishness. And I got some claws, so I can make that happen too! But I try to keep that at bay.
'''Why are you going to be the next winner of ''Big Brother''?''' First of all, we are about to create history in ''Big Brother'', because I’m going to be the oldest winner in ''Big Brother'' history. 58 years old, walking out that door with confetti, because I’m going to make it happen, baby! I’m a social game player, and I also get down physically, so watch out!{{cite web|url=https://parade.com/tv/big-brother-28-cast-photos-bios-interview-2026|title=Meet the ‘Big Brother’

He first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]'' and later appeared on ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]''. In ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]'', Mike, a rap enthusiast, was best known for being the first houseguest in [[Big Brother|''Big Brother'']] history to win a [[Head of Household]] competition, his [[showmance]] with [[Krista Stegall]] and friendship with [[Will Kirby]], and for creating the [[Chilltown]] alliance. Unfortunately, the rest of the house were anti-Chilltown, and as such, formed [[The Other People]] alliance, leading to Mike's target [[Nicole Nilson Schaffrich|Nicole]] being saved in week 1, which left Chilltown and Krista on the bottom. In Week 4, he was evicted by a 4-1 vote, placing 8th, and becoming the fourth houseguest and first ever male houseguest to be on [[The Jury|the jury]]. He voted for Will to win. In ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]'', Mike and Will revived their Chilltown alliance from ''Big Brother 2'' and managed to control most of the game, with the duo blatantly lying to most of the houseguests, forming fake alliances and orchestrating their evictions. He had a showmance with [[Erika Landin]], for whom he claimed to have no true feelings and only used to get further in the game. For these reasons, Mike is generally known as one of the most notorious villains in the show's history. Despite his closest ally's Will's eviction at the final four, Mike managed to make it to the final two and win the season in a 6-1 vote. Entering ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'' without Will for the first time, Mike was initially a [[coach]] to the new players. He was aligned with [[Frank Eudy]] who was his Dr. Will replacement. When the coaches had the opportunity to return to the game, Mike was the only coach who chose not to return, but was forced to return as the other coaches opted to. In Week 6, his teammate/ally [[Ian Terry]] managed to orchestrate his elimination. She attempted to align with [[Nathan Marlow]] and [[Jee Choe]], the former of whom kept her safe during the first week while he was [[Head of Household]]. She seemed to be in a good position as neither sides of the house were targeting her, but after her ally Jee won HOH, he decided to nominate her as a [[pawn]] to evict [[Erika Landin]], not realizing Erika was protected by the [[Elite Eight]]. Thinking she was safe, Michelle chose not to campaign for herself. After the Elite Eight decided keeping Erika would be better for their games, Nathan decided to turn on Michelle and vote to evict her. Ultimately, Michelle was evicted by a vote of 6-2, placing 11th.

{{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' known specifically as '''''OTEV The _____''''' is a recurring [[Power of Veto]] competition. For French-Canadian Celebrity Versions, OTEV was combined with the [[Yankee Swap]] competitions. ==Rules== OTEV is a musical chairs-style competition played in rounds, with one person being eliminated each round until there is only one person left. # The playing area features the OTEV statue with five (to begin with) kneeling spots in front of it at the top of a platform only accessible by a slippery ramp. Surrounding this are several different zones filled with the item of the challenge. # The six (or however many players there are left) kneel before the OTEV at the beginning of each round. There is one less kneeling spot than there are players left. # OTEV will sing a song or recite a rhyme describing, depending on the season: ## A previously evicted houseguest. ## Two previously evicted houseguests. ## A previously played competition. ## The day for a specific event in the house. ## A specific event. # When OTEV says "Go", the players must rush down the ramp and look for the item displaying, depending on the season: ## The name of the houseguest OTEV described. ## A mashup of the names of the two houseguests OTEV described. ## The name of the competition OTEV described. ## Numbers for the day of the event. ## The number of people who participated in the event. # Once the player has found the correct item, they head back up the ramp and kneel on one of the kneeling spots. One player will be left without a spot to kneel on. [[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 5]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a variant of [[Immunity Competition]] but at the same time a twist to the usual [[Nominations]] process. Winning this type of challenge will secure the winning housemates' safety from facing eviction while those who lose the challenge will be automatically nominated for eviction. The challenge first appeared in [[Pinoy Big Brother]] and later appeared in [[Big Brother Brazil]], [[Big Brother UK (franchise)|Big Brother UK]], [[Big Brother Nigeria]], [[Big Brother Sverige (franchise)|Big Brother Sverige]], [[Big Brother Canada]], and [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother US]]. ==Format== Usually introduced as a twist on the usual nomination process, the housemates will compete in a series of immunity challenges to save themselves from being one of the nominees. At the end of the competition, the losing housemates will automatically become part of the week's nominees and will face eviction. The competition format may differ for every appearance of the twist. In some instances, the housemates would compete individually while in other cases, Big Brother would make the housemates compete in teams. The nomination competition may last from one day to an entire week. There are two common formats for this competition, the Elimination format and the Score format. ===Elimination Format=== For this format, the players will compete in a series of rounds, often in three to four challenges. In each round of the challenge, there will be a winner or winners. Whoever wins in each round will be saved from the nominations and will be eliminated from the challenge, thus being ineligible to compete in future rounds. The housemates who remained and failed to win any rounds will become the week's official set of nominees for eviction. ===Score Format=== Sometimes, the point system is used for the competition. The players will compete in a series of challenges and would gain a point corresponding to their place in the challenge; the first place gains the largest points while the last place gains the least points. After they all finished the competition, The housemates who gathered the least total points at the end of the competition will become part of the official set of nominees for next week's eviction. ==History== ===Pinoy Big Brother: All In=== {| style="border: 1px solid; width: 75%; text-align:center;" |- | style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; width:35%" |'''Week''' | style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; width:35%" | '''Competition''' | style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; width:35%" | '''Nominated''' |- | style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC; width:35%" |'''Week 8''' | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | All Out Week | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | {{nowrap|[[Jane Oineza]]}}

On [[Big Brother 21 (US)|''Big Brother 21'' (US)]], Nicole was known for her kindness, quirkiness, and her relationships with [[Kemi Fakunle]], [[Ovi Kabir]] and [[Cliff Hogg III|Cliff Hogg III.]] Although she remained under the radar for most of the game, Nicole was a savvy social player, managing to flip the vote, and survived an eviction by a 6-4 vote in week 3 after being publicly ostracized by the controlling alliance, [[Unde9able]]. During the [[Unde9able]] reign, she was their main bullying target; unable to get in any of their conversations. Many viewers thought this was unfair bullying to Nicole. As the game progressed, Nicole and her main ally, Cliff, found themselves in a good position after the [[Gr8ful]] alliance broke up. They later formed a final four alliance with [[Jackson Michie]] and [[Holly Allen]]. In the middle part of the game, Nicole found herself as the deciding vote on several occasions. At the [[Double Eviction]], Nicole won her first [[Head of Household]] and made the move to evict power player, [[Christie Murphy]]. After saving Cliff with the [[Power of Veto]] at the final five, Nicole and Cliff chose to evict [[Tommy Bracco]] over Holly, after Jackson was able to falsely convince Cliff and Nicole that Tommy was targeting them. Despite winning HoH at the final 4, Jackson evicted Cliff after winning the Power of Veto. Nicole was unable to win Part 1 or Part 2 of the final Head of Household competition. She was evicted by Jackson, finishing in 3rd place, leaving her the 9th and final member of [[the jury]]. On Finale Night, Nicole's personality, kindness, and growth throughout the game made her a beloved fan favorite which resulted in her winning [[America's Favorite Houseguest]]. Nicole returned the following season for [[Big Brother 22 (US)|''Big Brother 22'' (US)]]. She initially tried to connect with [[Janelle Pierzina]] and [[Kaysar Ridha]]; however, after being placed on the block the second week by their ally, [[Memphis Garrett]], she lost trust with Janelle and Kaysar. This spiraled into Nicole campaigning that she would go after the duo the following week. Though she later found out she was wrong about everything, it was too little too late. She was evicted that week in a 10-2 vote against fellow ''Big Brother 21 (US)'' castmate [[David Alexander]], placing 15th. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | BB21= '''Age:''' 24

Despite this, [[Monte Taylor]] viewed his resume as too strong to keep in the game and used the final HOH to evict Turner as the last juror. Michael, a longtime superfan, played a strategic and observant game by keeping his cards hidden early, surviving an initial nomination from Head of Household [[Daniel Durston]] in Week 1 with a veto win that sparked a dominant competition run. He formed strong relationships, most notably with [[Brittany Hoopes]] and [[Taylor Hale]], and aligned with [[The Leftovers]] while maintaining flexibility across the house. Despite becoming a central force in the alliance with a historic nine competition wins, his dominance also made him the biggest target, with even allies eventually considering cutting him when the opportunity arose. During the Week 9 [[Double Eviction]], [[Monte Taylor]] used the Power of Veto to save [[Alyssa Snider]] and convinced HOH [[Matt Turner]] to shift the target onto Michael. After a failed campaign and a final speech exposing Brittany’s game, Michael was evicted unanimously 3-0 as a major threat. On finale night, he voted for Taylor Hale to win the game. Michael became the first houseguest to win 4 PoV's pre-jury, 6 in a single season and the first male to win 9 competitions tying [[Janelle Pierzina|Janelle Pierzina's]] Season 7 record for the most in any season. Because of this, Michael has been considered by viewers and fellow houseguests as one of the greatest physical competitors in the history of the show, as well as one of the greatest to not win. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

{{Philippines}} {{Finland}} }}The '''Power of Veto''' (abbreviated ''POV'') is a power that was first introduced in ''[[Big Brother 3 (US)]]'' before being adapted by other franchises. ==United States & Canada== The Power of Veto is a game-changing power that allows its holder remove one of the current [[Nominations]] from the Nomination Block (often referred to being “on the block”). The Power of Veto also guarantees the holder’s own safety for the week, unless they are the only eligible person who could be nominated as the replacement nominee. If the Veto is used, the [[Head of Household]] must name a replacement nominee. The Power of Veto is usually up for grabs each week in a dedicated [[List of Power of Veto Competitions|Power of Veto Competition]]. In the U.S., six houseguests compete: the Head of Household, the two nominees, and three other players (picked either by the guaranteed players themselves in early seasons, like ''[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]'', or by a random draw in later seasons). The Head of Household also picks a competition host, though this is rarely shown on the edited broadcasts. In ''[[Big Brother Canada]]'', starting with ''[[Big Brother Canada 7]]'', the Head of Household is ineligible to compete in the Power of Veto Competition until only five houseguests remain. While most Vetoes are earned through competitions, they can also appear as special twists, such as prizes from [[Pandora's Box]], though these are rare. ===The Powers of Veto=== ====Silver Power of Veto==== [[File:Sliver POV.jpg|150px|thumb|right|The Silver Power of Veto]] The Silver Power of Veto, used in ''[[Big Brother 3 (US)]]'', allowed the winner to remove one nominee off the Nomination Block if they so desired. However, the winner of the Silver Power of Veto could not remove him or herself off the Nomination Block. If the Veto were used, the HOH would select the replacement nominee. ====Golden Power of Veto==== [[File:Golden POV.jpg|150px|thumb|right|The Golden Power of Veto]] The Golden Power of Veto was the final Veto introduced at the end of ''Big Brother 3 (US)'' and has been used in every succeeding season. The Golden Power of Veto allowed the winner to remove one nominee off the Nomination Block if they so desired, including themselves. If the Veto were used, the HOH would select the replacement nominee. This version has become the staple version of the Veto ever since, a crucial part of the North American ''Big Brother'' format. ====Diamond Power of Veto==== [[File:Diamond POV.jpg|150px|thumb|right|The Diamond Power of Veto]] Main Article: [[Diamond Power of Veto]]
The Diamond Power of Veto was the final Veto of ''[[Big Brother 4 (US)]]'' and was essentially identical to the Golden Power of Veto at the time, before being revamped during ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', giving the Veto Holder the power to name the replacement nominee instead of the HOH. This version is one of the most popular and powerful powers in the game, with houseguests speculating its existence in nearly every season. ====Other Types of Veto==== *[[Blood Power of Veto]] *[[Boomerang Power of Veto]] *[[Double Power of Veto]] *[[Forced Power of Veto]] *[[Secret Power of Veto]] ====Non-Vetoes==== Some seasons have featured special twists and powers that allowed a houseguest to be taken off the block, but they were not specifically called Vetoes despite being functionally identical. Despite the houseguests finding out, they both made it to week 5, so they both joined the game as individual players. **[[Shelli Poole]] and [[Jeff Weldon]] revealed they each had a twin outside of the game. ==== Big Brother: Over The Top ==== Opposite of ''Big Brother 17'', this season did not include the twin twist but instead featured the secret siblings twist. ''[[Big Brother 22 (UK)]]'' }}'''Previously Evicted Houseguest''' is a recurring twist featured in several international versions of ''Big Brother'', including ''[[Big Brother Brazil]]'', ''[[Big Brother Canada]]'', ''[[Pinoy Big Brother]]'', ''[[Big Brother (UK)]]'', and ''[[Big Brother (U.S.)]]''. The twist gives [[Eviction|evicted]] [[housemates]] an opportunity to return to the game and resume their pursuit of the grand prize. The method of re-entry varies by season, most often involving either a public vote or a competitive challenge such as the [[Re-Entry Competition]] or [[Battle Back Competition]]. ==History== ===United States=== ====Big Brother 3 (US)==== In ''[[Big Brother 3 (US)]]'', the first four evicted houseguests were asked questions about how much they'd be willing to give up to re-enter the house. These questions left only [[Amy Crews]] and [[Eric Ouellette|Eric Ouellette]] remaining. The remaining seven houseguests then voted for one of the two to re-enter the game, with Amy winning with a 5-2 vote.  ====Big Brother 6 (US)==== In ''[[Big Brother 6 (US)]]'', the houseguests learned that either [[Kaysar Ridha]], [[Michael Donnellan]], or [[Eric Littmann]] would return to the game, with [[Ashlea Evans]] not eligible due to leaving sequester. Kaysar won the right to re-join the house after receiving 82% of the public vote. ====Big Brother 9 (US)==== ''[[Big Brother 9 (US)]]'' featured two previously evicted houseguests returning to the game for the first time in ''Big Brother'' history, although one of these was not due to a twist. [[Sharon Obermueller]] returned to the game to be the "soulmate" of [[Joshuah Welch]] after [[Neil Garcia]], Joshuah's original "soulmate", walked from the game.  Later on in the game, similar to ''Big Brother 3'', the remaining eight houseguests had a choice of voting back in a "Mystery House Guest" based on a public vote ([[Alex Coladonato]]) or the previously evicted houseguest, [[James Zinkand]]. James won the right to re-enter the game after being voted back in by a 5-3 vote. ====Big Brother 13 (US)==== ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]'' had a public vote to see which of the first four evicted houseguests ([[Keith Henderson]], [[Cassi Colvin]], [[Dominic Briones]], and [[Brendon Villegas]]) would return to [[Re-Entry Competition|battle]] with the fifth person evicted for a chance to re-enter the game and secure themselves a spot on the Jury. Brendon won the public vote, beating [[Lawon Exum]] in the battle and returning to the game. ====Big Brother 15 (US)==== ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]'' featured a [[The Jury|Jury]] member returning like BB Canada; however, unlike BB Canada, they competed in a competition and not a public vote. In ''Big Brother 18'', Paul was initially very vocal about getting the returning players out, forming an alliance to go against them. However, after their ally, [[Jozea Flores]], was blindsided, they started building trust with the other HouseGuests and began working with the returning players. [[Victor Arroyo]]; another ally of Paul was evicted in week 2. They then formed an alliance with [[Paulie Calafiore]]. Paul and Paulie worked together until Paul realized that it was best to evict him. After Victor re-entered the game, the pair formed the [[The Sitting Ducks]] alliance and remained close until late in the game, when both were nominated and Paul survived while Victor was evicted. A strong strategic and social player, Paul controlled much of the endgame through competition wins and manipulation, ultimately winning multiple HOHs and POVs to reach the final two. After winning the final HOH, they chose to evict James instead of Nicole, a decision widely viewed as a critical mistake. Paul was considered a very aggressive player, being unafraid to make big moves, willing to confront others, and having a hand in numerous evictions. Paul was known for being able to talk their way out of many situations and for playing a great social and strategic game. However, they received criticism for insulting other HouseGuests, making many jury members lose respect for their gameplay. Paul ultimately lost the game in a 5–4 jury vote, finishing as runner-up. Paul later returned for ''Big Brother 19'' with a heavily altered strategy, focusing more on manipulation and social control than pure competition wins. Paul used their early safety through a Week 1 twist and the Pendant of Protection to build relationships and navigate early nominations, while gradually positioning themself at the center of house decisions and forming key bonds. Despite multiple attempts to target them, Paul remained off the block until the final three due to strong gameplay, competition wins, and strategic influence over evictions. However, Paul's aggressive and controversial social style, including perceived manipulation and jury mismanagement, ultimately cost them the win, and they were narrowly defeated 5–4 by [[Josh Martinez]], finishing as runner-up for the second consecutive season. Along with [[Danielle Reyes]] and [[Dan Gheesling|Dan]], Paul is considered to be another victim of a bitter jury; despite what majority of viewers perceived as a stronger game than the actual winner. Paul has won the most competitions in Big Brother history with 14 wins over their two seasons. Various Co-Hosts | seriesrun = August 21, 2005 - }}'''''Pinoy Big Brother''''', also popularly known as '''PBB''', is the Philippine adaptation of the international reality show, ''Big Brother''. It first premiered on August 21, 2005, on [[ABS-CBN]]. Branded as the ''“Teleserye ng Totoong Buhay” (eng. “Real-Life Soap Opera”)'', ABS-CBN Executives put the concept of “Pagpapakatotoo” ''(staying true to oneself)'' as ''Pinoy Big Brother'''s core value, and adds "Pinoy" ''(a colloquial, slang name for "Filipino" identity, diaspora, and culture)'' in the title to emphasize and incorporate Filipino cultural values. When the program first aired, it marked a milestone in Philippine television as the country’s first locally produced reality show, emerging in an era dominated by soap operas, talent searches, and game shows. Since its debut, ''Pinoy Big Brother'' has significantly influenced Philippine television history and Filipino pop culture, becoming the most successful and longest-running reality show in the country. Due to its widespread success, the program has become a household name, with many former contestants achieving mainstream celebrity status following their appearance on the show. The program’s enduring popularity has been attributed to its Filipino-focused, family-oriented format, emphasis on Filipino values and culture, the personal stories of its housemates, and the moral and life lessons imparted by [[Big Brother (person)|Big Brother]]. These elements have resonated strongly with Filipino audiences both locally and overseas. ==How it Works== [[File:Direk Lauren- Even 'Big Brother' Producers amazed PBB lasted 20 years - ANC|right|250 px|thumb|Showmaker [[Laurenti Dyogi]]'s 2025 interview for Pinoy Big Brother's 20th Anniversary.]] [[File:Your PBB Questions—Answered|right|250 px|thumb|Marcus Vinuya [[Bianca Gonzalez]] answered the most curious questions about Pinoy Big Brother over the last 20 years.]] [[File:Pinoy Big Brother - Big Brother 20th Birthday Celebration Big Brother Universe|thumb|right|250px|Pinoy Big Brother feature in Big Brother's 20th Anniversary Tribute in 2019.]][[File:PBB Original Logo.png|thumb|150px|Original Pinoy Big Brother logo used from 2005 - 2009]][[File:Pinoy_Big_Brother_logo_(2011).png|thumb|150px|Official Logo used during 2010 - 2015 ]][[File:Pinoy Big Brother 7 Logo 1.png|thumb|150px|Season 7 Logo used in 2016-2017]] ''Big Brother'' is a reality television show in which a group of people lives together in a large house, isolated from the outside world but continuously watched by television cameras. Each series lasts for around three months, and there are usually fewer than 15 participants. The series aired on [[ABS-CBN]] for 112 days from August 21, 2005 to December 10, 2005. [[Nene Tamayo]] of Romblon emerged as the first-ever [[Big Winner]] of the series, taking home the grand prize package worth ‎₱6,000,000 (approx. $111,000) all-in-all; including a house and lot worth ₱2 million, a cash prize of ₱1 million, livelihood showcase worth ₱2 million and a brand-new Nissan Frontier Titanium.{{cite web|url=http://www.philstar.com/entertainment/313383/one-last-look-pbb|title=One last look at PBB|first=Leah|last=Salterio|date=23 December 2005|publisher=[[wikipedia:The Philippine Star|philstar.com]]|language=English}} ==Background== ===Series Format=== The debut season of ''Pinoy Big Brother'' set the format used in the succeeding seasons of the series. The season adopted the original [[Big Brother Netherlands (franchise)|Dutch]] format, wherein the contestants called ''[[Housemates|housemates]]'' must nominate two people and those nominated must face the public vote, with the viewers voting to save the housemate they want to stay. Whoever has the least amount of votes will be the one evicted during eviction nights that happen every other week, similar to its Dutch counterpart. [[File:PBB Balikbahay Ang kauna-unahang task sa Bahay ni Kuya!|thumb|right|335 px|Throwback Highlights of Season 1 Housemates entering the Pinoy Big Brother House, and discovering their first task.]] Throughout the season, the housemates must accomplish weekly tasks given by Big Brother in order for them to gain a shopping budget. This budget will determine how much they can spend on their groceries. The tasks require a team effort and communication to succeed. Losing a weekly task means that they have to deal with weekly rations for the entire week. However, in contrast to its international predecessors, Pinoy Big Brother delved deeper into the social experiment aspect of the series, integrating elements of value formations, most especially promoting Filipino values and respecting Filipino culture in the show.{{cite web|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/authenticity|title=Authenticity|last=Guignon, Charles & Varga, Somogy|date=11 September 2014|publisher=[[wikipedia:Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|plato.stanford.edu]]|language=English}} The Philippine version of Big Brother also focused on the concept of pagpapakatotoo, or in English, authenticity, making it a primary element in the series. Due to the show integrating Filipino culture and values, the series also explored various facets of what it is like to be a Filipino, adding nationalistic and cultural aspects within its narrative from subtle elements in house interiors to life lessons shared by Big Brother. {{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o3xmAVfnVII|title=The Best Of Pagpapakatotoo Moments inside Kuya’s house|date=7 August 2019|publisher=[[wikipedia:Youtube|Youtube]]|lang

This prompted the network to postpone Pinoy Big Brother 2's August launch, and instead replaced by the launch of Pinoy Dream Academy. With Pinoy Dream Academy launching on August 25, 2006, the second civilian edition of Pinoy Big Brother was then moved to air on February 2007.{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930190031/http://pinoydreamacademy.ph/tabid/230/Article/1061/Default.aspx|title=Welcome to Pinoy Dream Academy|first=|last=|date=25 August 2006|publisher=pinoydreamacademy.ph (via archive)|language=English}} In addition, ABS-CBN eventually decided to use the Pinoy Big Brother studio as the ''Academy'' for the new musical reality show. As early as Season 1's "Big Reunion" special, the season was promoted to be a "bigger", "better" and "more exciting" season, hinting some huge changes being made for the upcoming season. Prior to its official launch, the season was officially advertised with the tagline "Ang Tasks, mas malupit. Si Kuya, mas mahigpit. ''(eng. The tasks gets crueler. Big Brother gets stricter.)''" ===Casting=== On June 2006, open casting auditions were officially announced for Pinoy Big Brother 2, alongside auditions for the 1st season of Pinoy Dream Academy. The open casting were held in various cities nationwide as early as May 2006 up until June 2006. Worldwide Auditions were also held on various cities overseas from July 8, 2006 to August 11, 2006. For this season's casting, the age limit was set from 20 years old to 35 years old. The official lineup consisted of 14 housemates. However, as a first week twist, only 12 entered the house, while four potential housemates were introduced but only two would be joining the official 14 via public voting at the end of the week. Later in the season, 2 more potential housemates were sent in to the house where one was voted by the house to be an official housemate. The season is a two-part season featuring a teen and civilian editions aired consecutively. The season coincided with the 10th year of ''Pinoy Big Brother'', wherein it celebrated the series' first decade throughout the duration of the season. The theme for this season revolved around the concept of having a "''combination''" which was made apparent on the season's logo resembling a combination code, and the season being two editions combined into one. On January 28, 2015, ABS-CBN released a teaser with highlights of the past seasons and editions, including the big winners. The logo is inside the zero of a number 10, a symbol for the celebration of the 10 years of Pinoy Big Brother On February 23, 2015, [[Toni Gonzaga]] renewed her contract with her network; in the contract signing, Gonzaga revealed that she will be back to host the show. It was also revealed that the show will air in June 2015. In May 28, 2015, the show aired a teaser introducing that the season's title will be called as Pinoy Big Brother: 737, with the three and both sevens alluding to the show's ten years. On June 7, 2015, the show aired a teaser with the final official logo, stating that the show will return on June 20, 2015. ===Casting=== On February 14, 2015, the show announced that auditions would start in March 2015. On March 2, 2015, ABS-CBN, through its interactive mobile service called ''ABS-CBN Mobile'', launched a fast method for an early audition schedule on March 6, 2015. By this method, the first 2,000 auditionees will be booked for the auditions. Auditions were also held overseas in San Francisco Bay Area and Tokyo. Online auditions were held from April 13 to May 10, 2015, accepting auditionees locally and abroad. A total of 32,673 people auditioned across 10 key cities in the Philippines, 130 in the United States, 98 in Japan and 96 in Australia; 516 people also auditioned via online. ===Subtitle Changes=== [[File:PBB737_TenLogo.jpg|thumb|220px|right|Initial Logo for the season which was used in Auditions and Earlier Promotions. This record was broken 6 years later when [[Pinoy Big Brother 7|''Pinoy Big Brother 7'']] ended after 235 days. It is the first civilian season with a male winner, [[Slater Young]]. ==Background== ===Casting=== Auditions for the season started in Metro Manila on March 4, 2011 at the SM Mall of Asia where around 10,000 people attended. Show director [[Laurenti Dyogi|Lauren Dyogi]] said the turnout at the Mall of Asia audition was the largest in the show's history. Other auditions were held at several key cities in the Philippines from March to July 2011, plus overseas auditions in Tokyo and Los Angeles. The total number of aspirants for the season, as claimed by the show, was 30,789. A total of 37 housemates entered for this season; fourteen on opening night, fifteen on Day 8, six on Day 15, and two on Days 23 and 25. ===Pinoy Big Brother: Audition Stories=== In the run-up to the premiere, a special weekday afternoon primer entitled Pinoy Big Brother: The Audition Stories started airing on October 24, 2011. It featured several participants whose audition stories caught the interest of the producers. The afternoon primer lasted until November 4, 2011. It eventually gave way to the new show, Pinoy Big Brother: UnliDay, the day main program. The said program shows the latest happenings of the Day Housemates from the Industrial House. [[Mariel Rodriguez]] |version = Philippines |season = 1st Teen ''(3rd Overall)''}}'''''Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Edition 1''''' is the first teen season and the third overall edition of [[Pinoy Big Brother]]. It began airing on April 23, 2006, roughly three weeks after the end of the [[Pinoy Big Brother: Celebrity Edition 1|first ''Celebrity Edition'']]. It ran for 42 days and closely resembled the original [[Pinoy Big Brother]] format, unlike the relatively short [[Teen Big Brother|''Teen Big Brother'']], its British counterpart. In a fairytale-themed [[Big Night]] finale, 16 year old [[Kim Chiu]] emerged as the series' first Teen [[Big Winner]], winning various prizes including a condominium unit in [[wikipedia:Valenzuela City|Valenzuela City]], a livelihood showcase, ₱1,000,000 cash prize, and an all-expense paid trip to any Philippine destination. ==Background== ===Development=== In December 2005, after a successful grand final of the series' [[Pinoy Big Brother 1|debut season]], ABS-CBN Executives officially announced its succeeding seasons to feature celebrities and teens; with a celebrity edition airing on February 2006, and a teen edition airing throughout summer premiering on April 2006. In a similar manner to the Celebrity Edition, the Teen Edition aired with an aim to understand the everyday lives of the Filipino youth. Along with such an approach, the tasks and challenges given throughout the season aimed to teach the teen housemates various life-lessons. According to an interview with Aol Rivera, the show's story editor, he revealed that Big Brother prepared an exciting summer vacation, stating “It's going to be a lot of fun, but it’s going to be very challenging as well. They’ll really learn a lot (from the tasks and challenges).” In addition, a special set of rules were drafted, bringing a more challenging life for the teen housemates inside the house. Rivera added that the new house rules would be stricter yet "kid-friendly", in contrast to the house rules implemented on the series' first two seasons. Compared to the first two editions, this season would last only for 42 days, therefore having fast-paced gameplay with double evictions every week.{{cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060422195115/http://celeb1.pinoybigbrother.com/Default.aspx?tabid=134&articleType=ArticleView&articleId=396|title=12 teens brace for a unique summer vacation in Kuya’s house|first=|last=|date=20 April 2006|publisher=ABS-CBN Pinoy Big Brother|language=English|accessdate=15 July 2020}} ===Casting=== Nationwide Open Auditions were held throughout the cities of [[wikipedia:Cebu City|Cebu City]], [[wikipedia:Davao City|Davao City]], and [[wikipedia:Metro Manila|Metro Manila]] wherein 30,000 Filipino teenagers applied. Out of all auditionees, 12 teens were selected to be part of the final lineup. The cast for the first teen season featured Filipino teens from all walks of life; from teens that grew up in far-away provinces to well-off teenaged students of the country's most prestigious schools, from a high achiever teen to a teen mom. [[Ejay Falcon]] of [[wikipedia:Oriental Mindoro|Oriental Mindoro]] emerged as the season's [[Big Winner]] after receiving 36.31% of the total percentage of votes. ==Background== ===Developments=== On March 4, 2008, local news on ABS-CBN reported that Big Brother had already sent 30 Dream Keys along with special instructions in a sealed envelope. The instructions told the receiver that they must go to the final casting call in Manila without public information. From these thirty who answered the casting call, fourteen were chosen to enter the house. ===Subtitle Addition=== There are several reasons the word "Plus" was added to the edition name. One, as had been already stated, was Luis's return to the show. The second reason was the two housemates added to the announced twelve, both connected to the storied [[wikipedia:Ateneo De Manila University|Ateneo De Manila University]]-[[wikipedia:De La Salle University|De La Salle University]] Rivalry. The third was the secret additional area Luis revealed during the opening night of the edition. These rooms were occupied by the Housemates' Guardians, who were also the fourth reason. [[Mariel Rodriguez]] |version = Philippines |season = 3rd Teen (8th Overall)}}'''Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Clash 2010''' is the third teen edition and the eighth overall season of the hit Philippine reality series ''[[Pinoy Big Brother]]''. It is the first teen season to be aired after a civilian season, which broke the ''Civilian-Celebrity-Teen'' Edition airing pattern of the series. It began airing on the night of April 10, 2010 (PHT) and ended over two months later on June 26 of the same year. It lasted for 78 days, surpassing [[Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Edition Plus|Teen Edition Plus]] for the longest Teen Edition by only one day. [[James Reid]] emerged as the winner of the season. ==Background== ===Hosts=== [[Toni Gonzaga]], [[Bianca Gonzales]] and [[Mariel Rodriguez]] reprised their roles as hosts of the show. ===Casting=== There were two sets of auditions for this edition. The first was held simultaneously with those of the third regular season from March to May 2009. As these auditions were held a year in advance, the age limit was lowered to 14-17. A second set of auditions was held in March 2010, this time with an advanced registration through SMS, the age limit for auditioning was 15-18. A total of around 50,000 auditioned, from which 16 were chosen to enter the house on Day 1. A total of 27 housemates have entered the House, including the replacement housemate that entered on Day 20 and 10 foreign teens that entered on Day 22. == Teen Clash Season Twists == *'''[[Double Up|Teen Clash]]:''' This twist is technically the [[Double Up]] House twist carried over to Teen Edition from the previous [[Pinoy Big Brother: Double Up|season]]. [[Bianca Gonzalez]]
[[Robi Domingo]] |version = Philippines |season = 4th Teen (10th Overall)}}'''''Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Edition 4''''' is the fourth teen edition and the tenth overall season of ''[[Pinoy Big Brother]]''. The show premiered on Easter Sunday, April 8, 2012 almost a week after the [[Pinoy Big Brother: Unlimited|Unlimited]] season concluded, and ended on July 7, 2012, lasting for 13 weeks, making it the longest teen edition yet. [[Myrtle Sarrosa]] of Barotac Nuevo, Iloilo emerged as the [[Big Winner]] of the season. ==Background== ===Casting=== Auditions were held in major key cities in the Philippines and other parts of the world. A total of 22,305 teens auditioned for the season. Fifteen housemates entered this season, nine on opening night and six on Day 2. ===Hosts=== [[Toni Gonzaga]], [[Bianca Gonzales]] and [[Robi Domingo]] reprised their roles as hosts. They are joined by Pinoy Big Brother: [[Pinoy Big Brother: Celebrity Edition 1|Celebrity Edition 1]] ex-housemate [[John Prats]]. == Season Twists == '''2-in-1 Housemates''' - Two housemates who are related biologically or by other means, are joined as one competing housemate, assigned by Big Brother. The status of one would be the status of the other. On Day 71, a split of connections was cast, in which both of the twins survived. Their shared status remained for the rest of the season. '''House Players''' - They enter the house to test the remaining official housemates through tasks set by Big Brother and the audience. '''Power of One''' - The public may only vote once per day per mobile phone number. '''Big Jump to the Big Night''' - Remaining housemates compete to have a sure slot in the finals. '''SE Voting System''' - The public is given the chance to vote to save or evict a housemate. The housemate with the lowest net votes, Save and Evict votes combined, is evicted. The system is to be used in the season finale. == The House == '''The 70s House/Big Brother's Teenhood''' The House is decorated with various items from on the 1970s and 1980s, such as old vinyl records on the walls, disco balls, 1970s wallpapers, etc. in which Big Brother said that it was inspired by his own teenage life. This season's house featured only one house, the first time to do so since [[Pinoy Big Brother: Celebrity Edition 2|Celebrity Edition 2]]. This season used [[Pinoy Big Brother: Unlimited|Unlimited]]'s Luxury House with the same floor plan, except for a total redecoration spanning just a week since the previous edition's finale. This marked the franchise' fastest house makeover. Visibly so far, there are only five areas of the House: the House itself, the garden, the activity area, a secret hallway leading into Big Brother's Time Machine and Big Brother's Conference Room. == The Housemates ==

It is the very first special edition of [[Pinoy Big Brother]] due to its format and season's theme. For the first time ever in the history of [[Big Brother Wiki|Big Brother]] worldwide, the Civilian Adults, Celebrities and Teen housemates lived together inside the Big Brother house and competed against each other to become the next [[Big Winner]]. [[Toni Gonzaga]], [[Bianca Gonzalez]],[[Robi Domingo]], and [[wikipedia:John Prats|John Prats]] reprised their roles as hosts. Nineteen housemates had entered the house, 17 on Day 1, and two on Days 21 and 49, and the season lasted 120 days, ending on August 24, 2014. [[Daniel Matsunaga]] emerged as the season's winner, the third celebrity to win in the franchise. He became the first ever celebrity in the history of Big Brother worldwide to win in a non-all Celebrity season. ==Background== ===Developments=== Lauren Dyogi, the Director and Business Unit Head of the show, confirmed the show was renewed for a fifth season and audition schedules were soon to be announced. The network officially announced the auditions on September 15, 2013 during an episode in [[wikipedia:The Voice of the Philippines|The Voice of the Philippines]]. The official air date was not revealed in the announcement. ===Casting=== Initially the auditions for the fifth season were to be held on October 6, 2013 at the Quezon Memorial Circle in Quezon City as part of the [[ABS-CBN|network]]'s 60th anniversary celebration. However, the said auditions venue was postponed due to security and logistical issues. On November 30, 2013, it was announced that, for the first time in the franchise, there would be online auditions through one-minute video submissions. Online auditions ran from December 1, 2013 until January 15, 2014. On March 27, Dyogi announced that 33,064 people auditioned, of which 11,265 were online auditions. Due to casting problems, a special audition was held in Smart Araneta Coliseum on April 15, 2014 where 11,000 people auditioned. A special online audition was opened on the same day and ended by midnight. Overall, a total of more than 44 thousand people auditioned for this season. ===Promotion=== In April 2014, promotional teasers were aired. The first teaser was an audition video of [[Kim Chiu]], the franchise's first teen winner. Another teaser was aired about the love story of [[Melisa Cantiveros]] and [[Jason Francisco]] who [[Pinoy Big Brother: Double Up|became lovers inside the show]] and were now married. A grand mini reunion, attended by some of the former housemates of the Regular, Celebrity and Teen Seasons and hosts of the show, was also held at [[wikipedia:ASAP|''ASAP 19'']] on April 20. ===Scheduling=== In an interview aired February 10, 2014 on [[wikipedia:Banana Sundae|''Banana Nite'']], [[Toni Gonzaga]] confirmed that the show would return in March 2014. It was later moved on April 27, 2014. The show would occupy the vacated timeslot of [[wikipedia:The Biggest Loser Pinoy Edition: Doubles|''The Biggest Loser Pinoy Edition: Doubles'']]. The show's companion show, ''Pinoy Big Brother: All In Über'', was aired weekdays as part of the ''"Kapamilya Gold"'' block. As part of the franchise, this season introduced an online companion show. [[wikipedia:Endemol Shine Group|Endemol Shine Group]] |version = [[Pinoy Big Brother|Philippines]] |season = 7th}} '''Pinoy Big Brother 7''', officially known as '''''Pinoy Big Brother: Lucky Season 7''''', is the 7th season and 13th edition overall of [[Pinoy Big Brother]]. For its second consecutive year, the Philippine series featured a multi-part season and in this season, four previous editions of the franchise appeared: Civilian, Celebrity, Teen, and All In. This season is subdivided into four parts with the first part being a Celebrity Edition, followed by a Teen Edition, and then a Civilian edition. The fourth part was revealed as the ''Dream Team'', an all-star-like edition where finalists and wildcards from each batch returned for the series' final part towards the [[The Big Night|Big Night]] finale. The season revolved around the theme of ''luck'' and ''wheel of fortune'' where the concept of the phrases such as "passing your luck" and "luck is on your side" were highlighted throughout the season's game format and twists, connecting the four parts together. The season premiered on July 11, 2016, and lasted for 235 days, ending on March 5, 2017. It became one of the longest-running seasons of ''Big Brother'' and was the longest season in ''Pinoy Big Brother'', until [[Pinoy Big Brother: Otso|Pinoy Big Brother: Otso]] surpassed its feat for having 268 days. On June 15, 2020, the season had a re-run on [[ABS-CBN|Kapamilya Channel]] through the ''Pinoy Big Brother: Balikbahay Edition'' rewind telecast. ==Background== ===Developments=== [[ABS-CBN]] first announced the show having a new season on March 30, 2016. On April 3, a Facebook page about Pinoy Big Brother posted a photo of the house and tells its audience to share it for a chance to be an official housemate. The Big Brother staff immediately disowned the promo as fake and reminds its social media followers to always verify their sources. The official teaser for Lucky Season 7 was released on June 29, 2016. On July 2, 2016, Big Brother announced on [[wikipedia:It's Showtime (variety show)|It's Showtime]], that the season would begin with the entry of celebrity housemates. Other celebrities were introduced as housemates in various ABS-CBN shows days prior to the official premiere. ===Casting=== Open Auditions began on May 21, 2016, and lasted until June 26, 2016. Like the previous two seasons, the auditions for adult and teen housemates were held together. Online auditions were opened for overseas aspirants. {{PBB7 Audition Schedule}} ===Hosts=== [[Toni Gonzaga]], [[Bianca Gonzales]], and [[Robi Domingo]] reprised their roles as hosts. [[Mariel Rodriguez]] returns as host after her absence since [[Pinoy Big Brother: Teen Clash 2010|Teen Clash 2010]]. However, both Toni and Mariel temporarily left the show during the Teen part of the season due to pregnancy. Toni Gonzaga returned to the show at the premiere of Dream Team. === Logo & Naming Changes === For the first time since [[Pinoy Big Brother: Unlimited|Unlimited]], the show had a major logo change for this season. On ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', it worked as follows: # Each houseguest is given two balls: one yellow and one red. Everyone is also given an identical station consisting of a long, narrow, and curved platform with several numbered slots of ascending value beneath it and a small box at the very end of the track. # The goal of the competition is to successfully roll the ball down the track and get it into the box at the end, i.e. make the "perfect shot". # The yellow ball is intended to be used as a practice ball to let the houseguests figure out how to make the perfect shot. They can roll the yellow ball down the track as many times as they like. # Once they are confident they can make the shot, the houseguests can take their red ball and roll it down the track. The houseguests are only allowed to take one shot with the red ball. # The first person to get their red ball into the box wins Head of Household. If everyone takes a shot with the red ball and misses the box, the first person to get their ball in the slot with the highest numerical value wins Head of Household. On ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', it worked as follows: # There is only one track and one box for all the houseguests to use this time (In ''Big Brother 19'', there was an option of 3 tracks, all leading to a hole in the center of the course). # Plastic balls containing tokens are dumped into the backyard. The houseguests have to search through these balls for tokens that can be redeemed for balls. # A houseguest can redeem a token to receive a ball to make a shot. They can redeem a maximum of 3 tokens at one time to make 3 shots. # If a houseguest is currently making their shot(s), the other houseguests must wait in line for their turn to redeem their tokens and make their shot(s). # Houseguests are allowed to work together by giving tokens to one another and allowing one another to cut in line. # The first houseguest to successfully get a ball in the box wins Head of Household. On its first ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'' appearance, both challenge types were combined into one: # There is only one track and one box for all the houseguests to use this time. # Plastic balls containing tokens are in pools throughout the backyard. The houseguests have to search through these balls for tokens that can be redeemed for balls. # A houseguest can redeem a token to receive a ball to make a shot. # If a houseguest is currently making their shot(s), the other houseguests must wait in line for their turn to redeem their tokens and make their shot(s). # Houseguests are allowed to work together by giving tokens to one another and allowing one another to cut in line. # The first person to get their red ball into the box wins Head of Household. [[Melisa Cantiveros]] (PBB Otso Gold) |version = [[Pinoy Big Brother|Philippines]] |season = 8}} '''''Pinoy Big Brother 8''''', officially called by its edition name, '''''Pinoy Big Brother: Otso''''' is the 8th season and 14th edition overall of [[Pinoy Big Brother]]. Five separate editions called ''Batches'' aired continuously under ''Otso''. The season revolved around the ''Otso Hanggang Dulo (Eight 'til the End)'' theme by introducing new game mechanics that involved Official Housemates and Wildcard Contestants ([[Camp Star Hunt|Star Dreamers]]) competing for their place to live in the Big Brother House. Throughout the five-part season, it produced 58 official housemates and 71 contestants overall. The season premiered on November 10, 2018, and ended on August 4, 2019, and was on air for 268 days, making it the largest and longest ''Pinoy Big Brother'' season yet, and the third-longest season in the entire Big Brother franchise. ==Background== ===Development=== [[File:Pinoy Big Brother OTSO Teaser Coming Soon on ABS-CBN!|Pinoy Big Brother: Otso Announcement Teaser|thumb|right|225px]] On October 20, 2018, via [[wikipedia:ASAP (Philippine TV program)|ASAP]], ABS-CBN officially announced the reality show's comeback by launching the season's teaser ad. The teaser showed a montage of the past seasons' iconic highlights and [[Big Winner|Big Winners]]' winning moments from [[Nene Tamayo]] to [[Maymay Entrata]]. Big Brother's voice was also heard at the end of the teaser by saying ''"Did you miss my voice?"''. ====Logo Changes==== The teaser also showed a montage of the series' past season logos before the new logo was unveiled, adopting the rebranded 2018 logo of the Big Brother franchise. The new logo featured a graphical eye and has a flat, simplistic, and minimalist design. To fit with the ''Pinoy Big Brother'' brand, the generic Big Brother logo was customized by having elements of the Philippine flag and by using the country's national colors. A house outline was also added for this season's logo. According to bbspy, the new eye logo was intended to replace the branding of the international Big Brother franchises, with Pinoy Big Brother being the first franchise to adopt it. {{cite web|url=http://www.bbspy.co.uk/bb19/news/0117/endemol-introduces-new-generic-big-brother-eye-logo Endemol introduces new generic Big Brother eye logo|title=Endemol introduces new generic Big Brother eye logo|date=August 2018|publisher=bbspy.co.uk|language=English}} ===Casting=== ====Star Hunt: The Grand Kapamilya Auditions==== [[File:StarHunt The Kapamilya Grand Auditions|thumb|right|250px|First Promotional Ad of Star Hunt Auditions]] On March 29, 2018, [[ABS-CBN]] launched ''Star Hunt Grand Auditions''. {{United States}} }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring twist that was first introduced in ''[[Big Brother 9 (US)]]''. The twist requires houseguests to compete for safety during the premiere episode(s). Throughout the night, several houseguests will secure safety, leaving a few vulnerable. In most versions, either a group of houseguests or a single individual must choose who gets evicted, resulting in at least one houseguest leaving the house on the very first night. == United States == ===[[Big Brother 9 (US)]]=== On night one, the houseguests were divided into eight pairs who would play together for the season. The pairs competed in the inaugural [[Power Couple]] competition, where the winning couple immediately evicted another pair from the game. [[Jen Diturno]] and [[Parker Somerville]] won the competition and evicted [[Jacob Heald]] and [[Sharon Obermueller]] on Day 3. ===[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]=== On premiere night, twelve new houseguests and four returning coaches competed in the first challenge, "[[Hit The Road]]". The three top-scoring teams earned immunity, while the losing team was unprotected. [[Team Dan]] finished last, leaving [[Dan Gheesling]] to choose which of his three players to evict. He decided to evict [[Jodi Rollins]] on opening night. ===[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]=== On night one, houseguests were divided into teams chosen by four returning players. The next day, the four teams competed in another "[[Hit The Road]]" competition. As the challenge progressed, three teams won safety, leaving the fourth to fight among themselves for survival. [[Glenn Garcia]] lost the final challenge and was evicted from the game on Day 2. ===[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]=== On night one, it was revealed that a [[Big Brother Swap]] twist would send one of the new houseguests home, with [[Paul Abrahamian]] (a veteran) taking their place. Paul was allowed to grant safety to eight players, forcing the other eight to compete in a "[[Hit The Road]]" challenge. At the end, three houseguests remained unsaved and the house voted among them to evict [[Cameron Heard]] on Night 1. ===[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]=== Houseguests voted for [[Jackson Michie]] to become [[Camp Director]] on the first night, granting him safety for the week. He then had to banish four fellow houseguests, who faced off in the "[[Hit The Road]]" competition. [[David Alexander]] lost the competition and was evicted on the first night, although he later became eligible for [[Camp Comeback]]. == United Kingdom == ===[[Big Brother 16 (UK)]]=== On launch night, the public voted for five housemates, each to stand behind a podium assigned either a prize or a punishment. After three "timebombs" went off, two housemates remained. One of the final two bombs contained an eviction notice, while the other was empty. This season was considered unplanned by the show's executives due to both the [[The Impact of COVID-19 on Big Brother|2019-2020 Coronavirus Pandemic]] and the [[wikipedia: ABS-CBN franchise renewal controversy|ABS-CBN franchise renewal controversy]] that led [[ABS-CBN]] to cease its free-to-air broadcast operations as ordered by the [[wikipedia:National Telecommunications Commission|NTC]]. However, PBB Management announced on October 8, 2020, that the series would make a comeback in late 2020 for its ninth season.
