{{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]] competition. [[What's The Hold Up]] is viewed as a variation of this competition. ==Rules== In this competition, contestants are sequestered in a very uncomfortable enclosed setting, ranging from a small room, a glass box, or some other type of strange enclosure. The rules being simple, in that the winner who is the last person remaining inside, will win. At any time, a contestant wants out of the Pressure Cooker, they are immediately eliminated from the challenge. To make the challenge somewhat more unnerving, contestants usually are not permitted to sit or lie down, and are also told to keep their hands continually on the wall, or pressing a button (otherwise they would be immediately eliminated from the Pressure Cooker). Contestants are not allowed any rest breaks during the challenge. In some cases, even if contestants are eliminated from the competition, either by forfeiting or breaking a technical rule during the challenge (such as sitting down or taking their hands off the wall/button) until a set number of contestants are also eliminated from the challenge, they are still restricted inside the pressure cooker challenge location. If a contestant is eliminated from the Pressure cooker, either a prize will be awarded, or a punishment (usually making the Pressure Cooker challenge more difficult, such as loud noises and music, contestants being sprayed with water, bugs and insects being leashed into the pressure cooker etc.) will be sent out. The last contestant remaining inside the pressure cooker wins. ==History== ==List of ''{{PAGENAME}}'' Competitions== ===United States=== {| class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! colspan="4" style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Winner |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" |3 | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" |6 | rowspan="5" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" |Head of Household | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "Houseguest Soup" | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" |

The mini-documentary highlighted the struggles that the show's production staff have faced while producing the previous season, [[Pinoy Big Brother: Connect]], amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Having won the Backstage Boss pass during the premiere, Pooch started out in a relatively comfortable position as he was safe and he was able to build great relationships with most of the men in the house. However, his game started to crumble on the second week when he made a strategic error of volunteering to be the pawn so that house target [[Taylor Hale]] could be finally out of the house. Because his [[Oasis]] alliance mates [[Daniel Durston]] and [[Kyle Capener]] leaked the existence of the Oasis to some of the girls in the house, the Head of Household [[Jasmine Davis]] and her [[Girls Girls]] alliance decided to shift the target to Pooch and led the charge to evict him instead as he was deemed a physical and social threat. While some of the men such as [[Monte Taylor]], [[Matt Turner]] and even [[Joseph Abdin]] expressed their desire to keep Pooch, they eventually joined the rest of the house and evicted Pooch by a unanimous vote of 12-0. Because of Pooch's blunder on getting himself nominated and evicted, his castmates and fans started to call this move as "Pooching himself", which became a running gag throughout the season. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

== History== === Creation=== Following [[Paloma Aguilar]]’s [[walking]] from the game, the alliance was formed due to them all being close allies of hers. ===Short-Lived Dominance=== During Week 2, Po’s Pack controlled the game when they spearheaded [[Pooch Pucciarelli]]'s eviction. In Week 3, the [[Dynamic Duos|Festie Bestie]] twist was unleashed, Po’s Pack all picked partners outside of the alliance to ensure their safety in case they got nominated. ===Downfall=== The night before the POV meeting during Week 3, [[The Leftovers]] were formed, which included all male members from Po's Pack. The Leftovers decided to target [[Ameerah Jones]] in the upcoming POV meeting as she was deemed as the mastermind for controlling the events in the house. After Ameerah and [[Terrance Higgins]] were nominated, it seemed that Ameerah would survive as the Po’s Pack had the numbers. This left Ameerah and the other loyal allies from the remnants of Po's Pack to feel a false sense of security. On eviction night, The Leftovers pulled the wool on everyone's eyes as they blindsided Ameerah by a vote of 7-4, leaving all the outsiders shocked. ===Dissolution=== Due to the guys betraying the alliance in favor of The Leftovers and [[Nicole Layog]] being evicted the following week, this alliance was essentially dissolved. ==Trivia== *Every member of the alliance whom made it to jury voted for [[Taylor Hale]] to win. *Both times Po Pack's members got evicted during pre-jury: **They were women. **They were as a replacement nominee and [[backdoor]] target by [[Matt Turner|a]] [[Monte Taylor|male]] [[Head of Household]] from The Leftovers. {{US 24 Alliances}} [[Category:Alliances]] [[Category:Big Brother 24 (US) Alliances]] [[Category:Big Brother 24 (US)]]

Big Brother's Family). On June 20, 2024, [[Pinoy Big Brother: Kumunity Season 10|Kumunity Season 10]] celebrity alumna [[Alexa Ilacad]] was announced as one of the co-hosts this season, joining to present its digital companion shows.{{cite web|last=Felipe|first=MJ|date=June 20, 2024|url=https://news.abs-cbn.com/entertainment/2024/6/20/alexa-ilacad-surprised-to-be-part-of-pbb-gen11-after-manifesting-to-explore-hosting-012|title=Alexa Ilacad surprised to be part of ‘PBB Gen11’ after manifesting to explore ‘hosting’|publisher=ABS-CBN News|language=English}} ===Casting=== As per Executive Producer [[Laurenti Dyogi]]'s Instagram Live on April 6, 2024, the season's casting will be managed by Star Hunt, opening auditions for ''Pinoy Big Brother'', alongside the [[wikipedia:Star Magic|Star Magic]] and [[wikipedia:Pinoy pop|P-Pop]] idol trainee auditions. Star Hunt auditions commenced on April 27 and 28. Dyogi mentioned four areas where Star Hunt would hold open casting calls throughout its duration: Metro Manila, Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Once again, for the first time since 2024's ''[[Pinoy Big Brother: Gen11]]'', the ''Big Brother'' house opens its doors to regular Filipino civilians.{{cite web|last=|first=GMA News|date=14 August 2026|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/998539/pinoy-big-brother-announces-third-season-of-collab-edition-this-time-for-regular-housemates/story|title='Pinoy Big Brother' announces third season of Collab Edition, this time for regular housemates|publisher=GMA News|language=English}} On August 19, 2026, [[wikipedia:ABS-CBN News and Current Affairs|ABS-CBN News]] announced that the upcoming civilian adult season is scheduled to premiere in October 2026, and for the first time in the franchise's 21-year history, ''Pinoy Big Brother'' has relocated to a new location. While the specific site remains undisclosed, ABS-CBN executive [[wikipedia: Cory Vidanes|Cory Vidanes]] noted that the new facility is significantly more cost-efficient for production. Regarding the upcoming season, Vidanes stated, ''“We are launching 'Pinoy Big Brother Collab 3.0' in October in partnership with GMA. We are moving to a new PBB house that will be more cost-efficient for the network.”{{cite web|last=|first=GMA News|date=14 August 2026|url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/entertainment/showbiz/movies-series/2026/8/19/ggv-pbb-set-to-return-this-year-1041|title='Gandang Gabi Vice', 'Pinoy Big Brother' set to return this year|publisher=ABS-CBN News|language=English}} ===Casting=== For this season, the casting process was open internationally to Filipino civilians between the ages of 18 and 35. Online applications officially commenced on August 14, 2026, as announced via the news program [[wikipedia:24 Oras|24 Oras]], and remained open until August 31, 2026. Throughout the casting period, applicants had to submit a one-minute video including their name, age, location, occupation, and a response to the question, "Why do you deserve to become ''Big Brother'''s housemate?" Submissions were uploaded via ''https://www.joinnow.ph/pbbcollab''. ==Twists== ==Housemates== {{PhilippinesCollab3 Progress}} ==Task History== {{PhilippinesCollab3 Task History}} ==Competition History== {{PhilippinesCollab3 Competition History}} ==Nominations History== {{PhilippinesCollab3 Nominations History}} ==Game History== {{PhilippinesCollab3 Game

After Hayden nominated them in the first week, Brendon won the Power of Veto and saved himself, allowing Rachel to avoid eviction as [[Annie Whittington]] was sent home instead. Rachel won two early Head of Household competitions, using her first HOH to evict [[Monet Stunson]] and later targeting [[Hayden Moss]] and [[Kristen Bitting]], which exposed tension between her and the house. Despite her competition ability and loyalty to Brendon, Rachel struggled socially and was repeatedly viewed as a threat, especially by The Brigade. After [[Matt Hoffman]] nominated Rachel and Brendon during his HOH in Week 5, she fought to stay. However, when [[Britney Haynes]] won the Power of Veto and chose not to use it, Rachel was unanimously evicted on Day 41 for being seen as the more significant threat of the duo. She placed 9th and was the first member of the [[jury]]. She would cast her jury vote for [[Lane Elenburg]], feeling he had played the best social game. She returned to the game in ''Big Brother 13 (US)'' as part of the [[Dynamic Duos|dynamic duo]] twist, being partnered with her then fiancé, now husband, Brendon Villegas. Rachel immediately established herself as a major threat by winning two Head of Household competitions early on and leading the [[Veterans]] alliance after [[Dick Donato]] walked from the game. After the Veterans alliance fractured due to [[Daniele Briones|Daniele Briones']] attempt to backdoor fellow veterans [[Jeff Schroeder]] and [[Jordan Lloyd]], Rachel became a target and was nominated alongside Brendon by Daniele in Week 4; Brendon saved her with the Power of Veto but was evicted. This twist gives players who have previously won the opportunity to come back and win again, as well as giving previously evicted players the chance to win for the first time. ==Origins== Returning players, also known as "returnees," are contestants who have previously competed in a season of Big Brother and then come back for another chance to compete and win. The concept of returning players has been part of the franchise since early seasons. ===All-Stars=== All-Stars seasons in Big Brother feature entire casts of returning players. These seasons are designed to make very competitive environments by bringing back fan-favorite houseguests with proven track records. The first and most infamous All-Stars season was ''Big Brother 7 (US)'', included returning contestants from the first six seasons. Another notable All-Stars season is ''Big Brother 22 (US)''. ===Returnees vs. New Players=== Several Big Brother seasons have featured a blended cast of returning players competing alongside new players. For example, ''Big Brother Canada 5'' had eight returning houseguests with eight new players. Similarly, ''Celebrity Big Brother 19 (UK)'' marked the first time returning celebrity housemates competed directly against new celebrity contestants. These mixed casts show how well returnees can use their prior experience against new players. ===Other Variations=== Several Big Brother seasons have featured a blended cast where a single returning houseguest competes alongside an otherwise new cast. Seasons have also experimented with bringing back four veterans as team captains for new players, and three duo pairs to compete against first-time players in duos. Across these formats, the returning players are usually in the minority. ==Appearances== ===United States=== ====[[Big Brother 7 (US)]]==== ''Big Brother 7'', the first ''All-Stars'' season, featured 20 potential returnee candidates comprised of houseguests from the first six seasons of ''[[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother U.S.]]''. Fan votes trimmed the pool to 14, leaving 6 ineligible to return; producers also selected 6 of the 20 candidates themselves, meaning only 8 houseguests entered based on the public vote. ====[[Big Brother 11 (US)]]==== ''Big Brother 11'' featured 4 past houseguests competing for a single spot to re-enter the game, one aligned with each of the four cliques ([[The Athletes]], [[The Brains]], [[The Off-Beats]], and [[The Populars]]). The returning player tied to the clique that won the opening endurance competition moved in as the first [[Head of Household]]. ====[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]==== ''Big Brother 13'' featured 6 returning players competing alongside 8 new players. The returnees were paired into duos with partners from their original seasons, with each duo composed of one male and one female. ====[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]==== ''Big Brother 14'' featured 4 returning houseguests who entered as "[[Coach|coaches]]" mentoring 12 new players (3 per team). Each week, coaches competed in a [[Coaches Competition]] to grant immunity to a team member or trade players. In Week 3, the coaches were offered the chance to enter as individual players, which all but one accepted; had they declined, an evicted houseguest would have returned the following week. ====[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]==== ''Big Brother 18'' featured 4 returning players alongside 12 new players. ''[[Big Brother Kosovo VIP 3]]'' }} The '''Round Trip Ticket''' is a twist featured in Week 5 of ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', on ''[[Grande Fratello VIP 5]]'', on ''[[HaAh HaGadol 11]]'' and on ''[[Grande Fratello VIP 6]]''. ==Background== This twist was discovered by [[Paul Abrahamian]] when he cracked the code into entering the [[Secret Room]]. Within the Secret Room are twelve envelopes (one envelope for each houseguest). Paul was the first houseguest to discover these 12 secret envelopes. One of the twelve envelopes contains the Round Trip Ticket. The Ticket allows a houseguest to re-enter the house after they've been evicted. Houseguests are not allowed to open their envelope but instead hand them to Julie when evicted. Julie will open the ticket, and if it is a Round Trip Ticket, the houseguest will be able to return into the game. If the envelope is not a Round Trip ticket, then it is a "One Way" ticket which will send that evicted houseguest back home/to the Jury house. If a houseguest decides to open their envelope before eviction night, then that envelope will be void. The Round Trip Ticket twist will expire after four weeks of its appearance. After Paulie's eviction it was revealed that Paul had the round trip ticket. {{clear}} ==History== === [[Big Brother 18 (US)]] ===

{{Brazil}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]] competition. ==Rules== Houseguests start behind a line and must stay in a running position, keeping their hands on two to four buttons. A screen in front of them displays words that are very similar to the word "Go". Players must wait until the word "Go" appears and run across the finish, pushing a button. The last person to push a button is out of the competition. If they move their hands/feet off the button before "Go" appears, they will get a false start and be out of the competition. In the event that multiple players false start, the first one to commit the infraction is eliminated. This continues until one houseguest is left standing. In ''[[Big Brother 22]]'', the rules were changed slightly. Rather than the word "Go", houseguests would wait for math equations that equal the number 13 instead. If a houseguest releases their buttons on an equation that does not equal 13, they will be eliminated. Future iterations featured various dynamics for the competition, but the overall rules and structure remained intact, where the last person to hit their button or the first person to false start would be eliminated in each round. ==History== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 17]]'' as an HOH competition. [[Austin Matelson]] won, achieving his second HOH win of the season. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 18]]'', this time as a POV competition. [[Paulie Calafiore]] won, securing his second POV win of the summer. The competition next appeared on ''[[Big Brother 19]]'', again an HOH competition. It was the first competition in Big Brother history to be delayed because of the rain, or any bad weather. This was the first iteration of the competition where not a single race was ran, as every player false started until there was only one left, that being [[Christmas Abbott]] (who had a broken foot), making it her second HOH win of the season. As a result, this iteration earned the nickname, "Ready, Set, Throw the Competition!" Reappearing once again in ''[[Big Brother 22]]'', as a POV competition once again. It was merged with the [[Yankee Swap]] competition, and Christmas ended up winning this competition once again, having actually ran a race this time, and chose to take the Veto as her prize. ==List of ''Ready, Set, Woah'' Competitions== ===United States=== {|class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Winner ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Veto Holder or HOH |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 17 | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 9 | rowspan=3 style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "Ready, Set, Woah!" | colspan=2 style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" |

Jochen Schropp returns as the long standing host with the addition of Jochen Bendel as co-host. Early announcements claim a newly revised version of Big Brother after lack luster ratings from the 2016 series. Also, no live audience will be included until the live final where the viewers will fill an area outside of the studio and not be in the studio itself.Also confirmed is the theme "Alles oder Nichts" or "Everything or Nothing" https://www.dwdl.de/nachrichten/62556/promi_big_brother_in_diesem_jahr_ohne_livepublikum/ === House === On August 2nd the first trailer for the show was released. The trailer hints that a change to the house has been made. Instead of the house is divided into a more luxurious upstairs and a basement and sewer area under the house, the house is teased to be split down the middle where the two sides of the house can see and interact with each other through a glass divider. " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9fBDJ1Y6Vw The first images of the 'bad' side of the house were released on August 10th. The show's theme can be seen throughout these images with just an empty house with dirty white walls and brown carpet. The diary room is also featured with two pallets stacked to form a chair and dark gray walls covered in dirt.https://www.sat1.de/tv/promi-big-brother/bilder/das-promi-big-brother-haus-2017 The Duel Arena is brand new this year. It is now a large open air arena outside of the compound. This area also hosts the main stage for the hosts during the broadcasts. ==Twists== * '''Everything or Nothing: '''The house is split into two living quarters. Everything, as the name implies has everything a housemate cold desire beds, food, a beautiful garden. Nothing has literally nothing, house mates must share small cramped quarters and sleep on the floor and live off basic rations. Windows line the walls and the two sides can see each other and have minimal interactions. * '''Move In Twist: '''In a series first the housemates were not divided by Big Brother on launch night. All 12 housemates moved into the "Nothing" side of the house for the first two days. All housemates are only allowed 10 personal items from their luggage during their stay in the nothing quarters. * '''Big Spender:''' Big Brother revealed a vending machine on the nothing side of the house. The machine holds basic living items as well as a few luxuries. In order to earn tokens to spend on the machine, housemates must participate in tasks. * '''Duels: '''While duels are a mainstay in Promi Big Brother this year they have changed. All duels are pre-recorded with the exception of the launch night duel. $5,000 |TwitterUserName = CreamMeUpScotte |InstagramUserName = scottiexxsalton |HackerComp=0}} '''Scott Edward "Scottie" Salton''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]].'' Scottie was aligned with the ill-fated [[FOUTTE]] alliance. In week 2, he cast a rogue vote against his alliance member [[Chris Williams]]. However, this was fatal as he would be blamed for future rogue votes. In week 3, he became the HoH, targeted Level Six members [[Brett Robinson]] and [[Winston Hines]] with the former being his target, snagged a PoV win as well, but his plan failed as Winston was evicted. Despite being a backdoor target in week 5, he was kept off the block. In week 8, he was betrayed and nominated by his Foutte alliance member [[Faysal Shafaat]] after Brett falsely pinned Scottie for casting a rouge vote the previous week and [[JC Mounduix]] manipulated Faysal into believing Scottie was untrustworthy. Although his game was initially up when Brett won PoV and used it take himself off the block, Scottie ended up alienating the one ally he had left when [[Sam Bledsoe]] talked him in to suggesting to Faysal that he pick [[Haleigh Broucher]] as a replacement nominee. Consequently, he was evicted that week in a unanimous 6-0 vote. Despite returning to the game at the end of week 9 by winning the jury buyback competition, he was evicted again in week 10 in a unanimous 5-0 vote, placing 8th and becoming the fourth member of the jury. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | '''Age:''' 26

[[Scottie Salton]] |TwitterUserName = Mrs_ARockstar |InstagramUserName = angelamfnrockstar |FacebookUserName = angela.rochkstaar |HackerComp=0}} '''Angela Brooke "Angie Rockstar" Lantry'''{{cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Big_Brother_20_houseguests_(U.S.)|title=List of Big Brother 20 houseguests (U.S.)|publisher=Wikipedia|accessdate=14 July 2018}} was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''. Rockstar was a loyal member of the [[FOUTTE]] alliance, which was permanently relegated to the minority after the defection of [[Kaitlyn Herman]]. During Week 3, Rockstar developed a rivalry with [[Brett Robinson]] when he falsely accused her of wanting to flip the vote to save him right before the eviction took place. Despite getting nominated in Week 4, she managed to escape eviction. While she was nominated again in Week 6, she escaped eviction for a second time as she was seen as less of a threat than [[Bayleigh Dayton]]. Despite her closest ally, [[Haleigh Broucher]], becoming [[Head of Household]] in Week 7, [[Level Six]] member [[Kaycee Clark]] won the [[Hacker Competition]] and put her on the block as an easy target. Rockstar then infamously gave an answer to Level Six member [[Tyler Crispen]] during the [[OTEV]] [[Power of Veto]] competition, causing him to defeat her and her allies. She remained on the block and was evicted in a 5-1 vote, only gaining the vote of her ally, [[Scottie Salton]], as [[Faysal Shafaat]]'s vote was cancelled by the Hacker. She came in 10th place and became the second member of the [[jury]]. Rockstar giving the answer to Tyler during OTEV is infamously considered one of the worst moves in Big Brother history. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | '''Age:''' 34

[[Analyse Talavera]] |Days = 44 |OtherPrizes = Fiji Trip |TwitterUserName = bb21_sam |InstagramUserName = samsmithbb21 |}}'''Samuel Titus "Sam" Smith''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''. Sam was known as a loud, energetic player who quickly became a strong competitor and social presence in the house. He made an immediate impact by winning the first two Power of Veto competitions while also building relationships with both sides of the house. Sam became close with [[Nick Maccarone]] and [[Isabella Wang]] and was part of the [[Unde9able]] alliance, but he was never fully trusted by the dominant [[Gr8ful]]/[[Six Shooters]] group. As the season progressed, he recognized the power structure and became increasingly outspoken about the majority alliance’s control. After being nominated alongside Nick and later [[Kathryn Dunn]] by HOH [[Holly Allen]], Sam realized he was likely the target. In his final days, he exposed secrets about alliances, pre-game connections, and hidden deals in an attempt to shake up the game. Safety Suite Competition.head:
{{Template:Competition |image = safety suite.jpg |description = An immunity competition held before nominations that leaves the winner and his or her pick both immune. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} |seasonsappeared = [[Big Brother 22 (US)]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a new competition that premiered on [[Big Brother 22 (US)]]. Similar to the [[Immunity Competition]], the winner of the competition would get safety for the week but he or she must pick a "Plus One", making two people immune. The Plus One would receive a punishment in exchange for being safe. The current HOH is ineligible to enter the Safety Suite, and a houseguest can only enter the Safety Suite once before being ineligible for future rounds. If only one houseguest enters the Safety Suite, they will not be guaranteed safety - they will still have to complete the competition before their time runs out in order to win safety. It is unknown what happens if no one chooses to compete in the safety suite. This twist lasted for the first 3 weeks of that season. ==History== ===Week 1=== [[Kaysar Ridha]] and [[Janelle Pierzina]] played in the first Safety Suite Competition. The competition was Don't Miss A Beat and that competition was won by [[Kaysar Ridha]]. He would then save [[Janelle Pierzina]]. As a +1,  Janelle's punishment was to wear the All Star "Mascot" costume for the rest of the week. ===Week 2=== [[Bayleigh Dayton]], [[Christmas Abbott]], [[Cody Calafiore]], [[Da'Vonne Rogers]], [[David Alexander]], [[Ian Terry]] and [[Kevin Campbell |Kevin Campbell]] played in the second Safety Suite Competition. The competition was Gettin' Tipsy and that competition was won by [[Christmas Abbott]]. She would then save [[Ian Terry]]. As a +1,  Ian's punishment was to wear the BB’s All-Star Wars costume for the rest of the week. ===Week 3=== [[Daniele Briones]], [[Enzo Palumbo]], [[Memphis Garrett]] and [[Nicole Franzel]] played in the third Safety Suite Competition. The competition was Stealing Safety and that competition was won by [[Enzo Palumbo]]. He would then save [[Christmas Abbott]]. Forming an unbreakable trio with [[Kimo Apaka]] and [[T'kor Clottey]] and a [[showmance]] with [[Tucker Des Lauriers]], Rubina was in a comfortable spot for the first few weeks as the house evicted huge threats. On week 4, [[Quinn Martin]] targeted her in an attempt to weaken his rival Tucker as she was his closest ally, which backfired as Kimo and T'kor flipped to keep her instead. After T'kor's strategic oversight inadvertently sent Tucker home, Rubina stayed loyal to her and Kimo for the rest of the game, but this caused others to turn on the trio as the numbers dwindled for being a powerful voting bloc who would never turn on each other. Eventually outlasting all of her allies, Rubina managed to reach the final four, but found herself to be an outsider among the remaining houseguests. Unable to convince the final [[Power of Veto]] holder [[Makensy Manbeck]] to turn on [[Cam Sullivan-Brown]] instead, Rubina was ultimately evicted by her sole vote. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

I am mildly competitive, but I'm not trying to put a target on my back, so it'll come to play when it's the right time. I'm gonna trust the timing of my life. [[Big Brother 27 (US)]] }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring punishment in ''Big Brother''. It results from a [[Power of Veto]] competition. A HouseGuest who receives this punishment is required to complete a large number of repetitive actions within a limited time frame. Usually if they are unable to complete it they would be ineligible to compete in the next [[Head of Household]] or [[Power of Veto|Veto]] competition. It is usually won in the ''[[Yankee Swap]]'' competition. ==History== ===Big Brother 16 (US)=== [[Cody Calafiore]] received a punishment called penalty kick. This forced him to pull a lever which caused a show to kick him in the butt. For 24 hours, any time a whistle would blow, Cody had to pull the lever 10 times. [[Brittany Martinez]] received a punishment that tasked her with kicking 2,400 soccer goals in just 24 hours. She was not able to go inside until she completed the mission and failing it would result in her having to sit out the next Veto competition. ===Big Brother 17 (US)=== [[Shelli Poole]] had to perform a regimen with a sword 2,400 times in 24 hours. If she failed, then she would be ineligible to compete in the next Veto competition. ===Big Brother 20 (US)=== [[Rockstar Lantry]] received a punishment after the Week 6 Power of Veto competition that required her to wear a ridiculous chef costume and embrace a unique “fitness food” regimen. For a full week, she had to blend special health shakes using a basket of provided food items, drink them, and then run laps around the backyard—leaping over small hurdles as part of the routine. The punishment lasted until her eviction, and she even gave her eviction speech while still in costume. The theme and instructions came from [[Jessie Godderz]], contributing to the season's fitness-oriented punishment theme. ===Big Brother 22 (US)=== [[Bayleigh Dayton]] received the Triathlete Punishment, requiring her to complete 500 laps on a tricycle within 12 hours. If she failed, she would lose the chance to compete in the next Veto competition. ===Big Brother 25 (US)=== [[Izzy Gleicher]] and [[Cameron Hardin]] were dressed in piggy costumes and had to perform a demanding task in the backyard throughout the night. Their task involved making a total of 2,000 trips carrying dirt from one side of the backyard to another. Each trip was counted as two when they walked together. They used small mugs to scoop dirt from a pile, carried it to a trough, and then repeated the process. ===Big Brother 26 (US)=== [[Angela Murray]] faced a grueling task in the backyard, with 12 hours to retrieve 1,000 ping pong balls, one at a time, and deliver them to a container. The challenge required relentless back-and-forth trips across the yard. To make things more difficult, Angela had to periodically submerge herself in a slime bath for decontamination. If she failed to complete the task within the time limit, she would lose her eligibility to compete in the next Head of Household competition. ===Big Brother 27 (US)=== [[Zach Cornell]] and [[Rachel Reilly]] had to complete a punishment task called "Partners in Crime." For the task, they wore prisoner outfits and sat in a small jail cell. When a siren sounded, they had 12 hours to retrieve all the $25,000 money bags from a safe, carry it to a table, and open it. Only four bags contained actual fake cash, while the rest contained exploding blue goop bombs that would splatter on them. Despite the majority suspecting him to be [[The Saboteur|The Accomplice]] on Day 1, Rylie was in a comfortable position as a popular figure in the house being included in [[Heavy Hitters|several]] [[Burger Boys|alliances]]. He also engaged in a [[showmance]] with [[Katherine Woodman]] in which many audience members felt he was too possessive. After having his Week 4 [[Head of Household|HOH]] win [[Invisible HOH|stolen]] by [[Mickey Lee]], he lashed out and became an initial nominee. After [[Lauren Domingue]] won the Week 6 [[Power of Veto|POV]] and vetoed [[Vince Panaro]] against HOH [[Rachel Reilly]]'s wishes, Rachel nominated Rylie in retaliation, despite some voters not being decided. They’re gonna have to try to yank it. They’re gonna try to pull this for me as hard as I can. All y’all out there, I mean to get me out of this place, it’s going to be hard time. '''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' Bashful, extroverted, and extremely excitable
'''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' To be on ''Big Brother'' is a dream. I’ve never felt anything as exciting as this before. This is something you can only dream of, and it’s coming true in this very moment.
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I’m actually a new fan. I just started watching it not that long ago, and I’ve already blistered through about three seasons of it.
'''What’s your biggest strength and your biggest weakness?''' My biggest strength is that I’m extremely competitive. I’m going to try and win all the challenges, or at least the ones I need to. And I think my weakness is I have a loud mouth and I’m not going to back down from anyone in that house. Are you a hero or a villain? I see myself as a hero. But I think a lot of people in the house are going to see me as a villain just because I’m so competitive that I want to win, and I talk a lot of trash.
'''Have you thought about creating a fake identity for the game?''' I actually have a fake identity already. My real name’s not actually Rome, it’s Jack. My best friends have been calling me Rome since before I can even remember. So I went into the house, saying, “Hey, the new best friends I’m gonna make are gonna call me Rome. But my mom, if you ask her, will never call me anything but her sweet Jack.”
'''Do you have a secret you plan on keeping about yourself in the game?''' I think I’m not going to tell everyone my real name right away. I think I want everyone to know me as Rome first. And then the people that are closest to me that I trust can really know that I trust them by calling me Jack.
'''How do you normally handle conflict?''' Conflict resolution is one of my best qualities. I know when to talk to people softly, and I know when to be a little bit more expressive towards them. So, when it comes to conflict, I’m fine with that. But I won’t back down for anyone. If they come into my face, I will not be stepping back from them.
'''Do you have a secret talent or quirk you think will help you in the game?''' I tell people I’m a huge nerd, but no one really knows what that means. One of my biggest things is I collect trading cards in my free time, so it really shows that I’m not just the jock and the athlete that I do actually have that nerdy side that people can trust and say, “Oh, he actually isn’t as we expected.”
'''How will you crush your enemies?''' I’ll crush my enemies by being more confident than them. The way I present myself is everything to me. I walk into every room thinking that I’m the most confident person there, and I can get anything.
'''Are you open to showmances?''' I am open to a showmance. I’ve been single for a long time now, and it’s hard finding love in the real world. So why not do it in the house?

'''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' Fun, chaotic, and loyal.
'''What made you want to spend your summer in the ''Big Brother'' house?''' I wanted to spend my summer in the ''Big Brother'' house because it’s the next great adventure, and I love an adventure!
'''How do you think ''Survivor'' has prepared you for ''Big Brother''?''' On that island, you’re dealing with some big personalities, you’re trying to figure out how things work, and you’re causing a little bit of chaos. And I think those are things that are going to transfer well into the house.
'''What aspects of ''Big Brother'' do you think will be harder than ''Survivor''?''' I think the main thing that’s going to be harder on ''Big Brother'' than ''Survivor'' is the pace. You’re in here for such a long time. I really like to get going, and I’m really going to have to slow myself down just a little bit. Also, being away from my young kids is going to be really tough. It was tough out there on the island for 26 days. Now I’m going to be here all summer, hopefully!
'''What’s one ''Survivor'' skill that you think will translate to the ''Big Brother'' house?''' I think fire making is something that’s…oh, wait, no. [''Laughs''.] Probably relationships with people. Understanding how to bounce back when a relationship goes bad, not take it too personally, but be able to get right back on that horse and let them know we didn’t vote together this time, but that doesn’t mean we can’t vote together next time.
'''What would you anticipate being scarier: Tribal Council or being on the block?''' I think being on the block is going to be scarier than Tribal Council, because Tribal Council is where I do some of my best business. Whereas being on the block, you know you’re one of two people that has a chance of going home. It’s not everybody that could be going home, it’s just you and that one other person.
'''What do you think is your reputation coming into ''Big Brother''?''' I think the reputation I developed in ''Survivor'' is that I can be a chaotic player, and then I can make it hard for other people to play the game they want to play. They have to spend too much time reacting to me. So I need to kind of give the impression, whether it’s true or not, that, “No, I’m easy to play around! You don’t have to worry about me.”

April 23, 2024 - }} '''Secret Story''' is the French version of the international reality series, ''[[Big Brother (franchise)|Big Brother]]''. It was the revived and reformatted version of original French series called [[Loft Story France (franchise)|Loft Story]] and has been airing since 2007. The series has been hosted by [[wikipedia:Benjamin Castaldi|Benjamin Castaldi]] ''(season 1 to 8)'' and [[wikipedia:Christophe Beaugrand|Christophe Beaugrand]] ''(since season 9)''. It has been broadcast on the channel TF1 from 23 June 2007 to 26 September 2014 (season 1 to 8). During the season 9, the eviction episodes were broadcast on TF1 and the highlight episodes were broadcast on NT1. Since the season 10, Secret Story is broadcast on NT1 expect for the premiere which is broadcast on TF1. ==French Series== ===Secret Story Format=== Secret Story takes more or less the basic principles of ''Big Brother'', a reality show created in 1997 by the Dutchman ''John de Mol'', and in this way, comes after the ''Loft Story'', an earlier French adaptation of Big Brother, also hosted by Castaldi in 2001 and 2002 on the channel M6. The game contestants are cut off from the rest of the world during ten to fifteen weeks in a house called "house of secrets", where every room is fitted with video cameras, except the restroom. They have to keep a secret while trying to discover the other contestants' one. ==Differences from Original Big Brother== ===House of Secrets=== [[File:SSFranceHouse.jpg|thumb|225px|The outdoor area of the current Secret Story France house, which is actually built and located on the roof top of a building.]] At the beginning of each season, the "house of secrets" also contains hidden rooms. It contains for example a "Chamber of truths" in the first season (room accessible by pressing a button hidden in the tapestry), a "Cave of love" in the second season (room accessible by a passage in the pool), or "a house of intruders" in the third season (room accessible by a secret passage on the floor). Some "Secret rooms" are also set up for each season where two contestants announced as eliminated to the other candidates have to remain locked up in order to see all their comings and goings through television screens. Other rooms are features of Big Brother, as the "confessional" where each contestant goes every day to give his impression or opinion on events that happen in the house to "The Voice", or a double-door entrance, an intermediary passage between the house and outside, where "nominated" (contestants who have been chosen to leave the house by the others) learn their elimination or reintegration in the house where some contestants can come into contact with other candidates who have already been eliminated through a glass pane. ===The Voice=== An invisible male character named "The Voice" can speak at any time to the contestants through the speakers and give them instructions. This is the voice of the radio host Dominique Duforest. "The Voice" always starts its interventions with the sentence "This is the Voice" and ends with "That is all … for now ". At the beginning of the game, "the Voice" imposes some rules that the contestants have to obey during the whole game if they don't want to be penalized (no more warm water, withdrawal of a contestant's kitty bank for example). During the game, a "red phone" makes its appearance from which "The Voice" can get the contestants that answer win or lose money, give a resident one

{{twists |title = Secret Power Competition |image = Power Path.png |description = Houseguests are given the opportunity to compete for an anonymous special power in the game outside of the traditional HoH/PoV. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} |seasonsappeared = ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''

''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]''}} The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a twist featured in semi-regularly since ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. Spun off from the [[Whacktivity Competition]] introduced in ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'', houseguests are given the chance to compete for a special power to shake up the game. ==History== In ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]'', all houseguests in the game during Week 5 were given the opportunity to compete for one of three special powers: The Disruptor, The Replay, and The Blocker. They would be won by [[David Alexander]], [[Dani Briones]] and [[Christmas Abbott]] respectively. In ''[[Big Brother 25 (US)]]'', America voted for four houseguests to compete for the BB Power of Invincibility in Week 4. [[Cirie Fields]], [[Cory Wurtenberger]], [[Jag Bains]] and [[Matt Klotz]] were chosen by America, and Matt would go on to win the power. In ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'', any houseguest who voted "yes" to [[AINSLEY]]'s morality test during the premiere was given the opportunity to compete for in a special "Upgrade Competition". The houseguests were split into two different premiere groups, with one chance to vote in AINSLEY's test for each group. In the first group, [[Angela Murray]], [[Joseph Rodriguez]], [[Makensy Manbeck]] and [[Rubina Bernabe]] passed the test, while only [[Leah Peters]] and [[Quinn Martin]] did so in the second group. Makensy and Quinn would go onto win their respective competitions, earning themselves [[Diamond Power of Veto|America's Veto]] and the [[Invisible HOH|Deepfake HOH]] powers respectively. In ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'', the houseguests had to split up during the premiere into two different groups. Each group had the opportunity to compete for a game changing power. [[Zach Cornell]] was in the first group that had to rescue Julie from The Mastermind. He won $10,000 publicly, and it was later privately revealed to him that he has the ability to use this money to buy their way off the block as a final nominee by bribing the HOH. [[Jimmy Heagerty]] was in the second group that had to reclaim the HOH Relic, and he won power was to publicly choose which four houseguests would be eligible to play in the first HOH. Unlike the other powers, his had no added secret benefit. The competition would appear once again in BB27, during Week 2 in a similar format to BB22. Within [[The Black Box]] competition, one houseguest would win HOH while other powers would be up for grabs. [[Keanu Soto]] won a Veto Advantage, [[Kelley Jorgensen]] won the chance to earn a [[Double Power of Veto|second POV]], and [[Mickey Lee]] won an [[Invisible HOH|HOH Takeover]]. ==List of {{PAGENAME}}s== {| style="width: 18em; border: 1px solid; width: 60%; text-align:center;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Name ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Available Power ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Winner ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Used? |- | rowspan="3" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 22 | rowspan="3" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 5 | rowspan="3" style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" |"[[The Black Box|The Basement of Power]]" | style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);" | '''The Blocker''' | style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);" |

{| style="color:#3a3a3a;" |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6howie.jpg|Howie Gordon|Howie|9999CC|Jury}} |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6james.jpg|James Rhine|James|9999CC|Jury}} |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6janelle.jpg|Janelle Pierzina|Janelle|9999CC|Jury}} |} {| style="color:#3a3a3a;" |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6kaysar.jpg|Kaysar Ridha|Kaysar|666666|Evicted}} |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6rachel.jpg|Rachel Plencner|Rachel|9999CC|Jury}} |{{WhichBoxSmallSquare|Bb6sarah.jpg|Sarah Hrejsa|Sarah|666666|Evicted}} |}
===Creation=== The Sovereign Six was created in opposition to [[The Friendship]] alliance. The alliance was formed by [[Kaysar Ridha]] and later joined by [[Janelle Pierzina]], [[Howie Gordon]], [[Rachel Plencner]], [[James Rhine]], and [[Sarah Hrejsa]] beginning in Week 3 when they successfully [[Backdoor|backdoored]] [[Eric Littmann]] the leader of The Friendship. ===Fallout=== The power continued to shift week by week, but ultimately the downfall of the Sovereign Six came when [[Maggie Ausburn]] convinced [[Howie Gordon]] to turn on [[James Rhine]], who at that point, had become distrustful to the alliance for attempting to play both sides to save himself. Howie decided to nominate James and [[Sarah Hrejsa]]. This is known as one of the worst moves in the history of Big Brother. This forced the Sovereign Six into a minority position for the remainder of the game and gave The Friendship numbers in the jury. This caused James and Sarah to defect from the alliance, and Sarah was evicted. Even with [[Kaysar Ridha]] returning to the game, the alliance still remained a minority, especially after Kasayar gave up the HOH competition to The Friendship member [[Jennifer Vasquez]], who would betray him by getting him evicted that week. ===Destruction=== The power continued to change week by week, and [[Janelle Pierzina]] was able to be the last remaining Sovereign Six member left in the house, making it to the final 3. Janelle planned to bring [[Ivette Corredero]] to the finals over [[Maggie Ausburn]]. Janelle’s plan could’ve resulted in her winning the game. Janelle would get the jury votes of Howie, [[Rachel Plencner]], [[April Lewis]] (despite being a member of the opposing alliance revealed post-season she would’ve voted Janelle over Ivette in a final 2) and likely James. On Finale Night, however, Janelle failed to win the final HOH and was evicted after Ivette (who won the Final HOH) cast the sole vote to evict her on her, placing 3rd and becoming the 7th and final member of the jury. ==Big Brother 7 (US)== ===Members===

Showmance.head:
[[File:BrendonRachelBB13.jpg|thumb|Brenchel, a common example of a showmance.]] A '''{{PAGENAME}}''' (a portmanteau of the words show and romance) is a type of relationship formed in the ''Big Brother'' house. These involve two House Guests involved in a romantic and flirtatuous relationship, usually for entertainment purposes. However, many reality shows involve showmances. Some of the most memorable showmances are [[Brendon Villegas|Brendon]] and [[Rachel Reilly|Rachel]] ([[Big Brother 12|Seasons 12]] and [[Big Brother 13|13]]) (Brenchel), [[Jeff Schroeder|Jeff]] and [[Jordan Lloyd|Jordan]] ([[Big Brother 11|Seasons 11]] and [[Big Brother 13|13]]) (JeJo), [[McCrae Olson|McCrae]] and [[Amanda Zuckerman|Amanda]] ([[Big Brother 15|Season 15]]) (McCranda), & [[Jessica Graf|Jessica]] and [[Cody Nickson|Cody]] ([[Big Brother 19|Season 19]]) (Jody).

==Showmance(s) by Seasons==
This list only shows showmances in the season they originated in, as some seasons have had both showmance partners return, where the showmance then continued, such as Jeff and Jordan from BB11, and Brendon and Rachel from BB12, who all returned for BB13, where they continued their showmances. However if one person returned and had a showmance with different people in their original seasons than in their second seasons, it will be counted, such as Mike "Boogie" and Dr. Will showmancing Krista and Shannon during BB2 and Erika and Janelle during BB7. The same applies for if one person has a showmance with multiple people in the same season, such as Jessie having a showmance with both Natalie and Lydia during BB11.

[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' }}'''Solitary Confinement''' is a recurring punishment in ''Big Brother''. It results from a [[Power of Veto]] competition. A HouseGuest who receives this punishment is required to spend 24 hours inside a designated room. A camp toilet and [[slop]] (and in some cases bread) are provided. It is usually won in the ''[[Yankee Swap]]'' competition. ==History== ===Big Brother 7 (US)=== [[Danielle Reyes]] agreed to spend 24 hours inside the gym, which had been converted into a solitary confinement room. ===Big Brother 12 (US)=== [[Hayden Moss]] spent 24 hours inside the Have-Not Room. ===Big Brother 13 (US)=== [[Shelly Moore]] spent 24 hours inside the Have-Not Room. ===Big Brother 14 (US)=== [[Dan Gheesling]] agreed to spend 24 hours inside the Have-Not Room for a Solitary Dance Party. ===Big Brother 15 (US)=== [[Judd Daugherty]] spent 24 hours inside the lounge. An alarm clock that was set to go off every nine minutes was placed inside the lounge. ===Big Brother 23 (US)=== [[Xavier Prather]] spent 24 hours inside the Have-Not Room. ===Big Brother 25 (US)=== [[Felicia Cannon]] spent 24 hours inside the comic bedroom. ===Big Brother 26 (US)=== [[Joseph Rodriguez]] spent 24 hours inside the "Mattrix", which was the Have-Not Room. Slice.head:
[[File:Slice 3.png|thumb|200px]]
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a specialty television network in Canada, owned by Corus Entertainment. It was the original home of [[Big Brother Canada]] (BBCAN), the country's English-language version of Big Brother, between 2013 and 2014. It has also aired spin-off programming to both BBCAN and [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|Big Brother U.S.]] (BBUS), including Big Brother: After Dark and [[Big Brother Canada Sideshow|Big Brother Canada Side Show]].

Slice broadcasts lifestyle and entertainment programming aimed at women, such as the Real Housewives franchise, including local adaptation The Real Housewives of Toronto.
==Association with Big Brother==
===Big Brother U.S.===
Slice's sister network, [[Global]], has aired BBUS in Canada from its inception in 2000 until 2026. Since 2007, Slice has carried BBUS spin-off Big Brother: After Dark, a nightly three-hour television broadcast of its live feeds.

===Big Brother Canada===
Following the success of BBUS on Global, Slice announced on May 31, 2012 that it had commissioned BBCAN<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thetvwatercooler.com/2012/05/big-brother-canada-shaw-global-slice/|title=
Shaw to launch Big Brother Canada|publisher=The TV Watercooler|date=31 May 2012|accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref>, the first ever English-language adaptation of Big Brother in Canada.

The [[Big Brother Canada 1|first season]] of BBCAN began on February 27th, 2013, accompanied by its own version of Big Brother: After Dark, which also aired on Slice.

Slice renewed BBCAN for a [[Big Brother Canada 2|second season]], which began on March 5th, 2014, with After Dark returning. For this season, Slice also launched a second spin-off, Big Brother Canada Side Show, which aired once a week. It featured host [[Arisa Cox]] and two regular panellists discussing the past week's action, catching up with the latest evictees, and interviewing special guests.

After the first two seasons of BBCAN proved successful, it was announced in 2014 that BBCAN would be moving to Global<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.ca/2014/06/04/global-showcase-shaw-fall-tv-2014-15-lineup_n_5447282.html|title=
Global TV Lineup Fall 2014-15: Shaw Media Making Bold Moves|publisher=Huffington Post|date=4 June 2014|accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref> for its [[Big Brother Canada 3|third season]]. However, Slice remained the home of the After Dark and Side Show spin-offs during the third and [[Big Brother Canada 4|fourth]] seasons.

Both spin-offs were cancelled ahead of BBCAN's [[Big Brother Canada 5|fifth season]] in 2017, bringing Slice's association with the show to an end.

Steve was a covert member of the [[Scamper Squad]] who also fostered a side alliance called [[Rockstars]] with [[John McGuire]]. While [[The Sixth Sense]] was still alive, [[Vanessa Rousso]] decided to bring Steve into a side alliance with Austin and the twins (which eventually became the Scamper Squad). Steve was able to use this collaboration to further himself in the game. For most of the game he was under the radar and followed people, mainly Vanessa, but that was part of his strategy. However, Steve secretly wanted to evict Vanessa, fearing he could not beat her, but could not do so until the [[Austwins]] alliance was broken up. Steve targeted the trio during his Week 11 HOH, culminating in [[Julia Nolan|Julia Nolan's]] eviction. He played more aggressively at the end of the game, winning three out of the last four HOHs and being the sole vote to evict Vanessa at Final 3. After making it to the Final Two, the Jury accused him of floating throughout the game. However, Steve argued that he did not float because of his under-the-radar gameplay, and he made moves that benefited him throughout the game. He compared his own choices to [[Liz Nolan|Liz Nolan's]], as she followed [[Austin Matelson]] and Vanessa throughout her time in the Big Brother house. {{Canada}} }}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Power of Veto]] and [[Head of Household]] competition. ==Rules== In this competition, houseguests look through an area for letters. One at a time, they must bring them back to their board. Once brought back to their board, they must spell a word out and try to achieve the longest, correctly spelled word, which will be revealed one at a time. For [[Big Brother 17]] and [[Big Brother 18 (US)|Big Brother 18]], each letter was assigned a point value, so instead of the longest word, the contestants need to come up with a word with the highest point value. If there is a tie, the houseguest who did it the quickest will win. ==History== ===United States=== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 11]]'', during Week 1. [[Russell Kairouz]] won the competition, winning the first PoV of the season. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 12]]'', during Week 1 once again. [[Brendon Villegas]] won the competition, winning the first PoV of the season. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 13]]'', was the competition's next appearance. [[Brendon Villegas]] once again won the competition, winning his first PoV of that season. He used the exact same word as he used in the previous season. On ''[[Big Brother 15]]'', the houseguests competed in this competition, during the first week. [[McCrae Olson]] won the competition, winning his first ever PoV, alongside his first HoH win. On ''[[Big Brother 16]]'', the houseguests competed in this competition, during the first week. [[Donny Thompson]] won the competition, winning his first ever PoV. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 17]]'', during Week 1. [[Steve Moses]], eventual winner, won the competition, securing his first PoV win of the summer. In its next appearance, ''[[Big Brother 18]]'', [[Paulie Calafiore]] won the competition, winning his first PoV of the summer. After skipping the next summer edition, it reappeared on the special ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)|celebrity season]]'', where [[Shannon Elizabeth]] won her first PoV and became the first female of U.S. franchise to win this competition. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)|Big Brother 26]]'', during Week 1, [[Lisa Weintraub]] won the competition, securing her first and only PoV win of the summer. {{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]], [[Have/Have-Not Competition|Have/Have-Not]], and [[Power of Veto]] competition. ==Rules== Regular Format: #The competition is split into lanes for each participating houseguest, with a barrel of liquid at one end and an empty container with a ping pong ball inside. Typically, at least one more, smaller container will also be present. The lanes are heavily greased and often on a slope. #Each houseguest is given a scoop, and must use it to transport liquid from the barrel to the container at the other end of their lane. Along the way, they must try to avoid slipping and spilling their liquid. As the container fills up, the ping pong ball inside will begin to rise, making it possible to pull it out of the top of the container once it has been sufficiently filled up. #The first houseguest to pull their ball out of the main container will win either Head of Household or Veto, depending on the purpose of the competition. ##Conversely, houseguests may opt to fill up one of the smaller containers also present in order to earn a smaller reward, often with the catch that doing so will eliminate them from the competition. Rewards include safety for the week, a small cash prize, or an advantage in the main competition (such as larger scoops). However, in ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'', ''[[Big Brother 25 (US)]]'', and ''[[Big Brother 28 (US)]]'', there was an alternate format: Each participating houseguest will enter the room separately, they must collect water with different tubes which will shoot out the water randomly and then fill up the water tank in the fastest time in order to win the Veto. ==History== ===United States=== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]'', during Week 9. [[Zach Swerdzewski]] won the competition, winning his first HoH of the season, while [[Eric Stein]] won a phone call from home, which he then gave to [[Jessica Hughbanks]]. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)]]'', during Week 8. [[Kevin Campbell]] won, securing his first HoH win of the summer. Appearing again on ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]'', the houseguests competed during Week 7. [[Jeff Schroeder]] won the competition, winning his first HoH of the season. On the following season, ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'', houseguests competed during Week 6. [[Shane Meaney]] won the competition, winning his second HoH of the summer, while [[Mike Malin]] won $10,000, and [[Britney Haynes]] won immunity for the week. The competition reappeared on ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]'', during Week 2, as a duo competition. [[Aaryn Gries]] and [[Jeremy McGuire]] won the competition, but Jeremy gave the HoH to Aaryn, making this her first HoH of the season. On the following season, ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', houseguests competed during Week 10. [[Caleb Reynolds]] won the competition, securing his third HoH win of the summer, while [[Derrick Levasseur]] won $5,000 and 5,000 Hollas as a Luxury prize. {{United Kingdom}} }}'''Somewhere Over The Veto''' (known infamously as the '''Clown Shoe Veto''') is a recurring [[Head of Household]], [[Power of Veto]], and [[Power_of_Veto#United_Kingdom|Gamechanger]] competition. Due to its quick speed, the competition is usually completed in under 5 minutes. It is traditionally used as a live Veto competition during [[Double Eviction|Double Evictions]] for this reason. ==Rules== #The competition area is split into six lanes, with a buzzer at one end, some kind of barricade in the middle, and a ball pit at the other end. Buried within the ball pit is a certain amount of a themed item. Typically, only two or three of this item are present in each ball pit. Additionally, a veto symbol will be hanging on the wall of each pit ##Occasionally, the ball pit may also contain "dud" copies of the item in a different color. #The competing houseguests all start next to their buzzer. On "go", they must race across the backyard to their ball pit and begin to search for the object in question. Once one of the object is found, the houseguest must race back to their buzzer, deposit the item, and return to the ball pit to continue searching. Houseguests are only allowed to carry one of the item across the backyard at a time. #Once the houseguest had found and deposited the final of the object in their pit, they must return to their ball pit, grab the veto symbol, and return and hit their buzzer. The first houseguest to hit the buzzer wins the veto. ==List of ''Somewhere Over The Veto'' Competitions== ===United States=== {|class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Winner |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 10 | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 7 | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "Veto In A Haystack" | style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);"|

[[Xavier Prather]] |TwitterUserName = |InstagramUserName = taylorhale |theamazingrace = {{otherfandom|amazingrace|Kyland_&_Taylor}} |thetraitors = {{otherfandom|thetraitors|Taylor_Hale}} }}'''Taylor Mackenzie Dickens Hale''' is the [[Winners (US)|winner]] of ''[[Big Brother 24 (US)]]'' and the runner-up of ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]''. An underdog at the start of ''Big Brother 24 (US)'' who almost got evicted from Week 1 because of the numerous lies and negative perception mostly started by [[Paloma Aguilar]], Taylor eventually gained footing in the game because of her superb social skills, competition wins both by herself and her alliance [[The Leftovers]], and targets being prioritized over her whenever she was on the nomination block for eviction. While she lost some of her allies along the way, her great social game, persistence and Head of Household wins allowed her to reach the finale. She was also able to win back many of the people who bullied her with her kindness, which would help her with jury votes. On finale night, she gave a speech that cumulated her entire story with the resilience she had to bounce back from many adversities. She was then crowned the winner with a landslide vote of 8-1. It was later revealed that Taylor also won [[America's Favorite Houseguest]], making her the first ever Black woman to win a civilian ''Big Brother (US)'' season and the first houseguest to both win the game and AFH award in the same season. Returning for ''Reindeer Games,'' Taylor started in a good spot, being aligned with [[Xavier Prather]], [[Danielle Reyes]], and [[Josh Martinez]]. Despite keeping out of most danger by never competing in Santa's Showdown and displaying well-versed strategy, Taylor would still have several rivalries along the way such as [[Cody Calafiore]] and [[Frankie Grande]]. After making it to the Reindeer Games, she would defeat Frankie in the semifinals to advance to the Final 2 before losing to [[Nicole Franzel]], resulting in Taylor finishing as the runner-up of the season. ==Biography== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Biography'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from Parade.com''

In some seasons, they are also dunked into water to increase difficulty. Slime, rain or other liquids may be splatted onto the [[Housemates|houseguests]], similar to [[The Wall]]. After a while, the competition may be made more difficult by forcing the houseguests sit on whatever is below their disc. T'kor played a covert game as she found herself in the middle of warring alliances during the initial weeks. Together with her loyal ally and friend in [[Kimo Apaka]], she was also able to form an [[The Visionaries|alliance]] with [[Quinn Martin]], who then leaked the existence of [[The Pentagon]], a core alliance of a larger [[The Collective]], which made her realize she was unknowingly just being used as an extra number. This caused both her and Kimo to switch their votes to [[Cedric Hodges]] and kept [[Rubina Bernabe]] safe, with Rubina joining the duo as a loyal ally throughout the rest of the game. T'kor eventually became the Head of Household on week 6, but her attempt of being in the good graces of the house resulted to her ally [[Tucker Des Lauriers]] in becoming a pawn, which was a strategic oversight as her enemies evicted him when he was unable to gain any safety. After, others started seeing [[The Trio]] as a threat for being a voting block that would never turn on each other, which started to shake T'kor's position. '''Describe yourself in 3 words:''' If I had to describe myself in three words, it would be “all in one.”
'''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' It feels amazing to be on ''Big Brother''! It is literally a dream come true.
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I am a big fan of ''Big Brother''. I’ve been a casual viewer of ''Big Brother'' since I was a young girl. I fell off a little bit when I was in college, but because of a really bad breakup, for some reason, ''Big Brother'' was the only thing I could binge-watch for like six months. I watch episodes. I am not a live streamer.
'''What’s your strategy going into the house?''' My strategy going to ''Big Brother'' is called the “Big B Blowout.” I have this weird game plan that makes sense only in my head, but I’m very excited to see if it works out. The Big B Blowout is basically having a three-part team where there’s a team captain for the floaters, and there’s a team captain for the two tethered teams. And with that, we’re just going to use each other where there’s going to be a Final Three, and then we’re going to all work together with our teams to maneuver the house, the votes, and the competitions.
'''What are you going to bring to ''Big Brother'' that we’ve never seen before?''' I think I’m going to bring realness to the show. I think I’m going to bring light to the show, and I also think I’m going to bring love to the show. Something that viewers at home want to see, someone who can be relatable, someone who feels like I’m your sister, maybe even your cousin.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' The biggest misconception people have about me is that I’m all sweet and innocent until I open my mouth!
'''Are you a hero or a villain?''' I am a hero at heart. But actually, I’m just coming out of my villain era, so I might have to go back in. [''Flexes and grunts''.]
'''Why are you going to be the next winner of ''Big Brother''?''' I am going to be the next winner of ''Big Brother'' because I am that girl! I am able to be strategic, I am able to be social, and not only that, I am also able to be very competitive.{{cite web|url=https://parade.com/tv/big-brother-28-cast-photos-bios-interview-2026|title=Meet the ‘Big Brother’ Season 28 Cast — Including a Surprising ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ All-Star|date=7 July 2026|accessdate=7 July 2026|website=parade.com}} |} ==Player History - ''Big Brother 28 (US)''== ===Competition History=== {| style="border: 1px solid; width: 55%; text-align:center;" | rowspan=5 style="text-align:center; background-color:#CCCCCC;color:#3a3a3a;" |'''Week 1''' | style="width:40%;background-color:#FFD700;color:#3a3a3a;" | '''Immunity Part 1''' | style="width:35%;background-color:#FFD700;color:#3a3a3a;" | '''Win''' |- | style="background-color:#FFD700;color:#3a3a3a;" | '''{{nowrap|Immunity Part 2}}''' | style="background-color:#CC6666;color:#3a3a3a;" | '''Loss''' |- | style="background-color:#9966CC;color:#3a3a3a;" | '''HO

The Saboteur.head:
{{twists | image= [[file:Bb12saboteur.jpg|250px]] | description= A secret houseguest that would sabotage the house in order to win money instead of win the game. | countriesappeared={{United States}} | seasonsappeared= ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]''
''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]''
''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'' }}'''The Saboteur''' was a twist on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]''. It was later reintroduced on ''[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]'' as the '''AI Instigator'''. It returned in ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'' as the '''Secret Accomplice'''. The Saboteur was to wreak havoc on the houseguests by sabotaging a group, an individual, or the house as a whole by causing paranoia or physically sabotaging the game. The Saboteur would be granted $50,000 if he or she made it to the half-way point in the game, five weeks, undetected. The first Saboteur was [[Annie Whittington]] and after [[Matt Hoffman]] opened [[Pandora's Box]], the second Saboteur was [[Ragan Fox]]. The Saboteur communicated to the houseguests through the television in the living room while disguised behind static and appeared only as a silhouette. The Saboteur would threaten the houseguests and warn about upcoming sabotage. ==Background== ===[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]=== {| class="mw-collapsible" style="margin:auto; font-size: 8pt;" |- ! style="background-color: rgb(229, 228, 226); color:#3a3a3a;" | ''{{PAGENAME}} Press Release'' |- | style="padding:0.2em 0.5em;" | ''Retrieved from CBS.com''
The producers of BIG BROTHER are implementing a major twist for this season's batch of Houseguests that will top all past seasons. One Houseguest, known as the Big Brother Saboteur, will enter the house to play their own game, unbeknownst to their fellow competitors. The Saboteur's mission will be to carry out viewer suggestions on how best to disrupt the lives of fellow players. Upon moving into the house on premiere night, Houseguests will discover that one of them is not really there to win the game, but rather to sabotage their fellow players. While the saboteur's identity will remain a secret to the Houseguests, America will learn his/her identity on Thursday, July 15, during the first LIVE show. At that time, fans can begin offering suggestions for how the saboteur should disrupt the game. The longer the saboteur is able to maintain their anonymity while carrying out their fan-inspired sabotage, the more financially rewarding it will be for them. For instructions on how to submit suggestions to the Big Brother Saboteur, visit http://www.cbs.com/bbtwist. "We've inserted a game piece into the show this season that will make life for the Houseguests harder than ever before," stated Allison Grodner, Executive Producer of BIG BROTHER. "This is a twist that will wreak havoc on the house and the audience will be a part of it."https://www.welovebigbrother.com/who-is-the-big-brother-12-saboteur-updated-twist-details/ |} [[Annie Whittington]] was chosen to be the first Saboteur. Had she made it to Week Five, she would have collected $50,000 for being the Saboteur. However, she was evicted after committing only three acts of sabotage. One of the main reasons for Annie's eviction was because of suspicion of her being the Saboteur. After [[Matt Hoffman]] opened [[Pandora's Box]], a new Saboteur was released upon the house. The new Saboteur was decided by an America's Choice vote. [[Ragan Fox]] was chosen to be the new Saboteur. Ragan was tasked with commuting three acts of sabotage for two weeks, and if he stayed in the house for those two weeks, he would receive $20,000 as a reward. Ragan successfully completed the task and claimed the cash prize. ===[[Big Brother 26 (US)]]=== [[File:AI Insitgator.png|250px|right]] During Week 5, America voted for one houseguest to become the AI Instigator, who can spread chaos and misinformation throughout the house by framing their fellow houseguests with Deepfake Clones from the Proto Box, similar to how the [[Invisible HOH|Deepfake HOH]] operate

The alliance consisted of [[Enzo Palumbo]], [[Hayden Moss]], [[Lane Elenburg]], and [[Matt Hoffman]]. The Brigade, particularly Matt, pioneered the use of "parachute" alliances, where each member formed a duo alliance with a separate houseguest outside of their core group. This strategy allowed them to control every vote throughout the season, ensuring that none of them would be evicted if nominated. However, in Week 7, the Brigade turned against Matt, fearing he had built too many connections outside the alliance. The remaining three members continued to dominate the season in competitions, nominations, and eviction votes, ultimately making up the final three. Hayden defeated Lane in a 4-3 vote, securing his victory. ==Members==

==History== ===Creation=== The Brigade was formed on Day 2 when the four members gathered in Hayden's HOH room. During this meeting, Enzo assigned each member a nickname, solidifying their alliance. ====Nicknames and Roles==== Enzo took on the role of the ringleader, bringing the team together and dubbing himself "The Meow Meow." Hayden was given the nickname "The Animal," reflecting his competitive spirit. Lane, known for his strength, was called "The Beast," while Matt, recognized for his strategic thinking, was aptly named "The Brains." ===Strategy === The Brigade played a low-profile game, avoiding the spotlight while gradually eliminating their threats and winning crucial competitions. They managed to remain undetected, with Hayden securing 4 Head of Household wins and 1 Power of Veto, Matt winning 2 HOHs, Lane winning 1 HOH, and Enzo winning 1 POV. Each member also formed a "parachute" alliance with another houseguest to ensure their safety if any of them were nominated. Hayden aligned with Kristen, Lane with Britney, Matt with Ragan, and Enzo would have chosen Monet, had she not been evicted in Week 2. These duo alliances helped deflect attention from the Brigade until Andrew exposed Hayden and Kristen's showmance, leading to both being nominated against each other. The Brigade successfully avoided having two members on the block against each other until Week 6, when Brendon chose Matt as Ragan's replacement nominee opposite Lane. ===Fallout=== Enzo informed Matt that he would vote against him when Brendon selected Matt as the replacement nominee to sit opposite Lane on the nomination block, unaware that Matt secretly held the [[Diamond Power of Veto]]. Since his first appearance, Zingbot has become a well-liked figure. His appearance is widely anticipated by the houseguests each season, and the phrase "zing" has entered the house lexicon. To see a list of all his zings, click [[List of Zings|here]]. ==History== Zingbot first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', waking up the final eight houseguests by surprise in the morning before zinging them. He later made a cameo appearance in the audience during the season's finale. Zingbot's next appearance was on ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]''. After zinging the final eight houseguests, he revealed that he was looking to get married, challenging the houseguests to build him a wife in the "Bride of Zingbot" Veto competition, which was won by [[Jeff Schroeder]]. During Zingbot's appearance on ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'', he zinged the final eleven houseguests and then challenged the houseguests to help him create a baby to add to his family in the "Birth of Zingbot" competition, won by [[Frank Eudy]]. "Zingbot 4000", or "Baby Zingbot" an actor in a much smaller costume, appeared at the end of the challenge. Both Zingbot 3000 and Zingbot 4000 returned to the house during Week 9 ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]'' to celebrate Zingbot 4000's first birthday in the "Happy Zing Day" challenge, won by [[Amanda Zuckerman]]. Zingbot appeared by himself on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', but instead of zinging the final eight houseguests, instead complimented them and gave them "props." Comedian Kathy Griffin entered the house and revealed that Zingbot had malfunctioned, delivering the zings that Zingbot could not to half of the houseguests. After competing in the "Zingbot Reboot" competition, winner [[Frankie Grande]] was successfully able to fix Zingbot and allow him to deliver zings to the remaining houseguests. Zingbot re-entered the house during ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]'', newly minted as the Zingbot 9000. After zinging the remaining eight houseguests, Zingbot revealed he had split from his wife and asked the houseguests to help him re-enter the dating scene in the "[[Morph 'O' Matic|Newly Zingle]]" competition, won by [[Vanessa Rousso]]. During Zingbot's next appearance on ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', he returned to the house and revealed his campaign to run for president. The houseguests assisted him with his presidential campaign in the "[[Yankee Swap|Zingbot for President]]" competition, won by [[Victor Arroyo]]. Zingbot also appeared in the audience during the season's finale. Zingbot first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'' in the audience of the first double eviction. He entered the house properly during week 8 and revealed that he had successfully been elected President of Planet Zing. After zinging the remaining nine houseguests, he asked them to help him return to Planet Zing in the "[[Slippery Slope|Home Zing Home]]" competition, won by [[Jason Dent]].
