| seasonsappeared= ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]'' - present
}}The '''Unitard '''is a recurring item in American version of ''Big Brother.'' It is attire that is usually a form of punishment that a housemate can receive as a result of a [[Power of Veto]] competition (and in some cases a [[Head of Household]] competition). The houseguest that earns it will usually have it wear it for the remaining duration of the week or for seven days. The notable '''Red Unitard''' was used in seasons 8 through 10, and a different version has appeared in every subsequent season. It is typically earned in the ''[[Yankee Swap]]'' competition.
==History==
===Big Brother 8 (US)===
The unitard made its first appearance in [[Big Brother 8 (US)|season 8]], where it was won by [[Jen Johnson]] as a result of the ''Cutthroat Christmas'' [[Power of Veto]] competition in Week 2.
===Big Brother 9 (US)===
The unitard was earned by [[Sheila Kennedy]] in the Week 4 Power of Veto competition, ''Color of Veto''.
===Big Brother 10 (US)===
The unitard was earned by [[Michelle Costa]] in the Week 4 Power of Veto competition, ''Big Brother Slapshot''.
===Big Brother 11 (US)===
This was the first variation of the unitard. It featured oversized goggles, a black cape, and gold shorts with "Captain Unitard" written across the front of the top. It was earned by [[Lydia Tavera]] in the Head of Household competition, ''HOH Invitational Golf Tournament'', in Week 6.
===Big Brother 12 (US)===
This was the second variation of the unitard, which was tie-dyed and dubbed the "Hippietard". It was earned by [[Kristen Bitting]] in the Week 4 Power of Veto competition, ''The Wizards of Pinball''.
===Big Brother 13 (US)===
This was the third variation of the unitard, which was green, adorned with a pink tutu and a dunce cap, and had "I'm with stupid" written on the front. It was called the "Humilitard" and was earned by [[Jordan Lloyd]] in the Week 6 Power of Veto competition, ''Big Brother Cornhole''.
===Big Brother 14 (US)===
The fourth variation was won by [[Frank Eudy]] in the Week 4 Power of Veto competition, ''Field of Veto''. This version was purple with "BBU" written on the front and was adorned with a blue and white skirt. It was called the "Spiritard".
===Big Brother 15 (US)===
[[Candice Stewart]] was given a clown unitard, or "Clownitard", to wear as a punishment after the Week 6 Power of Veto competition, ''Frog Darts''.
===Big Brother 16 (US)===
[[Nicole Franzel]] was given a "Germitard" after winning it in the Week 4 Power of Veto competition, ''BB Cup''. The Germitard was a German folk costume and came with a large sausage attached to a pitchfork and a beer stein.
===Big Brother 17 (US)===
[[Jackie Ibarra]] was given a "Knight in Shining Armortard" after winning it in the Week 6 Power of Veto competition, ''Game of Throws''. The Knight in Shining Armortard was a silver unitard with a helmet, knight armor, and a shield. It also came with [[Vanessa Rousso]] becoming her "squire" and being shackled together with her for the next 24 hours, cleaning Jackie's shield, armor, and helmet. After the 24 hours were up, Vanessa was allowed to remove the squire costume, but Jackie had to continue wearing the armor for the rest of the week.
===Big Brother 18 (US)===
[[Nicole Franzel]] was given a Super Safety Costume after winning it in [[America's Care Package]] in Week 8, along with immunity for the week. The SSC is made up of an orange unitard with a yellow cape and a traffic cone hat, along with reflective tape that can light up.
[[Corey Brooks]] was given an American flag-themed unitard dubbed the "Patriotard" in the Week 8 Power of Veto competition, ''[[Zingbot Competition|Zingbot for President]]''. It came with a ballot box glove, a bald eagle puppet, and an American flag-themed top hat.

After [[Frank Eudy]] won HOH, the alliance was kept safe due and [[Wil Heuser]] was evicted. After [[Shane Meaney]] won HOH, the alliance decided to turn on and target Frank and Mike to make the first move against the other side of the house. Shane decided to nominate them alongside each other. This angered the duo as they fought to stay in the house. However to no avail as Mike was evicted. During the [[Double Eviction]] the alliance gained power once again with [[Ian Terry]] winning HOH. After Frank won the POV, the alliance decided to evict his best ally, [[Ashley Iocco]]. ===Dan’s Funeral=== Following Ashley’s eviction, outsider Frank won HOH. He originally targeted [[Dan Gheesling]] whom he blamed for his allies' eviction. He decided to nominate Dan and [[Danielle Murphree]]. Due to [[Pandora's Box]], Ian gained an additional POV. With this in mind the alliance made a plan to throw the veto to [[Britney Haynes]] or Shane to force Frank to nominate a houseguest outside of the alliance. However in the POV competition after Dan went against the plan and other outsider [[Jenn Arroyo]] won the POV, the alliance was angered. It didn’t help that Dan had to do a 24-hour solitary confinement punishment. However, Dan had one last trick. After finishing his punishment Dan decided to host a house meeting which he called his “funeral”. In which he threw Britney and Ian under the bus to Frank and Jenn. After giving a huge pitch to the both of them, he was successful as Jenn saved Dan and Frank targeted Britney. Ultimately, Britney was evicted by a vote of 4-1, being the first member of the alliance to be evicted. ===Dan’s Betrayals=== Following Britney’s eviction, Ian won HOH. Despite his best ally being evicted last week. He still decided he wanted to keep the quack pack and he nominated Frank and Jenn. Despite Dan and Danielle making a deal with the duo, they went back on it and finally evicted Frank. However it was announced that it was a double eviction. Dan went in to win HOH. Originally secretly targeting Ian for being a big threat. His plan was foiled as Ian won the POV. Instead he opted to evict [[Joe Arvin]]. Following Joe’s eviction, Ian won HOH. {{United States}} }} '''Triple Evictions''' occur on ''Big Brother'' to send three houseguests home in a single week. They are similar to [[Double Eviction]]s, in that they involve an additional eviction cycle during the same night; however, in a Triple Eviction, two people are evicted in the second cycle, resulting in three houseguests leaving the game in total. During a Triple Eviction, one [[Head of Household]] (HOH) is named, and they must nominate three houseguests for eviction. A [[Power of Veto]] competition follows—where the HOH is not allowed to compete—and then the Power of Veto Ceremony is held. The houseguests then cast their votes to '''''save''''' one of the nominees. The two nominees who receive the fewest votes are subsequently evicted. The first Triple Eviction occurred in ''[[Big Brother Canada 3]]'' and returned in ''[[Big Brother Canada 5]]'', ''[[Big Brother Canada 6]]'', and ''[[Big Brother Canada 10]]''. The first instance of a Triple Eviction on [[Big Brother U.S. (franchise)|BBUS]] took place during the finale of ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)]]''. Although not officially called a Triple Eviction, the format was quite similar. For the second eviction cycle of the night, the final four houseguests competed in the Final HOH competition. The winner had to evict two houseguests, leaving one to join them in the Final Two. As this occurred during the final eviction cycle, no Power of Veto competition was held. This format returned in ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2 (US)]]'', becoming the standard format for the final week of the American Celebrity seasons. The first officially branded Triple Eviction in the United States took place during ''[[Big Brother 22 (US)]]''. Unlike the ''Big Brother Canada'' format, the US version featured two Fast Forward eviction cycles in one night, instead of a single cycle with two evictions. ==History== ==US Results== ===Civilian=== {| class="wikitable" style="margin: auto; text-align: center; font-size: 8pt; height:60px; line-height:18px;" ! rowspan=2|Season ! rowspan=2|Day ! October 17, 2003 |filmingrun = July 30, 2003 - August 8, 2003 |sponsor = [[File:O2.png|20px]] |castphoto = [[File:TBBUK Cast in House.jpg|200px]] |video = [[File:Teen Big Brother UK - Series 1 (2003) - Official Opening Titles|200px]] |numberofhousemates = 8 }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' other known as '''Teen Big Brother '''was a teenage spin-off of ''[[Big Brother (UK)]]''. As this series was pre-recorded, it had similar aspects of the American version such as housemates voting to evict another and voting for a winner. ==Overview== ''Retrieved from Wikipedia''
Featuring eight 18-year-olds, it was broadcast between 13–17 October 2003 on Channel 4 and E4. Trailed as 'The Experiment', Teen Big Brother was originally shot in advance over the course of ten days between 30 July to 8 August, to air in 2003 as an educational item, screened as part of Channel 4's 4Learning programming. The tasks were created so as to promote such values as cooperation and team spirit, and topics like politics and religion were discussed. After editing, however, the footage was felt to be compelling enough for a more mass-market time slot, so the show was moved ahead to October 2003 and formatted to be shown over one week (five episodes). Teen Big Brother was different from the original Big Brother UK series in a number of ways. Since it was pre-recorded, the contestants themselves and not the audience decided which housemates were to be voted out. At the end, the eventual winner of a grand prize was decided by group decision (a cash prize was replaced by a round-the-world trip). No alcohol or cigarettes were allowed. The basic premise of the show, however, remained the same, and no special treatment was made for the housemates. On Day Six/Seven, Jade Dyer and Tommy Wright became the first Big Brother UK contestants to have sex on the show in its history. According to The Independent, this was the first real-life sexual act shown on British television (although nothing explicit was seen; the two were under bedcovers). This sparked controversy in the British media and comment on teenage safe sex education. An edited version of Teen Big Brother – The Experiment was eventually broadcast in January 2004 as part of 4Learning's morning schedule and was designed with formal curriculum teaching in mind. The incident featuring Jade and Tommy did not appear in this edit.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Big_Brother:_The_Experiment#Overview ==Twists== *'''Teenage Housemates:''' For the first time in UK history, the ''Big Brother House'' will be inhabited with eight 18-year-olds. *'''Voting Changes:''' Since the series was prerecorded, the housemates had to vote to nominate, evict, save, and to win. ==Housemates== {{Template:TBB Progress}} ==Tasks== {{TBB Tasks}} ==Nominations/Voting History== {{Template:TBB V/N History}} ==Game History== {{TBB Game History}} ==Trivia== ==References== {{Reflist}} {{UK Seasons}} {{Season Nav}} [[Category:Seasons]] [[Category:United Kingdom Seasons]] [[Category:Pre-Recorded Seasons]]

The competition is named "Black Box" due to the complete darkness inside the room, which significantly increases the difficulty as houseguests must navigate without being able to see. A similar variation of this competition is called '''[[The Haunting]]''', where houseguests are usually provided with headlamps to help guide them through the dark environment. == Rules == In this competition, houseguests enter a completely dark “Black Box.” They must locate specific items in the darkness and return them to designated spots. The houseguest (or team) that secures the highest number of items in the shortest time wins. === Format Variations === * '''''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]''''': Each houseguest had to keep one hand on a button while searching. Failure to return in time forced that player to leave the Black Box. * '''''[[Celebrity Big Brother 1 (US)]]''''': Players crawled through a mock restaurant and raced to escape in the fastest time. * '''''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]''''': Houseguests hunted for folders—one fewer than the number of competitors. The player left without a folder received a [[Unitard|punishment]]. One special folder granted its finder automatic advancement to the next round; any other folder simply avoided the punishment. * '''''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]''''': Players searched the darkness for the true exit while facing multiple decoy exits. The last to find the correct exit was [[Premiere Night Eviction|evicted on Day 1]]. == History == * '''''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]''''': Debuted as a Have/Have-Not Competition. [[Andy Herren]], [[McCrae Olson]], and [[Spencer Clawson]] won, becoming Haves for the week. * '''''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]''''': Returned as a Battle of the Block competition. {{United States}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring endurance [[Head of Household]], [[Re-Entry Competition|Re-Entry]] and [[Nomination Competition|Nomination]] competition. ==Rules== #Each houseguest stands on a narrow ledge attached to a large, upright wall. Depending on the season's design, handholds or grips may also have fixtures which houseguests can hang onto. #The houseguests must remain standing on their ledges for as long as possible while enduring various physical obstacles, including forward wall tilts, cold water, slime, moving footrests, or swinging props. #The moment that a houseguest touches the ground or falls off the wall, they are eliminated from the competition. The last houseguest remaining on the wall wins and is crowned the new [[Head of Household]]. ===Variations=== In certain seasons, objects (such as balls or tokens) are shot toward the wall. Winning may require catching a designated number of items first, or simply outlasting the rest of the field if no one completes the secondary objective. In certain seasons there may be [[Have-Not]] Punishments. The first select few houseguests to drop from the wall may automatically be designated as Have-Nots for the week, subjecting them to cold showers, slop, and uncomfortable beds. ==History== ==== United States ==== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 10 (US)]]'', during Week 4. Houseguest [[April Dowling]] won the competition, winning her first and only HOH of the season. The competition appeared again in ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', during Week 3. Houseguest [[Matt Hoffman]] won the competition, winning his first HOH of the season. On ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'' , [[Danielle Murphree]] won the competition, winning her first HOH of the season. On ''[[Big Brother 15 (US)]]'', the competition has divided in 2 parts (the jury re-entry competition & the HOH competition). [[Judd Daugherty]] was able returned to the house, but [[Elissa Slater]] was the winner, and winning her first and only HOH of the season. On ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'', the competition was played at the first part of final HOH, [[Cody Calafiore]] won it, and was able to take part in the final part of the HOH competition. ==List of ''{{PAGENAME}}'' Competitions== ===United States=== ====Civilian==== {|class="wikitable" style="margin:auto; text-align:center; font-size: 9pt;" |- style="background-color:#CCCCCC;" ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Season ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Week ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Competition Variant ! style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | Name Variant ! colspan="6" style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);"| Winner |- | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 10 | style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | 4 | rowspan="4" style="background-color:#CCCCCC; color:#3a3a3a;" | Head of Household | style="border: 1px dotted #CCC;" | "Livin' On The Edge" | colspan="6" style="border: 1px dotted rgb(204, 204, 204);" |

{{competition | image= [[file:Temptation Competition.PNG|250px]] | description= An immunity competition held before nominations that leaves the loser a third nominee, or a luxury competition where taking the prize leaves a consequence on the house. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} | seasonsappeared= [[Big Brother 19 (US)]]
[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]
[[Big Brother 28 (US)]] }}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a special kind of [[Luxury Competition|Luxury]] and [[Immunity Competition]] held in ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]''. The first competition of the season was a {{PAGENAME}} that gave the houseguests a chance at taking a cash prize, but as a consequence, the [[Big Brother Swap]] took place. Following [[Jessica Graf]]'s acceptance of the [[Den of Temptation]], the competition returned to the house. For weeks 5, 6 & 7, houseguests have the option to opt in to compete in the {{PAGENAME}}. The winner of the competition will win immunity for the week while the last place finisher will be automatically nominated as a third nominee. The immunity variant of this competition would return in ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'', while the luxury variant would return in ''[[Big Brother 28 (US)]]''. ==History== ===Big Brother 19=== ====Week 1==== The 16 houseguests were sequestered in separate pods and were given the offer of $25,000. The first houseguest to press their button would win the money. The identity of the person who pressed the button would remain anonymous, however their actions would unleash a consequence onto the winner and the house as a whole. [[Alex Ow]], [[Cody Nickson]], [[Jason Dent]], [[Kevin Schlehuber]], [[Mark Jansen]], [[Ramses Soto]] and [[Raven Walton]] all pressed their buttons, but Kevin was the fastest. Since he accepted the offer, it required him to throw the first Head of Household competition. As another consequence for the button being pressed, [[Paul Abrahamian]] from ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)|Big Brother 18]]'' entered the House as the 17th houseguest, setting off the [[Big Brother Swap]], which ended up causing [[Cameron Heard]] to get evicted, with Paul taking his place. ====Week 5==== [[Alex Ow]], [[Jason Dent]], [[Mark Jansen]], and [[Matt Clines]] played in the first new Temptation Competition. The competition was [[Bowlerina]] and Mark ended up winning immunity, while Jason got last place and was the third nominee. Jason ended up getting vetoed, leaving the HOH's two nominees on the block. This competition was done one at a time, with an audience. ====Week 6==== This week, everyone who was eligible played in the competition except for [[Christmas Abbott]]. The competition was [[The Haunting|Strangest Things]] and [[Cody Nickson]] ended up winning immunity, while [[Jessica Graf]] got last place and was the third nominee. Jessica ended up getting evicted that week in a 7-1-0 vote. This competition was played individually and privately and was timed. ====Week 7==== Once again, everyone who could play did, except for Christmas. The competition was Where Were You? and Mark won immunity for the second time, while Matt got last place and was the third nominee. Matt ended up winning the POV. This competition was played all at once by everyone. ===Big Brother 21 (US)=== In Season 21, the competition was brought back in its Immunity variation at the Final 10, known as "[[America's Field Trip]]". Three houseguests were voted into the competition, where the winner would earn immunity, the runner-up would earn a punishment, and the loser would be nominated. [[Jackson Michie]] came out on top, earning himself safety, while [[Analyse Talavera]] survived and was left with a chicken costume as her punishment. Missing summer on the Jersey Shore with my family. We're usually there during the weekends. The house isn't huge but my family is so there's a lot of people in a little house, playing games, drinking, cooking, making stupid videos, getting tan. There's nothing better than the summer with them.

My strategy is inspired by my mother. She cooks and cleans for the entire family and she's everyone's favorite person. I want to be the Italian mother of the house. I want to take care of everyone and make them feel safe and loved. No one wants to vote out that person.

The Impact of COVID-19 on Big Brother.head:
{{Underconstruction}}[[File:Coronavirus.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A three-dimensional view of the virus<ref>{{Cite web|url =https://www.state.gov/coronavirus/|title =Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19)|language = English|publisher = United States Department of State|accessdate = 13 March 2020}}</ref>]]
The '''[[wikipedia:COVID-19 pandemic|2019–21 coronavirus pandemic]]''' is a current ongoing pandemic around the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic|title = 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic|language = English|work = Wikipedia|publisher = Wikipedia|accessdate = 13 March 2020}}</ref> The virus has impacted various sporting events, social interactions, and television events. When the virus hit the ''Big Brother'' world, it became an unprecedented event, changing how many franchises around the world are dealing with the event.


==No Audience Live Shows==
Amid the rising numbers infected by the pandemic, precautionary measures strictly suggest minimizing social contact to avoid being infected by the disease. As a result, various shows all over the world started airing without a studio audience to observe social distancing and to prevent the spread of the COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.manilatimes.net/2020/03/10/news/latest-stories/abs-cbn-bans-studio-audience/701899/|title = ABS-CBN bans studio audience|language = English|publisher = The Manila Times|accessdate = 13 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.vulture.com/2020/03/late-night-shows-nyc-coronavirus.html|title = Late-Night Shows in New York Will Tape Without Audiences Due to Coronavirus
|language = English|work = Vulture|publisher = Vulture|accessdate = 13 March 2020}}</ref>

*On March 8, 2020, [[Grande Fratello (franchise)|Grande Fratello]] announced that there would be no more guests entering the house. Days later on March 11, it was announced that live episodes of its [[Grande Fratello VIP 4|4th Celebrity Season]] would no longer feature an audience.

*On March 12, 2020, [[Big Brother Canada (franchise)|Big Brother Canada]] followed suit in this precautionary measure and announced that live episodes on its [[Big Brother Canada 8|8th Season]] will broadcast without a studio audience after the outbreak of COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://etcanada.com/news/607577/big-brother-canada-to-tape-without-studio-audience-over-coronavirus-concerns/|title = ‘Big Brother Canada’ To Tape Without Studio Audience Over Coronavirus Concerns|language = English|work = ET Canada|publisher = ET Canada|accessdate = 13 March 2020}}</ref> However, the March 19 episode was broadcasted remotely from host [[Arisa Cox|Arisa Cox's]] home (see below). This practice has been continued for every season since.

*Also on March 12, 2020, [[Big Brother Brazil (franchise)|Big Brother Brazil]] decided it would not have a live audience for, at least, the 8th eviction on March 17, 2020 as a precautionary measure.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://oglobo.globo.com/cultura/revista-da-tv/por-coronavirus-eliminacao-do-bbb20-nao-tera-plateia-diz-boninho-24300321|title = Por coronavírus, eliminação do 'BBB20' não terá plateia, diz Boninho|language = Portuguese|work = globo|publisher = globo|accessdate = 16 March 2020}}</ref>

*Starting at the beginning of the season, [[Big Brother Portugal (franchise)|Big Brother Portugal]] decided not to have a live audience. However, starting on June 7, 2020, a live audience would be present in the studio.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://dioguinho.pt/gala-de-hoje-do-big-brother-2020-vai-ter-publico/|title = SURPRESA! Gala de hoje do ‘Big Brother 2020’ vai ter públicolanguage = Portuguese|work = dioguinho|publisher = dioguinho|accessdate = 7 June 2020}}</ref>

==History== ===Creation=== The Committee was formed in Week 1 during [[Cody Calafiore]]'s Head of Household reign after talking to [[Memphis Garrett]]. Memphis would then go ahead and reel in [[Christmas Abbott]], [[Dani Briones]], [[Nicole Franzel]] and [[Tyler Crispen]]. ===In Power=== The Committee alliance was in power during Cody's Week 1 HOH reign. Cody would go on and nominate [[Keesha Smith]] and [[Kevin Campbell]] for eviction, after his original plan was ruined by the [[Safety Suite Competition|Safety Suite]], with his target being Keesha. Despite not winning the Power of Veto, the nominations were kept the same and despite [[Janelle Pierzina]]'s attempts to get votes for Keesha, Keesha was sent packing by a 13-0 vote, solidifying their first successful HOH reign. === Is He With Us?=== Memphis would go on to win the second HOH of the season, this time, as both Janelle and [[Kaysar Ridha]] were vulnerable - it was clear who the targets were. Despite his alliance's pitches, Memphis played the middle and nominated [[David Alexander]] and [[Nicole Anthony]], with his primary target being David. Memphis and Tyler both competed in the Veto, and with distrust towards Memphis growing, Tyler was gunning for the Veto. Despite both landing in the final 2, Tyler lost the Veto, and Memphis officially had full power for the week. He discarded the Veto, angering the 5 who pitched backdooring Janelle from the House. Nicole was then evicted by a 10-2 vote. ===Getting out a Target === After the sneaky second week, Tyler would win the third HOH of the season. This time, nothing would come between the alliance's goal. Tyler nominated Janelle and Kaysar for eviction, with their target being Janelle. With Cody winning the POV, their fates were pretty much sealed. Janelle was finally evicted by a 9-2 vote. ===Eliminating their enemies=== The alliance continued to dominate. In Week 4, affiliate Enzo won HOH and aided the alliance

Day 65, 10, Day 71, & 11) |Lowest= [[Tiffany Mitchell]] (6/16) |Highest= [[Xavier Prather]] (1/16) }} '''The Cookout''' is the dominant alliance on [[Big Brother 23 (US)|''Big Brother 23 (US)'']], that was created on the first week of the season. The alliance consisted of [[Azah Awasum]], [[Derek Frazier]], [[Kyland Young]], [[Hannah Chaddha]], [[Tiffany Mitchell]], and [[Xavier Prather]]. The alliance was created with the goal of having the first ever black winner. In order to keep the alliance a secret, most of the members would pair up with someone not part of the alliance. Pairing up also kept them safe, as there was never a situation where two members went on the block, and the alliance had enough numbers to keep them safe in case one member was nominated alongside their pair. They dominated from the start; winning 10 of the 14 HOHs, 7 of the 13 POVs, influencing every eviction and nearly every nomination, and successfully evicting all non-members. With all the non-members evicted, they accomplished their goal of guaranteeing the first ever black winner. Due to their dominance in comps, nominations, and evictions, eliminating all of their opponents and managing to get all six members into the final 6, this alliance is one of the greatest and most dominant alliances ever. Despite their dominance, they were polarizing to the fans. Many fans found the season boring and predictable, due to the Cookout steamrolling the season. The most criticism they faced was for evicting all the non-alliance members, all of whom were not black, which made a lot of fans feel that the alliance based their votes and decisions on race. Many other fans, however, believe that the Cookout's mission of achieving the first-ever black winner of the series was important and long-overdue. == Members ==

== History== ===Creation=== Tiffany in Week 1, was talking to Derek F and Azah about creating an all-black alliance in the house. Xavier walked in on them and agreed to the plan. Apart of the group, they discussed how they would not be caught up with one another to avoid suspicion, yet help each other to advance with knowledge sought from around the house. Four of the members would each pair up with someone not in the alliance to hide the alliance, prevent two members from going on the block, and protect the alliance from eviction in case a member is nominated alongside their pair. Hannah was not an original official member of the Cookout, as the other members expressed worry that she was too young to understand the importance of the mission. However, in Week 4, Hannah was officially added to the Cookout after her and Tiffany started growing closer. By Week 6, as the jury phase begun, each member of the Cookout had their own pawn in the game to help themselves advance. Hannah had [[Derek Xiao]], Tiffany had [[Claire Rehfuss]], Derek F and Azah had [[Britini D'Angelo]], Kyland had [[Sarah Beth Steagall]], and Xavier had [[Alyssa Lopez]]. === Dominance === The Cookout dominated the game from the jump. After being left out of the [[The Original Six|initial power structure]], [[Danielle Reyes]] and [[Jason Guy]] created the alliance during the first few days of the game, dedicating their loyalty to each other. ===Dominance=== Despite the duo being blindsided at [[Lori Olsen]]’s eviction, their ally [[Marcellas Reynolds]] won the next [[Head of Household]] competition, leaving them room to maneuver and play the game. After Marcellas nominated [[Josh Feinberg]] and [[Tonya Paoni]], two members of the initial majority alliance, Danielle and Jason aided in evicting Tonya. They viewed Josh as someone on the outskirts of the majority alliance and thus more likely to flip. Despite Danielle and Jason losing an ally in [[Amy Crews]] in Week 3, they regained some power after [[Gerry Lancaster]] won Head of Household. Gerry targeted the [[showmance]] of [[Eric Ouellette]] and [[Lisa Donahue]], placing them on the block alongside each other. During the past few weeks, Danielle had been getting closer to Lisa and starting to talk game with her. This led to the duo deciding they needed to keep Lisa as an important number in the future. The duo created a plan where they would vote opposite ways, resulting in Gerry breaking the tie to evict Eric. However, after [[Chiara Jude Berti]] leaked that she was flipping her vote, Jason joined Danielle in voting out Eric. After Chiara won the Week 5 Head of Household competition, Danielle and Jason managed to convince her to go after Josh for his untrustworthiness, despite him being a member of her alliance. Later, Chiara put Josh on the block, and he was subsequently evicted in a unanimous vote. After Amy returned to the game through a house vote in which Danielle and Jason both voted for her, she won Head of Household. Amy used her power to target Chiara, whom she had a long-time rivalry with, nominating her and her showmance [[Roddy Mancuso]]. '''The Mastermind''' is the main antagonist of ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]'', where he appeared to introduce various twists throughout the season.
==Identity==
During the season finale, his identity was revealed to be ''[[Big Brother 2 (US)]]'' winner, [[Will Kirby|Dr. Will Kirby]]. However, it was later revealed that this was a set-up to frame Dr. Will, and that there was not one, but instead three Masterminds: [[Eric Stein]], [[Jessie Godderz]] and [[Frankie Grande]], all seeking out revenge for twists that cost them the wins in their respective seasons ([[America's Player]] from ''[[Big Brother 8 (US)]]'', the [[Coup d'Etat]] from ''[[Big Brother 11 (US)]]'' and the [[Rewind Button]] from ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]''). Each Mastermind had a different mask, and clues around their identity were hidden throughout the house.

== History ==

=== Saving Julie ===
The mastermind captured Julie and stole the HOH Relic. [[Zach Cornell]] saved [[Julie Chen-Moonves|Julie]], while [[Jimmy Heagerty]] recovered the [[Head of Household|HOH]] Relic.

=== Destroying The Lair ===
At the first HOH Competition of the season, [[Vince Panaro]] successfully was able to destroy the mastermind's lair after winning.

=== The Accomplice ===
The Mastermind recruited [[Amy Bingham]] to be the [[The Saboteur|Secret Accomplice]] in order to set the events of the premiere in motion, culminating in allowing [[Rachel Reilly]] into the cast, and then giving Amy an opportunity to become the true 17th houseguest herself. 

=== Powers ===
He also was responsible for introducing various [[Secret Power Competition|powers]] into the game within the first two weeks.

=== Month of Mayhem ===
==== White Locust Resort ====
In Week 9, the Mastermind kicked off his Month of Mayhem, which would start with a surprise elimination at the White Locust Resort, with one houseguest not returning to the Big Brother House. The houseguests were also told that there are more twists yet to come. The elimination would be orchestrated and done by his concierge, [[Big Brother 20 (US)|Season 20]] runner-up/fan favorite and [[Big Brother 22 (US)|Season 22]] All-Star [[Tyler Crispen]].

==== Showdown with Zingbot ====
The Mastermind confronted [[The Zingbot]] after he broke into Hotel Mystere to zing the houseguests. After a face-off with many failed attempts and plenty of zings, The Mastermind successfully destroyed Zingbot, setting up the next HOH competition.

==== Double Eviction ====
On Day 73, the Mastermind introduced the final BB Blockbuster, and following [[Kelley Jorgensen]]'s eviction, he announced that it was double eviction night and that it was, "all about him." The following Head of Household and Power of Veto competitions were both based on him.

==== The Sanctum ====
In Week 11, the Mastermind orchestrated an eviction all on his own, without the help of Julie. The Head of Household competition, nomination ceremony, and veto meeting all took place inside of "the Sanctum", which was a dark room dimly lit with several ritualistic candles. During the nomination ceremony, the Head of Household, Vince Panaro, made his nominations by placing voodoo dolls resembling each houseguest on a table in the middle of the Sanctum. Instead of casting their votes to evict secretly in the [[Diary Room]], the houseguests casted their votes to evict in front of the nominees by stabbing the voodoo doll of the nominee they wished to evict.

Victor became a major competition threat, winning multiple HOHs and a veto while helping eliminate key rivals like Paulie. Despite his strong second run, he was evicted again in a 2-1 vote during Week 9 after his own allies turned on him, but he returned once more by winning the jury re-entry twist, making ''Big Brother'' history as a two-time returnee in a single season. Victor once again reunited with Paul, and they briefly formed [[Final Four (BB18)|a final four alliance]] with [[Nicole Franzel]] and [[Corey Brooks]], but they were ultimately betrayed and Victor was permanently evicted in 5th place and became the seventh member of [[the Jury]]. Because of his funny personality and constant underdog position in the house, Victor has become one of the most popular contestants of his season. On finale night, Victor won [[America's Favorite Houseguest]], beating out James and Natalie. ==Biography== ''Retrieved from CBS.com'' '''Age:''' 25

Also, being one Google search away from proving someone wrong will be the hardest thing, ever.

{{Canada}} }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]] competition. ==Rules== Houseguests stand in a booth and listen to a clip of a houseguest saying something they have previously said in the house. One word or phrase is bleeped out, however. The houseguests competing must say if the word or phrase given to them as a possibility of being the bleeped word is true or false. If they get it right, they get a point. If not, they do not. The houseguest that gets the most points at the end of the competition wins HoH or PoV. ==History== The competition first appeared on ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)]]'' during that season's second [[Double Eviction]]. [[Derrick Levasseur]] notably won this competition in just one question. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 17 (US)]]'', eventual winner [[Steve Moses]] won the competition, securing himself a spot in the final three. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 18 (US)]]'', [[Paul Abrahamian]] won the competition after a tiebreaker with [[Nicole Franzel]], becoming the first member of the final three. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 19 (US)]]'', [[Paul Abrahamian]] won the competition and earned his spot in the final three for the second time. He won it with seven points. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 20 (US)]]'', [[JC Mounduix]] got his first win of the season through the competition and secured his spot in the final three. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 21 (US)]]'', once again played during a Double Eviction, [[Cliff Hogg III]] got his first Veto win of the season, beating [[Christie Murphy]] by just one point. ==List of ''What The Bleep?'' [[Celebrity Big Brother Quebec 6]] (twice)'' }}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a recurring [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]] competition. ==Rules== The houseguests have to watch a video or performance just before the competition begins, and then answer questions about what they saw. ==History== The Competition made its debut in ''[[Big Brother 7]]'', where, shortly before the Competition began, they were shown clips from the first 4 competitions which they were then quizzed on, having to answer either 'A' or 'B.' [[James Rhine]] won the competition. In ''[[Big Brother 10]]'', with the same set-up as in season 7, the competition returned in the traditional Final 4 format of the houseguests standing in a circle, having to move forward to answer true or backward to answer false. [[Dan Gheesling]] won the competition. The competition appeared with the exact same format from season 10 in ''[[Big Brother 14]]'', where [[Danielle Murphree]] won the Competition. The competition appeared twice in ''[[Big Brother 17]]. ''The first time, the houseguests watched a live, 90s dance performance and were asked true or false questions about the scene, and [[Liz Nolan]] and [[Shelli Poole]] won HOH. A variant of the competition then appeared during the second [[Double Eviction]] week of the season, where the houseguests were asked to watch clips of the road trip adventure the first 6 evicted houseguests went on, about which they were then quizzed through a series of true or false questions. Liz Nolan won once again. In ''[[Big Brother: Over The Top]]'', during the Double Eviction, just before the Competition began, the houseguests had to watch a video advertising products from the BB Shoping Network, and memorize details from the clip. [[Danielle Lickey]] won this competition. In ''[[Big Brother 19]]'', the season 17 version returned, but instead of watching a dance performance, the houseguests had to watch a live magic show with rapidly changing costumes. [[Alex Ow]] won HOH. The OTT version reappeared in ''[[Big Brother 20]]'', this time having the houseguests watch a video about the new Big Brother product launch. [[Scottie Salton]] won the competition. In ''[[Celebrity Big Brother 2]]'', the competition saw 2 more uses. The first aligned with the season 17 and 19 versions, this time having the houseguests watch a live skit from Gallagher involving the smashing of watermelons, which [[Lolo Jones]] won. Then, the competition inexplicably appeared as a [[Power of Veto]] competition during a double eviction, where the houseguests had to watch a sitcom and answer questions about the show. [[Tamar Braxton]] won this competition. '''What’s your reaction to getting to play ''Big Brother''?''' I am so excited. It hasn’t hit me. It doesn’t feel real yet. I am a massive fan of ''Big Brother''. I’m trying to keep my feet on Planet Earth. I’m trying to keep my head out of the clouds, and I’m trying to take it in and just absorb all of this as much as I can, until it hits me that it’s real. It feels surreal being a houseguest on ''Big Brother'' this season. Again, it hasn’t really hit me yet. I know that no matter what strategy you have coming into this, it could go out the window immediately. So it just is excitement, anxiousness. I’ve just sweat through my deodorant thinking about it. I am just ready to go. I’m eager. I’ve been waiting a very long time for this opportunity. '''What’s your strategy going into the game?''' I think my strategy coming into the ''Big Brother'' house is to compartmentalize this game down into weekly “mini-games” of ''Big Brother''. I want to view every single individual week as its own mini-game of ''Big Brother''. And all I need to do for those weeks is survive it one at a time and slowly, take one step at a time. You can’t say you’re going to win the World Series without winning enough games to get to the playoffs. So I have to win the individual days, individual conversations, weeks, whatever that may be. Take it one week at a time and adapt. And wing it, and then adapt, wing it, adapt. It’s the “WAWA” technique. You just wing, adapt, wing, adapt. That’s what I got to do. }}The '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is known specifically as a recurring type of [[Power of Veto]] or [[Head of Household]] competition.
==Rules==
==History==
===''Big Brother 12''===
Houseguests had to retrieve one puzzle piece at a time from a basket, race across a balance beam, and construct four puzzles that spell out the word "veto" while on a rotating platform. However, if they were to fall off the balance beam or rotating platform at any time, they were eliminated. 

===''Big Brother 13''===
Houseguests were tasked with building Zingbot's wife, by placing puzzle pieces onto an incomplete robot. Once all four sides were covered, a head and arms must then be connected. The first houseguest to assemble the robot correctly wins. 

===''Big Brother 14''===
Houseguests had to build a pipeline from the Zingtonium chamber to the transformer, passing through all six gateways. Once completed, they had to guide a Zingtonium orb through the pipeline and into the transformer, with the first person to finish winning. 

===''Big Brother 15''===
Houseguests competed in [[Ball Roll]], in which they had to throw their Zingtonium ball across a slope and catch it when it reaches the other side. When the ball crosses the top, the player gets an energy point. If at any time a ball drops, that houseguest's score resets to 0. Whoever reaches 250 energy points first wins the POV. 

===''Big Brother 16''===
Houseguests had to connect a series of cables through four circuit boxes, lighting up bulbs at each. Players had to follow circuit paths and plug-in cables correctly, making sure electricity can flow to each light bulb. The first person to light up all boxes wins the POV. 

===''Big Brother 17''===
Houseguests competed in [[Morph 'O' Matic]], in which players were shown images of three houseguests' faces morphed together. Players were then tasked with figuring out which houseguests were being shown and lighting up their names on the answer board. The player to correctly guess all mash-ups in the shortest amount of time wins. 

===''Big Brother 18''===
Houseguests competed in [[Yankee Swap]], in which they shot a bean bag onto a grid of numbers and aimed to get the highest score in each round, as to not be eliminated. Each time a player is eliminated, they earn a prize, such as the POV, a vacation, money, or a punishment. 

===''Big Brother 19''===
Houseguests competed in [[Slippery Slope]], in which each player must transport liquid in a small scoop from one container into another, while on a slippery slope. The houseguest to fill their jug first wins. 

===''Big Brother 20''===
Houseguests participated in [[Hide and Go Veto]], in which each player hides a veto in the house, and tries to locate other players' veto cards. After five out of six cards have been found, they are opened to determine who is knocked out of the competition, with the owner of the sole card left in the house being the winner. 

===''Big Brother 21''===
Houseguests competed in [[Pull Some Strings]], in which players use two ropes to maneuver a ball up a wall, while aiming to knock out multiple targets. Players also attempt not to drop their ball into any holes on the wall, with the first person to knock out each target winning the POV. 

===''Big Brother 22''===
Houseguests competed in Tiger Zing, in which players raced through a maze to find exotic alien tigers and bring them back to their corresponding cages. The player with the fastest time would win the competition and earn the POV.

On ''[[Big Brother 13 (US)]]'', eventual runner-up [[Porsche Briggs]] won her second Power of Veto of the season, as she won this competition. The following season, ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'', [[Danielle Murphree]] won the competition, winning her second PoV of the summer. {{Canada}} |image = Yankee Swap.jpeg}}'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (also known as the '''Prize Swapping Competition''') is a recurring [[Power of Veto]] and [[Head of Household]] competition. It is unique among competitions in that the winner of the competition does not automatically win the POV or HOH. This competition is notable for being the one that causes an unlucky houseguest to wear a [[Unitard]] for a week or be in [[Solitary Confinement]] for 24 hours. For French-Canadian Celebrity Versions, Yankee Swap was combined with the [[OTEV]] competitions. ==Rules== The players will compete in a series of rounds where they must try to score the highest number. The player with the lowest score each round will be eliminated from the game. If two or more players tie for the lowest score, they will play a tiebreaker round. Once they are eliminated, they must claim a prize which may contain money, vacations, advantages in the game, punishments, the power of veto, or the HOH key. The players that are eliminated in later rounds will have the option of keeping the prize that they have received or trading it for other prizes that have already been revealed. {{Competition |image = Wildcard Competition.jpg |description = An immunity competition held before nominations that leaves the winner the option to take safety, which results in a punishment that may affect them, their team, or the entire house. |countriesappeared = {{United States}} |seasonsappeared = ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]'' }} '''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a competition that was introduced in ''[[Big Brother 23 (US)]]''. The three teams that are not immune for the week will each select one competitor. Those three houseguests will then compete for immunity; if they win, they will be given the option to take safety, while the rest of their team remains vulnerable for nomination and eviction. Similar to the [[Den of Temptation]], if the winner decides to accept safety for the week, it will result in a punishment that may affect them, their team, or the entire house. Each team member may only play in one wildcard competition. Teams are given fifteen minutes to decide who should play in the competition. Should the team fail to agree, a random draw will decide who plays out of the remaining eligible houseguests. '''How does it feel to be on ''Big Brother''?''' It feels fantastic! It feels like I was born for this, competing, socializing, having fun. That’s what I do.
'''What’s your history with ''Big Brother''?''' I’m more of a casual viewer when it comes to ''Big Brother''. But recently I’ve been a ''Big Brother'' merchant. Every night, five hours a day, you name it, I’m watching.
'''What’s your strategy going into the house?''' When it comes to my strategy, I would tell you, except I’m not gonna. That’s top secret!
'''What are you going to bring to ''Big Brother'' that we’ve never seen before?''' Yash Patel. Silly question! Come on now.
'''What’s the biggest misconception people have about you?''' I think, because I’m very fun, people might not think I’m smart. But I’m actually secretly a nerd. Before I had this nice haircut, this nice beard, and this outfit, I had textbooks and pencils. That’s just the way it is.
'''Are you a hero or a villain?''' Asking whether or not I’ll be a hero or a villain is kind of tough, because I think I’ll be exactly what I need to be based on the situation.
'''Do you have a secret you plan on keeping about yourself in the game?''' So I don’t know if I actually want everybody to know that I’m a finance analyst. I might have to lie, say that I worked in marketing or something, because I don’t need people getting all insecure on me.
'''Are you open to showmances?''' Oh, of course I’m open to a showmance! You’re telling me I could win 750,000 and find a wife? Sign me up!
'''How do you normally handle conflict?''' There’s a lot of different ways I would handle conflict. I think it depends on the situation. If someone’s trying to get at me, I’ll most likely brush it off, but if there’s a conflict going on amongst other people, I’m in there making opportunity.
'''Do you have a secret talent or quirk you think will help you in the game?''' One of my hidden talents is that I’m really good at mazes. Ever since I was a kid, I’ve been very good at just putting a pencil on the paper and getting myself out of a maze. So, that’s one of those things where if there’s some sort of maze competition, maybe I could put that to use.
'''How will you crush your enemies?''' I will crush my enemies any which way, you name it. Socially, competitively, mentally, physically. Any way they need to be crushed.
